t: Set a cable pulley to its lowest position and attach a straight or EZ bar, then place a preacher bench a step in front of the machine facing away from it. | Sit on the bench and rest the backs of your upper arms flat against the angled pad, with your armpits near the top edge. | Reach down and grip the bar with an underhand (palms-up) grip at about shoulder-width, letting your arms straighten under the cable's tension. | Brace your core and keep your upper arms pinned to the pad as the starting position. | Curl the bar upward by contracting your biceps and brachialis until your forearms are nearly vertical, exhaling as you lift. | Squeeze at the top for a moment without letting your elbows drift off the pad. | Lower the bar slowly under control until your arms are almost fully extended, keeping tension on the muscle. | Complete your reps, then set the bar down with control and return the cable to the stack.

nH: פשיטות יד אחורית באחיזה הפוכה בכבלים (מוט SZ)
t: Attach an SZ-bar to a high cable pulley and set the pulley above head height. | Grip the angled ends of the SZ-bar with an underhand (palms-up) grip, hands roughly shoulder-width apart. | Step back slightly, stand tall with feet hip-width apart, and brace your core with a small forward lean from the hips. | Pin your upper arms against your sides so only your forearms move, and start with your elbows bent near 90 degrees. | Press the bar down by extending your elbows until your arms are fully straight, squeezing the triceps at the bottom. | Pause briefly in the locked-out position without letting your elbows drift forward or your shoulders round. | Let the bar rise under control back to the start, keeping tension on the triceps the whole way up. | Finish your reps, then guide the bar up to the stack and release it safely.

t: Set the cable pulley to the lowest position and attach a single handle. | Stand side-on to the machine with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, and grasp the handle with both hands down by the hip nearest the pulley. | Brace your core, keep your arms long, and set a slight bend in your knees. | Pull the handle up and across your body, rotating your torso and pivoting your back foot as you drive it toward the opposite shoulder. | Finish with your arms extended above the far shoulder, keeping your hips and trunk turned through the movement rather than only your arms. | Pause briefly at the top while keeping your core tight and your spine tall. | Lower the handle back down and across to the starting hip under control, resisting the cable the whole way. | Complete your reps on one side, then switch sides and repeat.
tRu: Установите блок троса в самое нижнее положение и прикрепите одинарную рукоять. | Stand side-on to the machine with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, and grasp the handle with both hands down by the hip nearest the pulley. | Напрягите корпус, держите руки длинными и слегка согните колени. | Pull the handle up and across your body, rotating your torso and pivoting your back foot as you drive it toward the opposite shoulder. | Finish with your arms extended above the far shoulder, keeping your hips and trunk turned through the movement rather than only your arms. | Pause briefly at the top while keeping your core tight and your spine tall. | Lower the handle back down and across to the starting hip under control, resisting the cable the whole way. | Выполните повторения на одну сторону, затем поменяйте стороны и повторите.
tHe: כוון את גלגלת הכבל למצב הנמוך ביותר וחבר ידית אחת. | Stand side-on to the machine with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, and grasp the handle with both hands down by the hip nearest the pulley. | הדק את הליבה, שמור על ידיים ארוכות וקבע כיפוף קל בברכיים. | Pull the handle up and across your body, rotating your torso and pivoting your back foot as you drive it toward the opposite shoulder. | Finish with your arms extended above the far shoulder, keeping your hips and trunk turned through the movement rather than only your arms. | Pause briefly at the top while keeping your core tight and your spine tall. | Lower the handle back down and across to the starting hip under control, resisting the cable the whole way. | בצע את החזרות בצד אחד, ואז החלף צדדים וחזור על התרגיל.

t: Set the pulley to the lowest position and attach a straight bar or handle. Grip it with both hands at about shoulder-width. | Stand facing the machine with feet hip-width apart and a slight bend in your knees. Step back so the cable is taut and stacks your weight over your midfoot. | Brace your core, pull your shoulder blades down, and set a flat, neutral spine. | Hinge at your hips and push your glutes back, letting the cable draw the bar down along the front of your thighs. | Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your back flat and shins near-vertical. | Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to standing, keeping the bar close to your body. | Finish fully upright with hips extended, then complete your reps and return the weight under control. | Step forward to rest the stack down safely once the set is done.

t: Set both cable pulleys to roughly shoulder height and attach a single handle to each side. | Sit upright on the bench between the cables, plant your feet, and draw your shoulder blades down and back against the seat. | Grab a handle in each hand and bring your arms out to your sides with a slight, fixed bend in your elbows. | Brace your core and start with the cables loaded, feeling a stretch across your chest at the outer position. | Squeeze your chest to bring both handles together in a wide arc in front of your chest, leading with your elbows. | Pause briefly when your hands meet and contract the pectorals hard at the top. | Lower the handles back out under control until you feel a stretch in your chest again, keeping the elbow angle constant. | Complete your reps, then return the handles to the stack one side at a time.

nR: Скрутки со скрещенными руками сидя на блоке
t: Set the cable pulley to roughly chest or shoulder height and attach a single handle. | Sit on a bench or stool side-on to the machine so the cable runs across your body, and plant your feet firmly for a stable base. | Reach across your body and grip the handle, bringing both hands together at the centre of your chest with your arms crossed. | Sit tall, brace your core, and set your shoulders so the tension is held by your trunk rather than your arms. | Rotate your torso away from the machine in a smooth, controlled arc, turning through the waist while keeping your hips and head facing forward. | Pause briefly at the end of the rotation, feeling the tension across the side of your waist. | Return under control to the starting position, resisting the cable rather than letting it snap you back. | Complete your reps on one side, then switch sides and repeat.

t: Set the cable pulley to a high position and attach a rope handle. | Sit on a bench or the floor facing the machine and grip the rope, bringing your hands alongside your head or in front of your collarbones. | Sit tall with a slight forward lean so the cable pulls against your abs and you feel tension before you start. | Brace your core and exhale as you crunch your torso down toward your thighs by rounding your spine, driving your elbows toward your knees. | Crunch using your abs rather than pulling with your arms or bending at the hips, squeezing hard at the bottom of the range. | Pause briefly in the fully contracted position to maximize tension on the rectus abdominis. | Inhale and slowly return to the upright start position under control, resisting the pull of the cable. | Complete your reps, then let the weight stack settle gently before standing up.

nR: Тяга к лицу сидя на блоке (с канатом)
t: Attach a rope to a cable pulley and set the pulley to face or upper-chest height. Sit facing the machine with your feet planted and your torso upright. | Grip the rope with a neutral (palms-facing-in) grip, holding one end in each hand with your thumbs pointing back toward you. | Extend your arms toward the pulley and let the weight gently stretch your shoulder blades forward, keeping your chest up and core braced. | Pull the rope toward your face, leading with your elbows and flaring them out and up so your upper arms stay roughly parallel to the floor. | As the rope nears your face, separate your hands and rotate them back, externally rotating at the shoulders so your knuckles finish facing the ceiling. | Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end position and hold for a brief pause without shrugging your traps. | Reverse the motion under control, letting your arms extend fully and your shoulder blades reach forward again. | Complete your reps, then return the weight to the stack with control.
tRu: Прикрепите канат к блоку и установите его на высоту лица или верхней части груди. Сядьте лицом к тренажёру, упритесь стопами в пол, корпус держите вертикально. | Grip the rope with a neutral (palms-facing-in) grip, holding one end in each hand with your thumbs pointing back toward you. | Extend your arms toward the pulley and let the weight gently stretch your shoulder blades forward, keeping your chest up and core braced. | Pull the rope toward your face, leading with your elbows and flaring them out and up so your upper arms stay roughly parallel to the floor. | Когда канат окажется у лица, разведите руки и разверните их назад, вращая плечи наружу так, чтобы костяшки в конце смотрели в потолок. | Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end position and hold for a brief pause without shrugging your traps. | Reverse the motion under control, letting your arms extend fully and your shoulder blades reach forward again. | Выполните повторения, затем подконтрольно верните вес на стек.
tHe: חבר חבל לגלגלת הכבל וכוון את הגלגלת לגובה הפנים או החזה העליון. שב מול המכשיר עם רגליים נטועות ופלג גוף זקוף. | Grip the rope with a neutral (palms-facing-in) grip, holding one end in each hand with your thumbs pointing back toward you. | Extend your arms toward the pulley and let the weight gently stretch your shoulder blades forward, keeping your chest up and core braced. | Pull the rope toward your face, leading with your elbows and flaring them out and up so your upper arms stay roughly parallel to the floor. | כשהחבל מתקרב לפנים, הפרד את הידיים וסובב אותן לאחור, עם רוטציה חיצונית בכתפיים כך שהאצבעות מסיימות פונות לתקרה. | Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end position and hold for a brief pause without shrugging your traps. | Reverse the motion under control, letting your arms extend fully and your shoulder blades reach forward again. | סיים את החזרות, ואז החזר את המשקל לערימה בשליטה.

Sit facing the machine with your feet braced and your knees slightly bent. | Reach forward and grip the handle, then sit tall with a long spine and your chest lifted. | Set your shoulders down and back, brace your core, and let your arms extend fully so you feel a stretch across your lats. | Drive your elbows down and back toward your hips, leading with the elbows rather than the hands to bias the lats. | Pull until the handle reaches your lower ribs or upper abdomen, squeezing your lats and lower traps at the end of the range. | Pause briefly in the contracted position, keeping your torso upright and avoiding any backward lean. | Extend your arms under control to the start, allowing your shoulder blades to travel forward for a full stretch on each rep. | Complete your reps, then return the handle to the stack with control.

t: Set the cable pulley to its lowest position and attach a single-grip handle. | Sit on a bench or seat facing the machine, feet flat on the floor, and grasp the handle in one hand with an underhand (palm-up) grip. | Let your arm hang down and slightly forward so the cable stays taut, keeping your elbow pinned close to your side. | Brace your core and sit tall, keeping your shoulder and upper arm still throughout the set. | Curl the handle up toward your shoulder by bending only at the elbow, squeezing the biceps at the top. | Pause briefly at the top, then lower the handle under control until your arm is almost fully extended and you feel a stretch in the biceps. | Complete all reps on one arm, then switch the handle to the other hand and repeat for an equal number of reps.

t: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, knees soft, and your weight balanced over the balls of your feet. | Brace your core and let your arms hang ready at your sides to swing for momentum. | Dip slightly by bending your ankles and knees, loading the calves like a spring. | Push explosively through the balls of both feet and swing your arms forward to hop a short distance ahead. | Keep the jump low and quick, leading with your ankles rather than driving hard through the hips. | Land softly on the balls of your feet, letting your ankles and knees bend to absorb the impact. | Reset your balance for a beat, then immediately bound into the next forward hop. | Continue for the planned time or distance, then slow to a stop and walk it off.

t: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, weight balanced over the balls of your feet and arms relaxed at your sides. | Brace your core and keep your knees nearly straight with only a slight, soft bend — the drive comes from your ankles, not a deep squat. | Push off the floor by extending through your ankles, springing up off the balls of both feet to leave the ground a few inches. | Keep your toes pulled up slightly as you rise so you land back on the balls of your feet, not flat-footed or on your heels. | Absorb the landing through your ankles and immediately rebound into the next hop, spending as little time on the ground as possible. | Use a quick, light arm swing in time with the hops to help rhythm and balance. | Continue for the planned time or rep count, keeping each jump small, springy, and evenly paced. | To finish, let the hops get smaller and lower until you settle to a still, standing position.

nE: Calf Raise from Deficit with Chair Supported
nR: Подъёмы на носки с дефицита с опорой на стул
t: Find a sturdy raised surface — a step, low platform, or weight plate — and place a stable chair within easy reach for support. | Stand on the edge with the balls of your feet on the surface and your heels hanging off the back, feet about hip-width apart. | Rest one or both hands lightly on the chair back for balance, keeping your weight through your forefeet rather than the chair. | Lower your heels under control until they drop below the level of your toes and you feel a deep stretch in your calves. | Pause briefly in the bottom stretch, keeping your knees straight but not locked. | Press through the balls of your feet and rise as high as possible onto your toes, squeezing your calves at the top. | Hold the top contraction for a moment, then lower slowly back into the deficit stretch. | Repeat for your target reps, then step off the edge with control.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and place a barbell on the ground across the middle of one calf. | Set your hands on the floor behind your hips and lift your seat slightly so your bodyweight presses the calf down onto the bar. | Cross your free leg over the working leg if you want to add extra pressure. | Roll slowly along the muscle by sliding your body forward and back, moving the bar from just above the ankle to just below the back of the knee. | When you find a tight or tender spot, pause and hold for 20–30 seconds while you breathe and let the tissue release. | Rotate the working leg in and out to roll the inner and outer heads of the gastrocnemius and the soleus beneath. | Turn over to face down and rest the front of the shin on the bar to roll the tibialis anterior, then sit back up to address the hamstrings the same way if desired. | Spend 30–60 seconds per area, then lower your hips, switch legs, and repeat on the other side.

t: Stand facing a wall about an arm's length away and place both palms flat on it at chest height. | Step one foot back roughly two feet, keeping that rear leg straight and both feet pointing forward. | Keep the heel of the rear foot pressed flat on the floor and the front knee softly bent. | Lean your hips and chest toward the wall by bending the front knee further until you feel a stretch through the upper calf of the rear leg (the gastrocnemius). | Hold this position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and keeping the rear heel down. | To target the deeper soleus, slightly bend the rear knee while keeping the heel planted, and hold again for 20–30 seconds. | Ease out of the stretch under control, then switch legs and repeat the same sequence on the other side.

t: Kneel on a mat with your knees hip-width apart and your shins and the tops of your feet pressing flat into the floor. | Stack your hips directly over your knees and place your hands on your lower back, fingers pointing down, to support the spine. | Draw your shoulder blades together, lift your chest toward the ceiling, and lengthen up through the crown of your head. | Press your hips forward over your knees as you begin to arch back, leading the movement with your chest rather than collapsing at the waist. | Keep your hands on your lower back, or, if it feels comfortable, reach back one hand at a time to rest your palms on your heels. | Allow your head to drop gently back only if your neck feels comfortable, keeping the throat soft and the breath steady. | Hold the pose for a few slow breaths, keeping your hips pressing forward and your thighs working. | To come up, draw your chin toward your chest, engage your core, and lead with your chest to lift your torso back to upright. | Sit back on your heels and pause for a breath before repeating.

t: Step up onto the captain's chair and place your forearms flat on the pads, gripping the handles with a firm hold. | Press your back against the back pad and let your legs hang straight down so your body forms a vertical line. | Brace your core and pull your shoulders down to take the slack out of your arms before you start. | Exhale and raise your knees toward your chest by flexing at the hips, curling your pelvis up slightly at the top. | Pause briefly at the top, keeping your back against the pad and avoiding any swing. | Inhale and lower your legs under control back to the hanging start position. | Complete your target reps, keeping each one slow and deliberate. | Lower your feet to the platform and step down to dismount safely.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your core braced. | Step one foot forward and lower into a lunge until both knees are bent to roughly 90°, with your back knee hovering just above the floor. | Drive explosively through both legs and jump straight up off the ground. | Switch the position of your legs in mid-air, bringing the back leg forward and the front leg back. | Land softly on the balls of your feet, immediately absorbing the impact by bending into a lunge on the opposite side. | Keep your torso upright and your front knee tracking over your toes as you land. | Repeat the jump and switch, alternating legs at a steady, controlled pace for the prescribed time or reps. | To finish, land in a stable lunge and step your feet back together to a standing position.

t: Start on all fours in a tabletop position, with your wrists directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips. | Spread your fingers wide and press evenly through your palms, keeping your arms straight without locking the elbows. | Set a neutral spine to begin, with your head and neck in line with your back and your gaze toward the floor. | Exhale slowly as you draw your navel toward your spine and round your back upward toward the ceiling. | Tuck your chin gently toward your chest and let your tailbone curl under, deepening the rounding through your mid and upper back. | Pause for a breath at the top of the stretch, feeling the muscles along your spine lengthen. | Inhale as you release and return smoothly to the neutral tabletop position. | Repeat for several slow breaths, moving with your breath rather than rushing the motion.

t: Start on all fours in a quadruped position, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips. | Set your wrists, knees, and shins firmly on the floor, and keep your spine in a flat, neutral position to begin. | Inhale gently to prepare, keeping your neck long and your head in line with your spine. | As you exhale, slowly round your back upward toward the ceiling, drawing your belly button in and tucking your chin toward your chest. | Continue arching until you feel a comfortable stretch along your spine and back muscles, without forcing the range. | Hold the rounded position briefly, breathing steadily and feeling the stretch through your erector spinae. | Inhale as you slowly release back to the flat, neutral starting position with control. | Repeat for the desired number of slow, controlled repetitions.

t: Start on all fours in a tabletop position, with your wrists stacked under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. | Set a neutral spine to begin: keep your back flat, your head in line with your torso, and your gaze toward the floor. | Inhale to prepare, keeping your core lightly engaged and your weight evenly distributed across your hands and knees. | As you exhale, slowly round your spine toward the ceiling, drawing your belly button up and tucking your chin toward your chest. | Continue arching one vertebra at a time until you feel a comfortable stretch across your upper, mid, and lower back. | Hold the rounded position for a breath or two, feeling the stretch spread through the erector spinae along your waist. | Inhale as you slowly release back to the flat, neutral tabletop position with control. | Repeat for 5 to 10 slow, breath-paced reps, never forcing the range of motion.

t: Start on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips, keeping your spine in a neutral, flat position. | Spread your fingers and press evenly through your palms, looking down at the floor with your neck relaxed and in line with your spine. | Exhale slowly as you round your spine toward the ceiling, drawing your belly button up and tucking your chin gently toward your chest. | Pause at the top of the arch and feel the stretch spread across your lower back, mid-spine, and the sides of your waist. | Inhale as you reverse the movement, letting your back return to a flat, neutral position without sagging at the lower back. | Move slowly and smoothly between rounding and flattening, syncing each phase with your breathing. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, then lower your hips back toward your heels to rest and finish.

t: Kneel on a mat with both knees together and the tops of your feet flat on the floor behind you. | Sit your hips back lightly toward your heels and brace your core so your lower back stays neutral. | Place your hands on your hips or reach back toward your heels for support. | Slowly lift your chest and tilt your head back to look up toward the ceiling, pushing your hips gently forward. | Keep pressing your hips forward until you feel a comfortable stretch down the front of your thighs. | Breathe slowly and hold the position for 20–30 seconds without bouncing. | Ease out of the stretch under control, returning your hips and head to a neutral kneeling position. | Rest briefly, then repeat for 2–3 holds on each side or as a single sustained hold.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, chest up, and core gently braced. | Shift your weight onto your left foot and drive your right knee up toward your chest in a controlled, deliberate motion. | At the same time, raise both arms in an upbeat, celebratory motion to add rhythm and momentum. | Lower your right foot back to the floor under control and return your arms to your sides. | Repeat on the other side, driving your left knee up while keeping your torso upright. | Find a steady, repeatable rhythm and continue alternating knees for your target time or rep count. | To progress, add a light hop on the standing leg as you drive the knee; to regress, step the knee up without leaving the ground. | Finish by slowing the pace, then bring both feet together and let your breathing settle.

nR: Растяжка с вытянутой ногой на стуле
t: Stand facing a sturdy chair, an arm's length away, with your feet hip-width apart and your weight evenly balanced. | Lift one leg and place your heel on the seat of the chair, keeping that knee straight and your toes pointing up toward you. | Square your hips so both hip bones face forward and keep your standing leg slightly soft, not locked. | Straighten your spine and lengthen through the crown of your head before you move. | Hinge forward from your hips, sliding your hands down the raised leg until you feel a gentle stretch along the back of the thigh. | Stop at the first point of mild tension, keeping your back flat rather than rounding your shoulders. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly and steadily. | Ease back upright, lower your foot to the floor, then repeat on the other leg.

t: Stand tall at the top of your mat with your feet hip-width apart and your weight balanced evenly through both feet. | Inhale and sweep your arms forward to shoulder height, reaching them straight out in front of you with the palms facing down. | Exhale and bend your knees, sending your hips back and down as if lowering toward a chair behind you. | Keep your knees tracking over your toes and your weight settling into your heels so your thighs move toward parallel with the floor. | Lengthen your spine and lift your chest, drawing your lower ribs in to keep the front of your torso long. | Reach actively through your fingertips while sliding your shoulder blades down your back, away from your ears. | Hold for 5 to 8 slow breaths, breathing steadily and keeping your core gently braced throughout the hold. | To release, inhale, press through your heels, and straighten your legs as you lower the arms back to your sides.

t: Stand tall in Mountain Pose with your feet together or hip-width apart and your weight balanced through both feet. | Inhale and sweep your arms overhead, reaching the fingertips toward the ceiling with palms facing each other. | Exhale and bend your knees, sending your hips back and down as if you were lowering into a chair behind you. | Keep your weight in your heels and your knees tracking over your toes, sinking until your thighs are as close to parallel with the floor as your mobility allows. | Draw your lower ribs in and lengthen your tailbone down to keep a long, neutral spine rather than rounding or over-arching. | Reach your arms up alongside your ears, relaxing your shoulders away from them, and gaze forward or slightly up. | Hold the pose for several steady breaths, keeping your thighs, glutes, and core engaged. | To release, inhale, press through your heels to straighten your legs, and exhale to lower your arms back to your sides.

t: Start in a high plank with your wrists stacked under your shoulders, fingers spread, and your body in one straight line from head to heels. | Engage your core, draw your shoulder blades down your back, and press the floor away to keep your upper back broad. | Shift your weight forward on an inhale so your shoulders move slightly past your wrists and you come onto the balls of your feet. | Exhale and bend your elbows straight back, keeping them tucked close to your ribs rather than flaring out to the sides. | Lower under control until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor and your elbows are bent close to 90°, holding your body in one line. | Hover here with your gaze slightly forward, keeping your hips level with your shoulders and your legs active. | Hold for a breath, then either lower all the way down or roll forward over your toes and press into upward-facing dog to continue the flow. | To exit, release your knees and chest to the mat or press back up to plank with control.

t: Start in a high plank with your shoulders stacked directly over your wrists, hands shoulder-width apart, and fingers spread for a stable base. | Press the floor away, broaden across your upper back, and draw your belly in to keep a straight line from the crown of your head to your heels. | Shift your weight forward on the balls of your feet until your shoulders move slightly past your wrists. | Bend your elbows straight back, hugging them in toward your ribs rather than letting them flare out to the sides. | Lower your whole body as one unit until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor and your elbows are bent to about 90 degrees. | Hover here in a low plank, keeping your shoulders level with your elbows and your gaze slightly forward. | Hold for a breath or two with the core and legs engaged, then either lower all the way down or roll forward into upward-facing dog. | To exit, press back up to high plank or set your knees down and rest in child's pose.

t: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, knees slightly soft, and your core braced. | Let your arms hang at your sides with your palms facing forward and your elbows close to your torso. | Begin the rep by curling toward your shoulders, leading with your biceps and keeping your upper arms fairly fixed. | When you reach the sticking point partway up, add a brief, controlled dip and drive of the hips to help the rep continue moving upward. | Finish the curl at the top by squeezing your biceps hard, with your forearms close to your upper arms. | Lower under full control over 2–3 seconds, resisting the descent and keeping your biceps loaded the entire way down. | Return to a full hang, reset your posture, and repeat for your target reps. | Stop the set when your lowering phase becomes uncontrolled rather than chasing extra reps with bigger swings.

nE: Chest and Front of Shoulder Stretch
t: Stand tall in a doorway or beside a wall, feet about hip-width apart, with your core gently braced and shoulders relaxed. | Raise one arm to roughly shoulder height and bend the elbow to about 90 degrees, placing your forearm flat against the door frame or wall. | Step the foot on the same side forward to create a stable, balanced stance. | Slowly turn your chest and torso away from the anchored arm until you feel a gentle stretch across the front of your chest and shoulder. | Keep your shoulder down and away from your ear, and avoid letting your lower back arch. | Hold the position for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and evenly without bouncing. | Ease out of the stretch, lower the arm, and switch sides to stretch the other shoulder. | Repeat for 2 to 3 holds per side, easing slightly deeper only as the tissue relaxes.

t: Lie flat on the bench with your eyes directly under the bar. t: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Place your hands lightly behind your head or cross them over your chest, keeping your elbows wide. | Brace your abs and exhale as you curl your head, shoulders, and chest off the floor. | As you lift, rotate your torso smoothly to one side, leading with your shoulder rather than your elbow. | Pause briefly at the top of the rotation, feeling the contraction along the side of your waist. | Inhale and lower your torso back to the floor under control, returning to a neutral, centered position. | Repeat the lift and rotate to the opposite side, alternating evenly for the desired number of reps.
tRu: Лягте на спину, согните колени и поставьте стопы на пол на ширине бёдер. | Положите руки слегка за голову или скрестите их на груди, удерживая локти широко. | Напрягите пресс и на выдохе оторвите голову, плечи и грудь от пола. | Поднимаясь, плавно разверните корпус в сторону, ведя движение плечом, а не локтем. | Pause briefly at the top of the rotation, feeling the contraction along the side of your waist. | Inhale and lower your torso back to the floor under control, returning to a neutral, centered position. | Repeat the lift and rotate to the opposite side, alternating evenly for the desired number of reps.
tHe: שכב על הגב עם ברכיים כפופות וכפות רגליים שטוחות על הרצפה, ברוחב האגן. | הנח את הידיים קלות מאחורי הראש או שלב אותן על החזה, תוך שמירה על מרפקים פתוחים. | הדק את הבטן ונשוף כשאתה מכופף את הראש, הכתפיים והחזה מהרצפה. | בעלייה, סובב את הגו בחלקות לצד אחד, בהובלת הכתף ולא המרפק. | Pause briefly at the top of the rotation, feeling the contraction along the side of your waist. | Inhale and lower your torso back to the floor under control, returning to a neutral, centered position. | Repeat the lift and rotate to the opposite side, alternating evenly for the desired number of reps.

t: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, knees soft, and your core gently braced. | Reach both arms behind your back and clasp your hands together at the base of your spine. | Pull your shoulder blades down and back, squeezing them toward each other. | Push your chest forward and up so you feel a stretch across the front of your chest and shoulders. | Straighten your arms behind you and lift your clasped hands slightly to deepen the chest opening. | Keep your chin level and your ribs from flaring out as you hold the position. | Breathe slowly and hold the stretched, chest-out position for your target time. | Lower your hands, release the clasp, and relax your shoulders to finish.

tHe: עמוד זקוף עם רגליים בערך ברוחב האגן, ברכיים רכות, והליבה בעדינות מכווצת. | Reach both arms behind your back and clasp your hands together at the base of your spine. | Pull your shoulder blades down and back, squeezing them toward each other. | Push your chest forward and up so you feel a stretch across the front of your chest and shoulders. | Straighten your arms behind you and lift your clasped hands slightly to deepen the chest opening. | Keep your chin level and your ribs from flaring out as you hold the position. | נשם לאט והחזק את התנוחה המתוחה, חזה קדימה, למשך זמן המטרה שלך. | Lower your hands, release the clasp, and relax your shoulders to finish.

t: Set up in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers spread, and your body in a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips do not sag or pike up. | Lower your chest toward the floor under control, keeping your elbows tucked at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | Press explosively through your palms so your hands leave the ground at the top of the rep. | As you push off, shift your weight onto one arm and quickly tap your opposite hand to your chest or front shoulder. | Return the tapping hand to the floor and absorb the landing softly with both arms, bending the elbows to cushion the impact. | Reset into a stable plank, then repeat, alternating which hand taps on each rep. | Complete your reps, then lower your knees to the floor and rest.

tHe: Set up in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers spread, and your body in a straight line from head to heels. | הדק את הליבה וכווץ את הישבנים כך שהאגן לא ישמוט ולא יתרומם. | הורד את החזה לכיוון הרצפה בשליטה, תוך שמירה על מרפקים צמודים בזווית של כ-45° לגוף. | Press explosively through your palms so your hands leave the ground at the top of the rep. | בדחיפה, העבר משקל לזרוע אחת וטפח במהירות ביד הנגדית על החזה או הכתף הקדמית. | Return the tapping hand to the floor and absorb the landing softly with both arms, bending the elbows to cushion the impact. | Reset into a stable plank, then repeat, alternating which hand taps on each rep. | Complete your reps, then lower your knees to the floor and rest.

t: Kneel on a mat with your knees roughly hip-width apart and the tops of your feet flat on the floor, big toes touching behind you. | Sit your hips back onto your heels and lengthen your spine, keeping the back of your neck long. | Fold forward from the hips, walking your hands out in front of you and lowering your torso toward the floor. | Rest your forehead lightly on the mat and let your chest sink toward your thighs. | Extend your arms forward with palms down to stretch the shoulders, or lay them alongside your body with palms up to relax them. | Breathe slowly and deeply into your back and ribs, letting your hips settle a little closer to your heels with each exhale. | Hold the pose for 30 seconds to a few minutes, staying relaxed and still. | To come out, walk your hands back toward your knees and slowly rise to a tall kneeling position.

t: Start on all fours with your knees under your hips and your hands under your shoulders on a mat. | Sink back into Child's Pose: send your hips toward your heels, lower your chest between your thighs, and stretch your arms forward as you exhale. | Pause in Child's Pose for one full breath, feeling the stretch through your back, hips, and shoulders. | On an inhale, glide your chest forward and low to the floor, sliding past your hands until you lie face down with legs extended behind you. | Press lightly through your hands and lift your chest into Cobra Pose, keeping your elbows soft and your shoulders drawn down away from your ears. | Hold Cobra for one breath, lengthening your spine and opening your chest without crunching your lower back. | Exhale and reverse the motion, pushing your hips back over your knees to return to Child's Pose. | Continue flowing between the two poses, moving with your breath for the desired number of rounds, then rest in a neutral position.

t: Set up two sturdy, stable benches roughly a body-length apart and check that neither will slide before you load them. | Sit between them and place your upper back and the tops of your shoulders on one bench, with the back of your head supported or relaxed neutral. | Rest your heels on the second bench, legs straight, so your body is suspended over the gap. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and lift your hips until your body forms one straight line from shoulders to heels. | Hold this rigid position, breathing steadily, without letting your hips sag toward the floor or pike upward. | Keep your neck neutral and avoid arching your lower back or pushing your chin up to overextend. | Hold for your target time, then lower your hips under control and sit back down between the benches to finish.

t: Sit or stand tall with your spine long, shoulders relaxed and down, and your gaze straight ahead. | Take a slow breath in, then exhale and gently nod your head forward, lowering your chin toward your chest. | Let the weight of your head do the work — avoid pulling or forcing — until you feel a light, comfortable stretch along the back of your neck. | Keep your shoulders relaxed and your jaw loose so the stretch stays in the neck and upper spine. | Hold the position for 15–30 seconds, breathing slowly and evenly throughout. | To deepen it slightly, you may rest your fingertips lightly on the back of your head, but never pull hard. | Slowly raise your head back to a neutral, upright position to finish. | Repeat for 2–3 gentle holds, easing off the moment you feel any pinching or pain.

t: Sit or stand tall with your spine neutral, shoulders relaxed down, and your gaze level with the horizon. | Without tilting your head up or down, slowly draw your chin straight back, as if making a double chin. | Imagine sliding your whole head backward over your shoulders, keeping your eyes and jaw level the entire time. | Stop at the point of a gentle stretch at the base of the skull and a mild contraction at the front of the neck, without forcing the range. | Hold the retracted position for 3 to 5 seconds, breathing normally. | Release slowly and return your head to the neutral starting position under control. | Repeat for your target reps, keeping every movement smooth and free of jerking.

t: Grip the pull-up bar with an underhand (supinated) grip about shoulder-width apart, wrapping your thumbs around the bar. | Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended, shoulders engaged, and core braced to limit swinging. | Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down and back, leading with your chest toward the bar. | Continue pulling past the normal top position, raising your chin and head up and over the bar. | Tilt your head slightly back as you clear the bar, keeping your neck relaxed and your shoulders stable. | Pause briefly at the top with the bar below your chin, staying in control. | Lower yourself slowly and under control until your arms are fully extended again. | Reset your hang, then repeat for reps before dropping off the bar safely.

t: Set a bar at about chest height — a power-rack pin, Smith bar, or low fixed bar works. | Sit into a squat directly under the bar and take an underhand (supinated) grip about shoulder-width apart. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and let your arms extend so your weight hangs partly from the bar. | Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down and back, squeezing your back muscles at the top. | Press lightly through your legs only as much as needed to complete each rep cleanly. | Pause briefly with your chin near or above the bar, keeping your shoulders down away from your ears. | Lower yourself under control back into the squat until your arms are fully extended. | Repeat for your target reps, then stand up and step away from the bar.

t: Grip a pull-up bar with an underhand (supinated) grip, hands roughly shoulder-width apart and thumbs wrapped around the bar. | Use a box, a controlled jump, or a partner's help to get your chin up over the bar so your elbows are fully bent. | Hold this top position with your chin above the bar, chest up and shoulder blades pulled down and back — squeeze hard and brace your core. | Maintain the isometric hold for 3–10 seconds, keeping your elbows tucked and your body from swinging. | Begin the negative by slowly straightening your arms, lowering yourself under full control over 3–5 seconds. | Keep tension in your lats and upper back the whole way down, resisting gravity rather than dropping. | Finish with your arms fully extended in a dead hang, then step back onto the box and reset. | Repeat for the planned reps, then drop off the bar safely with control.

t: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, core braced and knees soft. | Raise both arms out to your sides until they are level with your shoulders, forming a straight line from fingertip to fingertip. | Keep your elbows extended and your palms facing down, with shoulders relaxed and away from your ears. | Begin drawing small forward circles with both arms, moving from the shoulders rather than the elbows. | Gradually widen the circles, keeping the motion smooth and controlled with no momentum or swinging. | Continue forward circles for the set time or rep count, breathing steadily throughout. | Reverse direction and draw circles backward for an equal duration to work the muscles evenly. | Lower your arms slowly to your sides to finish and rest the shoulders.

t: Stand an arm's length from a wall and place a stability ball against it at about shoulder height. | Press one palm flat into the ball so it stays pinned to the wall, with your arm nearly straight and elbow soft. | Set your shoulder down and back, and brace your core so your torso stays still. | Keeping steady pressure on the ball, draw a slow, controlled circle with your hand, moving the ball through a smooth path on the wall. | Complete your reps in one direction, then reverse and trace circles the other way. | Switch arms and repeat, keeping the same constant pressure and tempo throughout. | Finish by easing off the ball and lowering your arm under control.

t: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, core braced, and chest lifted. | Raise both arms out to your sides until they are level with your shoulders, forming a straight line from fingertip to fingertip. | Keep your elbows straight or only slightly soft, with your palms facing down. | Begin tracing small forward circles with your hands, moving from the shoulders rather than the wrists. | Gradually widen the circles over several reps until you reach a comfortable full range of motion. | After completing your forward circles, reverse the direction and trace the same controlled circles backward. | Keep your shoulders down away from your ears and your torso still throughout. | Lower your arms to your sides and relax once you finish both directions.
tRu: Встаньте прямо, поставив ноги на ширине плеч, напрягите корпус и поднимите грудь. | Поднимите обе руки в стороны до уровня плеч, образуя прямую линию от кончиков пальцев одной руки до другой. | Keep your elbows straight or only slightly soft, with your palms facing down. | Начните описывать кистями малые круги вперёд, работая от плеч, а не от запястий. | Gradually widen the circles over several reps until you reach a comfortable full range of motion. | Выполнив круги вперёд, смените направление и опишите те же подконтрольные круги назад. | Keep your shoulders down away from your ears and your torso still throughout. | Lower your arms to your sides and relax once you finish both directions.
tHe: עמוד זקוף עם רגליים ברוחב הכתפיים, ליבה מכווצת, וחזה מורם. | הרם את שתי הידיים לצדדים עד לגובה הכתפיים, תוך יצירת קו ישר מקצות האצבעות ועד קצות האצבעות. | Keep your elbows straight or only slightly soft, with your palms facing down. | התחל לצייר עיגולים קטנים קדימה עם כפות הידיים, מתוך הכתפיים ולא מתוך שורשי כף היד. | Gradually widen the circles over several reps until you reach a comfortable full range of motion. | אחרי שסיימת את הסיבובים קדימה, הפוך כיוון ושרטט את אותם עיגולים מבוקרים לאחור. | Keep your shoulders down away from your ears and your torso still throughout. | Lower your arms to your sides and relax once you finish both directions.

t: Stand or jump up to reach the first bar and take a firm overhand grip with both hands, wrapping your thumbs around the bar. | Hang from the bar with your arms extended, letting your shoulders settle into an active, slightly engaged position rather than hanging fully loose. | Brace your core and avoid excessive swinging so your body stays under control before you move. | Reach one hand forward to the next bar while the other hand keeps you supported, then close your grip on the new bar. | Release the trailing hand and swing it forward to the following bar, moving hand-over-hand in a steady rhythm. | Use a small, controlled body swing to carry momentum between bars, timing each reach with the swing. | Continue traveling along the bars to the end of the structure, keeping your grip secure on each rung. | Lower yourself under control or drop to the ground with bent knees to absorb the landing.

t: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart and cup your hands together at chest height, elbows tucked, as if cradling a goblet against your sternum. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and squat straight down at the 12 o'clock (neutral) position until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor. | Drive through your mid-foot to stand back up, keeping your hands fixed at your chest throughout. | Step your lead foot out toward the 3 o'clock position to widen and angle your stance, then squat down and return to standing. | Reset to center, then step toward the 6 o'clock position (a longer stance) and perform another controlled squat. | Reset again and step toward the 9 o'clock position to mirror the 3 o'clock angle, squatting and standing with control. | Return your feet to center to complete one full clock circuit, keeping your torso upright the whole time. | Repeat the circuit for your target reps, then lower your hands and stand tall to finish.

t: Set up in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers forward, and your body in a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips neither sag nor pike up. | Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | Press back up to full arm extension to complete one push-up at the 12 o'clock position. | Keeping one hand planted as the pivot, step the other hand a short arc clockwise to the next clock position, resetting into a solid plank. | Perform another full push-up at the new angle, then walk the hand to the next position and repeat. | Continue around the clock until you complete the circle, then reverse direction or rest. | Lower your knees to finish the set and shake out your wrists and shoulders.

t: Grip a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands set roughly shoulder-width apart or slightly closer. | Hang at full arm extension with your shoulder blades active, core braced, and legs together or crossed behind you. | Pull your shoulder blades down and back to start the movement before your arms take over. | Drive your elbows down toward your ribs and pull your chest up toward the bar, keeping your elbows close to your body. | Continue until your chin clears the bar, squeezing your back and biceps at the top. | Lower yourself under control until your arms are fully extended and your shoulder blades reset. | Repeat for your target reps without swinging or kipping between repetitions.

t: Stand over the loaded barbell with feet hip-width apart and grip it just outside your knees with a hook grip, arms long. | Brace your core, drive through the floor, and pull the bar past your knees, extending your hips and knees explosively. | Pull yourself under the bar and catch it in a front-rack position at the bottom of a deep front squat, elbows high. | Stand up out of the squat, keeping the bar racked on your shoulders and your torso upright. | Dip your knees slightly, then drive through your legs to launch the bar upward into a press. | Press the bar to full lockout overhead, with biceps by your ears and the bar stacked over your midline. | Lower the bar back to the front rack under control, then return it to the floor to reset for the next rep.

t: Lie face down on the floor with your legs extended and the tops of your feet flat on the ground. | Place your hands flat beneath your shoulders, slightly wider than shoulder-width, with your elbows tucked close to your ribs. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips connected to the floor as you begin the press. | Press through your palms to straighten your arms, driving your chest up and forward while letting your lower back extend into a cobra arch. | Lift your head and chest until your arms are nearly extended, keeping your shoulders down and away from your ears. | Pause briefly at the top, feeling the contraction across your lower back, glutes, and chest. | Lower your chest back toward the floor under control, keeping your elbows tucked the whole way down. | Reset to the starting position and repeat for your target reps.

t: Lie face down on a mat with your legs extended and the tops of your feet pressing into the floor. | Place your hands flat under your shoulders, fingers spread and pointing forward, with your elbows tucked close to your ribs. | Press the tops of your feet, thighs, and pubic bone into the mat, and gently engage your glutes to support your lower back. | Inhale and slowly straighten your arms, lifting your head and chest off the floor while keeping your hips grounded. | Draw your shoulders down and back, opening the chest, and lengthen through the crown of your head without crunching the neck. | Keep a slight bend in the elbows and only lift as high as feels comfortable in your lower back. | Hold the stretch for 15–30 seconds, breathing slowly and evenly throughout. | Exhale and lower your chest, forehead, and head back to the mat with control to release the pose.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and your arms reaching overhead on the floor. | Brace your abs and press your lower back gently into the floor to remove the gap. | In one smooth motion, curl your knees toward your chest while crunching your head and shoulders up off the mat. | Reach your hands toward your shins or knees as you tuck into a tight cocoon position, exhaling fully. | Pause briefly at the top, feeling the squeeze through your abs and hip flexors. | Reverse under control, lowering your shoulders and extending your legs back out long without letting your feet or upper back slam down. | Hover your legs and arms just above the floor at full extension to keep tension, then begin the next rep.

t: Stand under the bar so it runs front-to-back relative to your shoulders, then grip it with both hands in line with the bar, palms facing each other, one hand in front of the other a few inches apart. | Hang with your arms fully extended, brace your core, and pull your shoulder blades down to set your back. | Pull yourself up and slightly toward one side, leading with the hand in front so your head clears past that side of the bar. | Continue until your shoulder or collarbone reaches bar height on that side, keeping your obliques tight to control the lean. | Lower under control back to a full dead hang with your arms straight. | Repeat the pull-up to the opposite side, passing your head past the other side of the bar. | Alternate sides each rep, keeping movement smooth, until you complete your set, then lower to a dead hang and step down.

t: Sit on the end of a bench with your feet planted wide and hold a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand (supinated) grip. | Lean forward slightly from the hips and brace the back of that arm's upper elbow against the inside of the same-side thigh. | Let the dumbbell hang straight down with your arm fully extended, keeping a small bend so the elbow stays loaded. | Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder by flexing only at the elbow, squeezing the biceps as you rise. | Pause briefly at the top with the biceps fully contracted, keeping your upper arm pinned against your thigh. | Lower the dumbbell under control back to the start, resisting the weight through the full range of motion. | Complete all reps on one arm, then switch the dumbbell to the other hand and repeat.

t: Set out your cones (or any small markers) in the pattern you want to run — common layouts are a straight line, an L-shape, or three cones spaced 5 yards apart. | Start in an athletic stance at the first cone: feet shoulder-width apart, knees bent, weight on the balls of your feet, and hips low. | Drive off explosively toward the next cone, keeping your steps short and quick rather than long and floaty. | As you reach each cone, drop your hips and decelerate under control, planting your outside foot to change direction. | Push off the planted foot to accelerate toward the next marker, staying low through the turn. | Pump your arms in rhythm with your legs to drive speed and keep your balance through each cut. | Complete the full pattern at a controlled but brisk pace, touching or rounding each cone as your layout requires. | Walk back to the start to recover, then repeat for the planned number of runs.

t: Stand facing an open corner, a doorway, or a flat wall, about one stride away from it. | Raise your forearms and place them flat against the surfaces, with your elbows bent roughly 90 degrees and at about shoulder height. | Step one foot forward into a short staggered stance and set your feet for stable balance. | Keeping your chest tall and your spine neutral, slowly lean your body forward until you feel a gentle stretch across your chest and the front of your shoulders. | Stop at the point of mild tension, not pain, and keep your shoulders down away from your ears. | Breathe slowly and hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds. | Ease back to the starting position under control, reset, and repeat for 2 to 3 rounds.

t: Stand next to a wall or open doorway, side-on, with your feet about hip-width apart. | Raise the arm closest to the wall to roughly shoulder height and bend the elbow to 90°, like a goal-post. | Place your forearm and palm flat against the wall, keeping the elbow level with your shoulder. | Step the inside foot forward slightly to create a stable, staggered base. | Slowly rotate your chest and torso away from the wall until you feel a comfortable stretch across the front of the chest and shoulder. | Keep your shoulder pulled down and back, your chest tall, and breathe steadily as you hold the position for 20–30 seconds. | Gently rotate back to release the stretch, lower the arm, and turn to face the other way. | Repeat the stretch on the opposite side, matching the time and intensity.

t: Lie flat on your back with your arms by your sides, palms down, and legs extended. | Brace your abdominals and roll your legs up and overhead until your toes reach toward the floor behind your head, supporting your weight on your shoulders and upper back. | Reach your hands back to lightly hold one ankle or shin for stability, keeping your neck long and relaxed. | Lengthen your top leg straight up toward the ceiling, squeezing the glute and hamstring to control the lift. | Switch legs smoothly, lowering the raised leg overhead as you reach the other leg to the ceiling, keeping your hips steady. | Continue alternating legs in a slow, controlled scissor-like rhythm, breathing evenly throughout. | To finish, bring both legs together overhead, then roll your spine down to the mat one vertebra at a time and lower your legs with control.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and together, arms resting alongside your body with palms pressed down for support. | Draw your navel toward your spine to brace the core, then lift both legs toward the ceiling until they are roughly vertical. | Keeping your legs straight and together, slowly lower them to one side in a controlled arc, letting your hips rotate only as far as your control allows. | Sweep your legs down and across the midline in a smooth circle, keeping your shoulders and upper back anchored to the mat. | Carry the legs up the opposite side and back to the vertical start, completing one full circle like a corkscrew. | Reverse the direction and circle to the other side, moving slowly and feeling the stretch through the waist and hip flexors. | Continue alternating directions for even repetitions, then lower your legs to the mat with control to finish.

t: Start in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and your body in a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core and set your shoulder blades down and back to stabilize your trunk. | Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor, keeping them tucked at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | As you descend, rotate your hips and torso and drive one knee diagonally across your body toward the opposite elbow. | Pause briefly near the bottom with the knee drawn in and your chest just above the floor. | Reverse the twist, returning the foot to the plank position as you press back up to full arm extension. | Repeat the rotation to the same side or alternate sides each rep, keeping your hips from sagging throughout. | Finish your reps and lower your knees to the floor to rest.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and your arms resting alongside your body, palms facing up. | Let your feet fall open naturally so your legs and hips relax outward without effort. | Move your shoulder blades gently down and slightly under you so your chest stays open and your neck is long. | Close your eyes and let your whole body sink into the floor, releasing your jaw, face, and any gripping in your muscles. | Breathe slowly and evenly through your nose, letting each exhale soften your body a little more. | Scan from your feet to your head, consciously releasing any area still holding tension. | Stay still and relaxed for 5 to 10 minutes, keeping your breath quiet and steady. | To finish, deepen your breath, wiggle your fingers and toes, then roll gently to one side before sitting up.

t: Stand tall with your feet much wider than shoulder-width and your toes pointed slightly outward. | Brace your core and keep your chest upright. You can extend your arms in front of you as a counterbalance. | Shift your weight onto one leg and bend that knee, sinking your hips down and back toward that heel. | Keep the working knee tracking over your toes while the trailing leg stays straight, with that foot's toes pulled up off the floor. | Lower until the bent leg's thigh is roughly parallel to the floor, keeping the heel of the working foot flat. | Drive through the working heel to push back up to the wide standing start position. | Shift your weight onto the opposite leg and repeat the descent on that side. | Continue alternating sides for your target reps, keeping your torso tall and movement controlled throughout.

t: Kneel with your back to a wall or couch and place your rear shin flat against it, with the top of your foot pointing up the wall and your knee tucked into the corner where the floor meets the wall. | Step your front foot forward and plant it flat on the floor, knee bent to about 90 degrees, so you are in a half-kneeling lunge position. | Place your hands on your front knee or the floor for balance and brace your core so your lower back does not over-arch. | Squeeze the glute of the rear leg and gently tuck your pelvis under to flatten the lower back and target the hip flexor. | Slowly raise your torso toward an upright position, easing into the stretch through the front of the rear hip and thigh. | Breathe steadily and hold the position where you feel a strong but tolerable stretch, keeping your spine neutral. | Hold for 30 to 60 seconds, then ease out of the stretch and switch sides.

t: Stand tall on one leg with your working foot flat and your other knee bent so the rear foot floats just behind you. | Extend your arms straight out in front of you at roughly shoulder height to act as a counterbalance. You can hold a very light plate or dumbbell in your hands if you want more reach. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and set your standing knee tracking over your toes. | Hinge at the hips and bend your standing knee to lower under control, letting your rear leg trail back and down behind you. | Descend until your rear knee lightly taps the floor, keeping most of your weight through the heel and mid-foot of your standing leg. | Drive through your standing foot and extend the hip and knee to stand back up, keeping your arms reaching forward for balance. | Complete all reps on one leg, then switch sides and repeat.

nR: Прыжок с противоходом, руки на бёдрах
t: Stand tall with your feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart and your weight balanced over the middle of your feet. | Place both hands firmly on your hips and keep them there for the entire jump. | Dip down quickly into a quarter squat, bending at your hips, knees, and ankles in one smooth countermovement. | Without pausing at the bottom, drive your feet hard into the floor and explode straight up. | Fully extend your hips, knees, and ankles at the top so your body reaches a tall, straight line in the air. | Spot the floor as you descend and land softly on the balls of your feet, then your whole foot. | Absorb the landing by bending your hips, knees, and ankles back into a controlled quarter squat. | Reset to a tall stance with your hands still on your hips, then repeat for the prescribed reps.

t: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart, weight balanced over the middle of your feet, and your arms hanging relaxed at your sides. | Brace your core and keep your chest up while looking straight ahead at a fixed point. | Drop into a fast countermovement by bending your hips, knees, and ankles into a quarter-squat as your arms swing back behind your hips. | Without pausing at the bottom, reverse direction explosively and extend your hips, knees, and ankles to drive straight up. | Pull your arms forcefully upward and overhead in time with the jump to add momentum and maximize height. | Reach full extension at the top, with your body straight and your feet leaving the ground together. | Land softly on the balls of your feet first, then settle through your whole foot, bending your hips and knees to absorb the impact. | Reset to a tall stance, regain your balance, and repeat for the prescribed number of reps.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and your spine tall. | Bend your right knee and cross it over your left, stacking your right knee directly on top of your left so both knees line up at the center. | Draw both heels in toward opposite hips and let your sitting bones settle evenly on the floor. | Reach your right arm overhead, bend the elbow, and let your right hand drop down between your shoulder blades. | Sweep your left arm behind your back and bend the elbow upward so your left hand climbs toward your right. | Clasp your fingers together between your shoulder blades, keeping your chest lifted and your top elbow pointing toward the ceiling. | Breathe slowly and hold for 30 to 60 seconds, easing into the shoulder and hip stretch without forcing. | Release the bind gently, unstack your legs, then repeat with the opposite arm on top and the opposite knee stacked.
tRu: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and your spine tall. | Согните правое колено и скрестите его поверх левого, укладывая правое колено прямо над левым так, чтобы оба колена оказались по центру. | Приведите обе пятки к противоположным бедрам и позвольте копчикам равномерно опуститься на пол. | Reach your right arm overhead, bend the elbow, and let your right hand drop down between your shoulder blades. | Sweep your left arm behind your back and bend the elbow upward so your left hand climbs toward your right. | Соедините пальцы рук между лопатками, удерживая грудь приподнятой, а верхнее локте направленным к потолку. | Дышите медленно и удерживайте в течение 5–8 глубоких вдохов, удлиняя боковую часть тела еще больше с каждым выдохом. | Release the bind gently, unstack your legs, then repeat with the opposite arm on top and the opposite knee stacked.
tHe: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and your spine tall. | כופף את ברך ימין והצלב אותה מעל שמאל, תוך ערימת ברך ימין ישירות על גבי שמאל כך ששתי הברכיים בקו האמצע. | Draw both heels in toward opposite hips and let your sitting bones settle evenly on the floor. | Reach your right arm overhead, bend the elbow, and let your right hand drop down between your shoulder blades. | Sweep your left arm behind your back and bend the elbow upward so your left hand climbs toward your right. | חבר את אצבעות ידיך בין לוחות הכתף, שמור על חזה מורם והמרפק העליון מכוון לתקרה. | נשיר לאט והחזיקו למשך 30 עד 60 שניות, מתחילים את המתיחה בכתפיים ובירכיים בלי לכפות. | Release the bind gently, unstack your legs, then repeat with the opposite arm on top and the opposite knee stacked.

t: Set up on all fours on a mat in a quadruped position, with your wrists stacked under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. | Spread your fingers wide and press evenly through your palms, keeping your spine in a neutral, flat starting position. | Inhale slowly and let your belly drop toward the floor as you tilt your pelvis so your tailbone lifts upward. | Lift your chest and gaze gently forward and up, allowing your shoulder blades to draw down your back. | Continue the gentle arch through your mid and lower spine without forcing the movement or cranking your neck back. | Hold the extended position for a breath or two, feeling the stretch across your abdomen and the openness through your spine. | Exhale and return to the neutral flat-back position, or flow directly into the cat stretch by rounding your spine. | Repeat for several slow, breath-paced reps, then finish back in a neutral quadruped position.

t: Start on all fours in a tabletop position, stacking your wrists directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips. | Spread your fingers wide and press evenly through your palms, keeping your spine long and neutral to begin. | Inhale as you slowly drop your belly toward the floor, letting your lower back gently arch. | Lift your chest and tailbone toward the ceiling, broadening across your collarbones. | Let your gaze rise softly forward or slightly upward without crunching the back of your neck. | Feel the stretch across the front of your torso through your abdominals and obliques as the spine extends. | Hold for a breath at the top, keeping your shoulders relaxed away from your ears. | Exhale and return to a neutral spine, or flow directly into Cat Pose by rounding your back. | Repeat for several slow breaths, moving with your inhale and exhale.

t: Sit on the floor with your knees bent, feet flat, and hands placed behind your hips with your fingers pointing toward your heels. | Press through your hands and feet to lift your hips off the floor until your torso and thighs form a flat, tabletop line. | Let your head fall back gently and keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears. | Drive your hips a little higher and squeeze your glutes to deepen the stretch across the front of your torso. | Feel the lengthening through your abdominals, hips, and shoulders, and hold the position with steady breathing. | Hold for 20–40 seconds, breathing slowly and keeping your core lightly engaged. | Lower your hips back to the floor under control to finish the stretch.

t: Sit on the floor with your knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, and your hands planted behind you with fingers pointing toward your heels. | Press through your hands and feet to lift your hips off the floor until your torso forms a flat tabletop, roughly parallel to the ground. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to hold your hips high and level — this is your starting position. | Step forward by moving your opposite hand and foot together, then the other hand and foot, staying low and controlled. | Keep your hips lifted throughout; avoid letting them sag toward the floor between steps. | Travel the planned distance forward, then reverse the pattern to walk backward to your start. | To work laterally, step both hands and feet to one side, then the other, keeping your chest open and shoulders stable. | Lower your hips to the floor under control to finish the set.

t: Squat down with your feet close together and place both hands flat on the floor shoulder-width apart, fingers spread wide. | Spread your fingers and grip the mat lightly, keeping your wrists, hands, and forearms set as a stable base. | Bend your elbows slightly back, as in a low push-up, to create a shelf for your knees on the backs of your upper arms. | Rise onto the balls of your feet and place your knees high up onto your upper arms, as close to your armpits as you can. | Shift your weight forward over your hands until your feet feel light and your gaze moves to the floor just ahead of your fingers. | Lift one foot and then the other off the floor, drawing your heels in toward your hips and rounding your upper back. | Balance with your knees squeezing your arms, hips lifted, and arms gradually straightening as much as is comfortable. | Hold for a few steady breaths, then lower your feet back to the floor with control and return to a squat.

t: Clear enough floor space and start on all fours in a bear-crawl position: hands under shoulders, knees under hips and hovering just off the floor, back flat and core braced. | Keeping your hips low, take a small step with one hand and the opposite foot to crawl a short distance forward, staying controlled and quiet. | To switch sides, lift one hand off the floor and rotate your hips and chest toward the ceiling, reaching that hand behind you to plant it. | Follow the rotation by turning your feet so you land in a crab position: hands behind your hips with fingers pointing toward your feet, feet flat, and hips lifted into a reverse tabletop. | Drive through your heels and palms to push your hips up, hold the crab briefly, then crawl backward a short distance keeping your hips elevated. | Reverse the movement by rotating your hips and chest back toward the floor and stepping a hand under your shoulder to return to the bear-crawl position. | Continue alternating smoothly between crawl and crab for the prescribed time or reps, keeping the transitions fluid and your core engaged throughout. | To finish, return to the bear-crawl position, then lower your knees and stand up under control.

t: Start standing tall at the top of your mat with your feet together and your weight evenly balanced. | Step your right foot back into a long lunge, keeping the front (left) knee stacked directly over the ankle and the back leg straight or with a soft bend. | Lower your hips toward the floor until you feel a gentle stretch through the front of the back hip and thigh, keeping the front knee at roughly 90 degrees. | Inhale and sweep both arms up alongside your ears, palms facing in or lightly touching, and lengthen up through your fingertips. | Lift your chest and gently arch back, drawing your shoulder blades down and keeping your lower ribs from flaring as you reach up and slightly back. | Hold the pose for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily and keeping your core lightly engaged to support your lower back. | To release, lower your arms, step your back foot forward to meet the front, and return to standing. | Repeat on the other side, stepping the left foot back to balance both hips.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and your arms resting by your sides or tucked under your hips for support. | Press your lower back into the floor and brace your abdominals to lock the pelvis in place. | Raise both legs a few inches off the floor, keeping them straight and your toes pointed. | Spread your legs apart into a wide V, then cross one leg over the other in a scissoring motion. | Open the legs again and re-cross with the opposite leg on top, keeping the movement controlled and continuous. | Maintain steady, even breathing and a tight core throughout each cross. | Continue alternating the crossing leg for your target reps or time, then lower both legs to the floor under control.

t: Lie face-down on a mat with your legs extended straight behind you and the tops of your feet resting on the floor. | Let your heels fall slightly outward and your toes turn in, so your lower back can relax rather than arch. | Bend your elbows and stack your forearms on the floor in front of you, crossing them loosely so each hand rests near the opposite elbow. | Lower your forehead onto your stacked arms, letting your head feel fully supported with no strain in your neck. | Soften your shoulders away from your ears and let your chest, belly, and hips sink into the floor. | Breathe slowly into your belly, feeling it press gently against the mat on each inhale and release on each exhale. | Hold for several slow breaths, staying relaxed and letting your lower back release with each exhale. | To finish, slide your hands beside your chest, press up gently, and rest in a neutral seated or kneeling position.

t: Stand facing a wall or sturdy support and place both hands on it at chest height for balance. | Step one foot back about a stride length and lower into a crouch, bending both knees and keeping your feet flat on the floor. | Shift your weight back over the rear leg so that heel stays planted and presses down toward the floor. | Sink your hips down and slightly back until you feel a stretch low in the calf and along the Achilles tendon of the rear leg. | Keep the rear heel anchored and avoid letting it lift as you deepen the position. | Hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and steadily throughout. | Ease out of the crouch gradually, then switch legs and repeat on the other side.

t: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and parallel, distributing your weight evenly across both feet. | Spread your toes and press down through the four corners of each foot to create a stable, grounded base. | Engage your legs gently and stack your hips directly over your ankles, keeping a neutral pelvis. | Lengthen your spine upward, drawing your lower ribs down so your torso stacks tall over your hips. | Relax your shoulders down and back, and let your arms hang naturally alongside your body with palms facing forward. | Lift the crown of your head toward the ceiling and gently lengthen the back of your neck, keeping your chin level. | Soften your gaze forward and breathe slowly and evenly through your nose, holding the pose for several steady breaths. | To release, relax the effort and move into your next pose or step out of the posture.

t: Set up between sturdy parallel or dip bars, gripping one bar in each hand with your palms facing inward. | Press down through your hands to lift your feet off the floor, supporting your full bodyweight with your arms straight and locked. | Relax your shoulders and let them rise up toward your ears, allowing your body to sink slightly between the bars. | Feel the gentle stretch and decompression across the tops of your shoulders and your upper back. | Now actively depress your shoulders — pull your shoulder blades down and away from your ears without bending your elbows. | Hold the depressed position for 2–3 seconds, keeping your chest tall and your neck long. | Breathe slowly and cycle between the relaxed (shrugged) and the depressed position for the desired time. | Lower your feet gently back to the floor to finish, then step off the bars under control.

t: Set a sturdy box roughly knee-height (around 30–45 cm to start) and stand on top of it with your toes near the front edge. | Step off the box — don't jump up or out — and let both feet drop straight down toward the floor. | Land on the balls of your feet with knees and hips slightly bent, absorbing the impact in a soft, athletic stance. | As soon as your feet touch down, reverse the movement and drive up into a maximal vertical jump. | Swing your arms upward as you extend your hips, knees, and ankles to add height to the jump. | Land softly from the jump with bent knees, reset your balance, and step back onto the box for the next rep.

t: Stand in an athletic stance with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and weight on the balls of your feet. | Raise both fists to guard height beside your chin, elbows tucked in and core braced. | Drive your right fist forward and across your body on an upward diagonal toward your opposite shoulder line, rotating through your hips and trunk. | Pivot your right foot and turn your hips into the punch so the power comes from rotation, not just the arm. | Snap the fist back to guard along the same path, keeping your chin protected. | Repeat with your left fist on the mirror-image diagonal, rotating to the opposite side. | Alternate sides in a steady rhythm, staying light on your feet and breathing out with each punch. | Continue for the set time or rep count, then return to a relaxed guard to finish.

t: Kneel on the floor and place your hands under your chest, bringing your thumbs and index fingers together so they form a diamond or triangle shape. | Walk your knees back until your body forms a straight line from your head through your hips to your knees, and brace your core and glutes. | Keep your knees on the floor as the pivot point and lift your feet so your shins are off the ground. | Lower your chest toward your hands under control, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides rather than flaring them out. | Bring your chest down until it lightly touches or nearly touches the back of your hands. | Press back up by extending your elbows, driving through your hands until your arms are fully straight. | Keep your hips level and your body in one line throughout, then complete your reps.
