t: Set up at parallel bars or a dip station with a grip roughly shoulder-width apart and your palms facing in toward each other. | Mount the bars by pressing up to a fully locked-out support position, arms straight, shoulders down and away from your ears. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes, keeping your torso upright or with a slight forward lean over the bars. | Bend your elbows and lower under control to your chosen hold position, stopping when your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor. | Hold the position statically, keeping your shoulders packed down, elbows tracking back, and your whole body tight. | Breathe in a steady, shallow rhythm and maintain tension through the chest, shoulders, and triceps for the planned time. | When the set is done, press back up to lockout or step down to the floor under control to dismount.

t: Sit on the front edge of a sturdy chair and place your hands on the edge beside your hips, fingers pointing forward toward your feet. | Slide your hips off the chair so your weight is supported on your hands, keeping your arms fully extended. | Walk your feet forward and rest your heels on the floor with your legs straight or knees slightly bent. | Keep your chest up, shoulders down away from your ears, and your hips close to the chair. | Bend your elbows to lower your body straight down until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your elbows pointing back rather than flaring out. | Pause briefly when you feel a stretch across your chest and triceps, without letting your shoulders shrug up. | Press through your palms to push your body back up until your arms are fully extended again. | Complete your reps, then plant your feet and sit back onto the chair to finish.

t: Place two sturdy chairs facing each other, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and check that both are stable and won't slide. | Grip the front edge of each chair seat with your hands and support your bodyweight on straight arms, keeping your shoulders down and away from your ears. | Extend your legs out in front of you with your heels on the floor, or rest your feet on a third chair to increase the difficulty. | Brace your core and lean your torso slightly forward to bias the chest, keeping your shoulder blades pulled down and back. | Bend your elbows and lower your body under control until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor or you feel a stretch across your chest. | Keep your elbows tracking back at about a 45° angle to your torso rather than flaring straight out. | Press through your palms to drive your body back up until your arms are fully extended. | Complete your reps, then lower your feet and step away from the chairs with control.

t: Lie flat on your back on the floor or a mat with your legs straight and your arms resting by your sides. | Press your lower back firmly into the floor and tilt your pelvis slightly so there is no gap beneath your spine. | Brace your abs and lift your shoulder blades a few inches off the floor, keeping your neck long and your chin slightly tucked. | At the same time, lift your straight legs off the floor so your body forms a shallow, curved dish shape from head to toe. | Keep your legs together, toes pointed, and arms extended either by your sides or overhead, whichever you can control. | Hold this position, breathing steadily, while keeping your lower back glued to the floor the whole time. | Hold for a set time, then lower your shoulders and legs to the floor under control to finish.

t: Start on your hands and knees with your knees under your hips, then lower onto your forearms so your elbows sit directly under your shoulders. | Keep your forearms parallel and shoulder-width apart, pressing them firmly into the floor; either keep palms flat or interlace your fingers loosely. | Tuck your toes under and lift your knees off the floor, sending your hips up and back toward the ceiling. | Walk your feet a few steps toward your elbows until your body forms an inverted V, lengthening through your spine. | Press your chest gently back toward your thighs and reach your heels toward the floor without forcing them down. | Let your head and neck hang relaxed between your upper arms, gaze toward your feet, and breathe slowly through your nose. | Hold for several steady breaths, then lower your knees back to the floor to release and rest in a brief child's pose.

t: Stand in an open doorway and place your forearm and palm flat against the frame, with your elbow bent to about 90 degrees and roughly at shoulder height. | Set the same-side foot slightly forward into the doorway to give yourself a stable base. | Keeping your chest tall and your core lightly braced, slowly rotate your torso away from the raised arm. | Step or lean gently forward until you feel a mild, comfortable stretch across the front of your chest and shoulder. | Hold the position and breathe steadily, relaxing into the stretch without bouncing or pushing into pain. | Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then ease back out of the stretch under control. | Switch to the other arm and repeat, aiming for 2 to 3 holds per side.

t: Set up five dots in an X pattern — four corners of a roughly 2-foot by 2-foot rectangle plus one in the center — using tape, chalk, or a printed dot-drill mat. | Stand with one foot on the left-back dot and one foot on the right-back dot, knees softly bent and weight on the balls of your feet. | Jump both feet together into the center dot, landing light and quiet with your knees bent to absorb the impact. | Spring off the center dot and split your feet apart to land one on each front dot, staying low and balanced. | Hop both feet back to the center dot, then split again to the two back dots to complete one up-and-back cycle. | Keep your eyes up, arms relaxed and pumping for rhythm, and drive each jump from the ankles and knees rather than the hips. | Repeat the pattern continuously for your target reps or time, keeping the contacts as fast and quiet as you can. | Slow your last few jumps to a stop, step off the dots, and rest before your next round.

t: Hold the rope handles at hip height with your elbows tucked close to your sides and your forearms turned slightly outward. | Stand tall with your feet together, knees soft, and your weight balanced on the balls of your feet. | Begin a steady single-bounce rhythm to find your timing before attempting the double pass. | Jump a little higher than a normal skip, driving through the balls of your feet while keeping your torso upright. | Spin the rope faster using quick wrist rotations so it passes beneath your feet twice during that single jump. | Land softly on the balls of your feet with your knees slightly bent to absorb the impact. | Reset your rhythm and repeat for the planned reps or time, keeping the rope turning at a constant pace. | Slow the rope back to single bounces to finish, then stop and let your breathing settle.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out, and your weight balanced through your whole foot. | Brace your core, hinge slightly at the hips, and lower into a squat until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor. | Drive explosively through your legs and jump straight up, swinging your arms upward for momentum. | Land softly on the balls of your feet, then your whole foot, bending your knees to absorb the impact and dropping straight back into a squat. | Immediately spring into a second jump from that squat, performing two consecutive explosive jumps before pausing. | Land softly again and reset to a stable squat or standing position to begin the next pair of jumps. | Continue for your target reps or time, keeping each landing controlled, then stop while your form is still clean.

t: Kneel down on a mat with both knees on the floor and your feet behind you, hip-width apart. | Point your toes straight back so the tops of your feet and your shins lie flat against the floor. | Keep your torso upright and place your hands on your thighs or the floor in front of you for balance. | Slowly sit back, lowering your hips toward your heels until you feel a gentle stretch along the front of your shins and ankles. | Stop the moment you feel a comfortable stretch — never push into sharp pain in the knees or ankles. | Hold the position and breathe steadily, keeping your shins pressed into the floor. | To increase the stretch slightly, lean your upper body back a little while supporting yourself with your hands. | Release by easing your hips forward off your heels, then come up onto all fours to finish.

t: Kneel on a mat with your knees roughly hip-width apart and your shins and the tops of your feet flat on the floor. | Sit your hips back toward your heels and place your hands on the floor behind you for support. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips lifted and your lower back from arching sharply. | Slowly lean your torso back, walking your hands behind you as the stretch builds along the front of both thighs. | Stop as soon as you feel a strong but comfortable stretch in your quadriceps and hip flexors, keeping your knees on the floor. | Hold the position and breathe slowly, letting the front of the thighs gradually release with each exhale. | Walk your hands forward and bring your torso upright to come out of the stretch under control. | Sit up tall over your heels for a breath before repeating or moving on.

t: Lie on your back with your knees pulled in toward your chest and your hands resting lightly on your shins. | Curl your head, neck, and shoulders off the mat, drawing your navel down toward your spine to flatten your lower back. | Inhale and reach your arms back past your ears while extending your legs out to a 45-degree angle, keeping your shoulders curled up. | Keep your lower back pressed into the mat throughout the reach so your abdominals stay engaged and your spine does not arch. | Exhale and sweep your arms out to the sides in a wide circle as you bend your knees back toward your chest. | Wrap your hands back around your shins and draw your knees in to return to the start position. | Repeat the reach-and-circle for the desired number of reps, then lower your head and legs to the mat under control.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended, then sit up tall on your sitting bones. nE: Double Plank Jack to 4 Mountain Climber
nH: ג'ק פלאנק כפול ל-4 מטפסי הרים
t: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders, fingers spread, and your body in a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and set your feet together so your shoulders stay stacked over your wrists. | Jump both feet out wide for the first plank jack, then jump them back together, keeping your hips level the whole time. | Repeat the jump for a second plank jack, landing softly and resisting any bounce or sag in your hips. | Without resetting, drive one knee toward your chest for the first mountain climber, then switch legs quickly. | Continue alternating knees for four mountain climbers total, keeping your shoulders steady and your back flat. | Return your feet together in the plank and immediately begin the next round of two plank jacks. | Keep the rhythm steady for the prescribed time or rounds, then lower your knees to finish and rest.

t: Set the rope length so the handles reach roughly to your armpits when you stand on the middle of the rope. | Stand tall with your feet together, elbows close to your ribs, and the handles held low at hip height. | Begin with a few relaxed single-under jumps to find a steady rhythm and stay on the balls of your feet. | Jump slightly higher than a single under, keeping your body straight and your knees only softly bent. | Snap the rope around twice using a fast flick from your wrists and forearms, not big arm circles, while you are in the air. | Land softly on the balls of your feet with quiet, controlled contact, then absorb the impact through your ankles. | Reset your rhythm and repeat, chaining the double unders together for time or for a target number of reps.

nH: שכיבות סמיכה כלב מביט מטה מול קיר
t: Stand facing a wall, about an arm's length away, and place your hands flat on the floor shoulder-width apart. | Walk your feet up the wall and your hands back toward it, hips piking high so your body forms an inverted V (downward dog) with your head pointing toward the floor. | Set your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and spread your fingers for a stable base. | Brace your core and keep your back flat, with your weight stacked over your hands and shoulders. | Bend your elbows and lower the crown of your head toward the floor under control, keeping your elbows tracking at roughly 45° to your torso. | Pause briefly just above the floor without letting your head touch down hard. | Press firmly through your hands to extend your arms and drive back to the starting inverted-V position. | Complete your reps, then walk your feet back down the wall and step away to finish.

t: Start on your hands and knees with your wrists under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, fingers spread wide. | Press evenly through your palms and the bases of your fingers, then tuck your toes under so the balls of your feet contact the floor. | Exhale and lift your hips up and back, straightening your legs to draw your body into an inverted V shape. | Lengthen your spine by reaching your hips toward the ceiling and your chest gently back toward your thighs. | Rotate your shoulders outward to draw them away from your ears, keeping your upper arms active. | Let your heels sink toward the floor without forcing them, allowing the stretch to spread through your hamstrings and calves. | Hold the pose while breathing evenly through your nose, keeping your weight balanced between your hands and feet. | To release, exhale and lower your knees back to the floor, returning to hands and knees to rest.

nE: Downward Facing Dog Adho Mukha Svanasana
nH: כלב מביט מטה אדהו מוקה שוואנסאנה

t: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, a dumbbell resting on the floor just outside each foot. | Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the dumbbells with a neutral (palms-facing) grip, keeping your chest up, back flat, and arms straight. | Brace your core and drive explosively through your legs, extending your hips, knees, and ankles together to accelerate the dumbbells upward. | As the dumbbells rise, shrug your shoulders and pull with your arms to keep the momentum going close to your body. | Drop your hips and bend your knees to drop underneath the dumbbells, rotating your elbows quickly forward. | Catch the dumbbells at shoulder height with your elbows up and forearms roughly vertical, absorbing the load in a partial squat. | Stand tall to finish the rep with the dumbbells racked on your shoulders, hips and knees fully extended. | Lower the dumbbells under control back to the hips or the floor and reset before the next rep.

Repeat for your target reps.

t: Lie flat on a bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs. | Use your legs to help bring the dumbbells to your chest, then press them up so they meet directly over your mid-chest with your arms extended. | Rotate your wrists so your palms face each other and press the inner heads of the dumbbells together, keeping them in firm contact. | Pull your shoulder blades down and together against the bench to create a stable pressing base. | Lower the dumbbells under control toward your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your torso. | Stop when the dumbbells lightly touch your chest, maintaining the inward pressure that keeps them together. | Press the dumbbells back up in a straight line until your arms are fully extended, squeezing your triceps and chest at the top. | Complete your reps, then bring the dumbbells back to your thighs and sit up to set them down safely.

nE: Dumbbell Close Grip Shoulder Press Sit-up
nR: Жим плечами узким хватом + сит-ап с гантелями
nH: לחיצת כתפיים באחיזה צרה + סיט-אפ עם משקולות
t: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, anchoring them under a support or having a partner hold them. | Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a close, neutral grip (palms facing each other) and bring them up to your shoulders. | Lower your torso back toward the floor under control, keeping the dumbbells stacked at shoulder height. | Brace your core and curl your torso up into a full sit-up, leading with your shoulders rather than yanking with your arms. | As you reach the top of the sit-up, press both dumbbells straight overhead until your arms are fully extended. | Lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders under control while you stay upright at the top. | Reverse the sit-up, lowering your torso back to the start with the weights held at your shoulders. | Complete your reps, then sit up and set the dumbbells down safely.

nE: Dumbbell Complex Push-Up Row Clean and Press
nR: Комплекс с гантелями: отжимания, тяга, взятие, жим
nH: קומפלקס עם משקולות: שכיבות סמיכה, חתירה, הנפה ולחיצה
t: Set a pair of dumbbells on the floor about shoulder-width apart and take a high plank position gripping the handles, hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line. | Perform a push-up: lower your chest toward the dumbbells with elbows tucked at roughly 45°, then press back up to the top of the plank. | From the top, row one dumbbell to your ribs, driving your elbow up and back while keeping your hips square to the floor, then return it and row the other side. | Lower both dumbbells, then step or hop your feet up toward your hands so you land in a low squat with the dumbbells beside your feet. | Clean the dumbbells: stand up explosively, pulling them up and flipping your elbows under so the weights rack at your shoulders. | Brace your core and press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully locked out, biceps near your ears. | Lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders, then set them on the floor and step or hop back into the plank to begin the next rep. | Complete your reps for the full sequence, then place the dumbbells down under control.

tHe: Set a pair of dumbbells on the floor about shoulder-width apart and take a high plank position gripping the handles, hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line. | Perform a push-up: lower your chest toward the dumbbells with elbows tucked at roughly 45°, then press back up to the top of the plank. | From the top, row one dumbbell to your ribs, driving your elbow up and back while keeping your hips square to the floor, then return it and row the other side. | Lower both dumbbells, then step or hop your feet up toward your hands so you land in a low squat with the dumbbells beside your feet. | נקה את הקטלבל לגובה הכתף כך שהמרפק מכופף וצמוד לפני הגוף, עם הפעמון מאוזן מעל אגרוף. כף היד פונה פנימה והאחיזה חזקה. | הדק את הליבה ולחץ את שני הדאמבלים מעל הראש עד שהידיים בנעילה מלאה, כשהדו-ראשי קרוב לאוזניים. | Lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders, then set them on the floor and step or hop back into the plank to begin the next rep. | בצע את החזרות שלך עבור כל הרצף, ואז הנח את הדאמבלים בשליטה.

t: Hold a single dumbbell at chest height with both hands (goblet position), or one dumbbell in each hand at your sides. | Stand with your feet much wider than shoulder-width, toes pointed slightly out, and brace your core. | Shift your weight to one side and bend that knee, sinking your hips down and back over the working leg. | Keep the trailing leg straight with its heel down, letting that foot's toes rotate up as you descend. | Lower until your working thigh is roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your chest tall and the dumbbell close. | Drive through the heel and midfoot of the bent leg to push back up to the wide standing start. | Repeat to the same side for your reps, then switch, or alternate sides each rep as programmed.

t: Hold a dumbbell at chest height with both hands, cupping one end like a goblet, and stand with your feet much wider than shoulder-width and toes turned slightly out. | Brace your core and keep your chest tall as you begin to shift your weight toward one side. | Bend the working leg and sink your hips down and back over that foot, keeping the opposite leg straight with its toes pointing up. | Lower until the working thigh is roughly parallel to the floor, keeping the heel of the bent leg flat on the ground. | Keep the dumbbell close to your chest and your torso as upright as your mobility allows at the bottom. | Drive through the heel of the bent leg to push back up to the wide standing position. | Shift across to the other side and repeat, alternating legs for your target reps. | Finish your set, then set the dumbbell down safely with control.

t: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip — palms facing your thighs and thumbs pointing forward. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and pin your upper arms against your sides. | Keeping your wrist neutral, curl one dumbbell diagonally across your body toward the opposite shoulder or pec. | Drive the movement from your elbow only, letting the dumbbell travel up and inward without swinging your torso. | Squeeze the brachioradialis and biceps hard at the top, holding the dumbbell just in front of the opposite shoulder for a beat. | Lower the dumbbell under control back along the same diagonal path to the starting position. | Complete your reps on one arm, then repeat with the other, or alternate arms each rep. | Finish the set, then lower both dumbbells to your sides with control.

t: Stand tall holding a single dumbbell in one hand, with your weight on the opposite leg (for example, dumbbell in the right hand, standing on the left leg). | Let the free foot rest lightly behind you and keep a soft, unlocked knee in your standing leg. | Brace your core and push your hips straight back, hinging at the hip rather than bending at the waist. | Lower the dumbbell across your body toward the outside of your standing foot, letting your trailing leg rise behind you in a straight line with your torso. | Descend until you feel a strong stretch in the hamstring of your standing leg, keeping your back flat and shoulders square. | Drive through the heel of your standing leg and squeeze your glute to return to a fully upright position. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch the dumbbell and standing leg to repeat.

t: Lie on your back on a mat with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, roughly hip-width apart. | Hold one dumbbell with both hands against your chest, or extend it over your chest with your arms straight. | Brace your core and press your lower back gently into the floor to set a stable starting position. | Exhale and curl your shoulders and upper back off the floor by contracting your abs, keeping the dumbbell close to your body. | Pause briefly at the top of the crunch, squeezing your abs hard without pulling on your neck. | Inhale and lower your upper back down under control until your shoulder blades return to the floor. | Complete your reps, then set the dumbbell down safely on the floor beside you.

t: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, arms hanging in front of your thighs and feet shoulder-width apart. | Brace your core and pull the dumbbells straight up into an upright row, leading with your elbows until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor. | Pause with your elbows high and the dumbbells hanging just below them, keeping your wrists neutral. | Keeping your elbows fixed in place, externally rotate your shoulders to swing the dumbbells up and over until they point toward the ceiling and your forearms are vertical. | From this rotated position, press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended without locking the elbows harshly. | Reverse the press by lowering the dumbbells back to the elbows-high position under control. | Internally rotate your shoulders to bring the dumbbells back down in front of your elbows, then lower them along the same path to the starting position. | Complete your reps with light, controlled weight, then set the dumbbells down safely.

t: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, feet shoulder-width apart, arms hanging at your sides with palms facing forward. | Brace your core and keep your elbows tucked, then curl both dumbbells up to your shoulders by flexing at the elbows. | Rotate your palms to face forward and press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended and the weights stack over your shoulders. | With the dumbbells locked out overhead, bend only at the elbows to lower the weights behind your head, keeping your upper arms vertical. | Extend your elbows to drive the dumbbells back to the overhead lockout, squeezing the triceps at the top. | Lower the dumbbells from overhead back down to shoulder height under control. | Reverse the curl to return the dumbbells to your sides, completing one full rep, then continue for your target reps.

t: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length by your sides with your palms facing forward. | Brace your core and keep your elbows tucked close to your torso. | Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders by bending at the elbows, keeping your upper arms still until the weights reach shoulder height. | Rotate your wrists so your palms face forward and bring the dumbbells to shoulder level, ready to press. | Press the dumbbells straight overhead until your arms are fully extended, keeping your head and torso steady. | Pause briefly at the top with the weights stacked over your shoulders. | Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder level under control, then reverse the curl to return them to your sides. | Complete your reps, then lower the dumbbells to the floor with control.

t: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet about hip-width apart and core braced. | Shift your weight onto your front (working) leg and keep your chest upright. | Step your other leg diagonally back and across behind the front leg, like a curtsey. | Bend both knees to lower straight down until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your front knee tracking over your toes. | Keep the dumbbells hanging at your sides and your torso tall throughout the descent. | Drive through the heel of your front foot to stand back up, returning the rear leg to the start. | Complete your reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat for the same number of reps. | Lower the dumbbells under control once both sides are done.

t: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, feet about hip-width apart and the dumbbells resting against the front of your thighs. | Hinge at the hips and bend your knees slightly to lower the dumbbells to the hang position at mid-thigh, keeping your back flat, chest up, and shoulders over the weights. | Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles (triple extension), driving the dumbbells upward and shrugging hard as they rise. | As the dumbbells reach their peak, pull yourself under them and rotate your elbows quickly forward, catching them on your shoulders in a partial squat (the clean). | Stand fully upright out of the catch with the dumbbells racked on your shoulders, hips and knees locked out. | Dip straight down a few inches by bending your knees, keeping your torso vertical, then drive explosively to punch the dumbbells overhead. | Catch the dumbbells locked out overhead, often with one foot stepping forward and one back (split) or in a slight squat, then bring your feet back in line. | Stabilize overhead with arms fully extended, then lower the dumbbells under control to your shoulders and back to the hang to begin the next rep.

t: Stand tall with your feet together and your arms at your sides, then bend your knees into a slight squat. | Shift your weight onto your right foot and lift your left thigh, crossing it over the right so the left knee stacks above the right. | Hook the top of your left foot behind your right calf if your balance allows; if not, keep the toes lightly touching the floor for support. | Extend both arms forward, then cross your right arm under the left so the elbows stack on top of each other. | Bend the elbows and wind the forearms around each other until your palms meet, raising the elbows to roughly shoulder height. | Sink a little deeper into the squat while keeping your spine tall and your gaze fixed on one point ahead for balance. | Hold for several steady breaths, then unwind the arms and legs and return to standing. | Repeat on the other side, crossing the right thigh over the left and the left arm under the right.

t: Set up under a sturdy pull-up bar and grip it with one hand, palm facing away from you (overhand grip). | Get your chin above the bar using both arms, a jump, or a controlled assist so you reach the top of a one-arm pull-up position. | Release the assisting arm and let your working arm take the full load, keeping your chin level with the bar. | Brace your core, pull your shoulder blade down and back, and keep your body from twisting away from the bar. | Lower yourself slowly and under control on the single arm, aiming for a 3–5 second descent. | Keep tension in your back and shoulder the whole way down, resisting the urge to drop fast at the bottom. | Continue until your arm is fully extended, then re-assist with both arms to reset for the next rep. | Complete your reps on one side, then switch arms and repeat.

t: Stand or sit tall and extend one arm straight out in front of you at shoulder height, fully straightening the elbow. | Turn that palm up to face the ceiling, moving into supination, and feel a gentle stretch along the inner forearm. | With your other hand, lightly draw the fingers and palm back toward you to deepen the inner-forearm stretch. | Hold the supinated position for 15-30 seconds while keeping the elbow straight and the shoulder relaxed. | Slowly rotate the same forearm so the palm faces down toward the floor, moving into pronation, and feel the stretch shift to the outer forearm. | Use the other hand to gently guide the back of the hand downward, holding the pronated position for 15-30 seconds. | Breathe steadily and ease in and out of each rotation rather than forcing the end range. | Switch arms and repeat, performing 2-3 rounds per side.

t: Place a stability ball on the floor and set up in a forearm plank with your shins or the tops of your feet resting on the ball. | Position your elbows directly under your shoulders and spread your forearms flat on the floor for a stable base. | Brace your abs, squeeze your glutes, and form a straight line from your heels to your head, keeping your hips level. | Keeping your core tight, push back through your elbows to roll the ball away as your body slides backward a few inches. | Reverse the motion smoothly, pulling forward through your forearms until you return to the starting plank position. | Continue this slow forward-and-back sawing motion under control, never letting your hips sag or pike. | Complete your reps or time, then lower your knees to the floor and rest.

t: Sit on the stability ball, then walk your feet forward and lean back until the ball supports your lower and mid back. | Press the soles of your feet together and let your knees drop open to the sides into a frog position. | Place your hands lightly behind your head or crossed over your chest, and let your trunk extend back over the ball to lengthen the abs. | Brace your core and exhale as you curl your head, shoulders, and upper back up off the ball. | Crunch until you feel a strong contraction in your abdominals, keeping your knees open and feet together throughout. | Pause briefly at the top without pulling on your neck. | Inhale and lower under control back over the ball to the starting stretch. | Complete your reps, then walk your feet back and sit up off the ball with control.

t: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your arms at your sides, palms down for stability. | Place both heels on top of a stability ball with your legs extended and close together. | Brace your core and drive your heels into the ball to lift your hips off the floor into a straight-line bridge from shoulders to heels. | Holding the bridge, bend your knees and curl the ball toward your glutes by pulling your heels in, keeping your hips high. | Pause briefly when the ball is close to your glutes and your knees are fully bent. | Slowly roll the ball back out by straightening your knees, keeping your hips lifted throughout. | Complete your reps, then lower your hips back to the floor under control.

nE: Exercise Ball Lower Back Prone Stretch
nH: כדור פיזיו תחתון גב בשכיבת בטן מתיחה
t: Kneel behind a stability ball with the ball positioned in front of your hips and thighs. | Slowly walk your hands forward and lean your torso over the top of the ball so your belly and chest rest across it. | Let your arms reach down toward the floor in front of the ball and allow your head and neck to relax. | Keep your knees or toes on the floor for balance, then gently roll forward until you feel a comfortable stretch through your back and along your sides. | Relax your glutes and let your hips drape over the ball so your lower back decompresses rather than holding tension. | Breathe slowly and let your body sink a little deeper into the ball with each exhale. | Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds, staying relaxed and avoiding any bouncing. | To come out, walk your hands back, push your torso up off the ball, and return to a kneeling position with control.

nH: מתיחת מרחיקים בשכיבה על כדור פיזיו
t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with a stability ball resting just to one side of your hips. | Bend the knee closest to the ball and rest your foot flat on the floor for stability. | Keep the opposite leg straight, then lift it and let it cross over your body toward the ball. | Drape the crossing leg over the top of the stability ball so the ball supports its weight. | Keep both shoulders flat on the floor and let your hips rotate gently to deepen the stretch through the outer hip. | Relax into the position until you feel a comfortable pull along the side of the hip and abductor region. | Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly and steadily. | Bring the leg back over the ball under control, return to the start, and repeat on the other side.

nH: מתיחת ארבע-ראשי בישיבה על כדור פיזיו

nR: Скольжения у стены на зубчатые на фитболе
nH: החלקת סראטוס על הקיר עם כדור פיזיו
t: Stand facing a wall, about an arm's length away, with your feet shoulder-width apart and your core lightly braced. | Place a stability ball against the wall at chest height and press into it with the heels of both hands, arms extended in front of you in a slight V (scaption) angle. | Push your hands firmly into the ball so your shoulder blades wrap forward around your ribcage (protraction) — this is the serratus engagement you want to keep throughout. | Keeping that pressure on the ball, slide it slowly up the wall as you reach overhead, letting your shoulder blades rotate upward while your arms stay in the V position. | Slide up only as far as you can without your shoulders shrugging toward your ears or your lower back arching. | Slide the ball back down under control to chest height, maintaining the forward press into the ball the entire way. | Complete your reps, then step back and lower the ball to finish.

t: Place a stability ball against a wall and lean your lower back into it so the ball sits between the small of your back and the wall. | Step your feet forward about a foot and set them roughly shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out, so your knees will track over your toes as you descend. | Brace your core and stand tall, pressing your back lightly into the ball to keep it in place. | Bend your knees and hips to lower yourself, letting the ball roll smoothly up your back as you descend. | Lower until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your knees behind or in line with your toes. | Pause briefly at the bottom, keeping tension in your glutes and quads. | Drive through your heels to stand back up, letting the ball roll back down as you extend your knees and hips. | Finish by standing fully upright, then step away from the wall and set the ball down when your set is complete.

t: Start in a forearm plank: elbows under your shoulders, forearms flat on the floor, and feet about hip-width apart. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and form a straight line from your head to your heels with no sag or pike. | Plant your right palm flat on the floor under your shoulder and press up onto that hand. | Push up onto your left hand the same way so you reach a full high-plank position with both arms extended. | Lower back down onto your right forearm, then your left forearm, returning to the starting plank. | Drive through each transition explosively while keeping your hips level and square to the floor. | Continue alternating which arm leads for the set time or rep count, then lower your knees to rest.

t: Set up in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and your fingers pointing forward. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. | Lower your chest toward the floor under control, keeping your elbows tucked at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | When your chest is near the floor, press through your palms as hard and fast as you can to launch your upper body upward. | Push with enough force that your hands leave the ground; if you have the power, clap your hands together at the peak. | Land softly on slightly bent arms, immediately absorbing the impact by lowering back into the next rep. | Reset your plank position if your form breaks, then continue for your target reps.

t: Stand tall and step your feet wide apart, roughly the length of one leg, with your arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height. | Turn your right foot out 90° so it points to the side, and angle your left foot slightly inward; keep your heels roughly in line with each other. | Bend your right knee until it stacks directly over your right ankle, with the shin vertical and the thigh working toward parallel with the floor. | Keeping your torso long, lower your right side and rest your right forearm lightly on your right thigh, or bring the right hand to the floor outside the foot. | Reach your left arm up and over your head so it forms one continuous line from your back heel to your fingertips, opening the chest toward the ceiling. | Press into the outer edge of your back foot, draw your belly in, and turn your gaze up toward your top hand if your neck is comfortable. | Breathe slowly and hold for 5 to 8 deep breaths, lengthening the side body a little more on each exhale. | To exit, press into your feet, inhale to rise back up to the wide stance, straighten the front leg, and repeat on the opposite side.

t: Set the bench to a moderate decline and sit at the lower end with your knees bent over the upper edge. | Hook your feet securely under the foot pads or roller so your legs stay anchored higher than your head. | Lie back until your torso is along the bench, keeping a slight bend in your knees and your chin gently tucked. | Cross your arms over your chest or place your fingertips lightly at the sides of your head without pulling on your neck. | Brace your abdominals and exhale as you curl your torso up, leading with your chest toward your knees. | Continue lifting until your upper body is well past vertical, keeping the movement controlled rather than swinging. | Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your abdominals. | Inhale and lower your torso back down under control until your shoulders return to the bench. | Complete your reps, then unhook your feet and sit up carefully to finish.

t: Set the EZ bar in a rack at upper-chest height and load it. t: Lie flat on your back on a firm mat or bench with both legs extended and your spine in a neutral, relaxed position. | Bend one knee and lift that foot off the floor, then place the outside of your ankle across the opposite thigh, just above the knee, to form a figure-4 shape. | Let the bent knee rotate outward and open toward the floor, keeping the ankle resting on the thigh. | Keep both hips level on the surface and avoid rocking your pelvis to one side. | Slowly lower the bent knee toward the floor, allowing gravity or a light press from your hand to deepen the hip and groin stretch. | Hold the open position for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing steadily and noting any tightness or discomfort in the hip or groin. | Bring the knee back up under control and slide your foot off the opposite thigh to release. | Return the leg to the floor, then repeat the same sequence on the other side.

nR: Растяжка стоп и лодыжек с вращением
t: Sit on a chair or the floor and lift one foot off the ground so the ankle can move freely. t: Set two cones or markers about 5 to 10 metres apart on a flat, non-slip surface to form the loops of your figure-eight. | Start at the centre point between the markers in an athletic stance — knees soft, chest up, and weight on the balls of your feet. | Begin jogging toward the first marker, circling around it in a smooth arc rather than a sharp stop. | Lean slightly into the turn and shorten your stride as you round the marker to keep your balance under control. | Cross back through the centre and run a mirror-image loop around the second marker, completing the figure-eight. | Keep your eyes up and your core braced, pumping your arms in time with your stride to drive the pace. | Continue running the pattern for your set work interval, accelerating on the straights and controlling the curves. | Slow to a jog and then a walk to finish, letting your heart rate and breathing settle before your next round.

t: Load a light-to-moderate barbell and either sit on a bench resting your forearms on your thighs, or stand holding the bar behind your back with an overhand grip. | Take a shoulder-width underhand grip (palms facing up) with your wrists just past the edge of your knees so your hands can move freely. | Let the bar roll down out of your palms toward your fingertips until your fingers are nearly fully open and the weight is held by the last joints of your fingers. | Curl your fingers closed, rolling the bar back up from your fingertips into the base of your palms. | Squeeze your hands fully shut at the top, holding the contraction for a brief beat to maximize grip tension. | Lower the bar back down to your fingertips under control to feel a full stretch in the forearm flexors. | Complete your reps, then set the bar down safely on a rack or the floor.

t: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders, then lift your palms so only your fingertips and thumbs press into the floor, fingers spread wide like a claw. | Set your feet roughly hip-width apart and brace your core and glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. | Keep your wrists firm and your knuckles slightly bent — do not let your fingers collapse flat or hyperextend backward. | Bend your elbows and lower your chest under control toward the floor, keeping your elbows tucked at about a 45° angle to your torso. | Lower until your chest is just above the floor while maintaining steady pressure across all ten fingertips. | Press back up by driving through your fingertips and chest until your elbows are fully extended. | Keep your hips level and your body rigid throughout — avoid sagging or piking. | Complete your reps, then lower your knees to the floor and shake out your hands to release the fingers.

t: Start in a high plank or downward-facing position with your hands planted shoulder-width apart on the floor. | Step one foot forward to the outside of your same-side hand, planting the sole flat on the floor. | Keep your back leg extended behind you, balancing on the ball of the back foot. | Lower your hips toward the floor, easing into the stretch through the front of the back hip and the inner groin. | Walk your hands slightly forward and let your chest sink down to deepen the opening, keeping your front knee tracking over your ankle. | Hold the position and breathe slowly, relaxing a little deeper into the stretch with each exhale. | Hold for 4–6 slow breaths, then press back to plank and repeat on the other side.

t: Stand an arm-and-leg length from the heavy bag in your fighting stance, lead foot forward, hands up to guard your chin. | Shift your weight onto your supporting leg and keep a slight bend in that knee for balance. | Drive your rear knee up and forward, chambering it toward your chest with the foot cocked back. | Extend the leg explosively, snapping the ball of your foot or instep into the bag at groin height. | Push your hips through the kick at impact to deliver power from your whole body, not just the leg. | Re-chamber by snapping the knee back immediately rather than letting the leg drop. | Return the foot to your stance and reset your guard, staying light on the supporting leg. | Alternate legs or repeat for time, keeping a steady rhythm and breathing out sharply on each strike.

t: Stand tall and step one foot a short distance forward, placing the heel on the floor with the toes pointing up and that knee kept nearly straight. | Bend the back knee slightly and rest both hands on the bent thigh for support. | Brace your core and keep your back flat and chest open rather than rounding your shoulders. | Hinge forward from your hips, sending your hips back and lowering your chest toward the straight front leg. | Stop when you feel a gentle, comfortable stretch along the back of the front thigh and into the hip — never push into pain. | Hold the position and breathe slowly and steadily, letting the muscle relax deeper with each exhale. | Hold for 20–30 seconds, then ease back up to standing under control. | Switch legs and repeat for the same time on the other side.

t: Stand in a fighting stance arm's length from the boxing bag, lead foot forward, weight balanced, and your hands up to guard your chin. | Shift your weight onto your supporting leg and chamber the kicking knee, driving it up toward your chest. | Extend the leg through the ball of your foot, pushing the bag forward and feeling the impact through your hips and core. | Keep your guard up and your supporting knee soft (slightly bent) to stay balanced as the bag swings away. | Re-chamber by snapping the knee back before lowering the foot, rather than letting the leg drop straight down. | Return the foot to your stance and reset your guard, ready for the next repetition. | Alternate or repeat with the same leg for your target reps, then switch sides to train both legs evenly.

t: Stand in a fighting stance facing your partner, feet staggered, knees slightly bent, hands up to guard your face. | Have your partner hold a kick pad or focus target at chest-to-stomach height, bracing for the impact. | Shift your weight onto your standing leg and lift the knee of your kicking leg up toward your chest. | Snap the kick straight forward, driving the ball of your foot or heel into the center of the pad. | Engage your core and squeeze the glute of the kicking leg at the moment of contact for power. | Quickly re-chamber the knee and return your foot to the floor, resetting into your fighting stance. | Reset your guard and rhythm, then repeat for reps before switching to the other leg. | Alternate legs or trade roles with your partner to keep the work continuous and conditioning-focused.

t: Stand in a staggered fighting stance, knees soft, hands up to guard your face, while your partner holds a pad at waist-to-chest height in front of you. | Shift your weight onto your front foot and grip your partner's shoulders or the pad for control if the drill calls for it. | Drive your rear knee explosively up and forward, pointing the knee toward the center of the pad. | Extend your hips at impact and pull your toes back so you strike with the front of the knee, not the shin. | Brace your core and exhale sharply as the knee makes contact to add power. | Snap the leg back down and return to your stance with your guard up. | Reset your balance, then alternate legs or repeat for the prescribed reps or time.

t: Start in a fighting stance with your lead leg forward, knees soft, hands up by your chin, and your weight slightly forward on the balls of your feet. | Shift your weight onto your rear leg and pivot on the rear foot to begin rotating your hips toward the target. | Lift your lead knee and drive it across your body, leading with the knee rather than the foot. | Pivot hard on the supporting foot so your hips and torso open, turning your standing heel toward the target. | Whip your lead leg out and around in a hooking arc, snapping the heel or sole through the target line at hip-to-head height. | Keep your hands up and your core braced throughout to protect your balance and guard. | Re-chamber the lead leg by snapping it back along the same arc, then set the foot down and reset to your fighting stance. | Repeat for reps or for time, then switch your lead leg to train the other side.

t: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, knees soft, and your core braced. | Bring your hands up in a relaxed guard near your chin to mimic a fighting stance and aid balance. | Shift your weight onto one leg, keeping that knee slightly bent as your supporting base. | Drive the opposite knee up toward your chest, then snap the lower leg out straight in front of you to kick. | Keep your torso upright and your standing foot planted as you extend, avoiding any backward lean. | Quickly re-bend the knee and lower the leg under control back to the start. | Repeat for your target reps or time, then switch and kick with the other leg. | Finish by standing tall, lowering your hands, and letting your breathing settle.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, core braced, and arms relaxed at your sides. | Shift your weight onto your left leg and find a stable, balanced base. | Lift your right knee up in front of you to about hip height, keeping your torso upright. | Reach one or both hands under the raised knee and tap your hands together, then release. | Lower your right foot back to the floor under control without letting your posture collapse. | Repeat on the other side, lifting the left knee and tapping underneath it. | Continue alternating legs in a steady, rhythmic pattern for your prescribed time or reps. | Finish by lowering both feet, standing tall, and recovering your breath.

t: Set up in a front plank on your forearms, elbows stacked directly under your shoulders and forearms flat on the floor. | Extend your legs behind you with your feet together, then brace your abs and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. | Keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears and your hips level, avoiding any sag or pike in your lower back. | Hop both feet a short distance to the right, landing softly on the balls of your feet while keeping your shoulders and hips square. | Immediately hop both feet back to the center, controlling the landing without letting your hips twist. | Hop both feet to the left the same distance, again landing lightly and keeping your core tight. | Continue hopping side to side at a steady, controlled rhythm for the prescribed time or number of reps. | Finish by hopping your feet back to center, then lower your knees to the floor to come out of the plank.

t: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out, and place your hands behind your head or crossed over your chest. | Brace your core and pull your shoulder blades back to set a tall, neutral spine. | Hinge at your hips, pushing them back and letting your torso tip forward until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, keeping a slight bend in your knees. | From the hinged position, bend your knees and sink into a squat, bringing your torso upright as your hips drop toward parallel. | Keep your heels flat and your knees tracking over your toes at the bottom of the squat. | Drive through your whole foot to stand up out of the squat back into the hinged position. | Extend your hips to return to a tall standing position, squeezing your glutes at the top. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, keeping the hinge and squat smooth and controlled.

tHe: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out, and place your hands behind your head or crossed over your chest. | הדק את הליבה ומשוך את השכמות לאחור כדי לקבע עמוד שדרה גבוה וניטרלי. | Hinge at your hips, pushing them back and letting your torso tip forward until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, keeping a slight bend in your knees. | From the hinged position, bend your knees and sink into a squat, bringing your torso upright as your hips drop toward parallel. | Keep your heels flat and your knees tracking over your toes at the bottom of the squat. | Drive through your whole foot to stand up out of the squat back into the hinged position. | Extend your hips to return to a tall standing position, squeezing your glutes at the top. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, keeping the hinge and squat smooth and controlled.

t: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels, and core braced. | Begin lowering into a push-up by bending your elbows and keeping them tucked at roughly 45 degrees to your torso. | As you descend, rotate your hips open and thread your right knee underneath your body toward your left elbow. | Keep your shoulders square and your supporting foot grounded as the working leg sweeps across. | Press back up to the high plank as you return the right leg to its starting position. | Repeat on the other side, threading your left knee toward your right elbow as you lower. | Continue alternating sides for your target reps, keeping each rotation controlled. | Finish in a stable high plank, then lower your knees to the floor to rest.
tRu: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels, and core braced. | Начните опускаться в отжимание, сгибая локти и удерживая их прижатыми под углом примерно 45 градусов к корпусу. | Опускаясь, раскройте бёдра и проведите правое колено под телом к левому локтю. | Keep your shoulders square and your supporting foot grounded as the working leg sweeps across. | Press back up to the high plank as you return the right leg to its starting position. | Repeat on the other side, threading your left knee toward your right elbow as you lower. | Продолжайте поочередно выполнять движения на разные стороны в течение целевого количества повторений, сохраняя каждое вращение под контролем. | Finish in a stable high plank, then lower your knees to the floor to rest.
tHe: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels, and core braced. | התחל לרדת לשכיבת סמיכה בכיפוף המרפקים תוך שמירתם צמודים בכ-45 מעלות לגו. | בירידה, פתח את האגן בסיבוב והשחל את ברך ימין מתחת לגוף לעבר מרפק שמאל. | Keep your shoulders square and your supporting foot grounded as the working leg sweeps across. | Press back up to the high plank as you return the right leg to its starting position. | Repeat on the other side, threading your left knee toward your right elbow as you lower. | Continue alternating sides for your target reps, keeping each rotation controlled. | Finish in a stable high plank, then lower your knees to the floor to rest.

t: Sit on the floor or a mat with your knees bent and feet flat, sitting tall through the spine. | Place your hands lightly behind your thighs or rest your fingertips on the floor for support. | Engage your abdominals and lean your torso back to roughly a 45° angle, keeping your back long rather than rounded. | Lift your feet off the floor and extend your legs until your body forms a low, shallow V. | Lower the torso and legs closer to the floor so the legs hover just above it, deepening the abdominal engagement. | Reach your arms forward alongside your legs, palms facing in, keeping the chest open and shoulders relaxed. | Breathe steadily and hold the position, keeping the lower back from collapsing toward the floor. | To release, bend your knees, lower your feet, and sit back up tall before resting.
tRu: Sit on the floor or a mat with your knees bent and feet flat, sitting tall through the spine. | Place your hands lightly behind your thighs or rest your fingertips on the floor for support. | Напрягите мышцы пресса и наклоните корпус назад под углом примерно 45°, держа спину прямой, а не округлой. | Lift your feet off the floor and extend your legs until your body forms a low, shallow V. | Lower the torso and legs closer to the floor so the legs hover just above it, deepening the abdominal engagement. | Reach your arms forward alongside your legs, palms facing in, keeping the chest open and shoulders relaxed. | Дышите ровно и удерживайте положение, не давая нижней спине прогибаться к полу. | To release, bend your knees, lower your feet, and sit back up tall before resting.
tHe: Sit on the floor or a mat with your knees bent and feet flat, sitting tall through the spine. | Place your hands lightly behind your thighs or rest your fingertips on the floor for support. | Engage your abdominals and lean your torso back to roughly a 45° angle, keeping your back long rather than rounded. | Lift your feet off the floor and extend your legs until your body forms a low, shallow V. | Lower the torso and legs closer to the floor so the legs hover just above it, deepening the abdominal engagement. | Reach your arms forward alongside your legs, palms facing in, keeping the chest open and shoulders relaxed. | נשום בצורה יציבה והחזק את התנוחה, מנע מהגב התחתון לקרוס לכיוון הרצפה. | To release, bend your knees, lower your feet, and sit back up tall before resting.

t: Lie face-down on the mat with your legs extended straight behind you and your forehead resting comfortably on the floor. | Press your forearms into the mat and lift your chest, drawing your shoulders down and away from your ears to set up a gentle backbend. | Bend your right knee and bring your right heel toward your right buttock. | Reach back with your right hand and take hold of the top of your right foot or your toes. | Rotate your right elbow toward the ceiling so your fingers point forward over the foot, then gently press the foot down toward the hip without forcing it. | Keep your left forearm planted for support and your chest lifted, breathing steadily into the stretch. | Hold for several slow breaths, keeping your hips square and level on the mat. | Release the foot slowly, extend the leg back to the floor, then repeat on the opposite side.
tRu: Lie face-down on the mat with your legs extended straight behind you and your forehead resting comfortably on the floor. | Press your forearms into the mat and lift your chest, drawing your shoulders down and away from your ears to set up a gentle backbend. | Согните правое колено и подтяните правую пятку к правой ягодице. | Reach back with your right hand and take hold of the top of your right foot or your toes. | Rotate your right elbow toward the ceiling so your fingers point forward over the foot, then gently press the foot down toward the hip without forcing it. | Keep your left forearm planted for support and your chest lifted, breathing steadily into the stretch. | Hold for several slow breaths, keeping your hips square and level on the mat. | Release the foot slowly, extend the leg back to the floor, then repeat on the opposite side.
tHe: Lie face-down on the mat with your legs extended straight behind you and your forehead resting comfortably on the floor. | Press your forearms into the mat and lift your chest, drawing your shoulders down and away from your ears to set up a gentle backbend. | כופף את ברך ימין והבא את עקב ימין לכיוון הישבן הימני. | Reach back with your right hand and take hold of the top of your right foot or your toes. | Rotate your right elbow toward the ceiling so your fingers point forward over the foot, then gently press the foot down toward the hip without forcing it. | Keep your left forearm planted for support and your chest lifted, breathing steadily into the stretch. | Hold for several slow breaths, keeping your hips square and level on the mat. | Release the foot slowly, extend the leg back to the floor, then repeat on the opposite side.

t: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out and arms relaxed at your sides. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and look straight ahead to set a stable, upright posture. | Bend your knees and sink your hips down and back, descending only about halfway to a full squat (roughly a quarter to a half knee bend). | Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and your heels flat on the floor throughout the movement. | Drive up through your feet to return to a tall standing position, swinging your arms forward for rhythm and balance if it helps. | Repeat at a smooth, steady tempo, breathing out as you stand and in as you lower. | Continue for the target time or rep count, then slow your pace gradually to a stop rather than stopping abruptly.
tRu: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out and arms relaxed at your sides. | Напрягите корпус, держите грудь вверх и смотрите прямо вперёд, чтобы занять устойчивое вертикальное положение. | Согните ноги и опустите бёдра вниз и назад примерно наполовину до полного приседа (сгиб в коленях примерно на четверть–половину). | Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and your heels flat on the floor throughout the movement. | Вытолкните себя вверх через стопы, чтобы вернуться в положение высокой стояки, раскачивая руки вперед для ритма и равновесия, если это помогает. | Repeat at a smooth, steady tempo, breathing out as you stand and in as you lower. | Продолжайте в течение выбранного времени — начните с пяти минут и постепенно увеличивайте до десяти-двадцати минут, когда практика станет вам знакома.
tHe: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out and arms relaxed at your sides. | הדק את הליבה, שמור על חזה מורם, והבט ישר קדימה כדי לקבע יציבה זקופה ויציבה. | כופף את הברכיים ושקע עם האגן למטה ולאחור, רד רק כחצי הדרך לסקוואט מלא (בערך רבע עד חצי כיפוף ברך). | Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and your heels flat on the floor throughout the movement. | Drive up through your feet to return to a tall standing position, swinging your arms forward for rhythm and balance if it helps. | Repeat at a smooth, steady tempo, breathing out as you stand and in as you lower. | Continue for the target time or rep count, then slow your pace gradually to a stop rather than stopping abruptly.

t: Kneel on one knee, then slide the opposite leg straight out in front of you with the heel on the floor and toes pulled back toward your shin. | Square your hips and place both hands lightly on your thighs or the floor for support. | Lengthen your spine and lift your chest so your back stays long and flat. | Hinge forward from your hips over the front leg until you feel a gentle stretch down the back of that thigh. | Stop at the first sign of mild tension — never to the point of pain — keeping the front knee soft, not locked. | Breathe slowly and hold the position for 20–30 seconds, relaxing a little deeper on each exhale. | Ease back up to the start with control, switch your kneeling leg, and repeat on the other side.
tRu: Kneel on one knee, then slide the opposite leg straight out in front of you with the heel on the floor and toes pulled back toward your shin. | Square your hips and place both hands lightly on your thighs or the floor for support. | Lengthen your spine and lift your chest so your back stays long and flat. | Hinge forward from your hips over the front leg until you feel a gentle stretch down the back of that thigh. | Stop at the first sign of mild tension — never to the point of pain — keeping the front knee soft, not locked. | Дышите медленно и удерживайте растяжку в точке комфортного легкого напряжения, а не боли. | Медленно вернитесь в исходное положение под контролем, поменяйте колено, стоящее на полу, и повторите с другой стороны.

nE: Half Kneeling PVC Pec Mobilization Stretch
nR: Мобилизация груди с ПВХ-палкой с полуколена
nH: מתיחת חזה בחצי כריעה עם מקל PVC
t: Drop into a half-kneeling position with one knee down and the opposite foot planted flat in front, hips square and your torso tall. | Hold the PVC pipe in the hand on the same side as your down knee, gripping it low near one end with your palm facing forward. | Brace your core and tuck your ribs down so your lower back stays neutral rather than arching to compensate. | Raise that arm and sweep the PVC pipe up and back overhead, letting the stick act as a lever that guides the arm into the stretch. | Continue until you feel a deep but tolerable stretch across the front of your chest and shoulder, keeping your elbow fairly straight. | Breathe slowly and hold the end position, exhaling to ease a little deeper into the available range without forcing it. | Return the arm under control to the start, then complete your reps or hold time before switching to the other side.
tRu: Примите положение на коленях, с одним коленом на полу и противоположной ногой, стоящей перед собой, бёдра параллельно корпусу. | Hold the PVC pipe in the hand on the same side as your down knee, gripping it low near one end with your palm facing forward. | Напрягите пресс и опустите рёбра вниз, чтобы поясница оставалась нейтральной, не прогибаясь. | Raise that arm and sweep the PVC pipe up and back overhead, letting the stick act as a lever that guides the arm into the stretch. | Продолжайте, пока не почувствуете глубокую, но терпимую растяжку по передней части груди и плеча, сохраняя локоть почти прямым. | Дышите медленно и удерживайте начальную позицию в течение 20–30 секунд, чтобы окружающие ткани начали расслабляться. | Return the arm under control to the start, then complete your reps or hold time before switching to the other side.
tHe: Drop into a half-kneeling position with one knee down and the opposite foot planted flat in front, hips square and your torso tall. | Hold the PVC pipe in the hand on the same side as your down knee, gripping it low near one end with your palm facing forward. | הדק את הליבה ואסוף את הצלעות למטה כך שהגב התחתון נשאר ניטרלי ולא מתקשת כפיצוי. | Raise that arm and sweep the PVC pipe up and back overhead, letting the stick act as a lever that guides the arm into the stretch. | Continue until you feel a deep but tolerable stretch across the front of your chest and shoulder, keeping your elbow fairly straight. | נשיר לאט והחזיקו את מצב הקצה, נשיר כדי להעמיק מעט אל תוך הטווח הזמין בלי לכפות זאת. | Return the arm under control to the start, then complete your reps or hold time before switching to the other side.

t: Drop into a half-kneeling position with your right knee on the floor and your left foot planted flat in front, both legs bent to roughly 90 degrees. | Square your hips forward, stack your shoulders over your hips, and brace your core to set a tall, stable spine. | Raise your arms in front of you or clasp your hands at chest height to fix a reference point for the rotation. | Inhale, then exhale as you rotate your torso smoothly toward the side of the planted (left) foot, turning from the rib cage rather than the arms. | Rotate as far as you can while keeping your hips square and your lower back quiet, feeling the stretch and contraction through your obliques. | Pause briefly at the end of the range, then rotate back through center under control. | Continue your reps on that side, then switch your kneeling leg and repeat the rotation to the opposite side for an even number of reps. | Finish by returning to center and standing up under control.

t: Begin in a wide standing position, turning your right foot to point forward and keeping your left foot slightly angled in. | Bend your right knee and reach your right hand toward the floor about a foot in front of and outside your right little toe, fingertips down or resting on a block. | Shift your weight onto your right foot and hand, then straighten your right leg as you float your left leg up until it is parallel to the floor. | Stack your hips by rolling your top hip open, and flex your lifted foot so the toes point out to the side. | Press firmly through your standing foot and reach your left arm straight up toward the ceiling, opening your chest. | Lengthen through the crown of your head and your lifted heel, keeping your core engaged and your spine long. | Gaze forward or, if balance allows, turn to look up at your top hand, breathing steadily. | To exit, look down, bend your standing knee, and lower your lifted leg back to the floor with control, then repeat on the other side.

t: Start on all fours or in a downward-dog position with your hands under your shoulders and your weight evenly balanced. | Bring your right knee forward and place it behind your right wrist, then angle your right shin across your body so the front of your shin lies on the mat. | Slide your left leg straight back, resting the top of the foot and the front of the thigh on the floor with the kneecap pointing down. | Square your hips so both hip points face forward and your weight stays centered, not collapsed onto one side. | Sit tall on an exhale to feel the stretch in your right glute and hip; keep your back foot pressing lightly into the mat. | On your next exhale, walk your hands forward and fold your torso down over the front shin, resting on your forearms or forehead as your hips allow. | Hold for 30–60 seconds, breathing slowly and letting the hips release a little deeper with each exhale. | Press back up through your hands, return to all fours, and repeat on the other side with the left shin forward.
tRu: Start on all fours or in a downward-dog position with your hands under your shoulders and your weight evenly balanced. | Поднесите правое колено вперед и поставьте его за правое запястье, затем наклоните правую голень через тело так, чтобы передняя часть голни лежала на коврике. | Slide your left leg straight back, resting the top of the foot and the front of the thigh on the floor with the kneecap pointing down. | Square your hips so both hip points face forward and your weight stays centered, not collapsed onto one side. | Sit tall on an exhale to feel the stretch in your right glute and hip; keep your back foot pressing lightly into the mat. | On your next exhale, walk your hands forward and fold your torso down over the front shin, resting on your forearms or forehead as your hips allow. | Hold for 30–60 seconds, breathing slowly and letting the hips release a little deeper with each exhale. | Press back up through your hands, return to all fours, and repeat on the other side with the left shin forward.
tHe: Start on all fours or in a downward-dog position with your hands under your shoulders and your weight evenly balanced. | הבא את ברך ימין קדימה והנח אותה מאחורי פרק יד ימין, ואז הטה את שוק ימין דרך גופך כך שהקדמת השוק נמצאת על המזרנת. | Slide your left leg straight back, resting the top of the foot and the front of the thigh on the floor with the kneecap pointing down. | Square your hips so both hip points face forward and your weight stays centered, not collapsed onto one side. | Sit tall on an exhale to feel the stretch in your right glute and hip; keep your back foot pressing lightly into the mat. | On your next exhale, walk your hands forward and fold your torso down over the front shin, resting on your forearms or forehead as your hips allow. | Hold for 30–60 seconds, breathing slowly and letting the hips release a little deeper with each exhale. | Press back up through your hands, return to all fours, and repeat on the other side with the left shin forward.

t: Sit on the floor and lean back onto your forearms or hands, keeping your chest open and your spine long in a half-seated position. | Bend one knee and plant that foot on the floor for support, then extend the other leg straight out in front of you. | Brace your core by gently drawing your navel toward your spine, and pin your shoulders down away from your ears. | Lift the extended leg a few inches off the floor with the foot lightly pointed. | Trace a slow, controlled circle in the air with the extended leg, keeping the motion smooth and driven from the hip. | Keep your pelvis and torso completely still so only the working leg moves. | Complete your reps circling in one direction, then reverse and circle the same number in the opposite direction. | Lower the leg under control, switch sides, and repeat with the other leg.
tRu: Sit on the floor and lean back onto your forearms or hands, keeping your chest open and your spine long in a half-seated position. | Согните одну ногу и поставьте стопу на пол для опоры, затем вытяните другую ногу прямо перед собой. | Напрягите пресс, мягко подтянув пупок к позвоночнику, и опустите плечи вниз, подальше от ушей. | Lift the extended leg a few inches off the floor with the foot lightly pointed. | Trace a slow, controlled circle in the air with the extended leg, keeping the motion smooth and driven from the hip. | Keep your pelvis and torso completely still so only the working leg moves. | Выполните повторения, вращаясь в одном направлении, затем измените направление и выполните то же количество кругов в противоположном. | Lower the leg under control, switch sides, and repeat with the other leg.

t: Lie on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Rest your hands lightly behind your head or across your chest, keeping your elbows wide and your chin slightly tucked. | Brace your core and flatten your lower back gently into the floor. | Curl your head, shoulders, and upper back off the floor by contracting your abs, rising only about halfway up. | Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your abdominals without pulling on your neck. | Lower your upper back down under control until your shoulder blades touch the floor. | Exhale as you curl up and inhale as you lower back down. | Repeat for your target reps, keeping the movement smooth and controlled throughout.

t: Stand tall with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width and your toes turned slightly out. | Brace your core, push your hips back, and bend your knees to drop into a half squat — roughly a quarter to halfway down, with your chest up. | Hold this half-squat height for the whole set; keep your weight in your midfoot and your knees tracking over your toes. | Reach one arm up and over your head, bending your torso smoothly to the opposite side until you feel a stretch along your waist. | Keep your hips level and facing forward as you bend, so the movement comes from your trunk and not from twisting or shifting your weight. | Return to center under control, keeping the half squat the whole time. | Reach and bend to the other side, mirroring the same motion. | Alternate sides for your target reps, then stand up tall to finish.

t: Stand tall in Mountain Pose with feet hip-width apart, arms at your sides, and your weight balanced evenly. Take a steady breath to settle. | Inhale and sweep your arms out and overhead, gently reaching up and lengthening through your spine and chest. | Exhale and hinge from your hips into a Forward Fold, letting your hands travel toward the floor or your shins with soft knees. | Inhale into a Halfway Lift: place your hands on your shins or thighs, flatten your back, and lengthen your spine until it is roughly parallel to the floor. | Exhale and release back into the Forward Fold, relaxing your head and neck toward the floor. | Inhale, bend your knees slightly, and rise back up with a flat back, sweeping your arms out and overhead to reach up again. | Exhale and lower your arms back to your sides, returning to Mountain Pose. That is one round. | Repeat the sequence for several rounds, moving smoothly so each movement begins and ends with a full breath.

t: Lie flat on your back with your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, palms down, to anchor your upper body. | Lift your feet and bend your knees to roughly 90 degrees, stacking your knees over your hips. | Brace your core and press your lower back gently toward the floor to set a stable starting position. | Keeping your knees together and bent, slowly lower both legs to one side, stopping partway down before they reach the floor. | Pause briefly when you feel your obliques engage, keeping both shoulder blades flat on the floor. | Use your obliques to pull your knees back to the centered, stacked position under control. | Lower your legs to the opposite side to the same partial range, then return to center to complete one full cycle. | Continue alternating sides for your target reps, then lower your feet to finish.

nE: Hammer Grip Pull-up on Dip Cage
nH: מתח באחיזת פטיש על כלוב מקבילים
t: Set up at the dip cage so the two parallel handles are above you, then grip one handle in each hand with your palms facing each other (neutral grip). | Hang from the handles with your arms fully extended, shoulders pulled down away from your ears, and your core braced. | Cross your ankles or bend your knees slightly so your body hangs free and stays stable. | Initiate the pull by driving your elbows down and back, leading with your chest toward the handles. | Continue pulling until your upper chest or chin reaches the level of the handles, squeezing your lats and mid-back at the top. | Hold the top position briefly without swinging, keeping your shoulder blades pulled down and together. | Lower yourself under control until your arms are fully extended and your lats are stretched. | Reset your shoulders at the bottom and repeat for the desired number of reps.

t: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat, heels positioned a comfortable stride away from your hips. | Place your arms at your sides, palms down, and brace your core to flatten your lower back lightly against the floor. | Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips toward the ceiling. | Continue until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees, keeping your weight on your heels. | Hold the top position for a moment, squeezing your hamstrings and glutes without overarching your lower back. | Lower your hips under control until they hover just above the floor, keeping tension on the posterior chain. | Repeat for your target reps, then rest your hips down to finish the set.

nR: Мостик на задней поверхности с ударами (вариант 2)
t: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart, and your arms resting at your sides. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips into a bridge, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your knees. | Shift your weight onto one foot and keep that hip fully extended to hold the bridge steady. | Without letting your hips drop, extend the opposite leg and kick it out straight in line with your torso. | Pause briefly at full extension, keeping your pelvis level and square to the ceiling. | Lower the kicking leg under control and return its foot toward the floor without resting your hips down. | Complete your reps on that side, then plant both feet, lower your hips, and switch to the other leg.
