t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with both legs extended and your lower back relaxed against the floor. | Bend one knee and plant that foot on the floor, or keep the resting leg straight along the mat — whichever keeps your back comfortable. | Raise the working leg toward the ceiling, keeping the knee as straight as is comfortable. | Reach up and clasp your hands behind your thigh, or loop a towel or strap around the sole of your foot if you can't reach. | Exhale and gently draw the straight leg toward your chest until you feel a mild stretch down the back of your thigh. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and keeping your hips and shoulders flat on the mat. | Relax the leg back to the floor under control, then repeat on the other side. | Perform 2–3 holds per leg, easing a little deeper into the stretch as the muscle releases.

t: Sit tall on the floor with one leg extended straight in front of you and the foot flexed toward the ceiling. | Bend the other leg and let it rest comfortably, with the sole of that foot against your inner thigh. | Keep your back long and your chest lifted rather than rounding your shoulders forward. | Hinge forward from your hips, reaching your hands toward the foot of the extended leg. | Stop when you feel a gentle pull along the back of the thigh, not pain, and hold that position. | Breathe slowly and hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds, relaxing a little deeper on each exhale. | Ease out of the stretch slowly and sit back up with control. | Switch legs and repeat the stretch on the other side.

t: Set up a fingerboard or hangboard at a height you can reach with arms extended overhead, and warm up your fingers and forearms thoroughly. | Place your fingers on a comfortable edge, then form a half-crimp: your first knuckles bend over the edge while your fingertips stay roughly vertical and your thumb rests beside your index finger. | Keep your wrist straight and your forearm aligned, with the load running through your fingers rather than collapsing into a full crimp. | Engage your shoulders by pulling them down and back, keeping a slight bend in your elbows rather than hanging fully dead. | Lift your feet off the ground and let your bodyweight settle onto your fingers, maintaining the half-crimp shape. | Hold the position for a set time, typically 7 to 10 seconds, breathing steadily and keeping tension in your fingers and forearms. | Lower your feet back to the ground under control before your grip fails, rest fully, then repeat for the prescribed number of hangs.

nH: תלייה על הנגבורד עם מרפק ב-135 מעלות
t: Set the hangboard at a height where you can reach it with your arms nearly straight, then chalk your hands if you have it. | Grip the edge or holds with all fingers, keeping your wrists firm and neutral rather than letting them collapse. | Lift your feet so your body weight loads your hands, allowing your arms to take the hang. | Pull yourself up partway until your elbows are bent to roughly 135 degrees, so your forearms are working under load rather than hanging fully passive. | Set your shoulders down and slightly back to keep your shoulder blades engaged instead of letting your shoulders shrug up to your ears. | Hold the position still, breathing steadily, and feel the effort in your forearms and grip. | Hold for your target time, usually around 5 to 15 seconds, keeping the elbow angle and grip steady throughout. | Lower your feet back to the floor under control to release the hang, then rest before the next hold.

t: Set the hangboard at a height that lets you reach the sloper holds with your arms fully extended overhead while your feet are still on the floor. | Place both hands flat over the slope with your fingers spread and slightly relaxed, keeping the palm and pads in broad contact with the surface (an open-hand grip — no crimping). | Drive your fingertips down and pull your thumbs toward your palm to maximize friction against the sloping hold. | Engage your shoulders by pulling them down and back, then lift your feet so your full body weight hangs from the holds. | Keep your arms slightly bent rather than fully locked out, and hold a tight, motionless hang. | Maintain the hang for your target time, breathing steadily and resisting the urge to let your hands slide off the slope. | Lower your feet back to the floor under control to unload the holds, then step down and shake out your forearms. | Rest fully between hangs to let the forearm and finger flexors recover before the next set.

nH: כפיפות בטן עם יד לברך נגדית
t: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Place your fingertips lightly at the sides of your head, or extend your arms toward your thighs. | Brace your core and press your lower back gently into the floor. | Curl your shoulders off the floor and rotate your torso, reaching one hand across toward the opposite knee. | Squeeze your obliques and abs at the top of the movement, holding briefly. | Lower under control until your shoulder blades return toward the floor without fully relaxing. | Repeat for the chosen reps, then switch to reach the other hand to its opposite knee. | Finish the set, then relax your back flat on the floor.
tRu: Лягте на спину, согните колени и поставьте стопы на пол на ширине бёдер. | Place your fingertips lightly at the sides of your head, or extend your arms toward your thighs. | Напрягите корпус и мягко прижмите поясницу к полу. | Поднимите плечи с пола и поверните корпус, протягивая одну руку к противоположному колену. | Squeeze your obliques and abs at the top of the movement, holding briefly. | Lower under control until your shoulder blades return toward the floor without fully relaxing. | Repeat for the chosen reps, then switch to reach the other hand to its opposite knee. | Finish the set, then relax your back flat on the floor.

nR: Круговые касания носков со сцепленными руками
t: Stand tall with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart and your knees soft, not locked. | Clasp your hands together and extend your arms straight overhead, lengthening through your spine. | Brace your midsection gently and begin sweeping your clasped hands out to one side and down in a smooth, circular path. | Continue the circle by reaching down toward your toes, hinging at the hips and letting your back round naturally as your hands travel toward the floor. | Keep the motion flowing across to the other side, feeling the stretch travel through your waist, lower back, and hips. | Carry your hands back up the opposite side and return to the overhead start position to complete one full circle. | Exhale as you reach down and inhale as you rise, keeping the tempo slow and controlled. | Complete your reps in one direction, then reverse the circle and repeat for the same count.

tHe: Stand tall with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart and your knees soft, not locked. | חבר את ידיך והקש את הזרועות ישר למעלה, מתיחה לאורך החוטש. | הקשיש בעדינות את אזור המרכז והתחל להוביל את הידיים הקשורות צידה ולמטה במסלול מעגלי חלק. | Continue the circle by reaching down toward your toes, hinging at the hips and letting your back round naturally as your hands travel toward the floor. | Keep the motion flowing across to the other side, feeling the stretch travel through your waist, lower back, and hips. | הוביל את הידיים חזרה למעלה לצד השני וחזור לעמדת ההתחלה מעל הראש כדי להשלים מעגל מלא אחד. | Exhale as you reach down and inhale as you rise, keeping the tempo slow and controlled. | בצע את החזרות שלך בכיוון אחד, ואז הפך את המעגל וחזור על זה באותו מספר.

t: Sit or stand and rest your forearm on a thigh or bench so your wrist hangs just past the edge, palm facing up. | Hold the weighted spring device firmly in your hand with your fingers wrapped around the handle. | Let your wrist relax and extend downward to lengthen the wrist flexors and reach a full starting stretch. | Curl your wrist upward by flexing your hand toward your forearm, squeezing against the spring's resistance. | Pause briefly at the top with your wrist fully flexed and the forearm muscles contracted. | Lower your wrist back down under control to the stretched starting position. | Complete your reps, then switch to the other hand and repeat.

t: Start in a high plank with your hands flat on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width and your fingers pointing forward. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. | Bend your elbows and lower under control, keeping them tucked at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | Continue until your chest and thighs rest fully on the floor and you are at a complete stop. | Lift both hands off the floor for a brief moment, keeping the rest of your body still and tight. | Replace your hands, then press explosively through your palms until your arms are fully extended. | Reset your plank position at the top and repeat for your target number of reps.

t: Warm up your wrists with circles, flexion, and extension stretches, since they bear most of your bodyweight in the hold. | Place your hands flat on the floor about a hand's width from the wall, slightly wider than shoulder-width, with fingers spread and pointing forward. | Bend one leg and keep the other extended behind you to prepare for the kick-up. | Kick your trailing leg up and push off your bottom foot to drive your hips over your shoulders until your heels rest against the wall. | Stack your wrists, shoulders, and hips in a straight line, squeeze your glutes and brace your core, and press the floor away to keep your shoulders active. | Hold the position while breathing steadily, gazing at the floor between your hands for the planned time. | To come down, peel one leg off the wall and lower it under control, then follow with the other foot to step back to standing. | Shake out your wrists and shoulders before your next set.

nE: Handstand Shoulder Press with Wall (between benches)
nR: Жим плечами в стойке у стены (между скамьями)
nH: לחיצת כתפיים בעמידת ידיים מול הקיר (בין ספסלים)
t: Place two sturdy benches shoulder-width apart, a few inches from a wall, and check that they are stable and will not slide. | Kick up into a handstand against the wall, then walk your hands onto the benches so your palms are flat and shoulder-width. | Set your body in a straight line with your heels resting lightly on the wall, core braced and glutes squeezed. | Bend your elbows and lower your head under control into the gap between the benches until your head is just below hand level. | Keep your elbows tracking slightly forward, not flaring wide, as you descend. | Press back up through your palms until your arms are fully extended and your body is stacked over your hands. | Complete your reps, then walk your hands off the benches and lower your feet to the floor under control.
tRu: Place two sturdy benches shoulder-width apart, a few inches from a wall, and check that they are stable and will not slide. | Kick up into a handstand against the wall, then walk your hands onto the benches so your palms are flat and shoulder-width. | Set your body in a straight line with your heels resting lightly on the wall, core braced and glutes squeezed. | Согните локти и подконтрольно опустите голову в просвет между скамьями чуть ниже уровня кистей. | Keep your elbows tracking slightly forward, not flaring wide, as you descend. | Press back up through your palms until your arms are fully extended and your body is stacked over your hands. | Выполните свои повторения, затем снимите руки со скамеек и опустите ноги на пол под контролем.

t: Warm up your wrists and shoulders, and clear a flat, open space with plenty of room to fall or bail safely. | Place your hands on the floor about shoulder-width apart, fingers spread and pointing forward, a short distance in front of your feet. | Kick up into a handstand one leg at a time, stacking your hips and feet over your shoulders and hands. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms one straight, rigid line from wrists to toes. | Find your balance by gripping the floor with your fingertips and making small pressure adjustments through your hands. | Begin walking by shifting your weight onto one hand and stepping the other hand forward a few inches. | Continue moving one hand at a time in a controlled rhythm, keeping your body tight and your gaze toward the floor between your hands. | To finish, stop walking, regain a stable balance, then bail by twisting out to the side or lowering one leg down under control.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, weight balanced evenly across both feet and your spine long. | Inhale and lengthen through the crown of your head, drawing your shoulders down away from your ears. | Exhale and hinge forward from your hip joints, leading with your chest and keeping your back long rather than rounding it. | Allow a soft bend in your knees as you fold, letting your torso drape toward your thighs. | Let your hands move toward your feet, resting your palms on your shins, the floor, or beside your feet as your flexibility allows. | Relax your head and neck completely, letting the crown of your head hang toward the floor. | Hold the pose and breathe steadily, easing a little deeper into the hamstring and calf stretch with each exhale. | To release, bend your knees, engage your core, and roll up slowly to standing one vertebra at a time.

t: Stand facing a fixed, sturdy bar set at roughly chest to shoulder height and take an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart. | Set your grip firmly, wrapping your thumbs around the bar, and step your feet back until your arms are fully extended. | Keep your arms straight and slowly shift your hips down and back, letting your bodyweight hang away from the bar. | Allow your chest to drop between your arms and your shoulders to open, feeling the stretch spread across your lats and upper back. | Keep your core lightly braced and your head in a neutral line with your spine, not dropped or craned up. | Breathe slowly and hold the position for 20 to 40 seconds, relaxing a little deeper into the stretch with each exhale. | To release, draw your hips back toward the bar and step your feet in until you are standing upright before letting go of the bar.

t: Take an overhand grip on the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and hang with your arms straight and shoulders active. | Depress and retract your shoulder blades, then pull down and back on the bar to drive your torso away from vertical. | Tuck your knees toward your chest and begin rotating backward so your hips rise and your back moves toward parallel with the floor. | Open the tuck into the advanced position: let your hips drop away from your chest so your thighs move past 90 degrees, keeping your knees bent and shins close to your torso. | Brace your core hard, posteriorly tilt your pelvis, and squeeze your glutes so your back stays flat and your hips do not sag. | Hold your torso horizontal with straight arms, keeping your shoulders pulled down and your body in one rigid line from shoulders to hips. | Maintain steady, controlled breathing and resist any rotation back toward vertical for the duration of the hold. | When you can no longer hold position, re-tuck, lower under control, and return to a dead hang before releasing the bar.

t: Reach up and grip a pull-up bar with both hands roughly shoulder-width apart, palms facing away. | Hang from the bar with your arms fully straight and let your shoulders rise up toward your ears in a fully relaxed, passive hang. | Keeping your elbows locked straight, pull your shoulder blades down and back to depress and retract them, drawing your body slightly upward without bending your arms. | Hold the bottom position for a moment with your chest lifted and your shoulders set away from your ears. | Let your shoulder blades slowly travel back up toward your ears under control, returning to the passive hang. | Repeat for your target reps, keeping the movement small and controlled with the arms straight throughout. | Step down and release the bar safely once the set is complete.

t: Reach up and take an overhand grip on a pull-up bar slightly wider than shoulder-width, then hang with your arms fully extended and feet off the floor. | Engage your core and let your body settle into a tall, straight dead hang with your legs together. | Without bending your knees or swinging, draw your hips and lower body to one side by contracting the muscles along that side of your waist. | Lean only as far as you can control, keeping your shoulders active and your grip firm. | Pause briefly at the end of the lean, feeling the squeeze along the side of your trunk. | Return your body to the centred hang under control, resisting the urge to drop back quickly. | Repeat to the other side, alternating evenly so both sides of your waist do equal work. | Once your reps are complete, lower your feet to the floor and release the bar with control.

t: Grip a pull-up bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with an overhand grip and hang at full arm extension, feet off the floor. | Engage your shoulders by pulling them down and away from your ears, and brace your core to stop your body from swinging. | Without bending your arms, raise your straight legs in front of you, hinging at the hips and curling your pelvis upward. | Continue lifting until your toes reach up and lightly touch the bar above your hands. | Pause briefly at the top with your toes at the bar, keeping your core tight and your legs as straight as you can. | Lower your legs slowly and under control back to a full dead hang, resisting the urge to drop them. | Reset your hang without swinging, then repeat for your target number of reps. | Once your set is complete, lower your feet to the floor and release the bar with control.

t: Set up at a leverage machine bar and take an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, hanging with your arms straight. | Pull your shoulder blades down and back to engage your lats, keeping your arms locked. | Brace your core and tuck both knees up toward your chest, rounding your lower back slightly. | Lean back and pull the bar toward your hips so your torso rotates from vertical to horizontal, back facing the floor. | Hold the tucked position with your hips, shoulders, and head in one level line, parallel to the ground. | Keep your knees tucked tight and maintain steady, full-body tension for the planned hold time. | Breathe in short, controlled breaths without letting your hips sag. | Lower under control by dropping your hips and returning to a dead hang to finish the set.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat and exhale as you draw both knees in toward your chest. | Reach up between your thighs and take hold of the outer edges of your feet, or grip your ankles or shins if your feet are out of reach. | Stack each ankle directly over its knee so your shins are roughly vertical and the soles of your feet face the ceiling. | Gently pull your knees down toward the floor on either side of your torso, guiding them toward your armpits while keeping your tailbone and lower back settled on the mat. | Flex your feet, press them lightly up into your hands, and let your shoulders and head relax against the floor. | Hold the position for 30 seconds to 1 minute, breathing slowly and deeply into your hips and lower back. | To deepen the stretch, you can rock gently side to side to massage the lower back, then keep your breath steady throughout. | Release by letting go of your feet, hugging your knees into your chest, and lowering your feet to the floor.

t: Stand tall with your feet roughly hip- to shoulder-width apart and your toes turned slightly out. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and shift your weight back into your hips as if sitting down. | Bend at the hips, knees, and ankles to descend slowly into a deep squat, letting your knees track over your toes. | Lower until your hips drop below your knees while keeping your heels flat and your spine neutral. | Hold the bottom position briefly, keeping tension through your glutes, quads, and inner thighs. | Drive through your whole foot and push your hips forward to stand back up under control. | Squeeze your glutes at the top, then reset your stance and repeat for the desired reps.

t: Grip a pull-up bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with an overhand grip, wrapping your thumbs around the bar. | Pull yourself up into a flexed-arm hang so your chin is at or above the bar and your elbows are fully bent. | Brace your core and squeeze your back and shoulder blades to lock in a stable starting position. | Push your body down and away from the bar by extending your arms in a controlled motion until they are nearly straight. | Without swinging, reverse the movement and pull yourself explosively back up toward the bar. | Return to the flexed-arm hang with your chin level with the bar, keeping tension through your back and arms. | Repeat for your target reps, then lower under control to a dead hang and step down safely.

t: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and your weight balanced over the balls of your feet. | Brace your core gently and keep your hips square and level to start from a stable base. | Rise up so your heels lift off the floor, keeping your ankles, knees, and hips aligned. | Lower your heels back down under control, feeling the movement through your hips and lower body. | Pause briefly at the bottom without letting your hips collapse or shift to one side. | Repeat for your target reps, keeping each drop smooth and controlled rather than dropping fast. | Finish by standing tall with your feet flat and your hips level.

t: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, set about hip-width apart and close enough that your fingertips can graze your heels. | Lift your toes off the floor so your weight rests on your heels, and let your arms lie at your sides with palms down for balance. | Brace your core and tuck your pelvis slightly to flatten your lower back into the floor. | Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees. | Pause at the top for a moment and squeeze your glutes hard without overarching your lower back. | Lower your hips under control until they hover just above the floor, keeping tension on the glutes. | Repeat for your target reps, then set your hips down and relax.

t: Stand facing a wall and place both hands on it at about chest height for support. | Step one foot back, keeping the back leg straight and the toes pointing forward toward the wall. | Press the back heel firmly down into the floor until you feel a stretch along the calf and ankle. | Keep your hips square and your back leg straight to direct the stretch into the upper calf (gastrocnemius). | Hold the position and breathe slowly and evenly, letting the calf relax into the stretch on each exhale. | Hold for 20 to 30 seconds without bouncing, easing deeper only as the tension releases. | Release gently, then switch legs and repeat on the other side.

t: Start in a fighting stance with feet staggered, knees soft, hands up by your chin, and your weight slightly forward. | Shift your weight onto your standing leg and brace your core as you prepare to drive the rear (or lead) leg forward. | Pull the kicking knee up toward your chest, keeping the knee high and the foot cocked so the kick travels in a straight line. | Thrust your hips forward and extend the leg, pushing through the ball or heel of your foot into the target. | Keep your toes pulled back and your standing foot rooted, turning the supporting heel out slightly for power and reach. | Snap the kicking leg back to the chambered knee position immediately after contact rather than letting it drop. | Return the foot to the floor and reset into your stance with your guard up, ready to repeat or chain another strike. | Alternate legs or repeat for the prescribed reps or time, keeping a steady breathing rhythm throughout.

nR: Скольжения в приседе на пятках у стены
t: Stand with your back flat against a wall and your feet about shoulder-width apart, a step or so out in front of you. | Raise your heels slightly so your weight sits toward the balls of your feet, keeping your toes pointed forward. | Brace your core and press your lower back, upper back, and shoulders into the wall. | Slide your back down the wall by bending your knees, keeping them tracking in line with your toes. | Lower under control until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor, or as far as you can go with good form. | Pause briefly at the bottom while keeping your back in contact with the wall. | Drive through the balls of your feet and slide back up until your legs are nearly straight. | Complete your reps, then step away from the wall and lower your heels to finish.
tRu: Stand with your back flat against a wall and your feet about shoulder-width apart, a step or so out in front of you. | Raise your heels slightly so your weight sits toward the balls of your feet, keeping your toes pointed forward. | Напрягите корпус и прижмите поясницу, верхнюю часть спины и плечи к стене. | Slide your back down the wall by bending your knees, keeping them tracking in line with your toes. | Lower under control until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor, or as far as you can go with good form. | Pause briefly at the bottom while keeping your back in contact with the wall. | Оттолкнитесь подушечками стоп и скользите обратно вверх, пока ноги не станут почти прямыми. | Выполните все повторения, затем отойдите от стены и опустите пятки, чтобы завершить.

t: Find a straight line on the floor — a floor seam, a length of tape, or an imaginary line works well. | Stand tall at one end of the line with your feet together, eyes looking forward, and arms relaxed at your sides. | Step forward and place the heel of your front foot directly in front of the toes of your back foot, so they almost touch. | Shift your weight smoothly onto the front foot, keeping your torso upright and your core gently braced. | Bring the back foot through and place its heel just in front of the toes of the now-planted foot, staying on the line. | Continue walking heel-to-toe in a slow, controlled rhythm for the planned distance or number of steps. | Pause briefly on each step if needed to steady yourself, keeping your gaze fixed ahead rather than down at your feet. | Stop at the end of the line, return with control, and rest before repeating.

t: Kneel on a mat with your knees together and your shins flat on the floor, feet pointing straight back behind you. | Spread your feet slightly wider than your hips so there is room for your hips to sink between them, keeping the tops of your feet pressing into the mat. | Sit back and lower your hips toward the floor in the gap between your heels, not on top of them. | If your hips do not reach the floor comfortably, slide a yoga block or cushion under them so you sit tall without straining your knees. | Lengthen your spine, stack your head over your hips, and let your shoulders relax down and back. | Rest your hands on your thighs with the palms facing down and soften your face and jaw. | Breathe slowly and hold for 30 seconds to a few minutes, feeling the stretch across the front of your thighs and ankles. | To release, press your hands into the floor, lift your hips, and extend your legs forward one at a time to ease out of the pose.

nR: Отжимания на наклонной на высокой перекладине
nH: שכיבות סמיכה בשיפוע על מוט גבוה

t: Stand facing a sturdy box or bench tall enough that your knee is at roughly hip height when your foot is planted on it. | Place one full foot flat on top of the box, keeping that shin close to vertical and your toes pointing forward. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and shift your weight over the foot on the box. | Drive through the heel and midfoot of the top leg to push your body straight up, keeping the trailing leg relaxed. | Stand tall on top of the box with the working leg, bringing the trailing foot up to balance without slamming it down. | Pause briefly at the top under control, keeping your hips level and torso upright. | Lower the trailing leg back to the floor slowly, letting the working leg control the descent. | Reset your footing, complete your reps on that side, then switch to the other leg.

nE: High Hurdle Jump to Sprint and Cut
nR: Прыжки через высокий барьер со спринтом и сменой направления
nH: קפיצת משוכה גבוהה לספרינט ושינוי כיוון
t: Set a single high hurdle and clear the space in front of it for a 5–10 metre sprint lane plus room to cut left or right. | Stand a short stride behind the hurdle with feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and your weight balanced over the middle of your feet. | Dip into a quarter-squat, swing your arms back, then drive both arms up and extend powerfully through your hips, knees, and ankles to jump over the hurdle. | Tuck your knees to clear the bar and spot your landing zone on the far side. | Land on the balls of both feet with knees bent and hips back, absorbing the impact softly rather than landing stiff-legged. | The instant you land, transition forward and accelerate into a sprint, staying low for the first few steps and pumping your arms. | After a few hard strides, plant your outside foot, drop your hips, and cut sharply in the chosen direction by pushing off that planted foot. | Decelerate under control, reset to the start, and repeat for your prescribed reps, alternating the cut direction.

nE: High Knee Lunge on Bosu Ball
nR: Выпады с высоким коленом на босу
t: Place the Bosu ball dome-side up on a flat, non-slip surface and stand a stride-length in front of it with your feet hip-width apart and your core braced. | Step one foot back onto the center of the dome, finding your balance on the soft, unstable surface. | Lower into a lunge, bending both knees toward roughly 90° while keeping your front knee stacked over your ankle and your torso upright. | Drive hard through your front foot and push off the dome to stand up explosively. | As you rise, drive the rear knee up toward your chest into a high-knee position, swinging the opposite arm forward for momentum and balance. | Control your descent and step the same foot back onto the dome to begin the next rep, keeping your movements rhythmic. | Complete your reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat, or alternate legs each rep for a continuous aerobic pace. | Step off the dome with control to finish, and reset your balance before the next set.

t: Stand facing a sturdy, knee-height box or step with your feet hip-width apart and your core braced. | Place your right foot fully onto the box, keeping the whole sole in contact and your knee tracking over your toes. | Drive through your right heel to stand tall on the box, straightening your hip and knee. | As you reach the top, explosively pull your left knee up high in front of you until your thigh is at least parallel to the ground. | Hold the balanced top position briefly, keeping your chest up and standing leg stable. | Step your left foot back down to the floor under control, then bring your right foot down to follow. | Reset your stance, then repeat leading with the same leg for your reps before switching sides. | Keep a steady, rhythmic pace to maintain an aerobic heart rate throughout the set.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart, and heels positioned a few inches from your glutes. | Rest your arms at your sides, palms down, and gently brace your core by drawing your navel toward your spine. | Press through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees. | At the top, hold the position for one to two seconds while keeping your abs braced and glutes fully contracted. | Avoid arching your lower back; keep the line of your body straight rather than letting your hips sag or hyperextend. | Lower your hips under control back toward the floor without fully resting your glutes down between reps to maintain tension. | Complete your target reps, then lower all the way down and relax.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your arms resting at your sides, palms pressing into the floor for stability. | Raise your legs so your hips and knees are bent at roughly 90 degrees, with your shins parallel to the floor. | Brace your abs and exhale as you curl your pelvis toward your ribs, lifting your hips a few inches off the mat. | Drive your knees toward your chest at the top while keeping the movement controlled, not swung. | Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your abs without using momentum to throw the legs. | Inhale and lower your hips back to the mat under control, keeping tension in your core. | Repeat for your target reps, then set your feet down and relax.

t: Set up in a forearm plank: elbows under your shoulders, forearms flat on the floor, and legs extended back with feet together. | Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. | Keep your shoulders and upper back still as you slowly rotate your hips to one side, lowering that hip toward the floor without touching it. | Pause briefly at the bottom of the rotation while keeping your core braced. | Reverse the movement and rotate your hips to the opposite side under control. | Continue alternating sides at a steady tempo, breathing throughout and keeping the rest of your body stable. | Finish the set, then lower your knees to the floor to come out of the plank.

t: Stand tall next to a wall or sturdy support, resting one hand on it for balance, with your feet hip-width apart. | Brace your core and shift your weight onto your supporting leg, keeping a soft bend in that knee. | Lift the working leg slightly off the floor, letting the foot hang relaxed. | Drive the knee up and across the front of your body, leading the circle with the hip. | Sweep the leg outward in a wide, controlled arc, opening the hip to the side. | Continue the circle back and down to return the leg toward the start, keeping your pelvis level throughout. | Complete your reps in one direction, then reverse the swirl to circle the other way. | Switch sides and repeat with the opposite leg.

t: Sit or kneel tall and plant your hands or forearms on the floor (or a low surface) beside you to support your upper body. | Set your hips squarely underneath your torso and draw a gentle breath in to lengthen through your spine. | Exhale and slowly rotate your hips and waist toward one side, letting your supporting arms control the movement. | Continue twisting only as far as you feel a comfortable stretch along your obliques and the side of your abdomen. | Pause at the end of your range and breathe slowly, allowing the muscles along your waist to relax and lengthen. | Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds without bouncing or forcing the rotation deeper. | Inhale as you slowly unwind your hips back to the centered, neutral position. | Repeat on the opposite side, matching the same controlled tempo and hold time.

t: Stand in a fighting stance about one leg-length from the bag, knees soft, hands up to guard your face and core braced. | Shift your weight onto your front (base) leg and lift your rear knee, chambering it across your body with the foot cocked. | Pivot hard on the ball of your base foot so the heel turns toward the bag and your hips open into the strike. | Extend the leg and whip the heel laterally across the face of the bag, leading with the heel rather than the toes. | Snap the foot back along the same path the instant it makes contact, recoiling the leg quickly instead of pushing through. | Re-chamber and lower the foot back to your stance, returning your guard and resetting your balance. | Exhale sharply on the snap and breathe steadily between strikes to keep a sustainable aerobic pace. | Repeat for timed rounds, alternating or isolating legs, then rest and reset between rounds.

t: Face your partner in a fighting stance, knees soft and hands up, with the pad held at roughly head or torso height on your kicking side. | Shift your weight onto your standing leg and pivot that foot so your heel begins to rotate toward the target. | Chamber the kicking leg by lifting the knee across your body, aiming it slightly past the pad. | Extend the leg outward as if reaching beyond the target, keeping your foot relaxed and your toes pointed. | Snap the leg back across your body so the heel hooks into the pad, striking with the heel or sole. | Retract the leg quickly along the same path, bringing the knee back to a chambered position under control. | Lower the foot and reset to your fighting stance, hands up and balanced for the next rep. | Complete your reps on one side, then switch legs or rotate roles with your partner.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, core braced, and arms relaxed at your sides. | Raise one hand to about waist or hip height in front of you to set a target for the knee. | Hop lightly on your standing leg while driving the opposite knee up to tap the raised hand. | Land softly on the ball of your standing foot, keeping a slight bend in the knee to absorb the impact. | Hop again and switch sides, bringing the other knee up to tap the opposite hand. | Continue alternating knees in a steady, springy rhythm, staying light and quick on your feet. | Keep your chest tall and your eyes forward, breathing in a controlled rhythm throughout. | Slow the pace to a stop for the final reps, then step out of the movement and recover.

t: Step into a Warrior I stance: front knee bent over the ankle, back leg straight with the back foot angled slightly out, hips squared toward the front leg. | Reach both arms behind your back and interlace your fingers, drawing your knuckles toward the floor to draw the shoulder blades together. | Lift your chest and lengthen the front of your torso, opening across the collarbones before you fold. | Inhale to grow tall, then exhale and hinge forward from the hips, lowering your torso to the inside of the front thigh. | Let your interlaced hands lift up and over your back as you fold, keeping a light grip rather than forcing the reach. | Bring the crown of your head toward the floor inside the front foot, keeping the back leg straight and active. | Hold for 5 to 8 slow breaths, softening a little deeper into the shoulders and hips on each exhale. | To exit, release the fingers, press into both feet, and rise back up to Warrior I with control. Repeat on the other side.

t: Set an incline bench to a low-to-moderate angle (roughly 20–45 degrees) and sit at the top end with your back flat against the pad. | Extend both legs straight out in front of you, parallel to the floor, with feet together and toes pointed. | Brace your core and press your lower back lightly into the bench to stabilize your pelvis. | Raise your right leg approximately 15–20 cm while simultaneously lowering your left leg the same distance. | Immediately reverse the motion, raising your left leg and lowering your right in a smooth, controlled scissoring rhythm. | Keep both legs straight and avoid letting either foot drop below hip level unless the exercise demands a fuller range. | Maintain steady breathing — exhale on every two or three kicks rather than holding your breath. | Continue alternating for the prescribed number of repetitions or duration, then lower both feet to the floor in a controlled manner to finish.

t: Place two chairs of equal height roughly shoulder-width apart, facing each other, and confirm both are stable and will not slide on the floor. | Sit between the chairs, then lower yourself to lie on your back on the floor with your head between the chairs and your shoulders roughly level with the chair seats. | Bend your knees and plant your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, so your body forms a tabletop position with your hips off the ground. | Reach up and grip the front edges of the chair seats with an underhand (supinated) grip — palms facing toward your face — hands roughly shoulder-width apart. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips level, forming a straight line from knees to shoulders throughout the set. | Exhale and curl your chin toward the chair seats by driving your elbows toward your hips, leading the movement with your biceps rather than shrugging your shoulders. | Continue until your chin clears the seat edge or your elbows reach full flexion — whichever comes first — and pause briefly at the top. | Inhale and lower yourself under control back to the starting position until your arms are fully extended without your shoulders dropping to the floor. | Complete all reps, then carefully sit up and step away from the chairs before standing.

t: Place two heavy, stable chairs back-to-back or side by side at a width slightly wider than your shoulders, and lay a sturdy bar, broomstick, or similar rigid object across the seats so it cannot roll or slip. | Sit on the floor between the chairs, reach up, and grip the bar with an overhand grip roughly shoulder-width apart. | Bend your knees and plant your feet flat on the floor directly beneath or slightly in front of your knees. | Straighten your arms and lower your torso toward the floor so your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders — this is your starting position. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your body rigid as you pull your chest up toward the bar. | Drive your elbows back and toward your sides, leading the movement with your shoulder blades squeezing together. | Pull until your chest lightly touches or nearly reaches the bar, holding the top position for a brief pause. | Lower yourself under control until your arms are fully extended, maintaining full-body tension throughout. | Complete all reps, then carefully release the bar and sit up.

t: Grip the pull-up bar with both hands close together (4–6 inches apart), palms facing toward you in a supinated grip. | Hang at full arm extension with your shoulders slightly retracted, core braced, and legs crossed or straight to minimize swinging. | Initiate the pull by depressing your shoulder blades and driving your elbows down and back toward your hips. | Continue pulling until your chin rises clearly above the bar, keeping your chest tall and your body in a slight hollow position. | At the top, hold this position isometrically — chin above the bar, elbows fully flexed, muscles fully contracted — for the prescribed duration (5–30 seconds). | Focus on squeezing the lats and biceps throughout the hold; breathe steadily and avoid letting the chin drop or the elbows flare. | After completing the hold, lower yourself in a slow, controlled manner back to a dead hang over 3–5 seconds. | Reset your position and repeat for the prescribed number of sets.

t: Stand with your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward, and the barbell or a moderate load absent — this is a bodyweight movement. | Hinge at your hips and bend your knees slightly into an athletic quarter-squat position, keeping your chest up, back flat, and arms hanging in front of your thighs. | Load your hips by pushing them back slightly and creating tension through your glutes, hamstrings, and adductors — this is your starting position. | Drive explosively through your feet, extending your ankles, knees, and hips simultaneously to generate maximum upward force. | As your body reaches full triple extension and your heels leave the ground, shrug your shoulders powerfully straight up toward your ears. | Allow your arms to remain relatively straight throughout — the shrug should come from the upper trapezius, not a biceps curl. | Let your feet leave the floor at peak height, maintaining an upright torso. | Land softly by absorbing impact through your ankles, knees, and hips in sequence, returning to the athletic hinge position. | Reset your posture fully between reps before initiating the next explosive drive.

t: Stand tall with the rope handles held loosely at your sides, one in each hand, with the rope looped behind your feet. | Hold the handles at roughly hip height and slightly out from your hips, keeping your elbows bent at around 90° and close to your torso. | Initiate the swing by rotating your wrists forward to send the rope up and over your head in a smooth arc. | As the rope swings down toward your feet, push off the balls of your feet and hop just high enough for the rope to pass underneath — roughly 1–2 inches of clearance. | Land softly on the balls of your feet with your knees slightly bent to absorb impact, staying light and springy. | Immediately prepare for the next rotation by letting your wrists flick forward again to keep the rope turning in a continuous arc. | Maintain an upright posture with your gaze forward and your core lightly braced throughout the set. | Continue for the target duration or rep count, then slow the rope to a controlled stop.

Your weight should be evenly distributed through the full foot. | Initiate the movement by driving your hips forward aggressively, extending your knees and hips simultaneously as if jumping — do not pull with the arm first. | As your hips snap forward and your body rises to a tall, upright position, use the momentum to guide the bell upward along a close path near your body. | At the top of the hip drive, shrug your shoulder and pull your elbow high to keep the bell moving upward. | Rotate your wrist and 'thread' your hand under the bell so that the bell flips around your forearm and settles in the rack position: bell resting on your forearm, elbow pointed forward and down, upper arm close to your chest at shoulder height. | Stand fully upright and absorb the catch by slightly bending your knees. tRu: Поднимите гирю в стойку, затем выжмите её одной рукой над головой, пока локоть полностью не выпрямится, а запястье не окажется над плечом. | Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and toes turned out 15–30 degrees to allow full hip depth. | Extend your free arm out to the side for balance, keeping it at roughly shoulder height throughout the movement. | Напрягите корпус, сделайте глубокий вдох и смотрите на гирю над головой — держите на ней взгляд на всём протяжении опускания. | Push your knees out in line with your toes and sit your hips back and down, descending slowly over 2–3 seconds into a full squat. | Внизу бёдра должны быть ниже колен, грудь вертикально, а гиря — строго над плечом на прямой руке. | Отталкивайтесь пяткой и серединой стопы, разгибайте тазобедренный сустав и колено, и прыгните вертикально. | Выполните все повторения на одну сторону, затем поменяйте руки.
tHe: נקה את הקטלבל למצב המדף, לאחר מכן לחץ אותו מעל הראש עם זרוע אחד עד שהמרפק שלך ננעל לחלוטין והפרק כף היד שלנך מונח מעל הכתף. | Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and toes turned out 15–30 degrees to allow full hip depth. | Extend your free arm out to the side for balance, keeping it at roughly shoulder height throughout the movement. | כווץ את שרירי הליבה, קח נשימה עמוקה, והתחל את הירידה על ידי דחיפת האגן אחורה וכיפוף הברך העומדת. | Push your knees out in line with your toes and sit your hips back and down, descending slowly over 2–3 seconds into a full squat. | בתחתית האגן צריך להיות מתחת לברכיים, החזה זקוף, והקטלבל בדיוק מעל הכתף עם יד נעולה. | Drive through your heels and mid-foot to stand, squeezing your glutes as you return to the top. | בצע את כל החזרות בצד אחד לפני החלפת הידיים.

nH: לחיצת דחיקה ביד אחת עם קטלבל
t: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height in the rack position — elbow tucked, wrist straight, and the bell resting against the back of your forearm. | Brace your core and glutes, keeping your torso upright and your free arm extended to the side or lightly resting on your hip for balance. | Initiate the movement with a quick, shallow dip by softly bending your knees 2–4 inches while keeping your chest up and heels on the floor. | Immediately reverse the dip by driving explosively through your legs to transfer power up through your hips and torso. | Use that upward momentum to press the kettlebell straight overhead, locking your elbow out fully at the top with your bicep close to your ear. | Hold the locked-out position for a brief moment, ensuring your wrist is stacked over your elbow and your core is tight. | Lower the kettlebell under control back to the rack position at your shoulder to begin the next rep. | Complete all reps on one side before switching hands.

t: Stand to the right of a bench (or with feet hip-width apart in a staggered stance). Hinge at the hips until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor, place your left hand and left knee on the bench for support, and let the kettlebell hang directly below your right shoulder with a neutral grip. | Brace your core and set your spine in a neutral position — no rounding in the lower back and no excessive arch. Your working shoulder should be level with the opposite shoulder. | Initiate the pull by retracting your right shoulder blade toward your spine before you bend your elbow. | Drive your elbow straight back and up toward your hip, keeping it close to your torso. The kettlebell should travel toward your hip, not your chest. | Pull until the kettlebell reaches hip or lower-rib height and your elbow is bent past 90°. Briefly hold at the top and feel the muscles of your upper back contract. | Lower the kettlebell under control back to the starting position, allowing your shoulder blade to protract slightly at the bottom to get a full range of motion through the lats. | Complete all prescribed reps on the right side, then switch sides and repeat.

t: Stand with your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart and the kettlebell on the floor a few inches in front of you, between your feet. | Hinge at the hips with a flat back and neutral neck, and hook one hand over the handle — fingers hooked, thumb relaxed — so the handle can rotate freely in your palm. | Hike the bell back between your legs, keeping your forearm against your inner thigh and your chest facing forward. | Snap your hips forward and drive through the floor, letting the hip extension throw the bell up in a tight vertical path close to your body. | As the bell passes hip height, pull your elbow high and keep the bell close to your torso — do not let it swing out in front of you. | At about shoulder height, punch your hand up through the handle so the bell rotates around your wrist and settles on the back of your forearm — punch, do not curl. | Finish with the arm locked out, wrist stacked over your shoulder, biceps near your ear and the shoulder packed down; hold for a beat to confirm balance. | Tilt the bell forward off your forearm and guide it down close to your body, hinging at the hips to let it swing back between your legs for the next rep. | Complete all reps on one side, park the bell on the floor between your feet, then switch hands and repeat.

t: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height with your elbow pointing forward and the bell resting on the back of your forearm. | Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement. | Descend into a squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor. | Drive explosively through your heels to extend your hips and knees, generating momentum upward through your legs. | As your body rises, use the leg drive to press the kettlebell straight overhead until your arm is fully locked out. | Hold the top position briefly with the kettlebell directly above your shoulder and your bicep next to your ear. | Lower the kettlebell back to shoulder height with control as you simultaneously descend into the next squat. | Complete all reps on one arm, then switch sides.

nR: Становая на одной ноге с гирей
t: Stand upright holding a kettlebell in one hand, feet hip-width apart. Choose the hand opposite the working leg for a cross-body grip, or the same-side hand for an ipsilateral grip. | Shift your weight onto the working leg and soften the knee slightly — this is your stance leg for the entire set. | Hinge forward at the hip, sending the non-working leg straight back behind you as a counterbalance while the kettlebell lowers toward the floor. | Keep your hips square to the floor throughout the descent — resist the urge to open the trailing hip toward the ceiling. | Lower the kettlebell until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor, or until you feel a strong stretch in the hamstring of the stance leg, whichever comes first. | Drive through the heel of the stance leg and squeeze your glute to return to the upright starting position, bringing the trailing leg back in line with your body. | Stand fully tall with hips extended at the top before beginning the next rep. | Complete all reps on one side before switching legs.

nH: קלין בכף יד פתוחה עם קטלבל
t: Stand with feet hip- to shoulder-width apart, the kettlebell on the floor between your feet and slightly in front of your ankles. | Hinge at the hips, grip the bell handle, and hike it back between your legs to load the posterior chain — as in the start of a swing. | Drive your hips forcefully forward, squeezing your glutes at the top to project the kettlebell upward along your centerline. | As the bell rises, guide it close to your body by keeping your elbow tucked and your forearm vertical. | At roughly chest height, begin to relax your grip: open your hand so the fingers are loose and the bell rotates around the wrist rather than flipping over the fist. | Receive the bell in the rack position with an open, relaxed palm — the handle resting diagonally across the heel of your hand, elbow pressed into your ribcage, and the bell balanced on your forearm. | Stand tall in the rack, feet planted, core braced, shoulder packed down and back. | To lower, tilt the bell forward off the forearm, guide it back into the hip hinge, and hike for the next rep — or set it down under control.

t: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell on the floor about 12 inches in front of you. Point toes slightly outward. | Hinge at the hips, push them back, and grip the handle with both hands in an overhand (pronated) grip — palms facing toward you, knuckles up. | Pull the kettlebell back between your legs in a hike pass, keeping your forearms in contact with your inner thighs and your spine neutral. | Drive your hips forward explosively, squeezing your glutes hard at the top of the movement to propel the bell forward and upward. | Allow the kettlebell to float to chest or shoulder height — roughly parallel with the floor. Your arms guide the arc; the power comes from your hips, not your shoulders. | Keep your wrists straight throughout the float. The pronated grip will rotate your forearms inward slightly compared with a neutral grip — do not let the wrists collapse or flex downward. | As the bell descends, push your hips back early, absorbing the load through your hamstrings and gluteus maximus rather than your lower back. | Let the bell hike back between your legs with control, forearms brushing the thighs, then immediately fire the next hip drive to link reps. | Complete your set, then park the bell by hiking it back and lowering it to the floor in a controlled hinge — do not let it drop or round your lower back on the finish.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward, holding one kettlebell with both hands in front of your hips. | Brace your core, pull your shoulder blades down and back, and hinge slightly at the hips to load your glutes and hamstrings. | Allow the kettlebell to swing laterally to one side — toward the outside of your hip — by initiating a controlled hip shift and rotation toward that side. | At the bottom of the arc, snap the hips back to center and use the momentum to drive the kettlebell across the body in a lateral arc to the opposite side. | Let your torso rotate slightly to follow the bell while keeping your spine neutral and your core braced — avoid bending sideways at the waist. | Control the bell at the apex of each side swing; do not let it pull your shoulders out of their packed position. | Continue alternating the lateral swing smoothly from side to side for the prescribed number of reps. | To finish, let the arc shorten until the bell settles in front of your hips, then hinge at the hips and set it down on the floor under control.

t: Lie on your back and hold the kettlebell in your right hand with the arm extended straight toward the ceiling, wrist neutral and elbow locked. | Bend your right knee so the right foot is flat on the floor; extend your left arm out to the side at roughly 45 degrees, palm down, to serve as a base. | Fix your gaze on the kettlebell and keep it there throughout the entire movement. | Press through your left forearm and right foot simultaneously to roll onto your left elbow, keeping the right arm vertical. | Straighten the left arm and press your left hand firmly into the floor, arriving at the hand-supported position with your torso upright and the kettlebell directly overhead. | Hold the hand-supported position for a full breath, confirming shoulder packing, a braced core, and a straight pressing arm. | Reverse the movement: lower back onto your left elbow under control, then lower your torso all the way to the floor. | Return to the starting position with the kettlebell still locked overhead, then lower the weight safely to complete the repetition. | Complete all reps on one side before switching the kettlebell to the left hand and repeating.

t: Place two kettlebells on the floor between your feet, roughly hip-width apart. Grip each handle with a firm overhand grip, thumbs pointing inward toward each other. | Tilt the kettlebells toward you so the handles angle diagonally inward — this pre-loads the movement and prevents the bells from swinging away. | Take a short breath, brace your core, and hike both kettlebells back between your legs in one controlled swing, as if snapping a football. | Explosively extend your hips and knees, driving tall through your heels. t: Clean both kettlebells into the front rack position: bells resting on the back of your forearms, handles at shoulder height, elbows pointed slightly forward and tucked close to your body. | Stand with your feet together or hip-width apart, glutes and core braced, ribs pulled down to prevent lumbar hyperextension. | Take a breath and brace your abdomen as if preparing to absorb a punch, keeping your spine neutral. | Press both kettlebells straight overhead simultaneously by driving your elbows up and slightly outward, keeping your wrists stacked directly over your forearms. | Continue pressing until your elbows reach full lockout overhead, biceps aligned close to your ears, with your wrists neutral — not bent back. | At the top, actively push the bells toward the ceiling and let your shoulder blades rotate upward to engage the serratus anterior. | Lower the kettlebells under control back to the front rack position in a smooth arc, keeping your elbows from flaring wide on the descent. | Reset your brace before initiating the next rep; do not use any knee dip or hip thrust to drive the weight up.

nR: Русские скручивания с весом с гирей
nH: טוויסט רוסי עם משקל עם קטלבל
t: Sit on the floor and hold a kettlebell with both hands at chest height, gripping the handle with fingers interlaced or each hand on one side of the handle. | Lean your torso back to roughly 45° from the floor, keeping your spine neutral and your chest tall. | Lift your feet a few inches off the floor and cross your ankles, or keep your heels lightly resting on the floor if you need more stability. | Brace your core and let the kettlebell hang just in front of your sternum as your starting position. | Rotate your torso to the right, moving the kettlebell toward the floor beside your right hip while keeping your hips square. | Pause briefly at the end of the range, then rotate back through center and continue to the left side in a controlled arc. | Keep your lower back neutral throughout — avoid rounding your lumbar spine as you rotate. | Complete the desired number of repetitions, counting each full left-right cycle as one rep, then lower your feet and set the kettlebell down with control.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and angle both feet roughly 45 degrees to the left, away from the arm that will hold the bell. | Press the kettlebell overhead with your right hand and lock out your elbow fully, keeping your gaze fixed on the bell throughout the entire movement. | Push your right hip out to the right as you begin to hinge laterally, shifting your weight onto your right hip. | Keeping the right arm locked overhead and the bell directly above your shoulder, slide your left hand down the inside of your left leg toward the floor. | Continue lowering until your left hand reaches your shin, ankle, or the floor — whichever your current hip and hamstring flexibility allows — while keeping the overhead arm vertical. | Pause at the bottom for one second, maintaining a neutral spine and steady gaze on the bell. | Drive through your right hip and engage your obliques to return your torso to upright, keeping the kettlebell locked out overhead throughout the ascent. | Complete all reps on one side before switching the kettlebell to the other hand and repeating.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a kettlebell with both hands by the handle, arms extended. | Rotate your hips and torso to one side, lowering the kettlebell diagonally toward the outside of your opposite knee while keeping a slight bend in both knees. | Brace your core firmly and keep your spine neutral — do not round your lower back as you load the starting position. | Drive through your hips to rotate your torso in the opposite direction, sweeping the kettlebell diagonally upward across your body toward the opposite shoulder. | Follow the arc naturally with your arms, allowing your trailing heel to rise slightly off the floor as your hips finish rotating. | Pause briefly at the top with the kettlebell held high, arms extended, and your core still braced. | Reverse the movement under control, lowering the kettlebell back along the same diagonal path to the starting position. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch your stance and repeat on the opposite side.

t: Sit on a bench or chair and hold a kettlebell by the handle in one hand with an underhand (supinated) grip. | Rest your forearm on your thigh or on the edge of the bench so that your wrist hangs just beyond your knee or the bench edge. | Allow the kettlebell to lower slowly, letting your wrist extend toward the floor until you feel a stretch in your forearm. | Curl your wrist upward, flexing the wrist fully so the kettlebell rises as high as comfortable. | Pause briefly at the top, squeezing the wrist flexors. | Lower the kettlebell under control back to the starting extended position. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch hands and repeat.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you and your torso upright. Brace your core and press your lower back tall — do not allow your hips to tilt back. | Clean the kettlebell to the rack position on the working side: wrist straight, elbow pointing down, the bell resting against the back of your forearm and upper chest. | Take a deep breath, brace your abs and glutes, and press the kettlebell directly overhead, extending your arm fully without letting your elbow flare excessively. | At the top, lock out the elbow and actively push the bell toward the ceiling, packing your shoulder by pressing your shoulder blade up and into the socket. | Lower the kettlebell under control back to the rack position, keeping your torso vertical and your opposite hand braced lightly on the floor only for balance if needed. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch hands and repeat.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, core braced, and arms relaxed at your sides. | Shift your weight onto your left foot and kick your right leg out to the side at hip height, keeping your standing leg slightly bent. | Bring your right foot back toward the ground and immediately push off your left foot to jump laterally to the right. | Land softly on your right foot with a bent knee to absorb the impact, keeping your chest upright. | As you land, kick your left leg out to the side at hip height to mirror the starting movement. | Without pausing, jump back to the left, landing on your left foot with a soft knee bend. | Continue alternating sides in a fluid, rhythmic pattern for the desired number of repetitions or duration. | Keep your core tight and your gaze forward throughout to maintain balance and control.

t: Start on all fours with your wrists directly below your shoulders and your knees directly below your hips. Keep your spine neutral — do not allow your lower back to sag or arch. | Brace your core lightly so your torso stays stable throughout the movement. | Keeping the working knee bent at roughly 90°, lift that knee off the floor and drive it upward and back, pressing the sole of your foot toward the ceiling. | Stop when your thigh is roughly parallel to the floor and your foot is directly above your knee. Your lower back should not rotate or arch at the top. | Pause for one count at the top, squeezing the glute of the working leg. | Lower the knee slowly back to the starting position just above the floor without resting it down. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat.

t: Start on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips. Keep your spine neutral and your core lightly braced. | Lift one knee off the floor, keeping it bent at approximately 90 degrees throughout the movement. | Brace your core and squeeze your glute on the working side to initiate the movement. | Kick the bent leg upward and back, driving your heel toward the ceiling until your thigh is roughly parallel to the floor and your foot points upward. | Hold the top position for a brief pause, focusing on the squeeze in your gluteus maximus. | Slowly lower your knee back toward the starting position under control, stopping just before it touches the floor. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat.

t: Start in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart, toes on the floor, and your hips level with your shoulders — this is also called a bear crawl position with knees hovering just off the ground. | Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor as you would in a standard push-up, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | Press explosively back up to the top of the push-up, fully extending your arms. | Shift your weight onto your left hand, rotate your torso to the right, and simultaneously kick your right leg through the space under your body, swinging it out to the left side. | Pause briefly with your right leg extended and your hips open toward the ceiling, feeling the stretch through your core and hip flexors. | Reverse the rotation and bring your right foot back to the starting position, returning to the high plank. | Perform another push-up, then rotate to the left and kick your left leg through to the right side. | Continue alternating the kick-through direction with each repetition for the target number of reps or time.

t: Kick up into a handstand with your heels resting against the wall, hands roughly shoulder-width apart and fingers spread, 6–12 inches from the wall. | Establish a tight, hollow body position — ribs down, core braced, glutes squeezed — with your body stacked vertically over your hands. | Begin the kip by bowing your hips toward the wall and bending at the knees to create an arched position, loading tension in your hips and shoulders. | Snap your hips back to a hollow body position explosively, driving your knees toward your chest to generate upward momentum through the torso. | Use that momentum to lower yourself quickly into the bottom of the press, letting your head descend toward the floor in a controlled dip. | As the momentum reverses, press forcefully through your palms, extending your arms and driving your body back up to a locked-out handstand. | At the top, reset your hollow body position and pause briefly before initiating the next kip cycle. | To dismount, carefully pike your hips, walk your feet down the wall, and step back to the floor.

t: Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with a false grip or standard overhand grip, arms fully extended, and body hanging in a hollow position — ribs down, core braced, legs together. | Initiate the kip by pressing the bar away and allowing your body to swing forward into an arch position — chest up, hips forward, legs behind you. | From the arch, aggressively drive your hips upward by snapping from the arch into a hollow, pulling your knees or legs toward the bar simultaneously. | As the hips rise and generate upward momentum, pull the bar toward your hips — not your chest — keeping your elbows wide and leading with the hips. | As your hips reach bar height, quickly rotate your wrists and pull your chest over the bar, transitioning from a pull to a push in one fluid motion. | Press down on the bar with both hands to push your body above it, extending your arms until your elbows are fully locked out in the support position. | Hold the support position with arms straight, shoulders pressing down, and core engaged. | Lower yourself back to the hanging position in a controlled manner or use the descent to re-initiate the kip for the next repetition. | Maintain the hollow-arch rhythm between reps, keeping the swing consistent and controlled to preserve momentum.

t: Sit on the edge of a bench or sturdy chair with your thighs fully supported and your lower legs hanging freely. | Sit tall, brace your core lightly, and plant both hands on the bench beside your hips to keep your torso upright. | Begin with the working leg hanging at roughly 90° of knee flexion — this is your start position. | Slowly extend your knee, driving your heel forward and upward until your leg is as straight as you can comfortably reach, squeezing the quadriceps at the top. | Pause for one to two seconds at full extension, feeling active tension in the quadriceps. | Lower your lower leg back down under control to the 90° start position, resisting gravity the entire way. | Complete all reps on one leg before switching to the other.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your hands resting lightly on a wall or sturdy surface for balance. | Shift your weight onto your left foot, keeping a very slight bend in the standing knee. | Lift your right foot off the floor by bending your right knee, bringing your heel toward your glutes. | Move slowly and with control, flexing the knee as far as your range of motion comfortably allows without forcing it. | Pause briefly at the end range, feeling a gentle stretch along the front of the thigh and through the calf. | Lower your foot back to the starting position in a smooth, controlled arc. | Complete all repetitions on one side before switching to the other leg. | Breathe steadily throughout — exhale as you flex the knee, inhale as you lower.

t: Kneel on a mat with your knees hip-width apart and your hips stacked directly over your knees. | Place your hands on your thighs or let them rest at your sides — keep your torso upright and your spine in a neutral position. | Take a relaxed breath in through your nose, allowing your belly to expand naturally. | As you exhale through your mouth, slowly draw your navel in toward your spine without rounding your lower back or tilting your pelvis. | Hold the drawn-in position for 5–10 seconds while continuing to breathe in shallow breaths — do not hold your breath. | Keep your shoulders relaxed and your chest open throughout the hold. | After the hold, release the contraction fully and allow your abdomen to relax before the next repetition. | Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions or time.

t: Position yourself beneath a fixed chin-up bar on a smooth floor or with a slider pad under your knees. Kneel upright with your knees hip-width apart and your shins resting on the surface. | Reach up and grip the bar with a supinated (palms-facing-you) grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended and your body hanging in a near-vertical line from the bar. | Brace your core and pull your shoulder blades down and together to create tension across your back before you begin the pull. | Begin pulling yourself up by driving your elbows down toward your hips. t: Kneel on the floor with your knees hip-width apart and your hips stacked directly over your knees. t: Kneel on the floor with your knees hip-width apart and your hips stacked directly over your knees. t: Anchor the ropes to a fixed point at ground level and lay them out straight in front of you. | Kneel facing the anchor, with knees hip-width apart and toes pointed behind you or tucked under — whichever allows a stable base. | Sit tall through the hips, brace the core, and keep the spine neutral from tailbone to crown. | Grip one rope end in each hand with an overhand grip, arms slightly bent and elbows close to the body. | To begin alternating waves, drive one arm down forcefully toward the floor while lifting the other, then switch rapidly to produce a continuous wave toward the anchor. | To perform simultaneous waves, drive both arms down and up together in unison, generating a double-wave pattern. | Maintain a steady rhythm throughout the set — focus on consistent wave amplitude rather than maximum speed. | Breathe continuously; exhale on each downward drive and inhale on the upward phase, or breathe in short rhythmic bursts if the pace demands it. | At the end of the set, slow the ropes gradually to a stop, set them down, and release the grip before standing.

t: Place a chair beside you on your dominant side and position a folded mat or towel on the floor to cushion your knee. | Kneel down on the padded surface so your right knee rests on the floor and your right shin points straight behind you. t: Stand facing a box, step, or sturdy elevated surface roughly 30–45 cm high. t: Lie on your back on a flat surface with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Place your hands loosely behind your head with your elbows wide — do not interlace your fingers. | Lift your feet off the floor so your hips and knees are both at roughly 90 degrees, bringing your shins parallel to the floor. | Exhale and simultaneously draw your right knee toward your left elbow while rotating your left shoulder toward the incoming knee. | Pause briefly at the top when your elbow and knee are as close as your flexibility allows. | Slowly lower your torso and extend your right leg back to the starting position under control. | Repeat the movement on the opposite side, driving your left knee toward your right elbow. | Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions, keeping your lower back in contact with the floor throughout.

t: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders, arms fully extended, and your body in a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your hips level before initiating any movement. | Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso, keeping your body rigid throughout the descent. | Press through your palms to push back up to the top of the plank position. | At the top, simultaneously draw both knees toward your chest by contracting your abs and hip flexors. | Hold the tucked position for one count, keeping your hips from rising too high or sagging. | Extend both legs back to the starting plank position in a controlled manner. | Reset your brace and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

t: Kneel on the floor and place your fists shoulder-width apart, knuckles facing down and wrists straight — the first two knuckles (index and middle finger) should bear the most contact with the floor. | Step your feet back into a high plank position with your body forming a straight line from head to heels; engage your core and glutes. | Rotate your fists so your knuckles point directly downward and your forearms are vertical when viewed from the side; avoid letting your wrists tilt inward or outward. | Inhale and lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at roughly a 45° angle from your torso — not flared out to the sides. | Descend until your chest is just above your fists or lightly touches them, maintaining a rigid plank throughout. | Exhale and press the floor away, driving through your chest and extending your arms back to the starting position. | Lock out your elbows fully at the top without shrugging your shoulders toward your ears. | Complete your reps, then lower your knees to the floor to finish the set safely.

t: Lay an agility ladder flat on the ground in a clear, open area with enough room to run through it completely. | Stand at one end of the ladder with your feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, and weight balanced on the balls of your feet. | Drive your right foot into the first square, followed immediately by your left foot so both feet land inside the same square. | Step your right foot out to the right side of the ladder, then your left foot into the next square, continuing the two-in, two-out pattern down the length of the ladder. | Pump your arms in opposition to your legs — right arm forward when left leg steps, left arm forward when right leg steps — to maintain rhythm and balance. | Keep your eyes forward and your chest upright throughout; resist the urge to look down at the ladder. | Land on the balls of your feet with each contact, minimizing the time each foot spends on the ground. | Walk back to the start after completing the full length of the ladder, rest 30–60 seconds, then repeat for the desired number of sets.

t: Fix one end of the barbell in a landmine attachment or wedge it securely into a corner. t: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing inward — this is your starting position for both the wrong and right demonstrations. | WRONG: Shrug your shoulders upward and swing the dumbbells up using momentum, allowing your torso to lean back and your elbows to drop below your wrists at the top. | WRONG: Raise the dumbbells overhead or past shoulder height, and turn your palms to face upward (like pouring water), which shifts tension away from the side delts. | Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position and reset. | RIGHT: Keep your shoulders down and back, and initiate the movement by driving your elbows outward — not by lifting your hands. | RIGHT: Raise the dumbbells in a smooth, controlled arc until your arms are parallel to the floor (no higher), keeping a slight bend in your elbows and your wrists level with or slightly below your elbows. | RIGHT: Pause briefly at the top, then lower the dumbbells slowly back to your sides over 2–3 seconds, maintaining tension throughout. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, keeping your torso upright and still on every repetition.
