t: Lie on your side on a mat with your legs stacked and your forearm placed flat on the floor, elbow directly beneath your shoulder. | Extend your top arm along your side or rest your hand on your hip to keep your torso from rotating. | Brace your core and press through your forearm to lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from head to feet. | Drive your bottom hip upward, actively contracting the gluteus medius to lift and hold the position — do not let the hip sag. | Keep your feet stacked or stagger the top foot slightly in front for additional balance if needed. | Hold the position for the prescribed duration, breathing steadily, without letting your hips pike upward or drop toward the floor. | Lower your hips back to the mat in a controlled manner, then repeat on the opposite side.

t: Lie on your side on a mat with your bottom knee bent to approximately 90 degrees and your top leg extended straight. | Place your bottom forearm on the mat directly beneath your shoulder, elbow at 90 degrees, forearm pointing forward. | Stack your top hip directly over your bottom hip so your body forms a straight diagonal line from your head to your top foot. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes, then press through your forearm and bent knee to lift your hips off the mat. | Drive your top hip upward until your head, shoulders, hips, and top leg form a straight lateral line — do not let your hips sag or pike. | Keep your top arm resting along your side or place your hand on your hip to help maintain balance. | Hold the position for the prescribed duration, breathing steadily without letting your hips drop. | Lower your hips back to the mat under control to complete one rep or one timed set. | Switch sides and repeat for the same duration or number of reps.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your weight balanced evenly on both feet. | Hinge slightly at the hips and brace your core to adopt a low athletic stance. | Push off your right foot and step quickly to the left, landing softly on the ball of your left foot. | Immediately bring your right foot in to meet the left foot, keeping the movement continuous and controlled. | Without pausing, push off the left foot and step rapidly to the right, landing softly on the ball of your right foot. | Bring your left foot in to meet the right foot to complete one full cycle. | Continue alternating directions at maximum speed for the prescribed duration or number of repetitions. | Stay low throughout — keep your hips down, chest up, and eyes forward the entire time.

t: Stand beside a box or step with your feet hip-width apart, the step to your right side. | Place your right foot fully on top of the step, toes pointing forward and knee aligned over the foot. | Brace your core, keep your torso upright, and press through your right heel to drive your body up onto the step. | Bring your left foot up to meet the right so you are standing fully on top of the step with both feet. | Pause briefly at the top with hips tall and glutes engaged. | Lower your left foot back down to the floor in a controlled manner, hinging slightly at the hip to maintain balance. | Return your right foot to the starting position beside the step to complete one rep. | Complete all reps on the right side before switching so your left foot leads.

t: Stand to the side of a step or box with the surface at roughly knee height, feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides. | Place the foot closest to the box flat on top of it, ensuring your entire foot is supported and your knee tracks over your toes. | Brace your core and shift your weight onto the foot on the box. | Press through the heel of the foot on the box to extend your hip and knee, driving yourself upward until you are standing fully upright on top of the box. | Bring the trailing foot up to meet the working foot so you are standing with both feet on the box. | Lower the trailing foot back down to the floor in a slow, controlled manner, keeping the working leg as the primary support. | Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of reps, then switch sides.

nH: עליית מדרגה צידית עם הרמת ברך
t: Stand to the side of a sturdy box or step, with the step to your right and your feet hip-width apart. | Place your right foot fully on top of the step, ensuring your entire sole is in contact with the surface. | Brace your core and press through your right heel to drive your body upward onto the step. | As you rise, simultaneously drive your left knee up toward your chest until your hip and knee reach roughly 90 degrees. | Hold the top position for a brief pause, keeping your torso upright and your standing leg fully extended. | Lower your left foot back down to the floor in a controlled manner, then step your right foot back to the starting position. | Complete all reps on the right side before switching: place your left foot on the step and repeat the sequence on the opposite side.

nE: Lateral Stretch On Floor Lying Down
t: Lie flat on your back on a comfortable surface with your legs extended and your arms resting by your sides. | Extend both arms overhead and clasp your hands or interlace your fingers, pointing your arms straight above your head along the floor. | Cross your ankles, placing one foot over the other, keeping your legs straight. | Inhale to prepare, then exhale as you arc both your arms and your legs together toward one side, forming a gentle C-curve with your entire body. | Hold the stretched position, breathing steadily, feeling the elongation along the side of your torso, waist, and obliques. | Hold for 20–30 seconds, or as long as is comfortable, without holding your breath. | Slowly return your arms and legs to the center starting position. | Repeat the stretch on the opposite side by arcing arms and legs in the other direction.

nR: Боковые прыжки на ящик со скруткой
nH: קפיצה על קופסה עם פיתול צידי
t: Stand alongside a sturdy box or platform at a height appropriate for your jumping ability, with the box to one side of you, feet hip-width apart and toes pointing straight ahead. | Hinge slightly at the hips and bend your knees to load into an athletic stance, swinging your arms back to prepare for the jump. | Explosively drive through both feet and swing your arms forward and upward, propelling yourself laterally toward the box. | As you leave the ground, rotate your hips and shoulders roughly 90 degrees toward the box so you finish squared up over the landing surface — the twist should happen mid-air, not after landing. | Land softly on top of the box with both feet at the same time, feet flat and square on the surface, knees tracking over your toes, and hips and knees slightly bent to absorb impact. | Stabilize for a brief moment on the box, keeping your chest tall and your weight balanced over the balls of your feet. | Step or hop down from the opposite side of the box, reset your stance, and prepare to jump back in the other direction. | Continue alternating sides for the prescribed number of reps or duration, maintaining consistent jump height and landing control throughout.

t: Begin in a high push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart, arms straight, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips level throughout the movement. | Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows outward at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso. | Press back up to the starting position in one controlled movement, fully extending your arms. | Step your right hand and right foot one step to the right, then follow with your left hand and left foot so you return to shoulder-width stance. | Perform another push-up in the new position. | Continue walking in the same direction for the desired number of reps or distance, then reverse and walk back to the left. | Complete the set by finishing with a final push-up in your ending position.

tHe: התחל במנח שכיבות סמיכה גבוה עם ידיים ברוחב הכתפיים, זרועות ישרות, והגוף בקו ישר מהראש לעקבים. | הדק את הליבה וכווץ את הישבן כדי לשמור על אגן מאוזן לאורך כל התנועה. | Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows outward at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso. | Press back up to the starting position in one controlled movement, fully extending your arms. | Step your right hand and right foot one step to the right, then follow with your left hand and left foot so you return to shoulder-width stance. | Perform another push-up in the new position. | Continue walking in the same direction for the desired number of reps or distance, then reverse and walk back to the left. | סיים את הסט בביצוע פעולת דחיפה אחרונה במצב הסיום.

t: Set up three cones in an L shape: one at the start, one 5 yards ahead, and one 5 yards to the right of the second cone. | Stand at the starting cone in an athletic stance — feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, weight on the balls of your feet. | On your signal, sprint from the start cone to the middle cone as fast as possible. | Plant your outside foot firmly at the middle cone and cut sharply toward the far cone. | Sprint to the far cone, plant, and reverse direction back toward the middle cone. | Cut around the middle cone and sprint back to the starting cone. | Walk back to the start to recover fully, then repeat for the desired number of reps.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, or sit upright on the edge of a sturdy chair or bench. | Hinge at the hips — not the waist — and slowly lean your torso forward, keeping your chest open and your spine long. | Rest your hands lightly on your thighs or let them hang toward the floor for balance. | Continue leaning until you feel a comfortable stretch through the front and sides of your hips; stop before any pain or rounding of the lower back. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing deeply and relaxing into the stretch with each exhale. | Slowly return to the upright starting position by engaging your core and lifting your chest. | Repeat for the desired number of holds, keeping each repetition smooth and controlled.

t: Stand upright next to a wall or sturdy surface, positioning it to your right side for initial support. | Cross your left foot behind your right foot, placing it a comfortable distance to the right so both feet are flat on the floor. | Extend your left arm overhead and place your right hand lightly on the wall or surface for balance. | Shift your hips to the left by pushing them out laterally, creating a gentle arc through your torso. | Lean your upper body to the right simultaneously, so the stretch runs along the entire left outer hip and glute. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and relaxing deeper into the stretch with each exhale. | Return to the starting position slowly, then switch sides by crossing your right foot behind your left and repeating.

t: Stand facing a wall at arm's length and place both hands flat against it at roughly shoulder height. | Step one foot back about 60–90 cm (2–3 feet), keeping the toes of both feet pointing straight forward. | Bend the front knee slightly while keeping the back leg straight. | Press the heel of the back foot firmly into the floor so the entire sole maintains contact with the ground. | Lean your body forward toward the wall by bending the front knee further, shifting your weight gently onto your hands. | Keep your back leg straight and your back heel grounded — do not allow it to rise. | Hold the stretched position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the calf and Achilles tendon to relax into the stretch. | Release, switch legs, and repeat on the other side. | Perform 2–3 holds per leg as part of a warm-up or cool-down routine.

t: Stand in a boxing stance with your left foot slightly forward, feet roughly shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and weight balanced evenly on the balls of your feet. | Raise your hands to guard position — fists near your cheekbones, elbows tucked close to your ribcage. | Shift your weight slightly onto your left foot and dip your left shoulder a few inches downward to load the punch. | Drive explosively off your left foot while rotating your hips and torso upward and to the right. | Simultaneously thrust your left fist in a tight upward arc — palm facing you — aiming to strike at chin height in front of you. | Keep your right hand at guard throughout the motion to protect your head. | Snap your left fist back to guard position immediately after the punch lands, using the same rotational path in reverse. | Reset your stance and repeat for the desired number of repetitions or rounds.

t: Set the gymnastic rings at a height that allows you to hang with your arms fully extended while your feet can still reach the floor — roughly waist to chest height works for most people. | Grip each ring with an overhand grip, hands roughly shoulder-width apart, and let your body hang at an angle with heels on the floor and legs extended in front of you. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your body in a straight line from heels to shoulders throughout the movement. | Initiate the pull by depressing your shoulder blades and driving your elbows down and back toward your hips. | Press lightly through your heels to assist the pull — use only as much leg drive as needed to complete the rep with good form. | Continue pulling until your chest approaches the rings and your elbows are fully bent and close to your sides. | Pause briefly at the top, squeezing the back muscles. | Lower yourself in a controlled manner back to the fully extended start position, resisting the descent rather than dropping. | Reset your brace and repeat for the target number of repetitions.

t: Place a flat bench beside you and lie on your side on the floor, positioning your feet and lower legs on top of the bench with your hip still resting on the floor. | Stack your feet on top of each other and rest your lower elbow directly beneath your shoulder, forearm flat on the floor and perpendicular to your torso. | Place your top hand on your hip or extend it toward the ceiling for balance. | Brace your core and squeeze your obliques, then drive your hip off the floor until your body forms a rigid straight line from head to feet. | Hold your neck in a neutral position — do not crane it upward or let it drop toward the floor. | Keep your hips fully extended and avoid letting them sag or pike upward during the hold. | Breathe steadily throughout the hold; do not hold your breath. | Hold the bridge position for the target duration (e.g., 20–45 seconds), then lower your hip under control. | Complete all reps or time on one side before switching to the opposite side.

t: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your arms at your sides, palms facing down for support. | Place both heels on top of a stability ball, keeping your legs straight and your feet hip-width apart. | Press your heels into the ball and lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to heels. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to maintain a rigid, elevated hip position throughout the set. | Curl the ball toward your glutes by bending both knees, rolling the ball in with your heels while keeping your hips high. | Pause briefly when your heels are directly under your knees and your shins are vertical, keeping your hips elevated. | Slowly extend your legs to roll the ball back out to the starting position, maintaining hip elevation throughout. | Complete all reps, then lower your hips to the floor in a controlled manner.

t: Sit upright on the stability ball with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and the ball positioned beneath your mid-to-lower back when you recline. | Walk your feet forward and lean back until your lower back and mid-back rest on the ball, with your hips slightly lower than your knees and your head and shoulders unsupported. | Place your hands lightly behind your head or cross them over your chest, keeping your elbows wide. | Engage your core and press your lower back gently into the ball to establish a stable starting position. | Exhale and perform a crunch by lifting your head, neck, and shoulder blades off the ball while simultaneously extending one leg straight out at hip height, pointing your toes forward. | Hold the top position for one count, feeling the contraction in your rectus abdominis and the tension in the extended leg's quadriceps. | Inhale and slowly lower your upper body back onto the ball while bending the knee and returning your foot to the floor in a controlled manner. | Alternate legs with each repetition, or complete all reps on one side before switching, depending on the variation prescribed. | Maintain a neutral neck throughout — avoid pulling on your head — and keep the ball as still as possible to preserve core tension.

t: Start in a high or forearm plank position with your hands (or forearms) directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Place your feet hip-width apart and press through the balls of both feet to create a stable base. | Brace your core by drawing your navel gently toward your spine, squeeze your glutes, and ensure your hips are level — neither sagging nor piked. | Inhale to prepare, then on an exhale lift your right leg a few inches off the floor, keeping it straight and your foot flexed. | Hold the extended position for 2–3 seconds while maintaining a neutral spine and level hips. | Lower your right foot back to the floor with control, re-establish your brace, then repeat on the left side. | Continue alternating legs for the prescribed number of reps or time, breathing steadily throughout. | To finish, lower both feet to the floor and rest in a kneeling or child's pose position.

t: Find a firm, flat surface such as a treatment table or exercise mat and lie face-up with your legs fully extended. | Slide both heels together so your legs are parallel and touching, with your toes pointing toward the ceiling. | Relax your hips, legs, and lower back completely — avoid actively pulling or pushing either leg. | Flex your hips and knees to bring both knees up to your chest, hugging them briefly to reset any pelvic tilt. | Slowly lower both legs back to a fully extended position, letting them settle naturally without adjusting. | Look down at your ankles from above, or have a partner observe at foot level to compare the position of the medial malleoli (inner ankle bones). | Note any visible difference between the height or position of the two ankles — a discrepancy may suggest a functional or structural leg length difference. | Repeat the reset-and-lower sequence two to three times to confirm the finding is consistent.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs straight and your arms at your sides, palms pressing lightly into the floor. | Curl your head and shoulder blades off the mat into a partial crunch position and hold them there for the entire set — do not rest your head down between reps. | Press your lower back into the mat by engaging your core before you begin moving your legs. | Keeping both legs straight and together, exhale and raise them until they are perpendicular to the floor at approximately 90 degrees. | At the top of the leg raise, contract your lower abdominals and curl your hips off the mat by tilting your pelvis posteriorly, lifting your tailbone 2–4 inches from the floor. | Hold the hip lift for one count, ensuring the effort comes from your abs rather than momentum. | Slowly reverse the movement: lower your hips back to the mat first, then begin descending your legs in a controlled manner. | Lower your legs until they are just above the floor without letting them touch, keeping tension in the core throughout. | Inhale as you lower your legs and prepare for the next repetition, maintaining the head-up position the entire time.

t: Place your mat perpendicular to a clear section of wall so that the short edge nearly touches the baseboard. | Sit sideways with one hip touching the wall, then swing your legs up the wall as you lower your torso onto the mat so you end up lying on your back with your legs extended vertically. | Scoot your hips as close to the wall as is comfortable, or allow a small gap if that feels better for your lower back. | Straighten your legs and let them rest passively against the wall, feet relaxed and hip-width apart. | Rest your arms on the floor beside you, palms facing up, and allow your shoulders and upper back to fully release into the mat. | Close your eyes, breathe slowly and evenly, and let your whole body become heavy against the floor. | Hold the position for 2–10 minutes, adjusting your distance from the wall if you feel any discomfort in the hamstrings or lower back. | To exit, bend your knees and bring them toward your chest, then roll gently onto one side and pause before pressing yourself up to seated.

t: Adjust the machine so the ankle pad sits securely just above your feet when your legs are bent and your back is flat on the pad. | Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet hooked under the ankle roller, hands either crossed on your chest or holding the handles if provided. | Press your lower back into the pad and find a neutral starting position with your head in line with your spine. | Exhale and curl your upper torso upward by contracting your rectus abdominis, shortening the distance between your ribcage and hips. | Continue curling until your shoulder blades are fully off the pad and your abs are fully contracted — do not jerk or use momentum. | Hold the top position for a brief pause to maximise tension on the abdominals. | Inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position under control, allowing the abs to lengthen without fully relaxing the tension. | Repeat for the target number of reps, keeping each repetition smooth and deliberate.

t: Adjust the seat height so the handles are at or just below shoulder level when you are seated upright. | Sit with your back flat against the pad, chest up, and feet planted firmly on the floor. | Grip the handles with a neutral (palms facing each other) hammer grip, wrapping your thumbs fully around each handle. | Brace your core and retract your shoulder blades lightly against the pad before initiating the press. | Press the handles upward in a smooth arc until your arms are nearly fully extended, without locking your elbows at the top. | Pause briefly at the top, keeping tension on the deltoids. | Lower the handles under control back to the starting position, allowing a slight stretch in the shoulders without letting the weight stack touch down between reps. | Complete the desired number of reps, then guide the handles back to the rest position before releasing your grip.

t: Adjust the machine seat and pad position so the thigh pads rest just above your knees when you are seated upright. | Sit tall with your back against the pad, feet flat on the footrests, and thighs together at the starting position. | Grip the handles lightly to stabilize your torso without pulling yourself out of an upright position. | Brace your core and keep your lower back in contact with the seat back throughout the set. | Push both thighs outward against the pads in a controlled arc, spreading your legs as wide as the machine allows. | Pause briefly at the end range and squeeze the outer hips. | Slowly return both thighs toward each other under control, stopping just before the pads touch so tension remains on the abductors. | Complete your reps, then release the weight stack fully before standing.

t: Adjust the machine's seat height so your hips are level and your feet rest flat on the foot platforms with your knees bent at roughly 90°. | Set the leg pads so they sit against the inner sides of your knees or lower thighs, not directly on your knee joints. | Position the starting angle so your legs are spread apart at a comfortable range — typically 30–45° from center — without overstretching your inner thighs. | Sit upright with your back fully against the seat pad and grip the side handles lightly for stability. | Exhale and press your legs together by squeezing the hip adductors, moving the pads inward in a smooth, controlled arc. | Bring your legs to the midline or until the pads nearly meet, pausing briefly at peak contraction. | Inhale and slowly allow your legs to return to the starting position, resisting the machine's weight on the way back. | Complete all reps with control before returning the load to rest.

t: Adjust the seat so that when your feet are on the platform, your knees form approximately a 90-degree angle without your lower back lifting off the pad. | Sit down and place your feet flat on the platform at roughly hip-width apart, with toes pointing slightly outward. | Grip the handles at the sides of the seat to brace your torso and keep your back against the pad throughout the movement. | Disengage the safety handles or locks and take control of the weight. | Press the platform away by extending your knees and hips simultaneously, driving through the full surface of both feet. | Stop just short of locking your knees out at the top of the movement, keeping a slight bend to maintain tension on the muscles. | Slowly lower the platform back toward the starting position under control, allowing your knees to bend until they return to approximately 90 degrees. | Complete all reps, then re-engage the safety locks before releasing your grip.

t: Sit in the leverage leg press machine and adjust the seat so your working knee forms roughly a 90-degree angle when the footplate is at the starting position. | Place one foot in the center of the footplate at approximately shoulder width, with toes pointed slightly outward. | Keep the opposite foot flat on the floor or resting on the machine frame so it does not assist the movement. | Grip the handles on the sides of the seat to stabilize your torso. | Disengage the safety locks and lower the footplate in a controlled manner, allowing your knee to bend until your thigh approaches parallel to the seat or slightly beyond. | Keep your working knee tracking in line with your toes throughout the descent — do not let it drift inward or outward. | Press through your heel and mid-foot to drive the footplate back to the starting position, fully extending your knee without snapping it into a locked position. | Complete all repetitions on one leg, re-engage the safety locks, then switch feet and repeat on the other side.

t: Adjust the seat height so that the machine's pivot point aligns with your spine at shoulder level when seated upright. | Sit down and secure your feet flat on the footrest or floor to anchor your lower body throughout the movement. | Grasp the handles or pad in front of you with both hands, keeping your elbows slightly bent and your chest tall. | Brace your core and sit upright with a neutral spine — avoid leaning forward or rounding your lower back. | Exhale and rotate your torso to one side in a slow, controlled arc, turning only as far as comfortable range allows without forcing the movement. | Pause briefly at the end of the range of motion to feel the obliques contract on the working side. | Inhale and reverse the rotation in a controlled manner back to the starting position — do not let the resistance snap you back. | Complete all reps on one side, then adjust the machine or switch grip to work the opposite side, or alternate sides per rep depending on machine design. | After completing your set, let the machine return to its resting position and release your grip before standing.

t: Attach a rope handle to the lever machine's overhead pulley and adjust the knee pad so your thighs are secured snugly under it when seated. | Sit facing the machine, grip the rope with both hands using a neutral (palms-facing) grip, and extend your arms fully overhead. | Lean back slightly at the torso — around 10–15 degrees — and brace your core to stabilize your spine throughout the set. | Initiate the pull by depressing and retracting your shoulder blades, pulling them down and back before your elbows begin to bend. | Drive your elbows down and back toward your hips, pulling the rope to chin level or just below while keeping the rope ends spread apart. | Squeeze your lats hard at the bottom of the movement and hold for one second. | Reverse the motion under control, allowing your arms to extend fully overhead and your shoulder blades to protract slightly to achieve a full lat stretch at the top. | Complete all reps without releasing the stretch or allowing momentum to drive the movement.

t: Start in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line. | Step your right foot forward and place it on the outside of your right hand, so your foot is flat on the floor and your knee is stacked directly above your ankle. | Lower your left knee to the mat and let the top of your left foot rest on the ground behind you. | Press your hands into the mat and lengthen your spine, avoiding rounding through the upper back. | On an exhale, sink your hips forward and down toward the floor, deepening the stretch in the front hip and groin. | Hold the position for 30–60 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing your hips to relax a little further with each exhale. | To deepen the stretch, lower onto your forearms if your flexibility allows, keeping your spine long and your hips level. | Press back through your hands to return to high plank and repeat on the opposite side by stepping your left foot forward.

t: Lie face down on a mat with your legs extended straight behind you, feet together or hip-width apart, and your arms resting alongside your body with palms facing down. | Rest your forehead lightly on the mat and take a slow breath in to prepare. | On an exhale, engage your core gently and press your pubic bone into the mat to stabilize your pelvis. | As you inhale, simultaneously lift your head, chest, and arms off the mat, reaching your fingertips back toward your feet. | Squeeze your glutes and lift your legs off the mat, keeping them straight and internally rotated so your big toes point toward each other. | Hold the top position for 3–5 breaths, keeping your gaze directed slightly downward to keep the neck long. | On an exhale, slowly lower your chest, arms, and legs back to the mat with control. | Rest briefly with your cheek to one side before repeating.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Extend both arms straight overhead, keeping them close to your ears and parallel to the floor — this is your starting position. | Brace your core by drawing your navel gently toward your spine. | Exhale and slowly curl your head, neck, and shoulder blades off the mat, reaching your extended arms forward and upward toward your knees. | Continue the upward curl until your shoulder blades are fully lifted off the mat, pausing briefly at the top of the movement. | Inhale and slowly lower yourself back to the starting position under control, keeping your arms extended throughout. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions without letting momentum take over between reps.

t: Stand tall with your feet together and your core lightly braced. | Step one foot far forward — roughly twice your normal stride length — so that your front knee ends up directly over your ankle. | Lower your back knee to the floor in a controlled descent, placing it gently on the mat or ground. | Sink your hips down and forward until you feel a stretch along the front of the back hip and inner thigh. | Keep your front shin vertical and your torso upright, hands resting on your front thigh or the floor for balance. | Hold the low position for the desired duration, breathing steadily and relaxing deeper into the stretch with each exhale. | Press through your front foot to rise, step back to the start, and repeat on the opposite side.

t: Set the decline bench or leverage machine to a moderate angle (30–45 degrees) and secure your feet under the footpads. | Lie back on the bench and extend both arms straight overhead, keeping them in line with your ears throughout the set. | Brace your core and press your lower back gently into the pad to establish a stable starting position. | Exhale and curl your torso upward, leading with your chest rather than your chin, until your torso is roughly perpendicular to the floor. | Keep your arms extended overhead and parallel to the floor as you reach the top — do not let them swing forward to generate momentum. | Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your abs. | Inhale and lower your torso under control back to the starting position, resisting the pull of gravity rather than dropping freely. | Reset your core brace at the bottom before beginning the next repetition.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you. t: Lie face-down on a mat with your hands placed flat on the floor just outside your shoulders, elbows bent. | Press your palms into the floor and slowly begin to extend your elbows, lifting your chest and upper abdomen off the mat. | Keep your hips and pelvis in contact with the floor — the stretch comes from spinal extension, not from lifting your hips. | Raise your torso to the height that produces a comfortable stretch in your lower abdominals and front of the waist — this may be a low prop-on-forearms position or a higher cobra-style extension. | Hold your shoulder blades gently together and down; do not shrug toward your ears. | Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing your lower trunk to soften with each exhale. | Lower yourself back to the floor with control and rest before repeating.

t: Stand with your feet together and arms at your sides. | Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to lower into a squat position, keeping your chest up and back flat. | Step your right foot out to the side while simultaneously raising both arms out and overhead. | Step your left foot out to the opposite side so both feet are shoulder-width apart, arms fully raised. | Step your right foot back in toward center while lowering your arms back to your sides. | Step your left foot in to meet the right, returning to the starting squat stance. | Continue alternating the stepping pattern at a steady, controlled pace. | Complete the desired number of reps or time interval, then stand to rest.

t: Begin in a standing position or transition from a high plank — step your right foot forward between your hands, placing it flat on the floor. | Lower your left knee gently to the floor directly behind your left hip, with the top of your left foot resting on the mat. | Ensure your right knee is directly above your right ankle so your front shin is vertical. | Lift your torso upright and place your hands on your right thigh or raise them overhead with palms facing each other. | Lengthen your spine, relax your shoulders, and tilt your pelvis slightly forward and down to deepen the stretch in the left hip flexor. | Hold for 20–60 seconds, breathing steadily and sinking a little deeper with each exhale. | Press through your front foot to rise back to standing or step back to plank, then repeat on the opposite side.

t: Begin in a tabletop position on all fours, with your hands directly under your shoulders and knees under your hips. | Step your right foot forward between your hands, placing it flat on the floor with your right knee directly above your right ankle. | Lower your left knee to the floor and slide it back until you feel a comfortable stretch along the front of your left thigh and hip. | Untuck your left toes and rest the top of your left foot on the floor. | Press through your right heel and engage your core to keep your hips level and square to the front. | On an inhale, sweep both arms overhead with palms facing each other, lengthening through your spine. | Draw your tailbone down toward the floor and lift your chest, keeping your gaze forward or slightly upward. | Hold the pose for 5 to 10 breaths, allowing your hips to sink deeper with each exhale. | To release, lower your hands to the floor, step your right foot back, and repeat on the opposite side.

t: Stand directly below the rope so it hangs vertically in front of you, then reach up and grip it as high as you can with both hands, thumbs wrapped fully around it. | From a dead hang, brace your core hard and raise both straight legs until they are parallel to the floor, forming the L-sit position. t: Stand tall with your feet together and your core lightly braced. | Step your right foot forward approximately two to three feet, planting it flat on the floor. | Lower your body until your right thigh is roughly parallel to the floor and your right knee is directly above your right ankle. | Allow your left knee to descend and rest gently on the floor, with the top of your left foot flat or toes tucked under as comfortable. | Sink your hips downward and forward to deepen the stretch through the left hip flexor, quadriceps, and glutes. | Keep your torso upright and your hands resting on your right thigh or on the floor beside your front foot for balance. | Hold the position for 20 to 60 seconds, breathing deeply and relaxing further into the stretch with each exhale. | Press through your right foot to rise back to standing, then switch sides and repeat. | Perform two to three holds per side as part of a warm-up or cool-down routine.

t: Lie flat on your back on a comfortable surface with your legs extended and arms resting at your sides. | Bend both knees and plant your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Slowly draw both knees toward your chest by lifting your feet off the floor. | Wrap your hands around your shins or the backs of your thighs to gently pull your knees closer to your torso. | Keep your head and shoulders relaxed against the floor throughout the movement. | Take a slow, deep breath in through your nose, then exhale fully through your mouth as you gently deepen the pull. | Hold the stretched position for 20–30 seconds, continuing to breathe slowly and steadily. | On an exhale, carefully lower your feet back to the floor and allow your legs to extend. | Rest for a moment, then repeat for 2–3 holds as needed.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat or firm surface with your legs straight and arms resting at your sides. | Position yourself so that the top of your head is near the edge of a mat or slightly off the edge of a low, stable surface if you want a deeper passive stretch — otherwise remain fully supported. | Allow your head to relax gently backward toward the floor, letting gravity guide a slow extension of the cervical spine. | Keep your shoulders flat and your upper back in contact with the surface — do not let them rise or round. | Breathe steadily and allow the front of your neck and throat to lengthen with each exhale, easing further into the stretch without forcing it. | Hold the extended position for 20 to 30 seconds while maintaining relaxed breathing. | To release, gently engage your core and use your hands to support your head as you slowly return your neck to a neutral position. | Rest briefly in neutral, then repeat for the desired number of sets.

nE: Lying Pelvic Floor Relaxation and Deep Breathing
nR: Расслабление тазового дна и глубокое дыхание лёжа
nH: הרפיית רצפת אגן ונשימה עמוקה בשכיבה
t: Lie on your back on a firm, flat surface with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Let your arms rest at your sides with your palms facing up. | Allow your lower back to settle into its natural position — do not flatten it forcefully or exaggerate the arch. | Close your mouth and inhale slowly through your nose for a count of four, directing the breath down into your belly and lower ribs rather than raising your chest. | As you inhale, consciously release and soften the pelvic floor — imagine the muscles in your pelvis gently expanding or dropping downward toward the floor. | Pause briefly at the top of the inhale for one to two counts, keeping the pelvic floor relaxed. | Exhale slowly through your mouth or nose for a count of six, allowing the pelvic floor to gently lift and recoil naturally without forceful contraction. | Keep your glutes, inner thighs, and abdomen soft throughout — avoid gripping or bracing any surrounding muscles. | Continue for six to ten breath cycles, maintaining a slow and steady rhythm. | When finished, bring your knees to your chest briefly, then roll to one side before sitting up.

t: Lie face-down on a mat with your legs straight and your forehead resting lightly on the floor or a folded towel. | Extend both arms in front of you at roughly 30–45° out from your torso to form the shape of the letter A, with your palms facing inward and thumbs pointing up toward the ceiling. | Relax your neck so it stays in a neutral line with your spine — do not crane your head up. | Take a breath in, then exhale and draw your shoulder blades down and together, engaging your lower trapezius before your arms move. | Keeping your thumbs pointing up, lift both arms off the floor by squeezing through the mid and lower back rather than shrugging your shoulders. | Raise your arms until they are a few inches off the floor and you feel full contraction in your mid-back, then hold for 1–2 seconds. | Lower your arms back to the floor under control, resisting the urge to let them drop. | Reset your shoulder blades and repeat for the desired number of reps.

t: Lie face-down on the floor with your forehead resting lightly on the ground and your legs extended straight behind you. | Position your arms out to the sides with your elbows bent to roughly 90° and your thumbs pointing toward the ceiling, so your body forms a W when viewed from above. | Keep your neck neutral — do not crane it upward or press your chin into the floor. | Brace your core lightly and squeeze your glutes to stabilize your lower body throughout the movement. | On an exhale, lift your hands, forearms, and upper arms off the floor by driving your elbows down and back and pulling your shoulder blades together and toward your hips. | Hold the top position for one to two seconds, feeling the squeeze across your upper back and between your shoulder blades. | Lower your arms back to the floor with control, letting them fully relax before the next rep. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, maintaining the W shape throughout and avoiding any shrugging of the shoulders toward your ears.

nH: מעבר W ל-T בשכיבה על הבטן
t: Lie face down on a mat with your legs straight and forehead resting lightly on the floor or hovering just above it. | Lift your chest slightly off the floor to engage your back muscles and establish a neutral spine throughout the movement. | Begin in the W position: bend your elbows to roughly 90 degrees, pull them back toward your hips, and squeeze your shoulder blades together and down. Your arms should resemble the letter W. | Hold the W for one second, focusing on the contraction in your mid-back and lower traps. | Slowly transition to the T position by straightening your arms and extending them out to your sides at shoulder height, thumbs pointing toward the ceiling. | Hold the T for one second, maintaining the squeeze between your shoulder blades and keeping your arms level with your torso. | Exhale during the transition from W to T; inhale as you return from T back to W. | Move back to the W position with control, completing one full rep. | Complete all reps, then lower your chest fully to the floor to rest between sets.

nH: מעבר W ל-Y בשכיבה על הבטן
t: Lie face down on a flat surface with your forehead resting on the floor and legs extended straight behind you. | Position your arms in the W shape: raise your upper arms out to the sides at roughly 90 degrees from your torso, bend your elbows to 90 degrees, and point your thumbs toward the ceiling. | Brace your core lightly and keep your neck in a neutral position — do not lift your head. | Squeeze your shoulder blades together and down, initiating the movement from your mid-back rather than your arms. | Maintaining the squeeze, slowly sweep your arms forward and upward, straightening them as you transition into the Y shape: arms fully extended overhead at a 30–45 degree angle from your midline, thumbs still pointing up. | Hold the Y position for one to two seconds, feeling the tension across your upper back. | Slowly reverse the motion, bending your elbows and drawing your upper arms back to the W position with control. | Relax the shoulder blades slightly at the bottom of the W before beginning the next repetition. | Complete all reps with deliberate, smooth movement — never rush the transition between positions.

t: Lie face-down on the floor with your legs extended and your forehead resting lightly on a mat or towel. | Extend both arms overhead at roughly a 30–45 degree angle from your midline to form a Y shape, with thumbs pointing toward the ceiling. | Engage your core and gently draw your shoulder blades down and together before you lift. | On an exhale, raise both arms a few inches off the floor by squeezing the lower trapezius and rear shoulder muscles — keep your neck neutral. | Hold the top position for one to two seconds, feeling the contraction in your upper back and posterior shoulders. | Lower your arms slowly back to the floor under control. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining consistent tension throughout the set.

t: Lie face-down on a flat bench or firm surface with your chest at or near the edge so your arms can hang freely toward the floor. | Let both arms hang straight down from your shoulders, palms facing each other, with a soft bend at the elbows. | Retract and depress your shoulder blades slightly — pull them together and down — before you begin each set. | Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, raise both arms out to your sides in a wide arc until they are level with your torso or just above. | Lead the movement from your elbows and upper arms rather than your hands, and keep your wrists neutral throughout. | Pause briefly at the top with your arms parallel to the floor, squeezing the back of your shoulders. | Lower your arms slowly under control back to the starting position over two to three seconds. | Repeat for the target number of reps, maintaining the same shoulder-blade position on every repetition.

nH: כפיפות להפעלת שריר ישר בטני בשכיבה
t: Lie on your back on a flat surface with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Place your hands lightly behind your head, fingertips touching the skull — do not interlace your fingers or pull on your neck. | Press your lower back gently into the floor to establish a neutral spine; this is your starting position. | Take a breath in, then as you exhale, draw your navel lightly toward your spine to pre-activate the abdominals. | Curl your head, neck, and shoulder blades a few centimetres off the floor by shortening the distance between your ribs and your pelvis — think of rolling up rather than reaching forward. | At the top of the movement, pause for one to two seconds and consciously squeeze the rectus abdominis before any tension fades. | Inhale as you slowly lower your shoulder blades back to the floor under control, taking about two to three seconds on the way down. | Reset your lower back contact with the floor between reps if needed, then repeat for the target number of repetitions.
tRu: Лягте на спину на ровную поверхность, согните колени и поставьте стопы на пол на ширине бёдер. | Place your hands lightly behind your head, fingertips touching the skull — do not interlace your fingers or pull on your neck. | Press your lower back gently into the floor to establish a neutral spine; this is your starting position. | Take a breath in, then as you exhale, draw your navel lightly toward your spine to pre-activate the abdominals. | Поднимите голову, шею и лопатки на несколько сантиметров от пола, уменьшая расстояние между ребрами и тазом — представьте, что вы сворачиваетесь, а не тянетесь вперед. | В верхней точке движения сделайте паузу на одну-две секунды и осознанно сожмите прямую мышцу живота, пока напряжение не ушло. | Inhale as you slowly lower your shoulder blades back to the floor under control, taking about two to three seconds on the way down. | Reset your lower back contact with the floor between reps if needed, then repeat for the target number of repetitions.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and your arms resting at your sides. Allow your head to rest fully supported on the surface. | Establish a neutral spine by making sure your lower back has a slight natural arch and your chin is gently tucked — neck packed — rather than jutting forward. | Take a slow breath in to prepare. On the exhale, gently tilt your head toward your right shoulder in a pure lateral flexion movement, keeping your face pointing straight up at the ceiling. | Move only 5–10 degrees — the range should be small and deliberate. You should feel a mild activation along the left side of your neck, where the scalenes are lengthening and engaging against gravity. | Optional: place your right hand lightly against your right temple and press your head into your hand with about 20–30% effort to add gentle isometric resistance. Your head should not actually move when resistance is applied. | Hold the position for 2–3 seconds while breathing normally. Do not hold your breath. | Slowly return your head to the center starting position and pause for a moment before switching sides. | Repeat the lateral tilt toward your left shoulder, applying the same controlled range and optional hand resistance on the left side. | Complete 8–12 repetitions per side for 2–3 sets, resting 30–60 seconds between sets.

t: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your legs extended and your hands placed lightly behind your head, elbows wide. | Lift both legs a few inches off the floor and brace your core so your lower back presses firmly into the ground. | Curl your head, neck, and upper shoulders off the floor into a crunch position and hold it throughout the set. | Raise your right leg to roughly 45 degrees while keeping your left leg low and hovering just above the floor. | In one controlled motion, switch the leg positions — lower the right leg and raise the left — in a smooth scissor-like alternating kick. | Continue alternating legs in a steady rhythm, keeping the crunch held constant so the rectus abdominis stays under tension the entire time. | Breathe steadily throughout — exhale as you switch legs rather than holding your breath. | After completing your target number of reps or time, lower both legs and your upper body to the floor together with control.
tRu: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your legs extended and your hands placed lightly behind your head, elbows wide. | Lift both legs a few inches off the floor and brace your core so your lower back presses firmly into the ground. | Поднимите голову, плечи и верхнюю часть спины с пола в положение скручивания и удерживайте его на протяжении всего подхода. | Raise your right leg to roughly 45 degrees while keeping your left leg low and hovering just above the floor. | In one controlled motion, switch the leg positions — lower the right leg and raise the left — in a smooth scissor-like alternating kick. | Продолжайте попеременно менять ногами в устойчивом ритме, удерживая скручивание, чтобы прямые мышцы живота оставались в напряжении всё время. | Дышите ровно на протяжении всего выдоха — выдыхайте, когда меняете ноги, а не задерживайте дыхание. | Выполнив целевое количество повторов или время, вместе подконтрольно опустите обе ноги и верх тела на пол.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs fully extended and your arms at your sides, palms facing down. | Press your lower back firmly into the mat by bracing your core and tilting your pelvis slightly posteriorly. | Lift both legs a few inches off the floor, keeping them straight, so your heels hover above the mat. | Raise your right leg to about 45 degrees while simultaneously lowering your left leg to just above the floor. | Reverse the motion smoothly, raising your left leg while lowering your right, creating a controlled scissoring pattern. | Continue alternating legs without letting either heel touch the ground throughout the set. | Keep your toes pointed and your knees as straight as possible on every rep. | Exhale steadily as you scissor; avoid holding your breath. | Lower both legs to the floor at the same time to finish the set.
tRu: Лягте ровно на спину на коврик, полностью выпрямив ноги и положив руки вдоль тела ладонями вниз. | Press your lower back firmly into the mat by bracing your core and tilting your pelvis slightly posteriorly. | Lift both legs a few inches off the floor, keeping them straight, so your heels hover above the mat. | Raise your right leg to about 45 degrees while simultaneously lowering your left leg to just above the floor. | Reverse the motion smoothly, raising your left leg while lowering your right, creating a controlled scissoring pattern. | Продолжайте попеременно менять ногами, не давая ни одной пятке касаться пола на протяжении всего подхода. | Keep your toes pointed and your knees as straight as possible on every rep. | Exhale steadily as you scissor; avoid holding your breath. | Lower both legs to the floor at the same time to finish the set.
tHe: שכב שטוח על הגב על מזרן עם רגליים ישרות לגמרי וידיים לצדי הגוף, כפות הידיים פונות מטה. | Press your lower back firmly into the mat by bracing your core and tilting your pelvis slightly posteriorly. | Lift both legs a few inches off the floor, keeping them straight, so your heels hover above the mat. | Raise your right leg to about 45 degrees while simultaneously lowering your left leg to just above the floor. | Reverse the motion smoothly, raising your left leg while lowering your right, creating a controlled scissoring pattern. | Continue alternating legs without letting either heel touch the ground throughout the set. | Keep your toes pointed and your knees as straight as possible on every rep. | Exhale steadily as you scissor; avoid holding your breath. | Lower both legs to the floor at the same time to finish the set.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs fully extended and your arms at your sides, palms facing down. | Brace your core and press your lower back firmly into the mat — maintain this contact throughout the set. | Lift both legs to roughly 6–12 inches off the floor, keeping them straight and toes pointed. | Open your legs slightly apart, then sweep the right leg over the left so they cross at mid-shin level. | Open your legs apart again, then sweep the left leg over the right to complete one full repetition. | Continue alternating the crossing leg in a controlled, fluid scissoring motion, breathing steadily — exhale on each cross. | Keep the movement deliberate and even; avoid letting momentum drive the legs rather than muscular control. | After completing the target number of repetitions, lower both legs slowly to the mat rather than dropping them.
tRu: Лягте ровно на спину на коврик, полностью выпрямив ноги и положив руки вдоль тела ладонями вниз. | Напрягите корпус и плотно прижмите поясницу к коврику — сохраняйте этот контакт в течение всего подхода. | Lift both legs to roughly 6–12 inches off the floor, keeping them straight and toes pointed. | Open your legs slightly apart, then sweep the right leg over the left so they cross at mid-shin level. | Open your legs apart again, then sweep the left leg over the right to complete one full repetition. | Продолжайте поочередно выполнять перекрестное движение ногами в плавном, контролируемом ритме, дыша ровно — выдыхая на каждом перекрестном движении. | Keep the movement deliberate and even; avoid letting momentum drive the legs rather than muscular control. | Выполнив целевое количество повторений, медленно опустите обе ноги на коврик, а не бросайте их.

tHe: Lie on your back on a firm, flat surface with your legs extended and your arms resting at your sides. | Extend both arms out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing up, forming a T-shape with your body. | כופף את ברך ימין והנח את כף רגל ימין שטוחה על הרצפה קרוב לישבן. | Keeping your right shoulder pressed into the floor, slowly rotate your upper body to the right by reaching your right arm across your chest and letting your torso follow. | תן ליד שמאל להישאר ישרה ותן למבט לעקוב אחר היד המסתובבת כדי להעמיק את המתיחה דרך הכתף והחזה. | Hold the end position for 20–30 seconds, breathing deeply to let the chest and waist relax further into the rotation. | Slowly return your torso and arm to the starting T-position. | Repeat on the opposite side by bending the left knee and rotating to the left. | בצע 2–3 החזקות בכל צד, תוך החלפה בין ימין ושמאל.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat or firm surface with your legs together and arms resting at your sides. | Take a slow breath in to prepare and lengthen your spine against the floor. | On the exhale, raise both arms overhead and extend them as far as possible along the floor behind you. | Simultaneously point your toes away from you, stretching through the front of your ankles and the length of both legs. | Reach in both directions at once — fingers pulling away from toes — to create maximal length through the entire body. | Hold the extended position for 20–30 seconds while breathing steadily and deepening the stretch with each exhale. | Gently release the tension, return your arms to your sides, and flex your feet back to neutral. | Repeat for 2–3 rounds as needed.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides. | Lift your right knee until your thigh is roughly parallel to the floor, or as high as is comfortable. | Lower your right foot back to the floor with control. | Immediately lift your left knee to the same height. | Swing your arms in opposition — right arm forward as left knee rises, left arm forward as right knee rises — to mimic natural walking mechanics. | Keep your torso upright and your core lightly engaged throughout. | Continue alternating legs at a steady, comfortable pace for the desired duration.

t: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, core braced, and knees slightly soft. | Hold a medicine ball with both hands directly in front of your chest. | Raise the ball up and begin guiding it in a wide, smooth arc around one side of your head, keeping your arms extended but not locked. | Continue the circular path so the ball travels around the back of your head, staying as close to your head as is comfortable without losing control. | Complete the arc on the opposite side and return the ball to the starting position in front of your chest — that is one full rotation. | Perform all reps in one direction, then reverse the direction for the same number of reps. | Keep your head still and your gaze forward throughout; let your arms and shoulders do the work.

nH: זריקות כדור כוח לאחור מעל הראש
t: Set up in an open area with nothing and no one behind you — the ball travels backward, out of your line of sight, and lands well past where you are standing. | Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball with both hands in front of your hips. | Hinge at the hips, pushing them back and bending slightly at the knees, lowering the ball toward the ground between your legs. | Keep your chest up, back flat, and core braced throughout the setup. | Explosively extend your hips and knees, driving your body upward as if jumping. | Allow the momentum from your hip drive to carry the ball upward and backward, releasing it overhead behind you at the peak of the movement. | Follow through fully with your arms, reaching overhead as the ball leaves your hands. | Land softly with a slight bend in the knees, then retrieve the ball and reset for the next repetition.

t: Stand upright holding a medicine ball with both hands, feet shoulder-width apart, with a wall or open space behind you. | Hinge at the hips and push them back, allowing a slight bend in the knees, and swing the ball down between your legs. | Load your hamstrings and glutes by sitting into the hip hinge — keep your chest up and spine neutral throughout. | Explosively drive your hips forward and straighten your legs, generating power from the posterior chain. | As your hips snap forward, swing the ball upward, allowing your arms to follow the momentum naturally. | Release the ball overhead and backward at the peak of the movement, projecting it as far behind you as possible. | Land softly with a slight bend in the knees after the release and reset to the starting position for the next rep.

t: Stand facing a wall or partner at arm's length plus about one step, feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent. | Hold the medicine ball at chest height with both hands, fingers spread wide and elbows bent and tucked in toward your ribs. | Brace your core and set your shoulder blades back and down so your chest is tall and open. | Explosively extend your arms and press the ball forward from your chest, pushing through your palms as if performing a standing chest press. | Release the ball at full arm extension, driving through your chest, shoulders, and triceps to maximize power. | Catch the ball on the return — from the wall rebound or your partner's pass — with slightly bent arms to absorb the load. | Bring the ball back to chest height under control, reset your stance and brace, then repeat for the target number of reps.
tRu: Stand facing a wall or partner at arm's length plus about one step, feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent. | Hold the medicine ball at chest height with both hands, fingers spread wide and elbows bent and tucked in toward your ribs. | Напрягите корпус и отведите лопатки назад и вниз, чтобы грудь была поднята и раскрыта. | Explosively extend your arms and press the ball forward from your chest, pushing through your palms as if performing a standing chest press. | Release the ball at full arm extension, driving through your chest, shoulders, and triceps to maximize power. | Поймайте мяч при возврате — отскока от стены или передачи партнера — с слегка согнутыми руками, чтобы amortизировать нагрузку. | Верните мяч под контроль к уровню груди, восстановите исходное положение и напрягите корпус, затем повторите для заданного количества повторений.
tHe: Stand facing a wall or partner at arm's length plus about one step, feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent. | Hold the medicine ball at chest height with both hands, fingers spread wide and elbows bent and tucked in toward your ribs. | הדק את הליבה וקבע את השכמות לאחור ולמטה כך שהחזה גבוה ופתוח. | Explosively extend your arms and press the ball forward from your chest, pushing through your palms as if performing a standing chest press. | Release the ball at full arm extension, driving through your chest, shoulders, and triceps to maximize power. | תפוס את הכדור בחזרה - מהקפיצה מהקיר או מהמסירה של השותף - עם זרועות מעט כפופות כדי לספוג את העומס. | הבא את הכדור בחזרה לגובה החזה בשליטה, אתחל את התנוחה והתכופף, ואז חזור על התרגיל למספר החזרות המבוקש.

nE: Medicine Ball Chest Pass against Wall
nR: Передачи медбола от груди у стены
t: Stand facing a solid wall at arm's length plus a foot or two — adjust the distance so the ball rebounds cleanly back to you. | Hold the medicine ball at chest height with both hands, fingers spread wide and elbows bent, tucked close to your sides. | Set your feet shoulder-width apart with a slight bend in your knees and a braced core for a stable base. | Explosively extend your arms and press the ball directly into the wall with maximum force, as if performing a two-handed chest pass. | Release the ball cleanly at full arm extension; do not grip it past the point of release. | As the ball rebounds off the wall, catch it with both hands at chest height, absorbing the impact by letting your elbows bend back into the starting position. | Immediately use the rebound momentum to load the next throw and repeat for the target number of reps. | At the end of the set, catch the ball and bring it to a controlled stop before setting it down.
tRu: Stand facing a solid wall at arm's length plus a foot or two — adjust the distance so the ball rebounds cleanly back to you. | Hold the medicine ball at chest height with both hands, fingers spread wide and elbows bent, tucked close to your sides. | Set your feet shoulder-width apart with a slight bend in your knees and a braced core for a stable base. | Explosively extend your arms and press the ball directly into the wall with maximum force, as if performing a two-handed chest pass. | Release the ball cleanly at full arm extension; do not grip it past the point of release. | Когда мяч отскакивает от стены, поймайте его обеими руками на высоте груди, смягчая удар и сгибая локти обратно в стартовое положение. | Immediately use the rebound momentum to load the next throw and repeat for the target number of reps. | В конце подхода поймайте мяч, контролируемо остановите его и только затем положите на пол.

t: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Hold the medicine ball against your chest with both hands, or extend it overhead for greater difficulty. | Engage your core by gently pressing your lower back toward the floor. | Tuck your chin slightly toward your chest without forcing it down. | Curl your upper back off the floor by contracting your abdominals, lifting your shoulder blades clear of the ground. | Pause briefly at the top of the movement, keeping tension in your abs. | Lower your upper back slowly back to the floor under control. | Repeat for the desired number of reps without letting momentum drive the movement.

nE: Medicine Ball Crunch on Stability Ball
nH: כפיפות בטן עם כדור כוח על כדור פיזיו
t: Sit on the stability ball holding the medicine ball at your chest, then walk your feet forward and lean back until the ball supports your mid-to-lower back. Keep your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Let your torso extend back slightly over the ball so your abs are in a stretched position. This is your starting point. | Brace your core and tuck your chin slightly toward your chest. | Curl your upper torso forward and upward by contracting your rectus abdominis — think of bringing your ribs toward your hips rather than your head toward your knees. | At the top of the movement, squeeze your abs hard for a one-count while keeping the medicine ball steady at your chest. | Slowly lower your torso back down over the stability ball, allowing your abs to fully lengthen. Do not let momentum pull you down. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, controlling both the upward and downward phases throughout the set.

Do not let momentum pull you down. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, controlling both the upward and downward phases throughout the set.

nE: Medicine Ball Half Kneeling Chest Push
nR: Толчок медбола от груди с полуколена
nH: דחיפת כדור כוח מהחזה בחצי כריעה
t: Place a medicine ball on the floor and kneel on your right knee, bringing your left foot forward so your left knee is bent at roughly 90 degrees directly above your left ankle — this is the half-kneeling position. | Pick up the medicine ball and hold it at chest height with both hands, elbows bent and pointing outward, fingers spread over the ball. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and ensure your torso is upright — avoid leaning forward or tilting to either side. | Take a breath in, then exhale as you press the medicine ball straight out from your chest, extending both arms fully without locking the elbows aggressively. | Pause briefly at full extension with the ball held steady, maintaining a square, level position through your hips and shoulders. | Draw the ball back to your chest in a controlled manner, resisting any urge to rotate the torso as the load returns. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch legs — kneel on your left knee with your right foot forward — and repeat for the same number of reps.

t: Stand facing a sturdy wall or rebounder at arm's length, feet shoulder-width apart with a slight athletic bend in the knees. | Hold the medicine ball at chest height with both hands, elbows pointing outward and the ball close to your sternum. | Load your hips by rotating slightly away from the wall — your torso, hips, and shoulders all turning together — while keeping the ball at chest level. | Drive through your legs and hips to initiate the movement, rotating powerfully back toward the wall. | Transfer that rotational force through your core and into your chest and shoulders as you push the medicine ball explosively forward. | Extend both arms fully as you release the ball into the wall or rebounder, generating as much horizontal force as possible. | Catch the rebounding ball with both hands at chest height, absorbing the impact by letting your elbows bend and your core brace. | Reset your stance and position before repeating for the next rep.

t: Start in a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your hips raised so your body forms an inverted V, similar to a downward-dog. | Keep your arms and legs straight and your heels pressing toward the floor at the top of the arc. | Begin the movement by bending your elbows and lowering your chin toward the floor, initiating the forward sweep. | Scoop your chest forward and down in a smooth arc, keeping your hips lower than at the start as your body sweeps through the bottom position. | Press through your hands and extend your elbows as you continue the arc, pushing your chest upward and forward into an upward-dog position with hips near the floor. | At the top of the press, your arms should be straight, your chest open, and your gaze forward or slightly upward — feel the stretch across the pectoralis major and through the front of the torso. | Reverse the arc by pushing your hips back and upward, returning to the inverted-V starting position. | Control the return so you feel the rectus abdominis engage as the hips rise. | Repeat for the prescribed number of reps, maintaining a smooth, continuous motion throughout each cycle.

t: Stand with feet hip-width apart and place your hands on your hips or extend them forward for balance. | Adopt a quarter-squat position by pushing your hips back slightly and bending your knees, keeping your chest tall and core braced. | Shift your weight onto your right foot and step your left foot diagonally forward and to the left, landing softly on the ball of your foot. | Follow with your right foot, stepping only far enough to return to a hip-width stance without letting your feet touch, and keep the squat depth as you step. | Continue stepping in the same diagonal direction for the prescribed number of steps or distance. | Reverse the pattern by stepping diagonally backward and to the right, leading with the right foot, to travel back to your starting position. | Finish the set by bringing your feet back to hip-width and standing tall out of the quarter-squat.
tRu: Stand with feet hip-width apart and place your hands on your hips or extend them forward for balance. | Примите положение четверть-приседа, слегка отведя бёдра назад и согнув колени, удерживая грудь высоко, а корпус напряжённым. | Shift your weight onto your right foot and step your left foot diagonally forward and to the left, landing softly on the ball of your foot. | Follow with your right foot, stepping only far enough to return to a hip-width stance without letting your feet touch, and keep the squat depth as you step. | Продолжайте шагать в том же диагональном направлении для назначенного количества шагов или расстояния. | Reverse the pattern by stepping diagonally backward and to the right, leading with the right foot, to travel back to your starting position. | Finish the set by bringing your feet back to hip-width and standing tall out of the quarter-squat.

t: Begin in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders, arms straight, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core and keep your hips level — they should not pike up or sag toward the floor. | Drive your right knee diagonally toward your left elbow, rotating your hip slightly to complete the cross-body movement. | Without pausing, kick your right leg out to the right side, extending it roughly parallel to the floor. | Return your right foot to the starting position under control. | Immediately repeat the sequence on the opposite side — drive the left knee toward the right elbow, then kick the left leg out to the left. | Continue alternating sides at a brisk, controlled pace, maintaining plank alignment throughout. | Complete the prescribed number of repetitions or time interval, then lower your knees to the floor to rest.
tRu: Примите упор лёжа на прямых руках: ладони точно под плечами, руки прямые, тело образует прямую линию от головы до пяток. | Напрягите корпус и удерживайте бёдра на одном уровне — не поднимайте их вверх и не провисайте к полу. | С силовым движением подтяните правое колено по диагонали к левому локтю, слегка поворачивая таз для завершения скрестного движения. | Without pausing, kick your right leg out to the right side, extending it roughly parallel to the floor. | Return your right foot to the starting position under control. | Immediately repeat the sequence on the opposite side — drive the left knee toward the right elbow, then kick the left leg out to the left. | Продолжайте попеременно менять стороны в быстром, контролируемом темпе, сохраняя положение планки. | Выполните указанное количество повторений или время, затем опустите колени на пол, чтобы отдохнуть.
tHe: התחל בפלאנק גבוה עם כפות ידיים בדיוק מתחת לכתפיים, זרועות ישרות, והגוף בקו ישר מהראש לעקבים. | הדק את הליבה ושמור על אגן מאוזן — אל תרים אותו למעלה ואל תשמיט אותו לכיוון הרצפה. | Drive your right knee diagonally toward your left elbow, rotating your hip slightly to complete the cross-body movement. | Without pausing, kick your right leg out to the right side, extending it roughly parallel to the floor. | Return your right foot to the starting position under control. | Immediately repeat the sequence on the opposite side — drive the left knee toward the right elbow, then kick the left leg out to the left. | Continue alternating sides at a brisk, controlled pace, maintaining plank alignment throughout. | בצע את מספר החזרות או המשך הזמן המרוקן, ואז הנמיך את הברכים לרצפה למנוחה.

t: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders, arms fully extended, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Engage your core and keep your hips level — do not let them rise or sag. | Drive your right knee toward your chest as explosively as possible. | Before that foot returns to the ground, simultaneously drive your left knee forward in a switching motion. | As both feet leave the ground during the switch, add a small explosive hop so both feet are briefly airborne at the same time. | Land softly with one knee drawn in and the opposite leg extended, absorbing impact through the balls of your feet. | Continue alternating legs in a rapid, rhythmic cadence for the target duration or repetitions. | To finish, bring both feet back to the starting plank position and hold briefly to stabilise.

t: Start in a high plank with your hands flat on the floor directly under your shoulders, arms straight, and body in a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and ensure your hips are level — neither piked up nor sagging toward the floor. | Drive your right knee forward and bring your right foot all the way up beside your right hand, landing in a low lunge position with your heel flat or close to flat on the floor. | Pause briefly in the lunge to feel the stretch at the front of your left hip, keeping both hands planted and your right knee tracking in line with your right foot. | Step your right foot back to the starting plank position with control, re-establishing a neutral spine before the next rep. | Drive your left knee forward in the same way, bringing your left foot up beside your left hand into the low lunge position. | Pause, then return the left foot to the plank. | Continue alternating sides for the prescribed number of reps or time, maintaining steady breathing throughout.

t: Place a folded towel on a smooth, hard floor — hardwood, tile, or laminate works best. | Get into a high-plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders, arms straight, and both feet resting on the towel. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and set a neutral spine — your body should form a straight line from head to heels. | Slide your right foot forward along the floor, drawing your right knee toward your chest without raising your hips. | Slide the right foot back to the starting position, fully extending the hip before the next rep. | Immediately slide your left foot forward in the same controlled manner, keeping your hips level throughout. | Continue alternating legs at a steady pace, maintaining shoulder position directly over your wrists for the duration of the set. | To finish, press back through your shoulders, step off the towel, and release the plank position.

t: Place your hands flat on the floor, slightly wider than shoulder-width, and extend both legs behind you into a high-plank position with your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Engage your core by bracing your abs and squeezing your glutes so your hips stay level with your shoulders throughout the set. | Lift your right foot and drive your right knee diagonally across your body toward your left elbow, rotating your hip slightly to allow full range of motion. | Pause for a brief moment at the top of the drive, feeling the contraction in your obliques and hip flexors. | Return your right foot to the starting position with control, keeping your hips from rising or dropping as the leg extends back. | Immediately drive your left knee diagonally toward your right elbow, mirroring the movement on the opposite side. | Continue alternating legs in a smooth, rhythmic pattern for the target number of repetitions or duration. | Keep your breathing steady throughout — exhale as each knee drives across, inhale as the foot returns.

t: Stand with your feet together or hip-width apart, toes pointing straight forward and the outer edges of your feet parallel. | Press all four corners of each foot — the ball of the big toe, the ball of the little toe, and both sides of the heel — evenly into the floor. | Engage your thighs lightly so the kneecaps lift, but do not lock your knees; keep a very slight, natural bend. | Tuck your tailbone just enough to neutralize the lower back — avoid an exaggerated arch or a full posterior tuck. | Lengthen through the entire spine, drawing the crown of your head upward as if a thread were pulling it toward the ceiling. | Roll your shoulders up, back, and down so your shoulder blades settle onto your upper back and your chest opens without your ribcage flaring forward. | Let your arms hang at your sides with palms facing your thighs or slightly forward; keep your fingers long and relaxed. | Soften your jaw and face, breathe steadily through your nose, and hold the pose for five to ten slow breaths. | Release by taking one deep breath, then step your feet together if they were apart and allow your body to relax.
