t: Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with an overhand grip, arms fully extended and body hanging straight. | Engage your core and retract your scapulae to create tension through your lats and upper back. | Initiate an explosive pull by driving your elbows down and back, pulling the bar toward your lower chest rather than your chin. | As the bar reaches chest height, lean forward aggressively and begin rotating your wrists so your hands transition from below to above the bar. | Use the momentum of the pull to drive your torso up and over the bar, keeping the bar close to your body throughout the transition. | Once your hips are level with the bar and your chest is above it, press your hands down into the bar to straighten your arms into the dip lockout position. | Pause briefly at the top with arms fully extended and body supported above the bar. | Lower yourself in a controlled manner back through the transition and into a full hang to complete the repetition.

t: Place a Bosu ball dome-side up on the floor and sit on the center of the dome. | Walk your feet forward and lower your lower back onto the top of the dome so it sits roughly at the level of your lumbar spine. | Let your torso arch back over the dome until your abs feel a full stretch, with your head, upper back, and arms hanging below the level of your hips. | Place your fingertips lightly at the sides of your head or cross your arms over your chest — do not pull on your neck. | Brace your core and exhale as you curl your torso upward, lifting your shoulders and upper back off the dome. | Continue curling until your abs are fully contracted and your torso has reached roughly a 30–45° angle above horizontal. | Hold the contracted position for one count, then inhale and slowly lower your torso back over the dome to the starting stretched position. | Control the descent fully — let the dome support your arch without bouncing off it. | Complete your reps, then carefully sit upright before stepping off the Bosu ball.

t: Stand with your feet slightly wider than hip-width apart and your toes angled out at roughly 45 degrees. | Lower your hips down into a deep squat, keeping your heels flat on the floor if possible; if your heels rise, place a folded mat or small wedge under them. | Allow your thighs to open wider than your torso so your knees track over your toes. | Bring your palms together at the center of your chest in a prayer position, thumbs lightly touching your sternum. | Press your elbows firmly against the inner surfaces of your knees, using this contact to encourage the knees to widen and the hips to open further. | Lengthen your spine upward, lifting the crown of your head toward the ceiling and drawing your shoulder blades slightly together to avoid rounding the upper back. | Breathe steadily, holding the position for five to ten slow breaths or as directed by your practice. | To exit, press through your feet, engage your legs, and rise back to standing in a controlled manner.

t: Place a flat bench behind you and sit on the floor in front of it, facing away. | Lean back and position both heels on top of the bench with your feet together or no more than a few inches apart — this narrow stance is the key challenge of the movement. | Plant your hands flat on the floor beside your hips for initial stability. | Brace your core, press through your heels, and lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to heels. | Lift your hands off the floor and extend your arms alongside your torso or hold them slightly out to the sides for balance, engaging the deltoid anterior and serratus anterior. | Hold the top position with your glutes lightly squeezed, but focus on drawing your lower ribs toward your hips to keep the rectus abdominis under tension. | Keep your hips level — resist any rotation caused by the narrow foot placement. | Lower your hips back to the floor under control to complete one repetition, or hold the top position for the prescribed time if performing an isometric variation.

t: Sit or stand beneath a chin-up bar and take a close, shoulder-width or narrower supinated (palms-facing-you) grip on the bar. | Hang at full arm extension, cross your feet if needed, and pull your shoulder blades down and back to activate the lats before you begin pulling. | Brace your core and depress your shoulders away from your ears to create a stable base. | Pull yourself upward by driving your elbows straight down toward your hips, keeping them close to your sides throughout the movement. | Continue pulling until your chin clears the bar or your upper chest approaches it, squeezing the lats and mid-back at the top. | Lower yourself in a controlled, slow manner back to full arm extension, resisting gravity on the way down. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, maintaining tension in the back and avoiding swinging.

t: Place a stable raised surface — weight plates, a low step, or a sturdy block — on the floor and stand on top of it with your feet hip-width apart or closer, toes pointing slightly outward. | Stand tall with your chest up, shoulders back, and arms extended in front of you or crossed at your chest for counterbalance. | Brace your core and shift your weight evenly through both feet, making sure your heels are fully supported by the platform. | Begin the descent by simultaneously pushing your hips back and bending your knees, allowing them to track over your toes. | Lower yourself as deep as your mobility allows — ideally until your thighs go below parallel — letting your heels drop toward the floor below the platform level to exploit the full deficit range. | Pause briefly at the bottom without collapsing your torso or rounding your lower back. | Drive through your entire foot to press the floor away, extending your hips and knees together as you return to standing. | Lock out at the top by squeezing your glutes and fully extending your legs before beginning the next rep.

t: Grip a pull-up bar with your hands placed 4–6 inches apart, palms facing away from you. t: Lie face-down on an exercise mat with your legs extended and the balls of your feet on the floor, hip-width apart. | Place your hands flat on the floor beside your chest, fingers pointing forward, to support yourself during setup. | Tuck your chin slightly and place your forehead, just below the hairline, flat on the mat — do not roll back onto the crown of your head. | Brace your neck muscles and press through your forehead and the balls of your feet to lift your torso and thighs off the mat. | At the top, your body should form a gentle arc from feet to head with your hips at roughly the same height as your shoulders — avoid letting the hips rise much higher than the head. | Keep your hands lightly hovering near the floor or cross them over your lower back once you feel stable, but keep them within reach for safety. | Hold the position for the prescribed duration, breathing steadily through your nose — do not hold your breath. | To finish a repetition, lower your torso back to the mat under control, leading with your chest, and remove your head last.

t: Sit or stand tall with your spine neutral, shoulders relaxed, and feet hip-width apart on the floor. | Relax your jaw and let your mouth close gently so your neck muscles are not braced. | Place your hands loosely in your lap or at your sides — do not use your hands to push or pull your head. | Slowly lift your chin up and away from your chest and begin to tilt your head backward, leading with the top of your skull moving toward the back wall. | Continue the movement until you feel a gentle stretch across the front of your throat and along both sides of your neck — stop well before any point of discomfort or dizziness. | Hold this position for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and evenly, allowing the anterior neck muscles to gradually release. | To release, gently bring your head back to neutral by lifting your chin and returning your gaze forward — do not let your head drop forward quickly. | Rest for a breath or two, then repeat for 2–3 rounds as needed.

t: Sit on a bench or sturdy surface with your feet flat on the floor and knees apart at roughly 90 degrees. | Lean forward slightly and brace the back of your right upper arm firmly against the inside of your right thigh, just above the knee. | Let your right forearm hang down toward the floor with your palm facing up. | Use your left hand or press your right knee inward against your forearm to assist curling your right forearm up toward your shoulder — this is the assisted concentric phase. | Once your forearm is fully curled and your biceps are contracted, remove the assistance completely. | Slowly lower your forearm back to the starting position over 3 to 5 seconds, resisting gravity with your biceps alone — this controlled descent is the negative phase. | At the bottom, pause briefly, then use your hand or leg to assist the next curl up. | Complete all reps on one arm before switching to the other side.

t: Lie on a flat bench and grip a fixed overhead support — a rack upright, bench uprights, or a sturdy post — with both hands at roughly ear level, thumbs wrapped around for a secure hold. | Brace your entire core, squeeze your glutes, and press your upper back firmly into the bench so your shoulder blades are the only point of contact below the hands. | Lift your legs and hips until your body is nearly vertical, forming a straight line from shoulders to feet with only a slight outward arch acceptable. | Initiate the lowering phase by controlling your hips downward — resist the pull of gravity with your iliopsoas and rectus abdominis rather than letting gravity drop you. | Keep your body rigid as a single unit: do not pike at the hips or allow your lower back to sag away from the straight line. | Lower at a slow, deliberate tempo — aim for 3 to 5 seconds per rep — until your body is just above parallel to the bench or as low as you can hold without losing spinal alignment. | Stop the descent before your hips touch the bench or your lower back breaks into a hyperextended arch. | Return to the starting vertical position by bending your knees to step or swing up carefully, or have a partner assist the concentric — do not attempt the raise under fatigue. | Reset your brace and grip fully before beginning the next rep.

t: Set a flat bench lengthwise and load a barbell on the floor at the foot end. Lie face-down on the bench so your hips are near the end and your torso is fully supported. | Reach down and grasp the barbell with a double-overhand grip, hands roughly shoulder-width apart. t: Stand facing a wall at arm's length and raise one arm to roughly shoulder height, pressing your palm flat against the wall. | Step your feet back slightly so your body is on a gentle angle and your extended arm bears some of your bodyweight through the wall. | Engage your core and keep a neutral spine throughout the movement. | Without bending your elbow, pull your shoulder blade down and back — think of driving your elbow toward your hip — to create tension through your lat and teres major. | Hold the retracted and depressed position for one to two seconds, feeling the muscles on the side of your back engage. | Slowly release the tension and allow your shoulder blade to protract back to the starting position. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch arms and repeat.

t: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and take an underhand (supinated) grip with one hand, positioning it so you hang directly beneath the working hand. t: Set up in a standard forearm plank position with both forearms on the floor, elbows directly under your shoulders, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core hard — draw your navel gently in, squeeze your glutes, and press your forearm into the floor to create full-body tension before you lift anything. | Shift your weight slightly onto one forearm, distributing it evenly across that arm to keep your shoulder stable. | Slowly lift the opposite arm off the floor and extend it straight in front of you, keeping it in line with your body rather than reaching wide. | Hold your hips level — your pelvis should not rotate, hike, or sag as the arm comes up. | Keep your gaze down and slightly forward to maintain a neutral neck, and breathe steadily throughout the hold. | Hold the position for the prescribed duration, then lower the raised arm back to the floor with control. | Rest briefly, then repeat on the other side.

nE: One Arm Twisted Clean and Press
nR: Взятие с толчком одной рукой со скруткой
t: Stand with the barbell on the floor in front of you, feet about hip-width apart. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to reach down and grip the bar with one hand, using a neutral or pronated grip directly beneath your shoulder. | Brace your core, keep your back flat, and set your shoulder down and away from your ear before you begin the pull. | Drive forcefully through your legs and extend your hips to accelerate the bar upward, keeping it close to your body. | As the bar passes your hips, rotate your torso slightly toward the lifting side — this is the twist — and pull your elbow high to guide the bar up. | Drop under the bar by bending the knees slightly and rotating your elbow around and underneath the bar to catch it in the rack position at your shoulder, with the bar resting on the heel of your palm and your elbow pointing forward. | Stand up fully from the catch position, hips and knees locked out, before initiating the press. | Press the bar directly overhead by extending your elbow until your arm is fully locked out, keeping your core tight and your ribs down to avoid excessive lumbar extension. | Lower the bar back to the rack position under control, then return it to the floor with a controlled hinge before the next rep.

t: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and grip it with your dominant hand using a full, closed grip — thumb wrapped around the bar and the bar seated in the base of your palm, not your fingers. | Step or jump up so your working arm is fully extended overhead and your body hangs freely with feet off the floor. | Keep your shoulder actively engaged by depressing and packing the shoulder blade downward — avoid letting the shoulder passively shrug up toward your ear. | Brace your core lightly, keep your hips square under the bar, and resist any swinging — a slow, natural rotation of the whole body is normal and does not need to be fought. | Breathe steadily and hold the position for the target duration, maintaining an active shoulder and a firm grip throughout. | To finish, reach up with your free hand or lower your feet back to the floor in a controlled manner — avoid dropping suddenly from the bar.

nE: One Legged Upward Bow Pose Eka Pada Urdhva Dhanurasana
nR: Мост на одной ноге (Эка Пада Урдхва Дханурасана)
nH: תנוחת קשת עליונה ברגל אחת אקה פאדה אורדווה דנוראסאנה
t: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart and close to your hips. | Place your palms flat on the floor beside your ears, fingers pointing toward your shoulders, elbows pointing upward. | Press firmly through your hands and feet, lift your hips, and arch your torso upward into full Wheel Pose, straightening your arms completely. | Establish a steady, even base: distribute weight equally across both hands and both feet and breathe steadily for a few cycles. | Shift your weight gradually toward one hand and the corresponding foot, keeping your hips level and your core engaged. | On an exhale, press firmly through the grounded foot and lift the opposite foot off the floor, keeping that knee bent initially. | Once balanced, slowly extend the lifted leg upward toward the ceiling, reaching through the heel until the leg is straight. | Hold the position for 3–5 steady breaths, keeping your arms straight, your hips as even as possible, and your gaze directed toward the floor or your hands. | Bend the lifted knee, lower the foot back to the floor with control, re-establish the full wheel position, then release by tucking your chin and lowering your spine vertebra by vertebra.

t: Stand tall with your feet together and your hands relaxed at your sides. Choose a firm, flat surface with enough clear space to reach in all directions. | Shift your weight onto your right foot, bending your right knee slightly to create a soft, athletic stance. Lift your left foot just off the floor. | Without losing your balance, reach your left foot forward (12 o'clock direction) as far as comfortable, lightly tapping the floor with your toes, then return it to the starting position. | Next, reach diagonally forward-left (10–11 o'clock), tap the floor, and return. | Continue around the star pattern — reaching left (9 o'clock), diagonally back-left (7–8 o'clock), directly behind you (6 o'clock), diagonally back-right (4–5 o'clock), and to the right (3 o'clock) — tapping and returning after each reach. | Keep the taps light; your supporting leg should bear your full weight throughout. Avoid shifting your hips or allowing your support knee to cave inward. | After completing all reach directions, lower your left foot and repeat the full sequence standing on your left leg. | Perform the prescribed number of sets on each side, focusing on smooth, controlled reaches rather than maximum range.

t: Start in a standard push-up position with your hands on the floor, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Move your right hand out to the side until your right arm is nearly fully extended and pointing perpendicular to your torso. This is your extended, or archer, arm. | Keep your left hand directly under your left shoulder — this is the working arm that will carry most of the load. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and inhale before you begin the descent. | Bend your left elbow and lower your chest toward your left hand, keeping your elbow at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. t: Lie on your side on a mat with your hips and knees bent to roughly 90 degrees. | Stack your knees directly on top of each other and keep them in contact throughout the movement. | Extend both arms straight out in front of you at chest height with your palms pressed together. | Inhale to prepare, keeping your lower arm flat on the mat and your knees stacked. | Slowly rotate your top arm up and over toward the floor on the opposite side, following the hand with your eyes and head. | Allow your upper back to rotate as far as comfortable, letting the back of your top hand approach or rest on the floor. | Pause for one to two seconds at end range and feel the stretch across your chest, front shoulder, and the sides of your torso. | Exhale and return your top arm back to the starting position, palms together. | Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other.

t: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and your hands lightly behind your head — do not interlace your fingers or pull on your neck. | Raise both feet off the floor so your hips and knees are at roughly 90 degrees, keeping your lower back in contact with the floor. | Exhale and simultaneously lift your right shoulder off the floor, rotating your right elbow toward your left knee while you draw that knee in toward your chest. | Extend your right leg out straight at about a 45-degree angle to the floor as you perform the rotation, mimicking a cycling motion. | Hold the cross-body contraction for a brief moment, feeling the squeeze through your left obliques and the center of your abdomen. | Lower your right shoulder and return your left leg to the bent starting position in a controlled manner. | Repeat on the other side — rotate your left elbow toward your right knee while extending your left leg — completing one full rep. | Continue alternating sides for the full set, breathing out on each rotation and keeping the movement slow and deliberate.

t: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent to about 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor. | Hold a weight plate or dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight overhead, keeping them locked out for the entire set. | Press your lower back gently into the floor and brace your core before you begin. | Exhale and curl your chin toward your chest, then continue raising your torso off the floor while keeping your arms overhead and elbows straight. | Rise in a controlled arc until your torso is fully upright, with the weight still extended above your head. | Pause briefly at the top, maintaining a neutral spine and vertical arms. | Inhale and slowly lower yourself back to the starting position under control, vertebra by vertebra. | Reset your brace before initiating the next repetition.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and core braced. nE: Overhead Sit-up with Legs on Bench

t: Start in a tabletop position on all fours with your hands stacked beneath your shoulders and your knees beneath your hips. | Bring your right knee forward and place it behind your right wrist, angling the shin so your right foot moves toward your left wrist — the more parallel the shin is to the front of your mat, the deeper the stretch. | Slide your left leg straight back, lowering the top of your left foot flat onto the floor so your left hip points directly down toward the ground. | Square both hips toward the floor by pressing your right hip gently downward and drawing your left hip forward until your pelvis is as even as possible. | Place your fingertips on the floor beside your hips to find balance, lift tall through your spine, and breathe in to check that your lower back is not collapsing. | On an exhale, hinge forward from the hips and walk your hands out in front of you until your forearms or forehead rest comfortably on the floor. | Relax your shoulders, keep your front foot lightly flexed to protect the knee, and allow your hips to sink toward the ground with each exhale. | Hold the position for 30–90 seconds, breathing steadily and letting tension release gradually. | To exit, press your hands into the floor, tuck your back toes, and push back into a tabletop position before switching sides.

t: Set two flat benches parallel to each other, roughly hip-width apart and spaced so your body forms an inverted V when you press up. | Place your hands shoulder-width apart on one bench and walk your feet up onto the opposite bench, driving your hips high so your torso is nearly vertical. | Brace your core, tuck your chin, and align your head between your arms so your body forms a tight pike position. | Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward the bench between your hands, keeping your elbows tracking at roughly 45° to your torso. | Descend under control until your head lightly touches or comes just above the bench surface — this is the bottom of the rep. | Press firmly through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the top, fully locking out your arms overhead. | Keep your hips as high as possible throughout each rep to maintain the vertical pressing angle that targets the shoulders. | Complete your reps, then step your feet down from the bench one at a time to dismount safely.

t: Position two flat benches parallel to each other, roughly 3–4 feet apart — enough so that when you place your hands on one and your feet on the other, your hips form a sharp inverted-V shape. | Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the near edge of one bench, fingers pointing forward, and step your feet onto the far edge of the second bench behind you. | Walk your hands back until your hips are stacked directly above your shoulders and your torso is as close to vertical as possible. | Brace your core, tuck your chin slightly, and keep your legs straight with toes pressing into the bench for stability. | Inhale and bend your elbows, lowering the top of your head toward the first bench while keeping your elbows tracking at roughly a 45–60° angle to your torso — not flared straight out to the sides. | Lower until your head is just above or lightly grazes the bench surface, maintaining your hips-over-shoulders position throughout. | Exhale and press firmly through your palms to extend your arms back to the starting position, squeezing through the shoulders at the top. | Complete your reps, then step your feet off the bench one at a time before releasing your hands.

t: Place two sturdy chairs shoulder-width apart (or slightly wider) and stand between them facing forward. | Hinge at the hips and place one hand flat on each chair seat, fingers pointing forward and wrists stacked under your shoulders. | Walk your feet forward and raise your hips until your body forms a sharp inverted-V (pike position), with your head between your arms and your gaze toward your feet. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and ensure your arms are fully extended before starting. | Bend your elbows and lower the crown of your head down between the chairs in a controlled manner, keeping your elbows tracking back and slightly outward — not flaring straight to the sides. | Descend until your head clears the level of the chair seats or your range of motion naturally stops, feeling a strong stretch through your shoulders. | Press firmly through both palms to drive yourself back up to the starting position, fully extending your elbows at the top. | Complete your reps, then carefully step back and lift your hands off the chairs to finish.

t: Place a flat bench or sturdy elevated surface behind you and face away from it. | Put your hands on the floor about shoulder-width apart, fingers spread and pointing forward. | Step back and place both feet on top of the bench so that your hips are high and your body forms a steep inverted-V shape. | Adjust your hand placement so your hips sit directly above or slightly forward of your shoulders, not over your wrists. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your legs straight throughout the movement. | Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward the floor in a controlled manner, keeping your elbows tracking roughly in line with your torso. | Stop when your head is just above or lightly touching the floor, maintaining the pike position throughout. | Press through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the starting position, fully locking out at the top. | Complete all reps, then carefully step your feet off the bench before standing.

t: Place a bench behind you and set your hands flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing forward. | Step your feet up onto the bench one at a time and walk your hands back until your hips are high and your body forms a sharp inverted-V, with your torso as vertical as you can hold it. | Brace your core and keep your hips elevated throughout the set — do not let them drop toward a push-up position. | Inhale, then bend your elbows outward at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso and lower the top of your head toward the floor between your hands. | Descend until your head is just above or lightly touching the floor, keeping your elbows tracking over your wrists. | Press firmly through your palms and exhale as you push back up to the starting pike position. | Lock out your elbows fully at the top without shrugging your shoulders toward your ears. | Complete all reps, then step your feet off the bench one at a time.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your toes pointing forward. | Soften your knees slightly, especially if your hamstrings are tight. | Inhale to lengthen your spine, then hinge forward at the hips — not the waist — keeping your back as flat as possible. | Lower your torso toward your thighs and let your arms hang toward the floor, or rest your hands on your shins. | Reach your fingertips toward the ground, going only as far as your flexibility allows without rounding your lower back excessively. | Relax your neck and let your head hang heavy. | Breathe steadily and hold the position for 20–60 seconds, sinking a little deeper on each exhale. | To come up, engage your core, bend your knees slightly, and slowly roll back to standing one vertebra at a time, or hinge back up with a flat back.

t: Begin in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart, wrists directly under your shoulders, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Press your hips up and back toward the ceiling, straightening your legs and lowering your heels toward the floor to arrive in a pike position — your body forming an inverted V. | Let your head hang naturally between your arms and hold briefly, feeling the stretch through your shoulders and hamstrings. | Shift your weight forward by bending your elbows and lowering your hips toward the floor in a smooth, controlled arc. | As your hips near the floor, press through your palms, straighten your arms, and lift your chest upward and forward into a cobra position. | Keep your hips low (or lightly touching the floor), roll your shoulders back and down, and gently extend your spine without straining your lower back. | Hold the cobra for a breath, then tuck your toes, press your hips back up toward the ceiling, and return to the pike position. | Continue flowing between pike and cobra for the desired number of repetitions, moving with your breath throughout.

t: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, weight balanced evenly, and knees soft. | Set your posture: lengthen your spine, draw your shoulder blades gently down away from your ears, and lightly engage your core to keep your torso still. | Extend one arm down by your side with a soft, unlocked elbow to reach the starting position. | Inhale to prepare, then slowly sweep the arm forward and up in a smooth arc across the front of your body. | Continue the circle overhead and then behind you, moving only from the shoulder joint while your torso stays square and quiet. | Return the arm to your side to complete one full, continuous circle without pausing or using momentum. | Perform the prescribed number of circles in one direction, then reverse and circle the same number of times the other way. | Lower the arm and rest briefly, then repeat the set on the other side.

t: Stand or kneel tall with your spine long, pelvis neutral, and feet or knees hip-width apart. | Extend both arms straight down in front of your thighs, palms facing back and shoulders relaxed away from your ears. | Take a full inhale to prepare, feeling your ribcage expand in all directions. | As you exhale, draw both arms straight back behind your hips, keeping them long with the elbows soft rather than locked. | As your arms reach their furthest point back, lift tall through the crown of your head, open your chest, and gently draw your shoulder blades together and down. | Hold the open position for one to two counts, feeling the stretch across the front of your chest and the front of your shoulders. | Inhale and slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, keeping the movement smooth throughout. | Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, maintaining an upright posture throughout.

t: Set the reformer to a light spring resistance suitable for stretching rather than heavy loading. | Lie on your back on the carriage with your head resting on the headrest and your arms relaxed at your sides. | Place the balls of your feet on the foot bar at hip-width, heels hanging free off the edge. | Extend your legs fully to push the carriage away from the foot bar until your knees are straight and your legs are long. | Slowly press through the balls of your feet, pointing your toes away from you (plantar flexion) to raise your heels as high as your range of motion allows. | Pause briefly at the top of the plantar flexion, keeping your ankles controlled before reversing. | Slowly flex your feet back toward your shins (dorsiflexion), feeling the lengthening deepen through the calf complex. | Continue in a smooth, rhythmic manner for the prescribed number of repetitions. | Bend your knees to return the carriage to the stopper before carefully stepping off.

t: Lie on your back on the Reformer carriage with your head on the headrest, shoulders against the shoulder rests, and your arms relaxed at your sides. | Place the balls of both feet on the foot bar about hip-width apart, heels together or parallel, with your knees bent and the carriage at the stopper. | Press evenly through both feet to push the carriage out until your legs are almost fully extended, keeping a neutral spine with a gentle natural curve in your lower back. | Rise onto the balls of both feet so both heels lift above the level of the foot bar — this is your starting position, with the carriage held out and still. | Keeping the carriage steady and both legs long, lower one heel down below the foot bar, letting that ankle flex and the calf lengthen, while the other heel stays lifted. | Lift that heel back up to the top as you simultaneously lower the opposite heel, allowing that knee to soften slightly — mimicking the alternating cadence of a slow jog. | Continue alternating heels in a smooth, controlled rhythm, keeping the carriage extended and stable rather than letting it travel in and out. | Keep your pelvis level and your lower back neutral throughout; do not let either hip hike upward or the carriage bounce. | After the desired number of repetitions or duration, bring both heels level, bend both knees to control the carriage back to the stopper, and step off the Reformer.

t: Lie on your back on the reformer carriage with your head toward the shoulder rests and your feet lightly resting on the footbar, legs extended. | Press through the footbar to fully extend your legs, allowing the carriage to glide away and your body to lengthen. | With control, continue pressing and lower your legs overhead, lifting your hips off the carriage so your spine curls vertebra by vertebra from tailbone upward. | Reach your legs to a position parallel to the floor overhead, creating a long diagonal line from your shoulders to your feet. | Hold the overhead position for one to two breaths, keeping your weight across your upper back and shoulder blades — never on your neck. | Slowly reverse the movement, rolling your spine back down onto the carriage one vertebra at a time as the footbar returns toward you. | Guide your feet back to the footbar in the starting position and repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.

t: Set the reformer to a light-to-medium spring tension — enough that the carriage carries some of your weight on the way out and does not pull you into the split faster than you can control. | Stand facing the footbar and place your front foot flat on the stationary platform, toes pointing straight ahead and the front knee softly bent. | Step your rear foot onto the carriage close to the platform, foot flat or on the ball of the foot, hips square to the footbar. | Rest your hands lightly on the footbar or the frame for balance, stand tall, and draw the lower ribs down to brace the core. | Tuck the pelvis slightly under (posterior tilt) so the stretch is felt in the front of the rear hip rather than in the lower back. | Exhale and let the rear leg slide the carriage away, lowering into the split only as far as you can go while keeping the pelvis square and the torso upright. | Stop at the point of firm but comfortable tension in the rear hip flexor and front hamstring, then hold for the prescribed duration, breathing steadily and releasing a little deeper on each exhale. | To exit, press the rear foot into the carriage and pull with the front leg to draw the carriage back to the stopper under control — never let the springs snap it home. | Step off carefully, reset the springs if needed, and repeat with the other leg forward.

t: Set up the reformer with appropriate spring resistance for your mobility level and stand facing the footbar with the carriage pulled in. | Step onto the carriage and position your feet in a wide turned-out stance — heels roughly shoulder-width apart with toes angled out at roughly 45°, similar to a ballet second position. | Hold the footbar or straps lightly for balance, keeping your spine tall and your shoulders relaxed down away from your ears. | Begin to lower into a squat by bending your knees directly over your toes, tracking them outward in line with your feet as the carriage slides back. | Descend slowly and with control, allowing your hips to sink deep between your heels while maintaining an upright torso. | At the bottom of the squat, pause briefly, feeling a stretch through the inner thighs, hips, and ankles without collapsing your arch. | Press evenly through the full length of your feet to drive the carriage back in, extending your legs and returning to the starting position. | Repeat for the prescribed number of reps, keeping your movements smooth and your breath steady throughout.

t: Set the reformer to a light or medium spring tension — heavier springs make the return easier, lighter springs increase the challenge on the adductors. | Stand sideways on the reformer with one foot flat on the stationary footbar platform and the other foot flat on the carriage, feet parallel and hip-width apart. | Engage your core, stand tall, and soften the knees slightly so neither leg is locked out. | Inhale to prepare, then exhale as you press the carriage foot outward, sliding your leg away from your body in a controlled arc — stop before your hips begin to tip to one side. | Keep your pelvis level and square throughout the slide; resist any temptation to hike the hip on the moving side. | At the end of the range, pause briefly, then inhale and use your inner thigh of the moving leg to draw the carriage back to the starting position with control. | Complete all reps on one side, then step off carefully and switch sides. | Perform 8–12 repetitions per side for mobility and strength, or 5–8 slow, controlled reps when focusing on balance and stability.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides, and your weight evenly balanced across both feet. | Shift your weight onto your left foot and drive your right knee upward to roughly hip height, flexing the foot so the toes point up. | As your right foot descends, simultaneously drive your left knee upward, mimicking the alternating leg action of running. | Keep a soft bend in the landing knee each time your foot touches down — never lock the knee on contact. | Pump your arms in opposition to your legs: when the right knee rises, the left arm swings forward with the elbow bent at roughly 90 degrees, and vice versa. | Land lightly on the balls of your feet rather than crashing down on your heels, keeping contact time with the floor brief. | Maintain an upright posture with your chest lifted, core gently braced, and gaze forward throughout the movement. | Continue at a steady, sustainable rhythm for the target duration or rep count, breathing rhythmically through your nose and mouth.

t: Set the parallel bars to a width slightly wider than your shoulders. Mount the bars and lock your arms out fully, holding your body upright above them. | Lean your torso forward aggressively, pushing your shoulders into protraction (rounding them forward) and shifting your hips in front of your hands. Your body should form a near-horizontal angle to the floor. | Brace your core and waist hard to hold the forward-tilted position. Keep your legs together and either straight or slightly tucked — do not let your hips sag or pike. | With control, bend your elbows and lower your body downward while maintaining the same forward lean throughout the descent. Your elbows will flare slightly outward. | Lower until your elbows reach roughly 90°, or as deep as your shoulder mobility and strength allow, without losing the planche lean. | Press firmly through the bars to extend your arms back to the starting locked-out position, keeping the forward lean intact throughout the push. | Complete your reps, then carefully return to an upright seated position on the bars before dismounting.

t: Begin from a solid full planche hold: hands flat on the floor shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended, body parallel to the ground with no leg contact. | Engage your core, glutes, and legs to form a single rigid plank; do not allow your hips to rise or sag before initiating the press. | Protract your shoulder blades fully and push the floor away to create maximum scapular spread. | Initiate the press by driving force through your palms and extending through the anterior deltoids, allowing your hips and torso to begin rising while maintaining horizontal body alignment as long as possible. | Continue pressing as your body pivots upward; your shoulders travel back from ahead of your hands until they finish stacked over them. | Finish in a balanced handstand with arms fully locked, body vertical, and shoulders stacked directly over your wrists. | To lower, reverse the movement under control: shift your shoulders forward, allow your body to descend in a slow arc, and resist with your anterior deltoids and triceps the entire way down. | Land back in the full planche position with arms straight and body parallel to the floor, absorbing the load through shoulder protraction rather than elbow bend.

t: Place a stability ball on the floor and kneel behind it. | Walk your hands onto the ball so your forearms or palms rest on top, and extend your legs behind you into a full plank position. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and align your body in a straight line from head to heels. | Keeping your hips level, lift your right hand off the ball and tap the side of the ball firmly. | Return your right hand to the top of the ball and immediately lift your left hand to tap the opposite side. | Continue alternating sides in a controlled rhythm, resisting any rotation or sagging of the hips with each tap. | Breathe steadily throughout — exhale as you tap, inhale as you return. | Complete your target number of reps per side, then step your feet in and return to a kneeling position to finish.

t: Set up in a forearm plank: elbows directly under your shoulders, forearms flat on the floor, legs extended behind you, weight on your toes. | WRONG — Pike: Deliberately raise your hips toward the ceiling until your body forms an inverted V. t: Set up in a high plank with your hands directly under your shoulders, arms fully extended, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and set your hips level — they should not rise or sag at any point during the exercise. | Keep your upper body completely still and your gaze on the floor a few inches ahead of your hands so your neck stays neutral. | Jump both feet out to the sides simultaneously, landing softly on the balls of your feet with a slight bend at the knees. | Immediately jump both feet back together to the starting position, maintaining the same hip height and core brace. | Continue the out-and-in leg movement for the target number of repetitions or time interval. | To finish, step your feet together, hold the plank briefly, then lower to the floor with control or press back into a rest position.

t: Kneel on a soft surface with your knees hip-width apart and the tops of your feet flat on the floor, toes pointing straight back. | Sit your hips back toward your heels so your body weight gently presses the ankles and feet into plantar flexion. | Place your hands on your thighs or the floor beside you for balance and to control how much pressure you apply. | Keep your spine tall and your torso upright rather than hunching forward. | Hold the stretched position for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the front of the shin and ankle to relax. | To deepen the stretch slightly, shift a small amount of additional body weight toward your heels; back off immediately if you feel sharp discomfort in the knee or ankle. | Release by lifting your hips and returning to an upright kneeling position before switching sides if working one leg at a time.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you, or on a chair with the foot to be stretched resting on the opposite knee. | Grasp the top of your foot and toes with both hands, or loop a towel or resistance band around the ball of your foot. | Gently pull your foot toward your shin (dorsiflexion) until you feel a stretch along the back of your calf. | While maintaining that dorsiflexion, slowly turn the sole of your foot inward (inversion) so it faces slightly toward the midline of your body. | Hold the combined dorsiflexion and inversion position until you feel a stretch along the outer lower leg and lateral ankle — the peroneal muscles. | Breathe steadily and relax the foot and ankle muscles throughout the hold. | Hold for 20–30 seconds, then slowly release the foot back to a neutral position. | Repeat on the other side, performing 2–3 holds per foot.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your arms alongside your torso, palms pressing down into the floor. | Engage your core and exhale as you lift both legs off the floor, bringing them to a 90-degree angle above your hips. | Continue to press your palms into the floor and slowly lower your legs over your head, reaching your feet toward the floor behind your head. | Keep your legs as straight as possible, using your quadriceps to hold the knees extended while the hamstrings lengthen. | Once your toes touch or approach the floor, interlace your fingers behind your back and press your arms into the mat to create stability. | Keep your neck long and your gaze toward your chest, and hold the pose, breathing steadily for 5–10 slow breaths. | To exit, unclasp your hands, place your palms back on the mat, and slowly roll your spine back down to the floor one vertebra at a time. | Lower your legs with control back to the starting position and rest briefly in a neutral supine position.

t: Stand with your feet together and arms at your sides, core braced and chest tall. | Bend your knees slightly to load the legs, then explosively jump upward and outward, spreading your feet wider than shoulder-width apart. | As your feet leave the ground, raise both arms out to the sides and overhead so they meet at the top. | Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees bent to roughly 30–45 degrees, absorbing the impact through your ankles, knees, and hips. | Immediately jump again, bringing your feet back together and lowering your arms to your sides in one fluid motion. | Breathe rhythmically — exhale on each jump, inhale as you land — and maintain a steady, controlled tempo throughout the set. | Continue for the prescribed duration or rep count without pausing between jumps.
tRu: Stand with your feet together and arms at your sides, core braced and chest tall. | Слегка согните ноги, заряжая их, затем взрывным движением прыгните вверх и в стороны, расставляя стопы шире плеч. | Отрывая стопы от пола, поднимите обе руки через стороны над головой, чтобы они встретились в верхней точке. | Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees bent to roughly 30–45 degrees, absorbing the impact through your ankles, knees, and hips. | Immediately jump again, bringing your feet back together and lowering your arms to your sides in one fluid motion. | Дышите ритмично — выдыхайте на прыжке наружу, вдыхайте на прыжке внутрь, или найдите ритм, который вы можете поддерживать. | Продолжайте в течение заданного времени или количества повторений без пауз между прыжками.
tHe: Stand with your feet together and arms at your sides, core braced and chest tall. | כופף קלות את הברכיים לטעינת הרגליים, ואז קפוץ בנפץ למעלה והחוצה, תוך פישוק כפות הרגליים רחב מרוחב הכתפיים. | בעזיבת הקרקע, הרם את שתי הזרועות לצדדים ומעל הראש כך שייפגשו למעלה. | Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees bent to roughly 30–45 degrees, absorbing the impact through your ankles, knees, and hips. | Immediately jump again, bringing your feet back together and lowering your arms to your sides in one fluid motion. | נשיר בקצב קבוע — נשיר בכל קפיצה, נשאב בעת הנחיתה — ושמור על קצב יציב ומבוקר לאורך כל הסט. | Continue for the prescribed duration or rep count without pausing between jumps.

t: Stand in an athletic stance with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and weight on the balls of your feet. | Designate a pattern on the floor — such as a ladder, cone layout, or marked squares — to guide your movement sequence. | Begin the drill by driving explosively off one foot to move laterally, forward, or diagonally to the first target position. | Land softly on the balls of your feet, immediately absorbing force by bending your knees to prepare for the next movement. | React quickly and push off again toward the next target position, maintaining low hips and an upright torso throughout. | Continue through the full pattern as fast as possible while keeping each footstrike controlled and precise. | Complete the sequence, rest briefly, then repeat for the prescribed number of sets.

t: Set up in a standard push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, body in a straight line from head to heels, and core braced. | Lower your chest to the floor under control, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | At the bottom, pause for a brief moment with your chest just above or lightly touching the floor. | Explosively press into the floor as hard and fast as possible, driving your hands upward so they leave the ground. | While airborne, keep your body rigid and your core tight — avoid letting your hips sag or pike. | Land with soft, slightly bent elbows to absorb the impact and immediately transition into the next rep. | Complete the target number of reps, maintaining explosive intent on every push.

t: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips or clasped in front of your chest. | Step your right foot wide to the side — roughly two to three feet from your left foot — keeping both feet pointing forward. | Shift your weight to the right, bend your right knee, and push your hips back to lower into a side lunge. Keep your left leg straight and your chest up. | At the bottom of the lunge, add one small controlled pulse by allowing your hips to sink slightly lower, then return to the starting lunge depth without fully standing. | Press through your right foot to return to the standing starting position. | Step out to the left and repeat the same movement on the left side, adding the pulse at the bottom. | Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.

t: Stand with your back flat against a wall and your feet shoulder-width apart, positioned about 60–70 cm from the wall. | Slide your back down the wall until your hips and knees are both at roughly 90 degrees, entering a wall-sit position. | Keep your chest up, core braced, and both feet fully planted on the floor. | Hold the bottom position for 1–2 seconds to establish stability. | Drive explosively through your heels and the balls of your feet, pushing off the ground to jump straight up. | Extend your knees and ankles fully at the peak of the jump, letting your back slide up the wall rather than pushing your hips away from it. | Land softly with slightly bent knees and immediately slide back down the wall into the squat position. | Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions without losing contact with the wall between reps.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointing slightly outward. | Brace your core and keep your chest tall throughout the movement. | Lower into a squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees to at least 90 degrees. | Keep your weight distributed across your entire foot and your knees tracking over your toes. | Drive explosively through your heels and midfoot to launch your body off the ground. | Extend your hips, knees, and ankles fully as you leave the ground. | Land softly with bent knees, allowing your hips and knees to absorb the impact immediately. | Transition directly into the next squat descent upon landing to maintain plyometric rhythm. | Exhale sharply on the jump and inhale on the descent.

t: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees fully extended, and arms relaxed at your sides. | Place a piece of tape or a reference marker at the base of your feet so you have a consistent measurement point. | Take a slow, deep breath in to lengthen the spine before beginning the movement. | Exhale gradually and hinge forward at the hips, lowering both hands toward the floor without bending your knees. | Reach as far as possible in a controlled manner — do not bounce or force the stretch. | Hold the lowest position for two to three seconds and note where your fingertips reach relative to the floor or reference line. | Return slowly to the upright position by engaging your core and stacking the spine vertebra by vertebra. | Rest for thirty seconds, then repeat the movement two more times. | Record the best of three attempts as your flexibility score, measured in centimeters above or below the floor reference.

t: Sit tall in a chair or stand upright with your spine neutral and shoulders relaxed. | Interlace your fingers and place both palms flat against the back of your head. | Keep your chin level and your gaze forward so your neck stays in a neutral position. | Gently press the back of your head into your hands as if you are trying to extend your neck backward. | Resist firmly with your hands so that your head does not actually move — this is the isometric contraction. | Apply only moderate, controlled force; the neck should feel working tension, never sharp pain. | Hold the contraction for 5–10 seconds while breathing steadily — do not hold your breath. | Release the pressure gradually, rest a few seconds, then repeat for the desired number of sets.

t: Sit on the floor with both legs extended straight in front of you. | Loop the rope around the ball of one foot, holding one end of the rope in each hand. | Sit tall with your back straight and your target leg fully extended. | Gently pull both ends of the rope toward you to dorsiflex your foot, drawing your toes back toward your shin. | Hold the stretched position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and avoiding any jerking or bouncing. | Slowly release the tension on the rope and allow your foot to return to a neutral position. | Repeat for the desired number of holds, then switch to the opposite foot.

t: Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell over mid-foot. Grip the bar just outside your legs with a double-overhand grip, hands roughly shoulder-width apart. | Hinge at the hips and bend your knees forward until your shins touch the bar, chest up, back flat, and shoulders positioned slightly in front of the bar. This is your starting position. | Begin the first pull by pressing the floor away with your legs, keeping your hips and shoulders rising at the same rate and the bar moving in a straight, close path up your shins. | As the bar passes your knees, sweep it back into your hips by extending your knees slightly and shifting your torso toward vertical — this loads the hips for the explosive second pull. | Drive the second pull by violently extending your hips, knees, and ankles simultaneously. Shrug your shoulders hard and allow your elbows to pull high and wide as the bar travels upward. | Once the bar reaches chest height and you have generated maximum upward momentum, pull yourself under the bar by bending your knees into a quarter-squat and rotating your elbows forward rapidly. | Receive the bar on your front deltoids and upper chest in the front rack position — elbows high, upper arms parallel to the floor, wrists extended. Your feet may move slightly outward as you catch. | Stabilize in the quarter-squat with the bar under control, then stand fully upright to complete the rep. | Lower the bar back to the floor under control — either by reversing through the rack and hinge positions or by a controlled drop if bumper plates and appropriate flooring are in use.

t: Load the power sled with an appropriate amount of weight plates for your training goal — heavier loads build strength, lighter loads emphasize speed and conditioning. | Stand behind the sled and place both hands on the upright handles or crossbar at roughly shoulder height, gripping firmly with a neutral or slightly pronated grip. | Lean your torso forward at roughly 45 degrees so your body forms a straight line from head to heels, creating a strong pushing angle. | Brace your core hard and keep your hips in line with your torso — avoid letting them rise above shoulder level. | Drive off your rear foot explosively, taking your first step forward and transferring that force directly into the sled. | Continue pushing with short, powerful strides, staying low and keeping constant pressure through your arms into the handles. | Keep your head in a neutral position, eyes looking a few feet ahead, and maintain full-body tension throughout the push. | Push the sled for the prescribed distance or time, then release the handles and stand upright before turning around or resetting. | Rest as needed, then reposition behind the sled for the next set.

t: Load the sled with an appropriate weight and attach a waist harness or hand straps so the sled trails directly behind you. | Face away from the sled and step into a wide, batwing stance with your feet 1.5–2 times hip-width apart and toes turned out 30–45°. | Brace your core and hinge slightly at the hips so your torso leans forward 15–30°, keeping your chest up and your spine neutral throughout. | Sink your hips into a quarter- to half-squat position, ensuring your knees track over your toes in line with the wide stance. | Drive powerfully through the balls of your feet to push the ground away and drag the sled forward, maintaining the batwing leg position as you step. | Take short, controlled steps and reset the wide stance after each stride to keep the thighs under continuous load. | Continue driving forward for the programmed distance, then stand tall, step out of the harness, and allow the sled to come to rest.

tHe: Load the sled with an appropriate weight and attach a waist harness or hand straps so the sled trails directly behind you. | Face away from the sled and step into a wide, batwing stance with your feet 1.5–2 times hip-width apart and toes turned out 30–45°. | הדק את הליבה וכופף מעט באגן כך שהגוף נוטה קדימה 15–30°, תוך שמירה על חזה מורם ועמוד שדרה ניטרלי לאורך כל התנועה. | Sink your hips into a quarter- to half-squat position, ensuring your knees track over your toes in line with the wide stance. | Drive powerfully through the balls of your feet to push the ground away and drag the sled forward, maintaining the batwing leg position as you step. | Take short, controlled steps and reset the wide stance after each stride to keep the thighs under continuous load. | Continue driving forward for the programmed distance, then stand tall, step out of the harness, and allow the sled to come to rest.

t: Attach two pulling straps to the power sled's harness point and load the sled with an appropriate amount of weight plates. | Stand facing away from the sled, holding one strap in each hand at your sides with your arms straight and slightly behind your hips. | Step far enough away from the sled to put tension in the straps before the set begins. | Set your feet hip-width apart, brace your core, and keep your torso upright with a slight forward lean at the hips. | Drive your heel into the ground and step backward with one foot, keeping the knee slightly bent as your foot makes contact. | Immediately follow with the other foot, establishing a steady walking rhythm while maintaining continuous tension on the straps. | Keep your arms straight throughout — do not pull with your arms or shorten the straps; all resistance should transfer through the legs. | Continue walking backward for the prescribed distance, typically 20–40 metres per set. | Once the set is complete, stop walking, set the straps down, and turn around before approaching the sled.
tRu: Прикрепите две тяговые лямки к точке крепления упряжи саней и нагрузите сани нужным количеством дисков. | Stand facing away from the sled, holding one strap in each hand at your sides with your arms straight and slightly behind your hips. | Step far enough away from the sled to put tension in the straps before the set begins. | Set your feet hip-width apart, brace your core, and keep your torso upright with a slight forward lean at the hips. | Упритесь пяткой в пол и сделайте шаг назад одной ногой, сохраняя колено слегка согнутым при касании пола. | Immediately follow with the other foot, establishing a steady walking rhythm while maintaining continuous tension on the straps. | Keep your arms straight throughout — do not pull with your arms or shorten the straps; all resistance should transfer through the legs. | Продолжайте идти назад на заданное расстояние, обычно 20–40 метров за подход. | Once the set is complete, stop walking, set the straps down, and turn around before approaching the sled.
tHe: חבר שתי רצועות משיכה לנקודת הרתמה של מזחלת הכוח והעמס על המזחלת כמות מתאימה של צלחות משקל. | Stand facing away from the sled, holding one strap in each hand at your sides with your arms straight and slightly behind your hips. | Step far enough away from the sled to put tension in the straps before the set begins. | Set your feet hip-width apart, brace your core, and keep your torso upright with a slight forward lean at the hips. | Drive your heel into the ground and step backward with one foot, keeping the knee slightly bent as your foot makes contact. | Immediately follow with the other foot, establishing a steady walking rhythm while maintaining continuous tension on the straps. | Keep your arms straight throughout — do not pull with your arms or shorten the straps; all resistance should transfer through the legs. | Continue walking backward for the prescribed distance, typically 20–40 metres per set. | Once the set is complete, stop walking, set the straps down, and turn around before approaching the sled.

t: Load the power sled with the desired weight plates and attach a waist or hip harness to the sled's tow strap, ensuring the connection point sits at or just below your hip bones. | Step forward until the tow strap is taut and stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, core braced, and shoulders relaxed back. | Lean very slightly forward from the ankles — not the waist — to create a small forward body angle that keeps tension on the strap throughout the drag. | Drive one foot forward with a powerful, dorsiflexed stride, planting your heel-to-midfoot and pushing through the full foot to propel yourself forward. | As your lead foot contacts the ground, drive the opposite knee forward and up, maintaining a rhythmic walking or marching tempo. | Keep your arms swinging naturally at your sides to maintain balance and momentum; avoid pulling on the harness with your upper body. | Continue walking forward, dragging the sled behind you, for the prescribed distance — typically 20–40 metres per set. | At the end of the distance, come to a controlled stop, reset your stance, and either rest or reverse course for the next set. | After completing all sets, unclip the harness from the tow strap before removing the weight plates from the sled.

tHe: Load the power sled with the desired weight plates and attach a waist or hip harness to the sled's tow strap, ensuring the connection point sits at or just below your hip bones. | Step forward until the tow strap is taut and stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, core braced, and shoulders relaxed back. | Lean very slightly forward from the ankles — not the waist — to create a small forward body angle that keeps tension on the strap throughout the drag. | Drive one foot forward with a powerful, dorsiflexed stride, planting your heel-to-midfoot and pushing through the full foot to propel yourself forward. | בנגיעת הרגל הקדמית בקרקע, דחוף את הברך הנגדית קדימה ומעלה, תוך שמירה על קצב הליכה או צעידה קצבי. | Keep your arms swinging naturally at your sides to maintain balance and momentum; avoid pulling on the harness with your upper body. | Continue walking forward, dragging the sled behind you, for the prescribed distance — typically 20–40 metres per set. | בסוף המרחק עצור בצורה מבוקרת, אפס את העמידה, ואז נוח או הפוך כיוון לסט הבא. | אחרי שסיימת את כל הסטים, נתק את הרתמה מרצועת הגרירה לפני הסרת פלטות המשקל מהמזחלת.

t: Attach two handles or straps to the front anchor points of the power sled and load it with an appropriate amount of weight plates. | Face the sled and pick up both handles, holding one in each hand with a neutral grip, arms extended in front of you toward the sled. | Step back far enough to put light tension on the straps before you begin. | Stand with your feet hip-width apart, a slight bend in your knees, and your torso inclined slightly forward from the hips — roughly 30 to 45 degrees. | Brace your core and retract your shoulder blades slightly to set a stable upper-back position. | With your elbows slightly soft, sweep both arms out to your sides in a wide arc, pulling the straps taut and dragging the sled toward you. | Continue the arc until your arms are roughly in line with your shoulders, squeezing the rear deltoids and upper back at the end of the movement. | Step backward to restore strap tension and reset for the next rep, or walk backward continuously while performing successive fly repetitions. | Complete all reps for the set, then set the handles down and step away from the sled safely.
tRu: Прикрепите две рукояти или лямки к передним точкам крепления саней и нагрузите сани нужным количеством дисков. | Face the sled and pick up both handles, holding one in each hand with a neutral grip, arms extended in front of you toward the sled. | Step back far enough to put light tension on the straps before you begin. | Stand with your feet hip-width apart, a slight bend in your knees, and your torso inclined slightly forward from the hips — roughly 30 to 45 degrees. | Напрягите корпус и слегка сведите лопатки, чтобы занять устойчивое положение верха спины. | With your elbows slightly soft, sweep both arms out to your sides in a wide arc, pulling the straps taut and dragging the sled toward you. | Продолжайте дугу, пока ваши руки не окажутся примерно на уровне плеч, сжимая задние дельты и верхнюю часть спины в конце движения. | Step backward to restore strap tension and reset for the next rep, or walk backward continuously while performing successive fly repetitions. | Выполните все повторения в подходе, затем положите рукоятки и безопасно отойдите от санок.
tHe: חבר שתי ידיות או רצועות לנקודות העיגון הקדמיות של מזחלת הכוח והעמס עליה כמות מתאימה של צלחות משקל. | Face the sled and pick up both handles, holding one in each hand with a neutral grip, arms extended in front of you toward the sled. | Step back far enough to put light tension on the straps before you begin. | Stand with your feet hip-width apart, a slight bend in your knees, and your torso inclined slightly forward from the hips — roughly 30 to 45 degrees. | הדק את הליבה וכנס קלות את השכמות כדי לקבע תנוחת גב עליון יציבה. | With your elbows slightly soft, sweep both arms out to your sides in a wide arc, pulling the straps taut and dragging the sled toward you. | Continue the arc until your arms are roughly in line with your shoulders, squeezing the rear deltoids and upper back at the end of the movement. | Step backward to restore strap tension and reset for the next rep, or walk backward continuously while performing successive fly repetitions. | בצע את כל החזרות לסט, ואף צעד אחורה לעבר העוגן לפני שחרור הידיות.

t: Attach a pulling harness or waist belt to the power sled's tow strap and load the sled with an appropriate weight. | Put the harness on and step far enough away from the sled so the strap is taut but not pulling you backward when you stand upright. | Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, core braced, and shoulders back. | Step one foot backward, placing the ball of that foot on the ground approximately two to three feet behind you. | Lower your rear knee toward the floor by bending both knees simultaneously, stopping when the rear knee is just above or lightly touches the ground. | Keep your front shin as vertical as possible and your torso upright throughout the descent. | Drive through the heel of your front foot to stand back up, pulling against the sled's resistance as you return to the starting position. | Complete all reps on one leg before switching, or alternate legs each rep depending on the protocol. | At the end of the set, step forward toward the sled to release strap tension before removing the harness.

tHe: חבר רתמת משיכה או חגורת מותניים לרצועת הגרירה של מזחלת הכוח והעמס על המזחלת משקל מתאים. | Put the harness on and step far enough away from the sled so the strap is taut but not pulling you backward when you stand upright. | Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, core braced, and shoulders back. | Step one foot backward, placing the ball of that foot on the ground approximately two to three feet behind you. | Lower your rear knee toward the floor by bending both knees simultaneously, stopping when the rear knee is just above or lightly touches the ground. | Keep your front shin as vertical as possible and your torso upright throughout the descent. | Drive through the heel of your front foot to stand back up, pulling against the sled's resistance as you return to the starting position. | בצע את כל החזרות עם רגל אחת לפני החלפה, או החלף בין הרגליים בכל חזרה בהתאם לפרוטוקול. | בסוף הסט צעד קדימה לכיוון המזחלת כדי לשחרר את מתח הרצועות לפני הסרת הרתמה.

t: Attach a hip harness around your waist or grip the sled handles, then position yourself facing away from the loaded power sled with the straps or handles taut. | Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, shoulders back, and core braced to create a stable base before the first step. | Step one foot backward — far enough that when your back knee descends, your front shin stays close to vertical. | Lower your back knee toward the ground in a controlled descent, stopping 1–2 inches above the floor as your body weight pulls the sled forward. | Drive through your front heel to return to a standing position, bringing your feet back to hip-width apart. | Alternate legs each rep, or complete all reps on one side before switching — follow your program's prescribed pattern. | Maintain an upright torso and level hips throughout; avoid twisting toward the stepping leg. | After your final rep, step toward the sled to release tension before setting down the handles or unclipping the harness.
tRu: Закрепите поясную упряжь на талии или возьмитесь за рукояти саней, затем встаньте спиной к нагруженным саням, натянув лямки или рукояти. | Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, shoulders back, and core braced to create a stable base before the first step. | Step one foot backward — far enough that when your back knee descends, your front shin stays close to vertical. | Lower your back knee toward the ground in a controlled descent, stopping 1–2 inches above the floor as your body weight pulls the sled forward. | Отталкивайтесь пяткой передней ноги, чтобы вернуться в положение стоя, возвращая ноги на ширину таза. | Чередуйте ноги каждое повторение или выполните все повторения на одну сторону перед сменой — следуйте схеме вашей программы. | Maintain an upright torso and level hips throughout; avoid twisting toward the stepping leg. | После последнего повторения шагните к саням, чтобы снять натяжение, затем опустите рукояти или отстегните ремни.
tHe: חבר רתמת אגן סביב המותניים או אחוז בידיות המזחלת, ואז עמוד עם הגב למזחלת הכוח העמוסה כשהרצועות או הידיות מתוחות. | Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, shoulders back, and core braced to create a stable base before the first step. | Step one foot backward — far enough that when your back knee descends, your front shin stays close to vertical. | Lower your back knee toward the ground in a controlled descent, stopping 1–2 inches above the floor as your body weight pulls the sled forward. | Drive through your front heel to return to a standing position, bringing your feet back to hip-width apart. | החלף רגליים בכל חזרה, או בצע את כל החזרות בצד אחד לפני ההחלפה — פעל לפי הדפוס שנקבע בתוכנית. | Maintain an upright torso and level hips throughout; avoid twisting toward the stepping leg. | לאחר החזרה האחרונה, צעד לעבר המזחלת כדי לשחרר את המתח לפני הנחת הידיות או ניתוק הרתמה.

t: Attach long straps or handles to the power sled's harness point and load the sled with an appropriate amount of weight plates. | Stand facing the sled at the far end of the straps with your feet hip-width apart, arms extended in front of you holding the handles with a neutral or overhand grip. | Take up the slack in the straps so there is light tension on the sled before you begin. | Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and step one foot back into a reverse lunge, lowering your rear knee toward the floor. | As you descend into the lunge, simultaneously row both handles toward your hips or lower chest by driving your elbows back behind you. | Pause at the bottom of the lunge with your front thigh roughly parallel to the floor and the handles pulled fully in, squeezing your shoulder blades together. | Push through your front foot to stand back up, straightening the knee and hip, while returning your arms to the extended starting position under control. | Alternate legs each rep or complete all reps on one side before switching, depending on your training goal. | Set the handles down safely once the set is complete and step away from the sled.
tRu: Прикрепите длинные лямки или рукояти к точке крепления упряжи саней и нагрузите сани нужным количеством дисков. | Stand facing the sled at the far end of the straps with your feet hip-width apart, arms extended in front of you holding the handles with a neutral or overhand grip. | Take up the slack in the straps so there is light tension on the sled before you begin. | Напрягите корпус, держите грудь расправленной и шагните одной ногой назад в обратный выпад, опуская заднее колено к полу. | Опускаясь в выпад, одновременно потяните обе рукояти к бёдрам или нижней части груди, уводя локти назад за спину. | Pause at the bottom of the lunge with your front thigh roughly parallel to the floor and the handles pulled fully in, squeezing your shoulder blades together. | Push through your front foot to stand back up, straightening the knee and hip, while returning your arms to the extended starting position under control. | Чередуйте ноги каждое повторение или выполните все повторения на одну сторону перед сменой, в зависимости от цели тренировки. | Set the handles down safely once the set is complete and step away from the sled.
tHe: חבר רצועות ארוכות או ידיות לנקודת הרתמה של מזחלת הכוח והעמס על המזחלת כמות מתאימה של צלחות משקל. | Stand facing the sled at the far end of the straps with your feet hip-width apart, arms extended in front of you holding the handles with a neutral or overhand grip. | Take up the slack in the straps so there is light tension on the sled before you begin. | הדק את הליבה, שמור על חזה גבוה וצעד עם רגל אחת לאחור ללאנג׳ לאחור, תוך הורדת הברך האחורית לכיוון הרצפה. | בירידה ללאנג׳, חתור בו־זמנית עם שתי הידיות לעבר האגן או החזה התחתון על ידי דחיפת המרפקים אחורה מאחוריך. | Pause at the bottom of the lunge with your front thigh roughly parallel to the floor and the handles pulled fully in, squeezing your shoulder blades together. | Push through your front foot to stand back up, straightening the knee and hip, while returning your arms to the extended starting position under control. | החלף רגליים בכל חזרה או בצע את כל החזרות בצד אחד לפני ההחלפה, בהתאם למטרת האימון. | Set the handles down safely once the set is complete and step away from the sled.

t: Attach two handles or loops to the sled's strap anchors so you have one grip point for each hand. | Load the sled with an appropriate amount of weight and position yourself facing the sled at the far end of the straps. | Hinge forward slightly at the hips — roughly 15–30 degrees — so your torso is angled toward the sled and your upper arms are close to your sides. | Grip both handles with a neutral or overhand grip, elbows bent and hands near your chest at the start of each rep. | Brace your core and keep your spine neutral throughout the set. | Drive your hands back and downward by straightening your elbows fully, pushing against the strap tension and drawing the sled toward you. | Pause briefly at full elbow extension to maximise triceps activation. | Return your hands to the starting position under control, allowing the sled to settle before the next rep. | Complete all reps for the set, then release the handles and step clear of the sled safely.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides, and your core lightly braced. | Begin jogging in place, then exaggerate the knee lift so each thigh rises to at least parallel with the floor on every stride. | As one knee drives up, swing the opposite arm forward to shoulder height to maintain balance and rhythm. | Land each foot on the ball of your foot rather than your heel, allowing the ankle to absorb impact softly before your heel briefly kisses the floor. | Keep the contact time short: spring back off the ground immediately, aiming for a light, bouncy feel rather than heavy stomping. | Maintain an upright torso — do not lean back or hunch forward; keep your chest open and gaze forward. | Control your breathing by matching your inhale and exhale to the rhythm of your strides. | Continue for the target duration or rep count, then slow gradually to a jog-in-place and return to standing.

t: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and a slight bend in the knees, or sit upright on a bench with feet flat on the floor. | Bring both palms together in front of your chest at sternum height, fingers pointing upward and elbows bent and angled down. | Press your palms firmly against each other to create isometric tension through the shoulders and chest. | Brace your core and keep your spine neutral so your lower back does not arch. | While maintaining palm-to-palm pressure, push your hands upward and forward in a controlled arc until your arms are fully extended overhead. | Hold the top position for one count with palms still pressed together and arms straight. | Lower your hands back down along the same arc, keeping continuous palm pressure throughout the descent. | Return to the starting position at chest height and pause briefly before the next repetition. | Complete the desired number of reps, then relax the arms and release the palm pressure.

t: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and toes turned out at roughly 45 degrees. | Bring your palms together at chest height in a prayer position (thumbs lightly touching your sternum). | Take a breath in, then on the exhale begin to lower your hips straight down toward the floor, keeping your chest tall and spine neutral. | Continue descending until your hips drop below knee level and your elbows are inside your knees. | Press your elbows gently outward against the inner thighs to encourage the knees to track over the toes and open the hips wider. | Keep your heels flat on the floor; if they rise, widen your stance slightly or place a folded mat under your heels for support. | Lift your chest, lengthen through the crown of your head, and breathe deeply, relaxing deeper into the stretch on each exhale. | Hold the position for 30–60 seconds, continuing to breathe slowly and evenly. | To exit, press through your heels, engage your glutes, and slowly rise back to standing.
