t: Set the preacher bench to a height where the upper arms rest flat on the pad with the armpits just clearing the top edge. | Load the EZ barbell with a light-to-moderate weight and grip the inner angled grips with an underhand (supinated) hold. | Rest both upper arms on the pad, let the bar hang at arm's length, and feel what the wrong position is: allow your wrists to bend backward (extend) under the bar's weight so the knuckles point toward the floor — notice the strain this creates. | Now actively correct your wrists: flex them very slightly or hold them neutral so they stay in line with your forearms and the bar sits across the base of your fingers rather than your palm. | Brace your core, keep your shoulders down, and maintain this neutral wrist position throughout the set. | Curl the bar upward by bending at the elbows, driving your forearms toward your upper arms while keeping the wrists locked in the neutral position — do not let them collapse back into extension as the weight increases. | Pause briefly at the top when your forearms are near vertical and confirm that your wrists are still neutral. | Lower the bar slowly and under control back to full elbow extension, continuing to hold the wrists neutral during the descent. | Complete the set, then re-check your wrist position on the last few reps, as fatigue is when the wrists are most likely to drift back into the wrong position.

t: Stand with your feet at hip-width, toes turned out slightly — the same foot position you use for your clean or snatch receiving stance. | Raise both arms directly overhead into your receiving position: shoulder-width apart for the snatch, or just outside shoulder-width for the clean and jerk. | Actively push your hands upward, engaging your deltoids, upper back, and triceps so your arms are under tension — not just held up passively. | Begin to lower yourself into a quarter to half squat, keeping your torso as upright as possible and your heels flat on the floor. | As you descend, drive your hands harder upward — press yourself under the imaginary bar rather than letting yourself fall. Think: push the ceiling while the floor pushes back. | Reach the bottom of your squat with both elbows fully locked out, wrists neutral, and shoulder blades actively engaged upward. | Hold the locked-out overhead position for 1–2 seconds, reinforcing proprioception and stability in the receiving position. | Stand back up while maintaining the overhead lockout, then lower your arms in a controlled manner before resetting for the next rep.

t: Lie on your right side on a flat surface with your hips and knees bent to roughly 90 degrees. | Stack your knees and keep your head resting on your right arm or a folded towel. | Bring your left knee forward toward the floor in front of you, letting it drop as far as is comfortable without lifting your right hip. | Reach your left arm straight up toward the ceiling. | Slowly rotate your left shoulder back toward the floor behind you, allowing your thoracic spine to rotate while your hips stay as stable as possible. | Let your left arm rest on the floor behind you, or as close to the floor as your range of motion allows. | Hold the position for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the gluteus medius and obliques to release with each exhale. | Return to the starting position, then repeat on the opposite side. | Perform 2 to 3 holds per side.

t: Kneel upright on a mat with your knees hip-width apart and your toes pointing behind you. Interlace your fingers and place both hands behind your head (prisoner position). Keep your chest tall and core braced throughout. | Step your right foot forward, planting it flat on the floor so your right knee is directly above your right ankle — you are now in a half-kneeling position. | Drive through your right heel and left toes to push your hips forward and upward, bringing your left foot up beside your right foot so you are standing fully upright. | Pause briefly at the top with hips extended, glutes squeezed, and hands still behind your head. | Reverse the movement by stepping your left foot back and lowering your left knee to the floor with control. | Then step your right foot back and lower your right knee to the floor, returning to the starting kneeling position. | That is one repetition. On the next rep, lead with the opposite foot (left foot steps forward first) to train both sides equally. | Continue alternating the leading leg for the desired number of repetitions or complete all reps on one side before switching.

t: Lie on your back with your knees bent at roughly 90° and your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Interlace your fingers and place your hands behind your head, with your elbows flared wide and pointing toward the ceiling — this is the prisoner position. | Brace your core by drawing your navel gently toward your spine, and press your lower back lightly into the floor. | Exhale and curl your head and shoulders off the floor, leading with your chest rather than your chin. | Continue raising your torso until it is at roughly 30–45° from the floor — do not sit all the way up. | Hold the top position for one count, keeping your elbows wide and your chin neutral (not tucked hard or jutting forward). | Inhale and lower your torso back to the floor under control, vertebra by vertebra, until your shoulder blades touch the floor. | Reset your brace and repeat for the target number of reps.

t: Start in a standard push-up position with your arms straight, body in a rigid line from head to heels, and toes on the floor. | Walk your hands backward so they rest beside your lower ribs or near your hips, with fingers pointing toward your feet or angled outward. | Protract your scapulae and push the floor away so your upper back rounds slightly — this engages the serratus anterior and begins the lean. | Shift your shoulders forward over or past your hands by leaning your entire body at an angle; the greater the forward lean, the closer you simulate planche mechanics. | Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso — roughly 30–45 degrees from your sides — to protect your shoulders and engage the triceps brachii. | Brace your rectus abdominis and obliques hard to prevent your hips from sagging or piking, maintaining a hollow-body alignment. | Lower your chest toward the floor under control by bending your elbows, keeping the forward lean constant throughout the descent. | Press back up to full arm extension, maintaining protraction and the lean angle throughout the push. | Complete your reps, then step your hands back to a neutral position to release.

t: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and grip it slightly wider than shoulder-width with an overhand grip, wrapping your thumbs fully around the bar. | Jump or step up using a box so your chin clears the bar and your elbows are bent at the top of the pull-up position. | Engage your core, retract your shoulder blades, and cross your ankles to keep your body stable and free of swing. | Begin lowering yourself slowly and under control, aiming for a descent of 3–5 seconds. | Keep your lats engaged throughout the descent — resist the urge to let gravity do the work. | Continue lowering until your arms are fully extended and your shoulders are in a dead-hang position. | Carefully drop down from the bar or use a box to reset, then repeat for the target number of reps.

nE: Pull-up with Bent Knee between Chairs
nR: Подтягивания с согнутыми коленями между стульями
nH: מתח עם ברך כפופה בין כיסאות
t: Position two sturdy, heavy chairs back-to-back or side by side with a gap between them wide enough to fit your torso. The chair backs or seats you grip must be at a height that allows your arms to be fully extended when you hang below them with bent knees. | Stand between the chairs and grip the top of each chair back (or the seat edges) with an overhand grip, hands roughly shoulder-width apart. Test that both chairs are stable and will not slide before loading your full bodyweight. | Lower yourself until your arms are fully extended and lift your feet off the floor by bending your knees to roughly 90 degrees, crossing your ankles if that helps keep your legs tucked. | Brace your core, depress your shoulder blades, and pull yourself upward by driving your elbows down and back toward your hips. | Continue pulling until your chin clears the level of your hands or your chest approaches the grip point — whichever range your shoulder mobility and chair height allow. | Pause briefly at the top with your shoulder blades fully retracted and depressed. | Lower yourself with control over 2–3 seconds until your arms are fully extended again. | That is one repetition. Keep your knees bent and feet off the floor for the entire set. | Complete the desired number of repetitions, then carefully place your feet back on the floor before releasing the chairs.

t: Lie face down on a mat with your arms extended overhead and your forehead resting on the floor, or hinge forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. | Pull your shoulder blades down and together before you begin, and keep that tension throughout the set. | Initiate the movement by squeezing your shoulder blades and rowing both arms back toward your hips, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45–60° angle from your torso. | Continue rowing until your hands are in line with your lower ribs and your elbows are pulled as far back as comfortable — this is the top of the range. | At the top position, perform 3–5 small, controlled pulses: move your arms an inch or two back and forward without losing shoulder-blade retraction or dropping the hands below the starting height. | Keep your neck neutral — do not crank your head up during the pulses. | After completing the pulses, slowly lower your arms back to the starting position under control. | That counts as one repetition. Repeat for the target number of reps.

t: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your arms resting at your sides, palms facing down. | Raise both legs until they are vertical, pointing straight up toward the ceiling at roughly 90° to the floor. | Press your lower back firmly into the floor and engage your core before you begin. | Exhale and contract your abs to lift your hips and legs directly upward in a small, controlled pulse — your feet should rise a few inches toward the ceiling. | Avoid swinging or using momentum; the movement should come entirely from your abdominals. | Lower your hips back to the floor with control, keeping your legs vertical throughout. | Reset your lower-back contact with the floor before initiating the next rep.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, hands raised in a loose guard position at chin height. | Step your right foot forward into a split-stance, lowering your hips into a shallow lunge position as your right knee tracks over your right toes. | Simultaneously drive your left fist forward in a straight punch, extending the arm fully while rotating your left shoulder toward the target. | Keep your core braced and your torso upright throughout the punch-and-step. | Push off your right foot to drive back to the starting position, returning your left fist to the guard. | Immediately step your left foot forward into a split-stance and punch with your right fist, mirroring the motion on the opposite side. | Continue alternating sides in a smooth, rhythmic pattern, matching the pace to your target heart rate or drill speed. | Complete the prescribed time or rep count, then bring your feet together and lower your hands to finish.

t: Begin on all fours with your knees hip-width apart and your hips directly above your knees. | Place your hands shoulder-width apart and spread your fingers wide to distribute weight evenly. | Slowly walk your hands forward along the mat, keeping your hips over your knees throughout the movement. | Lower your chest toward the floor, allowing your forehead or chin to rest gently on the mat. | Let your arms remain extended and your elbows lift slightly off the ground rather than collapsing to the sides. | Press the backs of your hands lightly into the mat and draw the shoulder blades apart to broaden across the upper back. | Breathe steadily, allowing the chest to sink deeper with each exhale without forcing the movement. | Hold the position for 30 to 60 seconds, or as long as comfortable tension can be maintained without pain. | To exit, walk your hands back toward your knees and return to the all-fours starting position.

t: Start in a kneeling or quadruped position on the floor with your hips stacked above your knees and your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart. | Shift your hips back toward your heels to create space and allow your torso to lower toward the floor. | Extend both arms straight out in front of you, pressing your palms flat against the floor. | Push your hands actively into the floor and reach your fingertips as far forward as possible. | Allow your chest to drop toward the floor and your upper back to round and spread, letting the stretch deepen between your shoulder blades. | Keep your arms straight and your elbows off the floor throughout the hold. | Breathe deeply, exhaling to relax further into the stretch on each breath. | Hold the position for 20–40 seconds, then gently walk your hands back and return to the starting position.

nE: Push-up and Triceps Dip on Parallel Bars
nH: שכיבות סמיכה ומקבילים ליד אחורית על מקבילים
t: Set the parallel bars at a height that allows you to perform a push-up between them with your chest at bar level — low, floor-level bars or dip bars positioned close to the ground work best. | Place your hands on the bars slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers pointing forward, and extend your legs behind you into a plank position with your core braced. | Lower your chest down between the bars by bending your elbows, keeping them at roughly a 45° angle to your torso rather than flaring them out. | Press back up explosively until your arms are fully extended, squeezing your chest at the top of the push-up. | Shift your weight onto your hands and straighten your arms fully to lift your body up so you are supporting yourself above the bars in the top dip position. | Bend your elbows and lower your body in a controlled manner until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the bars, keeping your torso upright and elbows tracking behind you. | Press back up through your palms until your arms are fully locked out to complete the triceps dip. | Lower back down into the push-up position with control to begin the next repetition.

t: Place two dumbbells side by side on the floor with their handles parallel and close together — roughly 6–10 inches apart, well inside shoulder-width — hex dumbbells are ideal because they will not roll. | Kneel behind the dumbbells, grip both handles firmly with a neutral (palms facing each other) wrist position, and step your feet back into a high plank so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. | Position yourself so the handles sit under your upper chest with your wrists stacked over them, hands roughly 6–10 inches apart and just inside your shoulder line. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and tuck your elbows so they point back toward your hips rather than flaring to the sides. | Inhale and lower your chest in a controlled manner toward the dumbbells, keeping your elbows tracking close to your torso throughout the descent. | Descend until your chest is just above or lightly touches the handles, feeling a stretch through the triceps and chest at the bottom. | Press forcefully through both dumbbell handles to drive your body back to the starting position, exhaling as you push. | Fully extend the elbows at the top without locking them aggressively, and reset your brace before the next repetition. | Complete the desired number of repetitions, then lower your knees to the floor in a controlled manner to dismount safely.

t: Begin on the floor in a high plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your arms fully extended. | Demonstrate the WRONG position first: allow your lower back to sag toward the floor, let your hips drop, and round or shrug your shoulders up toward your ears so you can clearly feel the difference. | Take note of how the incorrect position collapses the core and places excessive strain on the lower back and shoulder joints. | Reset to the CORRECT top position: press the floor away and straighten your arms fully, creating a rigid line from your head through your hips to your heels. | Squeeze your glutes and brace your core so your hips neither sag nor pike up above the line of your spine. | Pull your shoulder blades apart slightly (protract) and keep your shoulders packed down away from your ears to fully engage the chest and stabilize the shoulder girdle. | Hold the correct lockout for 2–3 seconds, consciously feeling the chest, anterior shoulders, and triceps engaged, then lower into the next rep or release.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides. | Hinge at your hips and bend your knees slightly as you reach both hands toward the floor in front of your feet. | Once your hands touch the floor, walk them forward one at a time until your body forms a straight plank — hands directly under your shoulders, core braced, hips level. | Hold the plank position for one to two seconds, feeling the stretch across your chest and through your hips. | Optionally lower your chest toward the floor in a push-up and press back up to reinforce the chest stretch. | Walk your hands back toward your feet in small steps, keeping your knees soft. | Once your hands are back near your feet, drive through your legs and roll up through your spine to return to a tall standing position. | Reset your posture at the top and repeat for the desired number of reps.

t: Start in a high push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart, body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core and keep your hips level throughout the movement. | Lower your chest toward the floor under control, then press back up to the starting position. | At the top of the rep, move your right hand one step to the right, then bring your left hand to meet it so both hands are in the new position. | Perform another push-up from this new hand position. | Move your hands one step further to the right in the same hand-by-hand manner, then perform another push-up. | After completing the desired number of reps or distance in one direction, reverse the lateral sequence back to the starting position. | Continue for the prescribed reps or sets, alternating the traveling direction each set if desired.

t: Start in child's pose: kneel on the floor, sit your hips back toward your heels, and extend both arms straight out in front of you with palms flat on the floor, forehead hovering near the ground. | Spread your fingers wide and press your palms firmly into the floor to create a stable base. | Engage your core and begin to shift your weight forward, sliding your chest toward the floor and transitioning into a low push-up position — hips near the ground, elbows bent at roughly 45–75° to your torso. | From the bottom of the push-up, press through your palms to straighten your arms and lift your chest, finishing in a high plank on your knees. | Keep your body in a straight line from knees to shoulders at the top; avoid letting your hips sag or your lower back arch excessively. | Hold the top position for a brief moment, then lower your hips back toward your heels to return to child's pose. | Let your arms stay extended and your chest drop toward the floor as you settle fully into child's pose. | Pause in child's pose to reset your breath, then repeat for the desired number of reps.

t: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Engage your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips level — they should not sag toward the floor or pike upward. | Begin lowering your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso. | As you lower down, jump both feet out wide simultaneously — landing softly with your feet wider than hip-width, as you would at the bottom of a jumping jack. | Descend until your chest nearly touches the floor, keeping your elbows from flaring out to 90 degrees. | Press through your palms to extend your arms back to the starting position. | As you push up, jump both feet back together so they return to their starting position at the top of the rep. | Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower down, maintaining a controlled tempo throughout. | Continue for the desired number of repetitions, landing softly on the balls of your feet each time to protect your joints.
tRu: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Напрягите корпус и сожмите ягодицы, чтобы держать бёдра на одном уровне — они не должны опускаться к полу или подниматься вверх. | Начните опускать грудь к полу, сгибая локти под углом примерно 45 градусов к корпусу. | Опускаясь, прыжком одновременно расставьте обе ноги широко — мягко приземлитесь на стопы шире бёдер, как в нижней точке прыжка «джек». | Опускайтесь, пока локти не образуют примерно прямой угол, сохраняя спину близко к скамье на протяжении всего движения. | Press through your palms to extend your arms back to the starting position. | Отжимаясь, прыжком сведите обе ноги обратно вместе, чтобы в верхней точке повтора вернуться в исходное положение. | Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower down, maintaining a controlled tempo throughout. | Продолжайте в течение заданного количества повторений, приземляясь мягко на носки при каждом повторении, чтобы защитить суставы.

t: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and set your feet hip-width apart. | Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso. | Press through your palms to return to the top of the push-up position. | As you reach the top, drive one knee toward your chest, keeping your hips level with your spine. | Return that foot to the starting position to restore full plank alignment. | Immediately lower into the next push-up rep. | On the next push-up lockout, drive the opposite knee to your chest, alternating sides each rep. | Continue the push-up and knee-drive sequence at a controlled, rhythmic pace for the prescribed duration or rep count.

nH: שכיבות סמיכה (יד אחת על כדור פיזיו)
t: Place a stability ball on the floor and kneel behind it to set your starting position. | Place one hand flat on top of the stability ball and the other hand on the floor, spacing your hands roughly shoulder-width apart so one arm is elevated. | Step your feet back into a full push-up position, forming a straight line from head to heels with your core braced. | Squeeze your glutes and engage your abs to prevent your hips from sagging or rotating toward the ball side. | Lower your chest toward the floor by bending both elbows, keeping the elbow of the hand on the ball tucked at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | Descend until your chest is roughly level with the hand on the ball, or until you reach your full comfortable range of motion. | Press firmly through both hands to extend your arms and return to the starting position. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch so your other hand is on the stability ball and repeat.

t: Lie face down and place your forearms flat on the floor, elbows directly beneath your shoulders and forearms parallel to each other. | Press through your forearms to lift your body so it forms a straight line from your head to your heels, as in a forearm plank. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your hips level — do not let them sag or pike. | While keeping your forearms in contact with the floor, push your body upward by extending your elbows, driving through the forearms and letting your torso rise. | Continue pressing until your elbows are as straight as your range allows and your torso is lifted, keeping the line from head to heels intact. | Lower your body under control by bending your elbows, returning your torso toward the floor until you reach the starting forearm-plank position. | Reset your brace and repeat for the desired number of reps.

nH: שכיבות סמיכה פייק עם נגיעה בבהונות
t: Start in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows at roughly a 45° angle to your torso. | Press explosively back up to the high plank position, fully extending your arms. | Immediately push your hips up and back, forming an inverted V (pike position) while keeping your arms and legs as straight as possible. | At the top of the pike, lift your right hand off the floor and reach across to touch your left foot or left ankle. | Return your hand to the floor, lower your hips back to the high plank position, and brace your core. | Perform another push-up, pike again, and this time reach your left hand to touch your right foot. | Continue alternating sides for the desired number of reps or time.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides. | Hinge at the hips, bend your knees, and place both hands on the floor just outside your feet. | Jump or step your feet back simultaneously so you land in a high plank — hands directly under your shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels. | Perform one push-up: lower your chest to the floor by bending your elbows, then press back up to the high plank position. | From the top of the push-up, jump both feet out wide (like the bottom of a jumping jack) and then immediately jump them back together — this is the plank jack. | Jump or step your feet forward toward your hands, returning to the low squat position. | Drive through your legs and swing your arms overhead to explode into a vertical jump, fully extending your body at the top. | Land softly with bent knees to absorb the impact, and immediately lower back into the starting position for the next rep.

t: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to lock in a neutral spine before any movement begins. | Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso. | Press through both palms explosively to return to the top of the push-up position. | At the top, shift your weight onto your left hand and lift your right hand off the floor. | Drive your right elbow up and back, pulling your right hand toward your right hip in a rowing motion. | Lower your right hand back to the floor with control and re-establish a stable plank. | Perform the next push-up, then repeat the pull on the left side, alternating arms each rep. | Continue alternating for the prescribed number of reps or duration, maintaining plank alignment throughout.

t: Stand behind your mat and decide on your hand-placement width — directly under your shoulders, fingers pointing forward or slightly outward. | Place your hands on the floor at the chosen width, then step both feet back until your body forms a straight line from head to heel — this is the correct plank start. | Check that your hips are neither sagging toward the floor nor piked up toward the ceiling; your spine should be neutral throughout. | Squeeze your glutes and brace your core as if bracing for a punch, locking the trunk into a single rigid unit. | Press the floor away with your palms so your shoulders are slightly protracted (pushed apart) rather than collapsing between your shoulder blades. | Align your head with your spine — chin slightly tucked, gaze directed a few inches in front of your hands, not straight down or craned upward. | Verify your elbows are fully extended but not hyperextended, with arms vertical when viewed from the side. | Take a breath in through the nose, hold it to reinforce spinal stiffness (Valsalva), and you are in the correct start position — ready to lower into the push-up. | For the WRONG position contrast: notice how a sagging lower back, flared elbows, raised hips, or a forward-jutting chin each compromise alignment — consciously avoid these before beginning any set.

t: Set up in a high plank position with your hands flat on the floor, slightly wider than shoulder-width, wrists under your shoulders, and feet hip-width apart. | Brace your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels before beginning any movement. | Inhale and lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso. | Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor, pausing briefly without collapsing your hips or arching your lower back. | Exhale and press explosively through your hands to return to the top of the push-up position. | Without pausing, use that momentum to pike your hips upward, shifting your weight onto one hand while lifting the other arm across your body toward the opposite foot. | Touch or reach as close as possible to your opposite foot, keeping both legs as straight as you can through the pike. | Return your hand to the floor and lower your hips back to a straight plank position — this is one rep. | Perform the next rep and reach with the other hand, alternating the toe touch side each rep.

tRu: Примите высокую планку с ладонями чуть шире плеч и запястьями строго под плечами, тело образует прямую линию от головы до пяток. | Напрягите корпус, сожмите ягодицы и удерживайте бёдра на одном уровне перед началом. | Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows at roughly a 45° angle to your torso, keeping your body rigid throughout. | Мощно выжмитесь вверх, пока руки полностью не выпрямятся. | В верхней точке отжимания слегка перенесите вес на одну руку и подтяните колено к груди или к противоположному локтю для варианта крест-накрест. | Hold the knee drive for a brief pause, feeling your abs and hip flexors contract. | Return the foot to the starting plank position with control. | Perform the next push-up and repeat the knee drive on the opposite side, or alternate sides each rep as desired. | Продолжайте в течение заданного количества повторений, затем опустите поднятую ногу на пол и поменяйте ноги, повторив ту же последовательность с другой стороны.
tHe: התחל בפלאנק גבוה עם ידיים מעט רחבות מרוחב הכתפיים, שורשי כף היד מתחת לכתפיים, והגוף יוצר קו ישר מהראש ועד העקבים. | הדק את הליבה, כווץ את הישבן, ושמור על אגן מאוזן לפני תחילת התרגיל. | Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows at roughly a 45° angle to your torso, keeping your body rigid throughout. | לחץ חזרה למעלה בצורה מתפרצת עד שהידיים ישרות לגמרי. | בשיא שכיבת הסמיכה העבר מעט את המשקל ליד אחת ומשוך ברך אחת לכיוון החזה או לכיוון המרפק הנגדי בווריאציית האלכסון. | Hold the knee drive for a brief pause, feeling your abs and hip flexors contract. | Return the foot to the starting plank position with control. | Perform the next push-up and repeat the knee drive on the opposite side, or alternate sides each rep as desired. | Continue for the target number of reps, maintaining a neutral spine and level hips throughout.

t: Place the push-up handles shoulder-width apart on a firm, non-slip surface with the grips parallel or angled slightly outward. | Grip the handles firmly and step into a high plank position: arms fully extended, hands under your shoulders, body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Squeeze your glutes, brace your core, and tuck your hips slightly to prevent your lower back from sagging. | Inhale and lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows at roughly a 45° angle to your torso — not flared straight out to the sides. | Continue lowering until your chest passes the level of the handles, taking advantage of the increased range of motion the bars provide. | Pause briefly at the bottom without resting your chest on the floor, keeping tension in your chest and shoulders. | Exhale and press through the handles, driving the floor away until your arms are fully extended at the top. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, maintaining a rigid plank position throughout every rep.

t: Place a sturdy, non-rolling chair on a flat surface and position yourself in front of it. | Place both hands on the front edge of the chair seat, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with fingers pointing forward. | Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels, with arms fully extended and core braced. | Squeeze your glutes and tighten your core to keep your hips level and your spine neutral throughout the movement. | Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the chair seat in a controlled manner, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso. | Lower until your chest nearly touches the edge of the chair, then pause briefly at the bottom. | Press through your palms to push your body back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms without locking your elbows. | Complete the desired number of repetitions while maintaining a rigid, plank-like body position throughout.

t: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a PVC pipe horizontally behind your back with both hands, palms facing away from your body. | Position your arms so the pipe rests across the back of your hips, with your elbows slightly bent and your grip about shoulder-width or slightly wider. | Brace your core lightly and keep your chest up and your shoulder blades gently retracted throughout the movement. | Slowly pull the pipe upward and away from your body by externally rotating both shoulders simultaneously, keeping your elbows close to your sides. | Continue lifting the pipe as high as your mobility allows without forcing the movement or shrugging your shoulders toward your ears. | Hold the top position for one to two seconds, feeling the contraction in your rotator cuff muscles. | Lower the pipe back down to the starting position in a controlled manner. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, moving smoothly through your full pain-free range of motion.

t: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hold a PVC pipe with a grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. | Bring the pipe to the front rack position: elbows raised to shoulder height, pipe resting across the front of your shoulders and upper chest. | Push your elbows up as high as possible while keeping the pipe in contact with your shoulders — do not let it drift forward. | With elbows raised, gently pull the ends of the pipe apart as if trying to widen it, creating outward tension. | Begin to squat or hinge slightly at the hips to load the stretch, keeping your chest up and your upper back engaged. | Hold the end position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the shoulder and thoracic tissues to relax into the stretch. | Lower your elbows slowly to release tension, then return to the starting position. | Repeat for 2–3 sets, focusing on progressively raising the elbows higher with each hold.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, toes pointing forward or slightly out, and place the stick across your upper traps — not your neck. | Grip the stick with both hands at a comfortable width outside your shoulders to keep it stable throughout the movement. | Brace your core lightly, maintain a neutral spine, and unlock your knees with a soft bend of about 15–20°. | Initiate the movement by pushing your hips straight back, not by bending your knees or rounding your lower back. | Hinge forward until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor, or until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings — whichever comes first. | Pause for a moment at the bottom, keeping your back flat and the stick level across your shoulders. | Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to the upright starting position. | Reset your brace and repeat for the target number of reps.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and toes pointing straight ahead or slightly out. | Hold a PVC stick (or dowel) vertically behind your back, gripping it with one hand at your lower back and the other behind your head. | Position the stick so it maintains three points of contact: the back of your head, between your shoulder blades, and your tailbone (sacrum). | Brace your core lightly, set your shoulders back and down, and keep your chest up before you move. | Initiate the movement by pushing your hips back — not by bending your knees — while keeping both feet flat on the floor. | Continue hinging until your torso approaches parallel to the floor, or until your hamstrings pull tight, whichever comes first. | Throughout the descent, verify that all three contact points remain on the stick and that your shins stay close to vertical. | Pause briefly at the bottom, then drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to a tall standing position. | Reset the stick contact points between reps before beginning the next repetition.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart or slightly wider, toes turned out 15–30 degrees. | Hold the PVC pipe with a wide snatch-width grip — hands well outside shoulder-width — and press it overhead until your arms are fully extended. | Rotate your shoulders outward to engage your upper back and pull the pipe apart slightly to create tension, keeping it directly above or just behind the crown of your head. | Brace your core, take a breath, and keep your chest tall before beginning the descent. | Push your knees out in line with your toes and sit your hips back and down simultaneously, descending into a full squat until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor. | Keep the pipe locked out overhead throughout the descent — do not let your arms drift forward or your elbows bend. | At the bottom, pause briefly to confirm your heels are flat, your chest is upright, and the pipe remains stacked above your feet. | Drive through your full foot to stand, keeping your knees tracking over your toes and the pipe locked out until you reach full hip and knee extension. | Reset your breath and brace before each rep.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and hold a PVC pipe in front of your thighs using a wide overhand grip — hands spaced well outside shoulder width. | Brace your core lightly and keep your elbows soft but not deeply bent throughout the movement. | Begin the forward pass by raising the pipe upward in a smooth arc, keeping your arms as straight as comfortably possible. | Continue the arc overhead, allowing your shoulders to rotate naturally as the pipe passes above your head. | Lower the pipe behind your back until it rests against your glutes or upper hamstrings, maintaining control throughout. | Pause briefly at the bottom of the behind-back position, then reverse the arc to bring the pipe back overhead and down to the starting position in front of your thighs. | That is one repetition. Perform 8–15 controlled reps, adjusting grip width as needed to complete the full range of motion.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, then step your right foot forward about 3–4 feet and your left foot back, keeping both feet flat on the floor. | Angle your back (left) foot out to roughly 45° to give your hips a stable base, and square your hips as much as possible toward the front of the mat. | Place your hands on your hips and draw your shoulder blades down and back to lengthen your spine. | On an inhale, grow tall through the crown of your head, creating as much length in the torso as possible. | On an exhale, hinge at the hips — not the waist — and fold your torso forward over your front (right) leg, keeping your back flat. | Lower as far as your hamstring flexibility allows: rest your hands on your shin, ankle, the floor beside your foot, or on blocks for support. | Hold the position for 5–10 slow, steady breaths, relaxing deeper into the stretch with each exhale. | To come out, engage your core, press through both feet, and rise back up on an inhale with a flat back. | Step your feet together, then repeat on the opposite side with the left foot forward.

tHe: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, then step your right foot forward about 3–4 feet and your left foot back, keeping both feet flat on the floor. | הטה את כף הרגל האחורית (שמאל) החוצה לזווית של כ-45° כדי לתת לאגן בסיס יציב, ויישר את האגן ככל האפשר לקדמת המזרן. | Place your hands on your hips and draw your shoulder blades down and back to lengthen your spine. | On an inhale, grow tall through the crown of your head, creating as much length in the torso as possible. | On an exhale, hinge at the hips — not the waist — and fold your torso forward over your front (right) leg, keeping your back flat. | Lower as far as your hamstring flexibility allows: rest your hands on your shin, ankle, the floor beside your foot, or on blocks for support. | Hold the position for 5–10 slow, steady breaths, relaxing deeper into the stretch with each exhale. | To come out, engage your core, press through both feet, and rise back up on an inhale with a flat back. | Step your feet together, then repeat on the opposite side with the left foot forward.

t: Lie face-down on a flat surface with your legs extended and your forehead resting on your free hand or a folded towel. | Keep your hips pressed evenly into the floor and your core lightly engaged so your lower back stays neutral. | Bend your right knee, bringing your right heel toward your right glute. | Reach back with your right hand and grasp the top of your right foot or your ankle. | Gently pull your heel closer to your glute until you feel a firm stretch along the front of your right thigh — do not force the movement. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing the muscle to relax into the stretch. | Release your foot, straighten your right leg, and return to the starting position. | Repeat on the left side: bend the left knee, grasp the left foot or ankle with the left hand, and hold for 20–30 seconds. | Complete 2–3 rounds per side, resting briefly between rounds.
tRu: Lie face-down on a flat surface with your legs extended and your forehead resting on your free hand or a folded towel. | Keep your hips pressed evenly into the floor and your core lightly engaged so your lower back stays neutral. | Согните правое колено, подтягивая правую пятку к правой ягодице. | Reach back with your right hand and grasp the top of your right foot or your ankle. | Gently pull your heel closer to your glute until you feel a firm stretch along the front of your right thigh — do not force the movement. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing the muscle to relax into the stretch. | Release your foot, straighten your right leg, and return to the starting position. | Repeat on the left side: bend the left knee, grasp the left foot or ankle with the left hand, and hold for 20–30 seconds. | Выполните 2–3 круга на каждую сторону, делая короткие паузы между кругами.
tHe: Lie face-down on a flat surface with your legs extended and your forehead resting on your free hand or a folded towel. | Keep your hips pressed evenly into the floor and your core lightly engaged so your lower back stays neutral. | כופף את ברך ימין והבא את עקב ימין לכיוון העכוז הימני. | Reach back with your right hand and grasp the top of your right foot or your ankle. | Gently pull your heel closer to your glute until you feel a firm stretch along the front of your right thigh — do not force the movement. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing the muscle to relax into the stretch. | Release your foot, straighten your right leg, and return to the starting position. | Repeat on the left side: bend the left knee, grasp the left foot or ankle with the left hand, and hold for 20–30 seconds. | בצע 2–3 סבבים לכל צד, עם מנוחה קצרה בין הסבבים.

t: Stand tall with your feet together and your gaze fixed on a point ahead of you to help maintain balance. | Shift your weight onto your left foot and bend your right knee, bringing your right heel up toward your right glute. | Reach back with your right hand and grasp the top of your right foot or ankle. | Draw your right heel as close to your glute as comfortably possible while keeping your knees close together and your right knee pointing straight down. | Squeeze your glutes and keep your hips level — avoid letting the right hip hike up or rotate outward. | Stand tall through your spine; do not lean forward at the waist or arch your lower back excessively. | Breathe slowly and deeply, allowing the quadriceps to relax further with each exhale. Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds. | Release your foot gently, return to the starting position, then repeat on the opposite side.
tRu: Stand tall with your feet together and your gaze fixed on a point ahead of you to help maintain balance. | Shift your weight onto your left foot and bend your right knee, bringing your right heel up toward your right glute. | Отведите правую руку назад и захватите верхнюю часть правой стопы или лодыжку. | Приведите правую пятку как можно ближе к ягодице, сохраняя колени близко друг к другу и направив правое колено прямо вниз. | Squeeze your glutes and keep your hips level — avoid letting the right hip hike up or rotate outward. | Stand tall through your spine; do not lean forward at the waist or arch your lower back excessively. | Дышите медленно и глубоко, плавно углубляясь в растяжку с каждым выдохом, не форсируя ее. | Release your foot gently, return to the starting position, then repeat on the opposite side.
tHe: Stand tall with your feet together and your gaze fixed on a point ahead of you to help maintain balance. | Shift your weight onto your left foot and bend your right knee, bringing your right heel up toward your right glute. | הושט לאחור עם יד ימין ואחוז בחלק העליון של כף רגל ימין או בקרסול. | Draw your right heel as close to your glute as comfortably possible while keeping your knees close together and your right knee pointing straight down. | Squeeze your glutes and keep your hips level — avoid letting the right hip hike up or rotate outward. | Stand tall through your spine; do not lean forward at the waist or arch your lower back excessively. | נשיר לאט ועמוק, מאפשר לשרירי הירך הקדמיים להרפות עוד יותר עם כל נשימה. החזיקו את המתיחה למשך 20–30 שניות. | Release your foot gently, return to the starting position, then repeat on the opposite side.

t: Place a sturdy box or bench behind you at roughly knee height and stand about one step in front of it. | Shift your weight onto your left foot, reach back, and place the top of your right foot on the box so the laces face down. | Lower your right knee toward the floor, keeping your torso upright, until you feel a stretch along the front of your right thigh. | Position your left knee directly over your left ankle so your front shin stays vertical. | Place your hands on your left thigh or a stable surface for balance if needed. | Breathe out and gently deepen the stretch by pressing your hips slightly forward and down without arching your lower back. | Hold the stretch for 20 to 45 seconds, breathing steadily throughout. | Carefully step your right foot off the box, return to standing, and repeat on the opposite side.
tRu: Place a sturdy box or bench behind you at roughly knee height and stand about one step in front of it. | Shift your weight onto your left foot, reach back, and place the top of your right foot on the box so the laces face down. | Lower your right knee toward the floor, keeping your torso upright, until you feel a stretch along the front of your right thigh. | Position your left knee directly over your left ankle so your front shin stays vertical. | Place your hands on your left thigh or a stable surface for balance if needed. | Выдыхайте, когда позволяете колену занять положение, позволяя суставу расслабиться в этой позиции, не форсируя ее. | Hold the stretch for 20 to 45 seconds, breathing steadily throughout. | Осторожно сойдите с ящика правой ногой, встаньте прямо и повторите с противоположной стороны.

t: Position yourself on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, hip-width apart. | Brace your core and set your spine to neutral — your back should be flat, neither rounded nor overarched. | Lift your right knee off the floor and raise your thigh until it is roughly parallel with the floor, with the knee bent at approximately 90°. | From that position, actively curl your right heel toward your glutes by contracting your hamstring, flexing the knee as far as you can while keeping your thigh still. | Pause briefly at the top of the curl, squeezing the back of your thigh. | Lower your foot under control until your knee returns to the 90° starting position, keeping your thigh parallel to the floor throughout. | Complete all reps on the right leg, then switch to the left side and repeat for the same number of reps.
tRu: Position yourself on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, hip-width apart. | Напрягите корпус и займите нейтральное положение позвоночника: спина ровная, без округления и чрезмерного прогиба. | Lift your right knee off the floor and raise your thigh until it is roughly parallel with the floor, with the knee bent at approximately 90°. | From that position, actively curl your right heel toward your glutes by contracting your hamstring, flexing the knee as far as you can while keeping your thigh still. | Pause briefly at the top of the curl, squeezing the back of your thigh. | Lower your foot under control until your knee returns to the 90° starting position, keeping your thigh parallel to the floor throughout. | Выполните все повторения на правой ноге, затем поменяйте на левую сторону и повторите для того же количества повторений.
tHe: Position yourself on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, hip-width apart. | הדק את הליבה וקבע את עמוד השדרה לניטרלי — הגב צריך להיות שטוח, לא מעוגל ולא קשור יתר על המידה. | Lift your right knee off the floor and raise your thigh until it is roughly parallel with the floor, with the knee bent at approximately 90°. | From that position, actively curl your right heel toward your glutes by contracting your hamstring, flexing the knee as far as you can while keeping your thigh still. | Pause briefly at the top of the curl, squeezing the back of your thigh. | Lower your foot under control until your knee returns to the 90° starting position, keeping your thigh parallel to the floor throughout. | בצע את כל החזרות עם הרגל הימינה, ואז החלף לצד השמאל וחזור על אותו מספר חזרות.

t: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your weight balanced on the balls of your feet. | Begin running forward at a controlled pace, keeping your torso tall and your core lightly braced. | Bring your feet in toward the center with two quick, choppy steps, staying light on the balls of your feet. | Immediately step both feet back out to a stance just past shoulder-width with two more quick steps. | Continue alternating the in-out pattern — in, in, out, out — while inching forward and keeping your steps rapid and light. | Pump your arms in rhythm with your feet, keeping your elbows bent at roughly 90° and your hands relaxed. | Stay on the balls of your feet throughout; avoid letting your heels drop heavily with each contact. | Complete the drill for the prescribed distance or time, then decelerate gradually to a walk.
tRu: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your weight balanced on the balls of your feet. | Начните бег вперёд в контролируемом темпе, удерживая корпус высоким, а мышцы кора слегка напряжёнными. | Сведите ноги к центру двумя быстрыми резкими шагами, оставаясь на носках. | Immediately step both feet back out to a stance just past shoulder-width with two more quick steps. | Продолжайте поочередно выполнять паттерн «внутрь-внутрь-наружу-наружу», продвигаясь вперед, и делайте шаги быстрыми и легкими. | Pump your arms in rhythm with your feet, keeping your elbows bent at roughly 90° and your hands relaxed. | Stay on the balls of your feet throughout; avoid letting your heels drop heavily with each contact. | Выполните упражнение на заданную дистанцию или время, затем постепенно замедлитесь до ходьбы.
tHe: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your weight balanced on the balls of your feet. | התחל לרוץ קדימה בקצב מבוקר, תוך שמירה על גו זקוף וליבה מעט מהודקת. | הביא את הרגליים למרכז בשני צעדים מהירים וקצרים, נשאר קל עכשיו על כפות הרגליים. | Immediately step both feet back out to a stance just past shoulder-width with two more quick steps. | Continue alternating the in-out pattern — in, in, out, out — while inching forward and keeping your steps rapid and light. | Pump your arms in rhythm with your feet, keeping your elbows bent at roughly 90° and your hands relaxed. | Stay on the balls of your feet throughout; avoid letting your heels drop heavily with each contact. | בצע את התרגיל למרחק או לזמן המוגדר, ואפחות בהדרגה להליכה.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your weight balanced over the balls of your feet. | Hinge forward slightly at the hips — enough to keep your center of mass over the front of your feet without rounding your back. | Raise your arms to roughly a 90° bend at the elbows, the same position you would hold while jogging. | Begin alternating your feet in very short, rapid steps, lifting each foot just a few centimeters off the ground. | Drive your arms in a controlled back-and-forth swing in time with your feet to build rhythm and maintain balance. | Keep your steps as fast as possible while staying light on your feet — contact time with the ground should be minimal. | Breathe in a steady, rhythmic pattern throughout; do not hold your breath. | Maintain the drill for your target duration or rep count, then slow your feet gradually to a stop rather than stopping abruptly.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your weight balanced on the balls of your feet. | Engage your core and keep your torso upright with a slight forward lean at the hips. | Raise your arms to roughly waist height and bend your elbows at 90 degrees to help drive rhythm. | Begin alternating your feet as fast as possible, lifting each foot only 1–2 inches off the floor. | Keep your steps short and controlled — feet should land directly beneath your hips, not out in front. | Maintain continuous, rapid contact with the floor, avoiding any single large jump or bound. | Drive with your hip flexors and thighs to sustain the quick tempo throughout the set. | Continue for the prescribed duration (typically 10–30 seconds), then lower both feet flat to the floor and stand tall to recover.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and your spine tall. | Let your arms hang relaxed at your sides with your hands loosely open. | Brace your core lightly to keep your torso stable throughout the drill. | Begin swinging both arms forward and back simultaneously in a controlled but brisk pendulum motion. | On the forward swing, raise each arm to roughly shoulder height while keeping your elbow slightly soft. | On the backward swing, drive your arms behind your hips as far as comfortable range of motion allows. | Increase tempo progressively until you are moving at a quick, rhythmic pace without losing posture. | Keep your shoulders level and your head neutral — avoid hunching or shrugging as speed builds. | Continue for the target duration or rep count, then slow the swing gradually before stopping.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, arms bent at roughly 90 degrees at your sides. | Engage your core and keep your torso upright with a slight forward lean from the ankles. | Lift your right knee toward hip height while simultaneously driving your left arm forward. | Quickly lower your right foot and immediately lift your left knee, swinging your right arm forward. | Alternate legs in a continuous, brisk rhythm — aim for a jogging cadence faster than a casual jog. | Land softly on the balls of your feet each time, avoiding heavy heel strikes. | Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears; let the arms swing naturally from the shoulders. | Maintain steady breathing — inhale for two steps, exhale for two steps — to sustain the pace. | Continue for the prescribed duration or rep count, then slow to a walk to recover.

nH: מתיחת שוק עם כף רגל מורמת
t: Stand facing a low step, box, or raised surface roughly 15 to 30 centimetres high. | Shift your weight onto your left foot and place the top of your right foot on the raised surface so the toes point away from you and the laces face down. | Stand tall with your hips square and your hands on your hips or lightly resting on a wall for balance. | Slowly bend your left knee and lower your body slightly to allow the right ankle to plantarflex, which brings the shin closer to the surface. | Gently press your right shin forward and down until you feel a stretch along the front of the lower leg, just below the knee and along the shin bone. | Keep the top of your right foot and toes pressed into the raised surface throughout so the ankle stays plantarflexed. | Hold the stretched position for 20 to 45 seconds, breathing steadily. | Slowly straighten your left leg and lift your right foot off the surface to release the stretch. | Repeat on the opposite side.

t: Stand facing a bench, step, or sturdy elevated surface roughly hip to waist height. | Lift one leg and place your heel on the surface with the leg extended straight, toes pointing upward. | Stand tall with your supporting leg slightly soft at the knee and your hands resting on your hips or on the surface for balance. | Keeping your back flat, hinge forward from your hips — not your waist — until you feel a strong but comfortable stretch along the back of the raised thigh. | Hold the stretched position for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing the hamstrings to relax with each exhale. | Return to an upright position by engaging your core and lifting your torso back to neutral. | Lower the raised leg and repeat on the opposite side, completing 2–3 holds per leg.

t: Start in a high push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, arms fully extended, and your body forming a straight line from head to heel. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and lift one foot a few inches off the floor, keeping that leg straight and the hips level — this is your starting position. | Inhale and lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows at a 45–75° angle to your torso, keeping the raised leg in line with your body. | Continue lowering until your chest is an inch or two from the floor, maintaining a flat back and level hips throughout. | Press through your palms and exhale to push yourself back up to the starting position, keeping the leg elevated the entire way. | Complete all reps on one side, then lower the foot, rest briefly, and repeat with the other leg raised.

On each exhale, try to deepen the reach slightly without straining. | Hold for 20–30 seconds, then slowly release your hands, relax your shoulders back, and return to an upright posture. | Repeat 2–3 times as needed.

t: Stand or sit tall with your feet hip-width apart and your spine neutral. | Raise your right arm straight overhead, keeping your bicep close to your ear. | Bend your right elbow so your right hand drops down behind your head and toward the middle of your upper back. | Allow your elbow to point toward the ceiling and stay close to the side of your head. | Reach your left hand up and gently grasp your right elbow or forearm. | Apply light downward pressure with your left hand to deepen the stretch through the right triceps. | Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily throughout. | Release the pressure, straighten your right arm, and lower it to your side. | Repeat on the left side, performing an equal number of sets on each arm.

tHe: Stand or sit tall with your feet hip-width apart and your spine neutral. | הרם את יד ימין ישר מעל הראש, תוך שמירה על הזרוע קרובה לאוזן. | כופף את מרפק ימין כך שיד ימין תרד מאחורי הראש ולכיוון אמצע הגב העליון. | תן למרפק לפנות לעבר התקרה ולהישאר צמוד לצד הראש. | Reach your left hand up and gently grasp your right elbow or forearm. | לחץ קלות כלפי מטה עם יד שמאל כדי להעמיק את המתיחה ביד האחורית של יד ימין. | החזק את המתיחה 20–30 שניות, תוך נשימה סדירה לאורך כל הזמן. | Release the pressure, straighten your right arm, and lower it to your side. | Repeat on the left side, performing an equal number of sets on each arm.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, or sit upright on a bench or chair with both feet flat on the floor. | Inhale and raise both arms straight overhead, palms facing inward or toward each other. | Actively reach your fingertips toward the ceiling, lengthening through your entire spine. | Gently press your shoulders down and away from your ears to avoid shrugging. | Tilt your pelvis slightly and engage your core to prevent your lower back from arching excessively. | Hold the fully extended position for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and deeply throughout. | To deepen the stretch, interlace your fingers and turn your palms toward the ceiling, pushing upward. | Release by slowly lowering your arms back to your sides on an exhale. | Repeat 2–3 times, resting a few seconds between holds.

t: Stand in your fighting stance with your dominant (rear) foot back, knees slightly bent, hands raised to guard position. | Shift your weight onto your front foot, keeping your front knee soft and your torso upright. | Chamber your rear leg by driving your knee upward toward your chest as you begin to extend the leg. | Continue extending the leg overhead in a wide arc, straightening the knee and pointing your toes as the foot rises above head height. | At the peak of the arc, flex your foot so the heel faces downward toward the target. | Drive the heel straight down with controlled force, striking through the target and following through to approximately waist level. | Retract the leg and return your foot to the floor in your original stance, keeping your guard up throughout. | Reset your weight and stance before repeating.

nE: Rear Delt Fly with Bed Sheet
nR: Разводка на заднюю дельту с простынёй
t: Fold a bed sheet lengthwise and tie a secure knot near the middle, then close it in a sturdy door at roughly chest height so equal lengths hang on your side. | Grip one end of the sheet in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), standing close to the door. | Step back until your arms are extended in front of you and the sheet is taut, then lean your torso back slightly so your body forms a diagonal line — the farther you step back, the harder the exercise. | Brace your core and keep your feet hip-width apart for a stable base throughout the set. | With a slight bend in your elbows, begin pulling both arms out to your sides in a wide arc, leading with your elbows and keeping them at shoulder height. | Continue the fly motion until your arms are roughly parallel to the floor and your hands are in line with your shoulders, squeezing the rear delts and mid-traps at the top. | Pause for one second at the peak contraction, feeling the muscles between and behind your shoulder blades engage. | Slowly return your arms back to the starting position in front of you, maintaining control against the sheet's tension — do not let it snap you forward. | Complete all reps, then step forward to release tension before setting the sheet down.

nE: Rear Delt Row with Bed Sheet
nR: Тяга на заднюю дельту с простынёй
t: Fold a bed sheet lengthwise into a thick rope, then close it in a door at roughly chest height, leaving equal length on each side. Tug firmly to confirm the door holds your weight. | Grip one end of the sheet in each hand, palms facing each other, and walk your feet toward the door until your arms are fully extended and your body is on a backward lean — the steeper the lean, the harder the exercise. | Set your feet together or hip-width apart directly below the anchor point. Keep your body in a straight plank line from heels to shoulders throughout the movement. | Inhale, then initiate the row by driving your elbows out wide — to roughly 90° from your torso — rather than letting them stay close to your sides. | Pull your chest toward your hands, squeezing the shoulder blades together and down as your elbows move behind your torso. | Pause for one count at the top when your hands are at chest level, feeling the contraction in your upper back and rear shoulders. | Exhale and lower yourself with control back to the start, fully extending your arms before the next rep. | Complete your reps, then step your feet back toward the door before releasing the sheet.

t: Stand on the center of a resistance band with your feet hip-width apart, holding one end of the band in your right hand with your palm facing your body. | Hinge at your hips and push them back, lowering your torso until it is roughly parallel to the floor while keeping your back flat and your core braced. | Let your right arm hang straight down, keeping slight tension in the band at the bottom position. | Drive through your heels and extend your hips to stand tall, pulling the band upward as you rise — this is the deadlift phase. | As your hips reach full extension and your torso is upright, immediately drive your right elbow back and up toward your hip, rowing the band to your lower ribcage. | Squeeze your right shoulder blade toward your spine at the top of the row, then lower your arm under control back to the hanging position. | Hinge at your hips again to return to the start position, maintaining a neutral spine throughout the descent. | Complete all reps on your right side, then switch to your left hand and repeat.

t: Stand on the center of a resistance band with your feet hip-width apart, holding one end of the band in each hand (or both ends together) with a supinated grip so your palms face forward and the band runs along the front of your thighs. | Stand tall with your shoulders back and down, core braced, and arms fully extended in front of your hips. This is the starting position. | Initiate the movement by driving your elbows backward — not upward — while simultaneously bending at the elbows. Your elbows should begin to travel behind the plane of your torso as your hands start to rise. | Continue curling by dragging your hands up along the front of your body, keeping them close to your torso throughout the movement. t: Sit on the floor in front of a bench or sturdy box and loop a resistance band just above both knees. | Slide your upper back onto the bench so that your shoulder blades rest across the edge, your feet are flat on the floor roughly hip-width apart, and your hips hang down toward the ground. | Press your knees outward against the band until they are directly over your toes — this is your starting position. | Brace your core, tuck your chin slightly, and drive through your heels to lift your hips toward the ceiling. | Continue pushing your knees out against the band as your hips rise, maintaining the outward pressure throughout the lift. | Squeeze your glutes firmly at the top until your thighs and torso form a straight line from knees to shoulders — do not hyperextend your lower back. | Lower your hips slowly back toward the floor until you feel a full stretch in the glutes, keeping the band tension steady. | Pause briefly at the bottom without fully resting your hips, then drive back up for the next rep.

t: Anchor a resistance band at elbow height to a stable post, rack upright, or door anchor. Hold the band with the hand of your working arm. | Bend your elbow to 90° and tuck it firmly against your side. nE: Resistance Band Half Kneeling Face Pull
nR: Тяга к лицу с полуколена с лентой

t: Stand with both feet on the center of the resistance band, hip-width apart, holding one end of the band in each hand. | Let your arms hang at your sides with your palms facing your thighs — this is the neutral grip you will maintain for the entire set. | Brace your core and stand tall with your shoulders pulled back and down. | Curl both hands up toward your shoulders by bending at the elbows, keeping your palms facing each other throughout the movement. | Keep your upper arms pinned against your sides and avoid letting your elbows drift forward as you curl. | Squeeze at the top of the movement when your forearms are roughly vertical and your fists are near shoulder level. | Lower your hands back down in a slow, controlled manner, resisting the pull of the band on the way down. | Repeat for the target number of reps, then step off the band to finish the set.

nE: Resistance Band High Knee Lunge with Single Arm Row
nR: Выпады с высоким коленом + тяга одной рукой с лентой
nH: מכרע ברך גבוהה עם חתירה ביד אחת עם גומייה
t: Anchor the resistance band at roughly waist height to a fixed point in front of you. Stand facing the anchor and hold one end of the band in your right hand, arm extended. | Step your right foot back into a reverse lunge, lowering your right knee toward the floor while keeping your left knee tracking over your left foot. | From the bottom of the lunge, drive up explosively through your left foot and simultaneously pull the band toward your right hip in a single-arm row — elbow driving back, shoulder blade retracting. | As you reach standing, continue the momentum by lifting your right knee up to hip height in a high knee drive. | Hold the high knee and fully contracted row position for one count. | Step back into the reverse lunge to begin the next rep, letting the band arm extend again as you lower. | Complete all reps on one side before switching the band to the opposite hand and stepping back with the other foot.

t: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the edge of a sturdy bench, knees bent, and feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart. | Loop or drape the resistance band across the front of your hip crease, anchoring each end under your hands or through your hands pressed against your thighs to keep it in place. | Brace your core and tuck your chin slightly so your spine stays neutral throughout the movement. | Drive through your heels to press your hips upward, squeezing your glutes as you rise. | Continue pressing until your hips are fully extended and your torso forms a straight line from shoulders to knees — do not hyperextend your lower back. | Pause for one second at the top, maintaining the glute squeeze and keeping your shins roughly vertical. | Lower your hips under control back toward the floor, stopping just before they touch, then immediately begin the next rep. | Complete all reps, then guide your hips to the floor and carefully remove the band.

nE: Resistance Band Jump Lunge with Single Arm Row
nR: Выпады в прыжке + тяга одной рукой с лентой
nH: מכרע בקפיצה עם חתירה ביד אחת עם גומייה
t: Anchor a resistance band at roughly hip height to a sturdy fixed point and stand facing it, holding one end of the band in your right hand with your arm extended and feet together. | Step your left foot back into a staggered lunge stance, lowering your back knee toward the floor until both knees are near 90 degrees. | From the bottom of the lunge, drive through both feet explosively to jump straight up, switching leg positions in the air so your right foot lands back and your left foot lands forward. | As you land softly back into the lunge position with your right foot forward, immediately pull the band toward your hip and ribcage in a single-arm row, driving your right elbow straight back. | Squeeze your back muscles at the end of the row with your elbow past your torso, then extend your arm back to straight in a controlled manner. | Use the momentum of the arm extension to help initiate the next jump, switching legs again in the air. | Continue alternating jump lunges while performing a row with your right arm on each landing, completing all reps for that side. | Switch the band to your left hand, face the anchor point, and repeat the sequence for the same number of reps on the left side. | Land each jump with a soft bend at the knee and hip to absorb impact before going into the next rep.

t: Place a resistance band around both legs, just above the knees or around the ankles depending on your strength level — above the knees provides less resistance and is better for beginners. | Stand with your feet hip-width apart, toes pointing forward, and create tension in the band by pressing your knees outward against it. | Hinge slightly at the hips and bend your knees to lower into a quarter-squat athletic stance, keeping your chest tall and core braced. | Take a controlled step to one side with your lead foot, landing softly with your feet hip-width apart again and maintaining band tension throughout. | From that new position, push your hips back and down to squat to roughly parallel, keeping your knees tracking in line with your toes. | Drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to return to the quarter-squat standing position — do not let your knees cave inward as you rise. | Step the trailing foot in to close the gap back to hip-width, maintaining the athletic stance and band tension. | Continue stepping in the same direction for the desired number of reps, then repeat the sequence stepping in the opposite direction.

t: Anchor a resistance band securely to a low, fixed point at or near floor level — a rack upright, door anchor, or heavy furniture leg. | Lie face down on the floor with your head toward the anchor, and loop or attach the free end of the band around both ankles. | Extend your legs fully so there is light tension on the band even at the start position. | Rest your forearms flat on the floor and keep your hips pressed down throughout the set. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes slightly to stabilize the pelvis. | Curl both heels toward your glutes by bending the knees, pulling against the band resistance until your hamstrings are fully contracted. | Pause for one count at the top with your hamstrings squeezed. | Slowly lower your feet back to the floor, resisting the band on the way down. | Complete all reps before releasing tension and resting.

nE: Resistance Band One Leg Kickback (Bent Position)
nH: בעיטת רגל אחת לאחור עם גומייה (ברגל כפופה)
t: Anchor one end of the resistance band at floor level — around a sturdy post or through a door anchor — and loop the other end around the ankle of your working leg. | Step back far enough to create tension in the band, then hinge forward at the hips until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor, placing both hands on a wall or sturdy surface for support. | Bend the working knee to about 90 degrees, keeping your foot flexed and your core braced. | Keeping your back flat and hips level, drive the working heel straight back and upward by squeezing the gluteus maximus. | Continue extending the hip until your thigh is parallel to the floor or slightly above — do not hyperextend the lower back to gain range. | Pause for one second at the top, holding the glute contraction. | Lower the knee back to the starting bent position under control, resisting the pull of the band on the way down. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch the band to the other ankle and repeat.

t: Stand on the center of the resistance band with your feet shoulder-width apart or slightly wider, toes turned out slightly. | Grip the band with both hands wide enough that your arms form a wide overhead position, similar to a snatch grip. | Press the band overhead with straight arms and pull outward on it to create tension throughout the upper back. | Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and take a breath in before descending. | Push your knees out in line with your toes and sit your hips back and down simultaneously. | Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor or lower, keeping the band locked out directly overhead. | Maintain an upright torso throughout — avoid letting the band drift forward or your chest collapse. | Drive through the full foot to stand back up, keeping arms locked and band overhead until you reach full extension. | Reset your breath and brace before each subsequent repetition.

t: Loop a resistance band around both feet, just above the ankles, so it sits flat and secure. | Get into a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders, arms fully extended, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your hips level — avoid letting them sag or pike up. | Drive your right knee toward your chest, pulling against the resistance of the band, until your thigh is roughly parallel to the floor. | Pause for one count at the top, maintaining a neutral spine throughout. | Return your right foot to the floor with control, resisting the band on the way back. | Immediately drive your left knee toward your chest in the same manner, completing one full march cycle. | Continue alternating legs at a controlled pace for the desired number of reps or time, keeping your hips square and still throughout.

t: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and hold a resistance band with both hands, palms facing down. | Raise your arms in front of you so they are angled downward at roughly 45 degrees from horizontal — hands at approximately upper-chest height, fingertips pointing toward the floor at a diagonal. | Set your grip so there is light tension in the band at the start position, with hands roughly shoulder-width apart or slightly wider. | Retract your shoulder blades slightly and brace your core before initiating the movement. | Pull the band apart by driving both hands outward and back, keeping the 45-degree downward angle constant throughout the motion. | Continue pulling until the band touches your chest, squeezing the rear delts and upper back at the end range. | Pause briefly at the fully stretched position, feeling the contraction in the posterior deltoid and between the shoulder blades. | Reverse the motion under control, allowing the band to return to the start position without letting your arms drift above or below the 45-degree angle. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, maintaining a steady tempo and consistent arm angle on every repetition.
