nH: דדליפט ברגל אחת ישרה עם חתירה ביד אחת עם גומייה
t: Stand with one foot centered on the middle of the resistance band, holding both ends (or one end looped) in the opposite hand at your side. | Shift your weight onto the standing leg and lift the opposite foot slightly off the floor, keeping a soft bend in the standing knee. | Brace your core and maintain a neutral spine, then hinge forward at the hip, sending the free leg back behind you as your torso lowers toward the floor. | Lower until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor, or as far as your hamstring flexibility allows without rounding your back. | At the bottom of the hinge, drive your elbow back and row the band toward your hip, squeezing the back muscles at the top of the pull. | Slowly lower your arm back to the starting position, keeping control of the band tension throughout. | Drive through the standing heel and squeeze the glute to return to the upright starting position, completing one full rep. | Perform all reps on one side before switching the foot on the band and the rowing arm to complete the set on the other side.

nR: Жим на тибиалис сидя на полу с лентой

nE: Resistance Band Split Jump with Single Arm Row
nR: Прыжки вразножку + тяга одной рукой с лентой
nH: קפיצה מפוצלת עם חתירה ביד אחת עם גומייה
t: Anchor a resistance band at hip-to-chest height to a stable post or rack. Stand facing the anchor, feet together, and grasp the band in one hand with your arm fully extended and light tension already in the band. | Set your distance from the anchor so the band is taut but not pulling you forward. This is your starting position. | Explosively jump upward, scissoring your legs in the air, and land in a split stance — one foot forward, one back — with both knees soft and bent to absorb impact. | At the moment your feet contact the ground, drive your elbow straight back and row the band toward your lower chest, squeezing your back at the end of the pull. | Hold the row for one count at the bottom of the split, keeping your torso upright and chest tall. | Push off both feet explosively to jump again, simultaneously straightening your rowing arm back to full extension as you leave the ground. | While airborne, switch your legs so the opposite foot lands forward. Land again with soft, bent knees in the new split stance. | Row again as you land, completing one rep on each side. Continue alternating legs and rowing for the prescribed time or rep count, keeping a steady rhythm throughout.

nR: Сплит-присед с удержанием Паллофа с лентой

t: Anchor a resistance band at chest height to a stable post, rack upright, or cable column. Stand perpendicular to the anchor point — the anchor should be directly to one side of you. | Grasp the band with both hands and step laterally away from the anchor until there is firm tension in the band. This is your starting position for setting up the Pallof hold. | Step one foot forward and one foot back into a split squat stance, keeping your feet roughly hip-width apart side to side for balance. The front foot should be flat; the back foot balanced on the ball. | Press both arms straight out in front of your chest at shoulder height, elbows fully extended and hands together — this is the horizontal Pallof hold position. The band will pull you toward the anchor; brace your waist to resist it. | Keeping your arms extended and your torso upright and square, inhale and slowly lower your back knee toward the floor, descending in a controlled split squat. | Stop just before your back knee touches the ground, then press through your front foot to drive back up to the starting position. Keep your arms extended and resist any rotation throughout the movement. | Complete all reps on this side while maintaining the Pallof hold, then lower your arms and rest briefly. | Switch sides — reposition so the anchor is on your opposite side and the opposite leg leads — and repeat the same number of reps to balance the work.

This is your starting position. | Напрягите пресс, стабилизируя мяч и не давая ему откатываться. | Squeeze your glutes and lift both legs upward and back until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your heels, or until you reach your comfortable range of motion. | Pause for a moment at the top, focusing on the contraction in your glutes and hip extensors. | Lower your legs slowly and under control back to the starting position, resisting the pull of gravity on the way down. | Repeat for the desired number of reps without letting your hips sink or the ball shift excessively between repetitions.

t: Begin on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips, maintaining a neutral spine. | Brace your core and draw your navel gently toward your spine to protect your lower back throughout the movement. | Keeping the knee bent at roughly 90 degrees, drive your right heel toward the ceiling by squeezing your right glute, until your thigh is parallel to the floor. | Pause at the top for one count, fully contracting the glute without allowing your lower back to arch or your hips to rotate. | Lower your right knee slowly back toward the floor in a controlled 2–3 second descent, stopping just before it touches. | Complete all reps on the right side, then switch to the left leg and repeat. | To finish, lower both knees to the floor, release the tension, and rest in a neutral position.

tHe: התחל בעמידת שש עם כפות ידיים בדיוק מתחת לכתפיים וברכיים בדיוק מתחת לאגן, תוך שמירה על עמוד שדרה ניטרלי. | הדק את הליבה ומשוך בעדינות את הטבור לכיוון עמוד השדרה כדי להגן על הגב התחתון לאורך כל התנועה. | Keeping the knee bent at roughly 90 degrees, drive your right heel toward the ceiling by squeezing your right glute, until your thigh is parallel to the floor. | Pause at the top for one count, fully contracting the glute without allowing your lower back to arch or your hips to rotate. | Lower your right knee slowly back toward the floor in a controlled 2–3 second descent, stopping just before it touches. | בצע את כל החזרות בצד ימין, ואז עבור לרגל שמאל וחזור על התרגיל. | To finish, lower both knees to the floor, release the tension, and rest in a neutral position.

nE: Reverse Lunge High Knee Forward Lunge

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides. | Step one foot straight back and lower your rear knee toward the floor, stopping just before it touches. Keep your front shin vertical and your torso upright. | Push through your front heel to return to standing, then immediately drive your rear knee up in front of you until your thigh is parallel to the floor. | Pause for a moment in the high-knee position to find your balance before stepping forward. | Step that same foot forward into a forward lunge, lowering your back knee toward the floor while keeping your front knee tracking over your toes. | Push through your front heel to bring both feet back together at the starting position. | That is one rep. Complete all reps on one side before switching, or alternate legs each rep depending on your preference.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides or hands on your hips for balance. | Brace your core, keep your chest up, and shift your weight onto your left foot. | Step your right foot directly back, lowering your body until your right knee hovers just above the floor and your left thigh is roughly parallel to the ground — this is the bottom of the lunge. | Pause briefly at the bottom to ensure your front knee tracks over your second toe and does not cave inward. | Drive through your left heel to stand back up, swinging your right leg forward as you rise. | As your right leg swings forward, extend it into a controlled front kick at hip height, straightening the knee with your quadriceps at the top of the kick. | Hold the kick position for one count, then lower your right foot back to the starting position with control. | Complete all reps on the right leg, then switch sides, or alternate legs each rep depending on your goal.

tHe: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides or hands on your hips for balance. | הדק את הליבה, שמור על חזה מורם והעבר את המשקל לרגל שמאל. | Step your right foot directly back, lowering your body until your right knee hovers just above the floor and your left thigh is roughly parallel to the ground — this is the bottom of the lunge. | Pause briefly at the bottom to ensure your front knee tracks over your second toe and does not cave inward. | Drive through your left heel to stand back up, swinging your right leg forward as you rise. | בהנפת רגל ימין קדימה, יישר אותה לבעיטת חזית מבוקרת בגובה האגן, תוך יישור הברך עם הארבע־ראשי בשיא הבעיטה. | Hold the kick position for one count, then lower your right foot back to the starting position with control. | בצע את כל החזרות עם הרגל הימינה, ואז החלף צדדים, או החלף בין הרגליים בכל חזרה לפי המטרה שלך.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you and your feet together. | Place your hands on the floor behind your hips, roughly shoulder-width apart, with fingers pointing toward your feet or angled slightly outward. | Press through your palms and engage your core, then drive your heels into the floor to lift your hips up off the ground. | Continue pressing until your body forms a straight line from your heels to your shoulders — squeeze your glutes to hold the position. | Keep your head in a neutral position, looking slightly upward, without letting it drop back excessively. | Hold the position for the desired duration while breathing steadily, maintaining a flat body line throughout. | To finish, lower your hips back to the floor with control.
tRu: Сядьте на пол, выпрямив ноги перед собой и соединив стопы. | Place your hands on the floor behind your hips, roughly shoulder-width apart, with fingers pointing toward your feet or angled slightly outward. | Press through your palms and engage your core, then drive your heels into the floor to lift your hips up off the ground. | Продолжайте жим, пока ваше тело не образует прямую линию от пяток до плеч — сожмите ягодицы, чтобы удержать положение. | Keep your head in a neutral position, looking slightly upward, without letting it drop back excessively. | Hold the position for the desired duration while breathing steadily, maintaining a flat body line throughout. | Чтобы завершить, подконтрольно опустите бёдра обратно на пол.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and place your elbows directly beneath your shoulders, forearms flat on the ground. | Point your toes toward the ceiling and press your heels firmly into the floor. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes, then drive your hips upward until your body forms a straight diagonal line from head to heel. | Keep your chin slightly tucked so your head is neutral — neither drooping toward your chest nor tilting back. | Hold the raised position, maintaining even pressure through both elbows and both heels. | Breathe steadily throughout the hold; avoid holding your breath. | To finish, lower your hips back to the floor in a controlled manner and rest before repeating.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and your heels pressed into the ground. | Place your hands flat on the floor just behind your hips, fingers pointing forward or slightly outward. | Press through your palms and heels to lift your hips off the floor, squeezing your glutes and driving your hips upward. | Continue raising your hips until your body forms a straight line from heels to shoulders — avoid letting your hips pike up too high or sag toward the floor. | Pull your shoulder blades together and down to keep your chest open and your shoulders stable. | Hold your head in a neutral position — either looking straight up toward the ceiling or keeping your chin slightly tucked. | Breathe steadily throughout the hold, keeping your glutes, hamstrings, and core actively engaged. | To finish, lower your hips gently back to the floor in a controlled manner.

t: Start in a standard push-up position with your hands flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart and directly under your shoulders. | Rotate both hands so your fingers point toward your feet and your palms remain in full contact with the floor — this is the reverse hand position that defines the exercise. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your body in a straight line from your head to your heels. | Inhale and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your elbows tracking close to your sides rather than flaring out. | Lower under control until your chest is a few centimeters from the floor or until you reach the end of your comfortable range of motion. | Exhale and press firmly through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the starting position. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a rigid torso throughout every rep.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, chest lifted, and chin slightly tucked. | Bring both arms behind your back and interlace your fingers, or clasp one wrist with the opposite hand if interlacing is uncomfortable. | Straighten your arms as fully as possible and squeeze your shoulder blades together, opening your chest forward. | Without hunching your upper back, slowly lift your clasped hands upward and away from your glutes until you feel a stretch across the front of your shoulders and chest. | Keep your elbows as straight as you can and your palms pressed together or facing inward throughout the hold. | Hold the end position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and deepening the stretch slightly on each exhale. | Lower your arms, release your hands, and gently roll your shoulders forward to decompress before repeating.

nE: Reverse Sliding Leg Curl on Floor with Towel
nR: Обратные сгибания ног со скольжением на полу с полотенцем
nH: כפיפות רגליים הפוכות בהחלקה על הרצפה עם מגבת
t: Place a folded towel on a smooth, low-friction floor surface and lie flat on your back with your arms at your sides for stability. | Bend your knees to roughly 90 degrees and position both heels on the center of the towel, hip-width apart. | Press through your heels and brace your core to lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from shoulders to knees. | Keeping your hips elevated, slowly slide both heels outward along the floor, allowing your legs to extend and your hips to lower in a controlled descent. | Stop the slide when your legs are nearly fully extended and your hips are just above or lightly touching the floor. | Dig your heels into the towel and contract your hamstrings to curl both heels back toward your glutes, simultaneously driving your hips back up. | Return to the starting bridge position with hips fully elevated and knees at 90 degrees. | Pause briefly at the top, squeeze your glutes and hamstrings, then begin the next repetition. | Complete all reps in a controlled manner, maintaining tension throughout the movement rather than using momentum.

t: Stand with your feet wide apart, roughly 3–4 feet, turning your right foot out 90 degrees and your left foot in about 15 degrees. | Bend your right knee until your thigh is approximately parallel to the floor, stacking the knee directly over the ankle. | Extend both arms out to the sides at shoulder height, parallel to the floor. | Inhale and flip your right palm to face upward, then sweep your right arm up and overhead toward the back of the room. | Lower your left hand to rest lightly on the back of your left leg — shin or thigh — without pushing into it for support. | Gently lean your torso back and to the left, creating a long arc through the right side of your body from hip to fingertips. | Keep your right knee bent and pointing toward your right pinky toe throughout the pose. | Hold for 3–5 breaths, feeling the stretch along the right side body and hip flexors. | Inhale to rise back to center, then repeat on the opposite side.
tRu: Stand with your feet wide apart, roughly 3–4 feet, turning your right foot out 90 degrees and your left foot in about 15 degrees. | Согните правое колено, пока бедро не станет примерно параллельно полу, удерживая колено строго над лодыжкой. | Extend both arms out to the sides at shoulder height, parallel to the floor. | Inhale and flip your right palm to face upward, then sweep your right arm up and overhead toward the back of the room. | Lower your left hand to rest lightly on the back of your left leg — shin or thigh — without pushing into it for support. | Gently lean your torso back and to the left, creating a long arc through the right side of your body from hip to fingertips. | Keep your right knee bent and pointing toward your right pinky toe throughout the pose. | Hold for 3–5 breaths, feeling the stretch along the right side body and hip flexors. | Inhale to rise back to center, then repeat on the opposite side.

t: Stand with your feet together and arms at your sides. | Bend your knees and lower your hips as if sitting back into a chair, keeping your weight in your heels and your torso upright — this is Chair Pose (Utkatasana). | Bring your palms together at your chest in a prayer position. | On an exhale, rotate your torso to the right, hooking your left elbow outside your right knee. | Press your elbow firmly against your knee to deepen the twist and keep your knees aligned. | Extend through the crown of your head to lengthen your spine, and gently open your chest toward the ceiling. | Hold the position for 5–10 breaths, keeping your hips level and your core engaged. | On an inhale, unwind back to center and return to Chair Pose. | Repeat the twist on the opposite side, rotating to the left with your right elbow outside your left knee.
tRu: Встаньте, поставив стопы вместе, руки вдоль тела. | Согните ноги и опустите бёдра, как будто садитесь на стул, удерживая вес в пятках и корпус вертикально — это поза стула (Уткатасана). | Сведите ладони на уровне груди в положении молитвы. | On an exhale, rotate your torso to the right, hooking your left elbow outside your right knee. | Press your elbow firmly against your knee to deepen the twist and keep your knees aligned. | Extend through the crown of your head to lengthen your spine, and gently open your chest toward the ceiling. | Hold the position for 5–10 breaths, keeping your hips level and your core engaged. | On an inhale, unwind back to center and return to Chair Pose. | Repeat the twist on the opposite side, rotating to the left with your right elbow outside your left knee.
tHe: עמוד עם רגליים צמודות וידיים לצדי הגוף. | כופף את הברכיים והורד את האגן כאילו התיישבת לאחור על כיסא, תוך שמירה על המשקל בעקבים והגוף זקוף — זוהי תנוחת הכיסא (אוטקאטאסאנה). | הבא את כפות ידיך יחד בחזה. | On an exhale, rotate your torso to the right, hooking your left elbow outside your right knee. | Press your elbow firmly against your knee to deepen the twist and keep your knees aligned. | Extend through the crown of your head to lengthen your spine, and gently open your chest toward the ceiling. | Hold the position for 5–10 breaths, keeping your hips level and your core engaged. | On an inhale, unwind back to center and return to Chair Pose. | Repeat the twist on the opposite side, rotating to the left with your right elbow outside your left knee.

t: Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front of you. Bend your right knee and draw the sole of your right foot against the inside of your left thigh, letting your right knee fall out to the side. | Flex your left foot so the toes point toward the ceiling, keeping the left leg straight and the back of your knee in contact with the floor. | Inhale and grow tall through your spine, sitting evenly on both sit bones. | Exhale and rotate your torso slightly toward the left leg, then begin to hinge and side-bend to the left, reaching your left hand toward your left foot. | Extend your right arm up and over your head, reaching toward the left foot so both hands can hold the foot, ankle, or shin — whichever is reachable without rounding your lower back. | Turn your chest gently upward toward the ceiling to deepen the spinal rotation, keeping your shoulders relaxed away from your ears. | Hold the position for 5–10 slow breaths, using each exhale to ease a little deeper into the stretch. | Inhale to rise back to an upright seat, then repeat on the opposite side.

t: Stand at the top of your mat with your feet together, then step your left foot back about 3–4 feet into a lunge, lowering your back knee toward the floor if needed to find stability. | Align your right knee directly over your right ankle, keeping your front shin vertical and your back leg extended or knee resting gently on the mat. | Place your hands together at your chest in a prayer position (Anjali Mudra) and take a tall breath in to lengthen your spine. | On an exhale, rotate your torso to the right, hooking your left elbow outside your right knee. Use this contact as leverage to deepen the twist without collapsing your chest. | Press your palms firmly together and use the resistance between your elbow and knee to open your chest upward, rotating your top shoulder back and your bottom shoulder forward. | Keep your hips as square to the front of the mat as possible — resist letting the back hip swing open as you twist. | Gaze upward toward the ceiling or keep your eyes level if that is more comfortable for your neck. | Hold the pose for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and deepening the rotation a little more with each exhale. | To release, unwind the twist on an inhale, return your hands to the mat, and step your back foot forward. Repeat on the opposite side, stepping the right foot back.

t: Begin in a high lunge with your right foot forward, knee stacked over the ankle, and your left leg extended straight behind you with the ball of the left foot on the mat. | Square your hips toward the front of the mat and press back through the left heel to straighten the back leg and stabilize the stance. | On an inhale, lengthen through the crown of the head and lift your torso upright, engaging the core. | On an exhale, rotate your torso to the right, bringing your left elbow to the outside of your right knee. Press elbow and knee against each other to deepen the twist. | If the twist allows, lower your left hand to the mat or a block on the outside of the right foot, pressing the palm flat to create a stable foundation. | Extend your right arm overhead and in line with your right ear, reaching the fingertips forward to create a long diagonal line from the back heel through the top hand. | Turn your gaze upward toward the ceiling or, if that strains the neck, look straight ahead. t: Stand with your feet together, then step your left foot back about 3–4 feet, keeping both feet pointing forward and your legs straight. | Square your hips as much as possible toward the front of your mat, pressing the outer edge of your back foot firmly into the floor. | Inhale and extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, creating a T shape with your torso. | Exhale and hinge forward from your hips, keeping your spine long, and bring your torso over your front (right) leg. | Place your left hand on the floor outside your right foot, or on a block positioned beside your right shin if you cannot reach the floor. | Inhale to lengthen your spine, then exhale and rotate your torso to the right, stacking your right shoulder above the left. | Extend your right arm straight up toward the ceiling, opening your chest and gazing up at your raised hand if your neck allows. | Hold for 5–10 slow breaths, maintaining an elongated spine rather than collapsing into the forward fold. | To exit, lower your top arm, inhale to lift your torso back to upright, and step your feet together before repeating on the opposite side.

t: Adjust the saddle height so your knee has a slight bend (about 25–35°) at the bottom of the pedal stroke, with your foot flat on the pedal. | Set the handlebar height so you can reach it comfortably without rounding your lower back or locking out your elbows. | Before setting off, do 5 minutes of easy spinning at low resistance to warm up your legs and elevate your heart rate gradually. | Clip in or place the ball of your foot over the center of the pedal, then push off and begin pedaling in smooth, circular strokes. | Sit tall with a neutral spine, a slight forward lean from the hips, and relaxed shoulders — avoid hunching or gripping the bars too tightly. | Maintain a cadence of 70–90 RPM for general fitness; shift to an easier gear to keep your cadence in range rather than grinding a heavy gear. | Ride at a conversational pace for the bulk of your session if you are building base fitness, or follow a structured interval plan for higher-intensity work. | In the final 5 minutes, reduce intensity and spin in an easy gear to cool down and bring your heart rate back toward resting. | Dismount carefully, check your bike is secured, and stretch your quads, hamstrings, and hip flexors after the ride.

t: Stand with your left foot forward and right foot back, feet roughly shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent. | Raise your hands into guard position — left fist near your chin, right fist beside your right cheek, elbows tucked in. | Pivot your right foot, turning the heel outward so your right hip rotates forward. | Drive the rotation through your core and torso, letting your right shoulder follow the hip forward. | Extend your right arm in a straight line toward the target, rotating your fist so the palm faces down at full extension. | Make contact with the first two knuckles of your right hand, keeping your wrist straight and aligned with your forearm. | Exhale sharply as you extend, engaging your core throughout the punch. | Pull your arm back along the same path immediately after contact, returning your fist to guard position. | Reset your stance and weight distribution before throwing another punch or combination.

t: Stand in an orthodox boxing stance: feet shoulder-width apart, left foot forward, knees slightly bent, and weight evenly distributed between both feet. | Raise your hands to guard position — left fist near your left cheekbone, right fist protecting your right cheekbone, elbows angled down toward your ribs. | Shift a small amount of weight onto your right (rear) foot by bending the right knee, loading the hip for rotation. | Initiate the punch by driving your right hip explosively forward and pivoting on the ball of your right foot, letting your heel rise naturally. | As your hips rotate, allow your right shoulder to follow through and bring your right elbow up to roughly shoulder height, forming approximately a 90° bend at the elbow. | Deliver the hook in a tight horizontal arc toward the target, keeping your right fist level with your shoulder at the moment of contact. | Keep your left hand pressed firmly against your left cheekbone throughout the entire movement to maintain your guard. | At the moment of impact, exhale sharply and tighten your core to transfer force through the punch. | Snap your right hand back to guard position by reversing the hip rotation, then reset your balanced stance and prepare for the next combination.

t: Stand in a boxing stance with your left foot forward, feet roughly shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and weight balanced across both feet. | Raise both hands to guard position: fists near your chin, elbows tucked close to your ribs. | Slightly drop your right shoulder and bend your right knee a few inches to load the punch. | Drive off your right foot and rotate your hips and torso to the left, transferring weight onto your front foot. | As your hips rotate, drive your right fist upward in a short arc — palm facing you — toward chin height. | Keep your elbow bent at roughly 90° throughout the movement; this is not a wide swing but a tight vertical strike. | Snap your fist to the target and immediately return your right hand to guard position, resetting your stance. | Stay light on your feet between repetitions, maintaining your guard at all times.

t: Set the rings low enough that you can lie face-down underneath them and grip them with straight arms, your body forming a plank roughly parallel to the floor. | Hold one ring in each hand with a neutral grip, arms fully extended overhead. t: Adjust the rings so they hang just a few inches above the floor, enough clearance to kneel beneath them comfortably. | Kneel on a mat and grip one ring in each hand with a neutral or pronated grip, hands roughly shoulder-width apart. | Brace your core, posteriorly tilt your pelvis, and slowly walk your knees back while extending your arms forward and overhead until your body forms a straight, hollow-body line — hips in line with your torso, arms fully extended. | Hold that extended position: arms straight and pressed down against the rings, ribcage depressed, glutes and abs fully contracted, and hips just above floor level. | Keep your gaze toward the floor and your neck neutral so your spine stays in alignment throughout the hold. | Breathe in controlled nasal inhales and exhale slowly without releasing the abdominal brace — do not hold your breath for the entire set. | Maintain the hollow-body position for the target duration, typically 10–30 seconds, resisting any temptation to let the hips drop or the lower back arch. | To finish, bend your elbows and pull the rings back toward your hips while walking your knees forward, returning to the kneeling start position under control.

tHe: כוון את הטבעות כך שייתלו רק כמה אינץ׳ מעל הרצפה, עם מספיק מרווח לכרוע תחתיהן בנוחות. | Kneel on a mat and grip one ring in each hand with a neutral or pronated grip, hands roughly shoulder-width apart. | הדק את הליבה, הטה את האגן לאחור, ולך לאט עם הברכיים לאחור תוך יישור הידיים קדימה ומעל הראש עד שהגוף יוצר קו ישר וחלול — האגן בקו הגו, הידיים ישרות לגמרי. | Hold that extended position: arms straight and pressed down against the rings, ribcage depressed, glutes and abs fully contracted, and hips just above floor level. | Keep your gaze toward the floor and your neck neutral so your spine stays in alignment throughout the hold. | נשור בנשימות אף מבוקרות ונשור לאט בלי לשחרר את הגימור הבטני — אל תחזוק את הנשימה למשך כל הסט. | Maintain the hollow-body position for the target duration, typically 10–30 seconds, resisting any temptation to let the hips drop or the lower back arch. | To finish, bend your elbows and pull the rings back toward your hips while walking your knees forward, returning to the kneeling start position under control.

nR: Удержание отжиманий на прямых руках на кольцах
nH: החזקת שכיבות סמיכה בידיים ישרות על טבעות
t: Set the rings low, roughly 15–30 cm off the floor — high enough to clear your body but low enough that you can hold a straight line from head to heel with your feet on the ground. | Grip a ring in each hand with your palms facing each other and press up into a top push-up position, hands directly under your shoulders. | Brace your core hard, squeeze your glutes, and push through the balls of your feet to make a rigid plank from head to foot. | Keeping your arms straight but not hyperextended, let the rings travel outward away from your midline into a wide fly position until your arms sit roughly 30–45° out from your torso. | Hold there: hands wide, arms straight, hips level, body in one line — do not let the rings drift further out than you can control. | Breathe in short, steady breaths; do not let the hips sag toward the floor or pike upward. | Hold for the prescribed time — start with 5–10 seconds and build toward 20–30 seconds as strength improves. | To finish, pull the rings back in until they are under your shoulders, then lower your knees to the floor and step out of the position.

nR: Сгибания на бицепс одной рукой на кольцах
nH: כפיפות דו-ראשי ביד אחת על טבעות
t: Set the ring to roughly hip or waist height — lower rings increase the difficulty by increasing your lean angle. | Stand facing the anchor point and grip the ring with one hand using an underhand (supinated) grip. | Place your free hand on your hip or behind your back to prevent it from assisting the movement. | Walk your feet forward until your body is on a diagonal lean, with your arm extended and your weight supported by the ring. | Brace your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels throughout the movement. | Curl your body up toward the ring by bending your elbow, driving it straight back rather than flaring it out to the side. | Continue curling until your hand is near your shoulder and your bicep is fully contracted. | Lower yourself back to the start position under control, fully extending your arm before beginning the next rep. | Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other arm.

nR: Подтягивания на одной руке на кольцах
t: Set the rings at a height that allows a full dead hang with feet off the floor. Grip one ring firmly with your working hand, palm facing toward you or at a neutral angle. | Place the free hand lightly on the wrist or forearm of your working arm for assistance, or let it hang at your side if attempting the unassisted version. | Before initiating the pull, depress and retract the shoulder blade on the working side to create a stable, packed shoulder joint. | Engage your core, squeeze your glutes, and establish a hollow-body position — ribs down, abs braced — to minimize swing. | Drive your elbow forcefully down and back toward your hip to initiate the pull, keeping the ring close to your body rather than letting it drift outward. | Pull continuously until your chin clears the height of the ring on the working side, maintaining as upright a torso as possible. | Lower yourself under full control back to a dead hang, resisting the descent rather than dropping, to maximize back engagement on every rep. | Complete all planned reps on one arm, rest adequately, then repeat on the opposite side.

t: Set the rings at roughly chest height for a standing variation, or suspend them overhead if performing a bodyweight hanging version. | Stand facing away from the anchor point, grasp one ring in each hand with an overhand grip, and step forward until the straps are taut and your arms are extended overhead at roughly a 45-degree angle. | Lean back so your body is at a slight angle, engage your core, and keep your legs straight — your body should form a rigid plank from head to heels. | Inhale, then begin the movement by driving your hands downward and backward in a smooth arc, as if sweeping them from overhead toward your hips. | Keep a slight, consistent bend in your elbows throughout — do not let the elbows fully lock or excessively bend; the arms act as levers, not pullers. | Focus on initiating the arc with your lats rather than your triceps; imagine trying to bring your elbows toward your hip pockets. | Continue the arc until the rings reach roughly hip or thigh level and you feel a strong contraction across the lats and through the teres major. | Exhale at the bottom of the arc, pause briefly, then slowly reverse the motion to return the rings overhead under control. | Complete the target reps, then step back toward the anchor to release tension before letting go of the rings.

t: Set the rings at a height where you can hang freely with your arms fully extended and your feet clear of the floor. | Grip each ring with a neutral or slightly supinated grip, wrapping your thumbs fully around the handles, and let yourself hang at a dead hang to settle your shoulder blades. | Engage your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight, controlled line from head to heel. | Initiate the pull by drawing your shoulder blades down and together, then drive your elbows toward your hips to bring your chest up toward the rings. | As you rise, allow your wrists to rotate naturally so the rings turn outward at the top of the movement. | Continue pulling until your chin clears the level of the rings and your chest is close to them. | Pause briefly at the top, maintaining tension in your back and keeping your shoulders packed down away from your ears. | Lower yourself under control back to a full dead hang, resisting the urge to drop quickly. | Reset your position at the bottom before beginning the next rep.

nH: מתח ביד אחת בסיוע גומייה על טבעות
t: Set the rings at a height that gives you a complete dead hang with feet clear of the floor. Loop a resistance band through the ring on your working side so it forms a secure foot or knee loop hanging below. | Grip the ring with your working hand, palm facing toward you or in a neutral position. Step one foot or knee into the band loop, then lower yourself into a dead hang, letting the band bear a portion of your bodyweight. | Before pulling, pack the shoulder on your working arm — actively depress and retract the scapula so the shoulder joint is stable rather than elevated and loose. | Brace your core and hold a hollow-body position: ribs down, abs engaged, free leg long or crossed behind the banded leg to minimise swing. | Drive your elbow forcefully down and back toward your hip, keeping the ring close to your torso rather than letting it drift outward. | Pull continuously until your chin clears the height of the ring on the working side, maintaining as upright a torso as you can throughout. | Lower yourself under full control back to a dead hang, resisting gravity the entire way down rather than dropping, to maximise lat and bicep engagement on the eccentric. | Complete all planned reps, then switch sides, matching the band setup and rep count.

t: Adjust the rings so they hang roughly 6–12 inches off the floor, then lie face down and place the top of each foot into a ring. | Press up into a high push-up position with your arms fully extended and your hands directly under your shoulders. | Squeeze your glutes, brace your core, and align your body into a rigid plank — hips level, spine neutral, no sag or pike. | Inhale to brace, then initiate the movement by drawing your knees toward your chest and letting the rings travel forward beneath your body. | Keep your arms straight throughout — do not bend the elbows as you tuck. | Continue pulling until your knees are near or past your elbows, or as far as your core control allows. | Pause briefly in the tucked position at the peak of the contraction. | Exhale and slowly extend your legs back to the full plank start position, resisting the rings' momentum and keeping your hips from dropping below the plank line. | Complete the target reps, then lower your knees to the floor and step your feet out of the rings to finish.

t: Set the rings to roughly hip height and face the anchor point. Stand close enough to hold both rings with your arms extended in front of you. | Walk your feet forward and lean back so your body forms a slight diagonal — arms straight, rings at chest height, heels on the floor with toes pointing up. | Brace your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels throughout the set. | With a slight bend in your elbows, pull both rings out and back in a wide arc, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top. | Pause briefly when your arms are roughly in line with your torso and your hands are level with your shoulders. | Reverse the motion under control, returning the rings to the start position without letting your shoulders round forward. | Complete your reps, then step forward to unload before releasing the rings.

nR: Подтягивания Рокки с тягой на кольцах
nH: מתח רוקי עם משיכה על טבעות
t: Set the rings so that when you hang from them your arms are fully extended overhead and your feet clear the floor. | Grip the rings with an overhand or neutral grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, arms fully extended and core braced in a slight hollow position. | Depress and retract your shoulder blades to initiate the pull, so the lats take over before the arms do — avoid a passive shrug at the bottom. | Pull yourself upward by driving your elbows down and back, as in a standard pull-up, until your chin clears the rings. | At the top, pause briefly with your chin above the rings and your chest close to them. | From that top position, drive your elbows further down and back — as if performing a lat pulldown — squeezing the lats hard for a count while turning the rings out slightly. | Release the squeeze under control, settling back to the chin-over-rings position without dropping out of the top. | Lower your body under control to the full dead hang, taking at least two seconds on the descent, then reset your shoulder position before the next rep.

t: Set the rings low — roughly 6–12 inches above the floor — so they hang just above knee height when you are kneeling in front of them. | Kneel on a mat with your knees hip-width apart and grip one ring in each hand, palms facing inward. | Brace your core hard, tuck your pelvis slightly, and keep your spine neutral — do not let your lower back arch before the movement begins. | Exhale and begin rolling the rings forward by extending your arms in a controlled arc, keeping your hips in line with your shoulders. | Continue extending until your body forms a straight diagonal line from knees to hands, or as far as you can go while maintaining a neutral spine. | Hold for a brief pause at the extended position, resisting the urge to let your hips sag or your lower back hyper-extend. | Pull the rings back toward your knees by contracting your abs and lats simultaneously, reversing the arc under control. | Return to the starting position with arms beneath your shoulders and reset your brace before the next rep.

nE: Ring Single Arm Rear Delt Row
nR: Тяга на заднюю дельту одной рукой на кольцах
nH: חתירה לכתף אחורית ביד אחת על טבעות
t: Set the ring to roughly shoulder height — lower rings will increase difficulty by deepening your lean. | Stand facing the anchor point and grip the ring with one hand using a neutral or slightly pronated grip, palm facing inward. | Place your free hand on your hip or hold it across your chest to prevent it from assisting the movement. | Walk your feet forward until your body is on a diagonal lean, with your working arm extended in front of you and your weight supported by the ring. | Brace your core and keep your body in a straight, rigid line from head to heels throughout the set. | Initiate the pull by driving your elbow straight back horizontally at shoulder height — keep the elbow in line with your shoulder, not dropping toward your hip. | Continue pulling until your hand reaches the side of your chest and your elbow is pointing directly behind you, squeezing the rear delt at the top. | Lower yourself back to the start position under full control, letting the arm extend completely before the next rep. | Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other arm.

t: Set the rings at a height that lets you hang freely with your feet clear of the floor throughout the rotation. | Grip the rings with an overhand grip, palms facing away from you, and hang at full arm extension with your core lightly braced. | Press your shoulders down and away from your ears to establish a stable, active hang — avoid passively dumping into your joints. | Tuck your knees toward your chest, then drive your hips upward, guiding your legs overhead toward an inverted position. | Continue rotating backward, allowing your arms and wrists to turn naturally with your body as your legs pass through and behind you into the German hang — arms extended overhead, body hanging below. | Pause briefly at the bottom of the German hang to allow the shoulder stretch to deepen, keeping your arms straight. | Reverse the movement by tucking your knees and driving your legs back through the way they came, rotating your body forward with the same controlled tempo. | Lower your feet back to the starting hang position to complete one full repetition.

t: Set the rings wider than shoulder-width — roughly 1.5 times shoulder-width is a useful starting point — and adjust them to the same height. | Hang from the rings with a neutral or slightly pronated grip, arms fully extended, and let your shoulder blades rise naturally at the bottom. | Engage your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from shoulders to feet. | Depress and retract your shoulder blades — pull them down and back — before initiating the pull. | Drive your elbows out and down toward your hips, pulling your chest up toward the rings. | Continue pulling until your chest reaches ring level or your chin clears the rings, keeping your torso upright rather than letting it swing. | Pause briefly at the top, then lower yourself under control back to a full hang. | Complete your reps without kipping or swinging, resetting your shoulder position between reps if needed.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs spread wide in a straddle position, as far apart as is comfortable without forcing range. | Sit up tall, place both hands on the floor in front of you for support, and let your feet flex or relax naturally. | Inhale to lengthen your spine, then exhale and slowly rock your weight forward, walking your hands out ahead of you. | Pause at the limit of your comfortable range for one or two breaths, feeling a stretch along the inner thighs and groin. | Slowly rock back to the starting position, keeping your back relatively upright rather than collapsing into a slump. | Continue rocking forward and back in a smooth, controlled rhythm for the desired number of repetitions or time. | To add a lateral component, shift your weight toward one leg, pause briefly, then rock back through center and toward the other leg. | When finished, bring your legs together slowly before standing up.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward and arms hanging at your sides. | Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to lower into a squat until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up and your weight through your heels. | As you reach the bottom of the squat, swing your arms back behind your hips to load the movement. | Explode upward by driving through your legs and swinging your arms forcefully overhead, leaving the ground as high as possible. | At the peak of the jump your body should be fully extended — legs straight, arms reaching straight up above your head. | Begin pulling your arms back down as you descend so they help absorb the landing. | Land softly by bending your knees to cushion the impact, allowing your hips to drop back into the bottom of the squat position. | Use the momentum from the landing to flow directly into the next repetition without pausing at the bottom. | Continue for the prescribed number of repetitions or duration, maintaining consistent jump height and soft landings throughout.

t: Kneel on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, hip-width apart. Keep your spine neutral and your head in line with your back. | Take a slow breath in to prepare, bracing your core lightly without holding your breath. | Exhale as you push your hips back toward your heels, lowering your torso toward the floor in a controlled slide. Allow your arms to extend naturally in front of you as your hips descend. | Pause briefly in the lowered position — your hips should be close to or resting on your heels and your chest near your thighs, resembling child's pose. | Inhale and shift your weight forward, pressing through your hands to return to the starting quadruped position. Keep the movement smooth and continuous rather than jerky. | Continue rocking back and forth at a steady, unhurried pace for the prescribed number of repetitions or time. | To finish, hold the lowered position for two to three breaths before returning to neutral and resting.

t: Kneel on the floor with one foot flat on the ground in front of you, knee bent at roughly 90°, and the other knee resting on the floor behind you for support. | Place your hands on your front knee or the floor for balance. | Keeping your front heel firmly on the floor, slowly rock your body weight forward so your front knee travels over your toes — this is the dorsiflexion (toes-up) end of the movement. | Rock back to the starting position, allowing your ankle to return to neutral. | Continue rocking forward and back in a smooth, controlled rhythm, going a little further into dorsiflexion each time as the joint loosens. | Perform the desired number of reps, then switch legs and repeat on the other side. | To increase intensity, you can perform the exercise standing with one hand on a wall for support, rocking the working knee forward over the toes.

t: Place a foam roller on the floor and kneel behind it, then lower the front of your left shin onto the roller just above the ankle. | Support your upper body with both hands flat on the floor in front of you, arms straight, so you can control how much bodyweight presses into the roller. | Keep your right knee on the floor or extend the right leg out to the side to adjust the load on the working leg. | Brace your core slightly and keep your spine neutral — avoid letting your lower back sag. | Using your arms, slowly push your body forward so the roller travels up the front of the shin toward the knee, moving at roughly one inch per second. | When you reach a tender spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and letting the tissue relax. | Continue rolling from ankle to just below the knee, covering the full length of the anterior lower leg — never roll directly over the knee joint. | Complete 2–3 slow passes up and down the shin, then switch legs and repeat the same sequence on the other side.

nE: Roll Around the World Lying on Floor
nR: Круги лёжа на полу с роллом
nH: עיגולים בשכיבה על הרצפה עם רולר
t: Place the foam roller on the floor perpendicular to your spine. Sit in front of it, then lean back so the roller contacts your mid-back at roughly the level of your shoulder blades. | Lower yourself until your upper back rests on the roller with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Support your head lightly with your hands or let your arms rest at your sides to start. Engage your core to keep your hips low and your lower back relaxed. | Slowly extend both arms out to your sides, then sweep them up overhead in a wide arc, as if making a snow angel — this is the "around the world" motion. | Continue the sweep, bringing your arms around and back down to your sides, completing a full circle. Move at a slow, controlled pace and breathe steadily throughout. | Pause at any point in the arc where you feel tightness in the upper back, holding for two to three seconds to allow the tissue to release. | Reverse the direction of the arm sweep for the next repetition to work the muscles from both angles. | After completing your reps, shift the roller slightly up or down your spine to address different segments of the thoracic region before repeating.

t: Place a foam roller or cylindrical roll on the floor perpendicular to your body. | Sit on the floor in front of the roller, then lean back so the roller contacts the middle of your upper back, just below the shoulder blades. | Cross your arms over your chest or support the back of your head with both hands to keep your neck neutral. | Plant your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and engage your glutes to lift your hips slightly so your body forms a gentle arc over the roller. | Allow gravity to extend your thoracic spine over the roller, breathing out as you relax into the stretch. | Hold the stretched position for one to two seconds, then use your feet and glutes to drive your hips up and roll the foam roller a few centimetres toward your upper back. | Pause again at each new segment, letting the spine extend over the roller before rolling further. | Continue rolling upward until you reach the base of the neck, then reverse direction and work back down toward the lower thoracic area. | Complete the desired number of passes, then roll to one side and press up to a seated position.

t: Place the rollball on the floor and get down onto your forearms, positioning yourself face-down or slightly to one side so you can reach your inner thigh. | Lift one leg out to the side at roughly a 45-degree angle from your body, and position the rollball against the inner thigh just above the knee. | Shift enough bodyweight onto that leg to create firm, tolerable pressure through the ball — support the rest of your weight on your forearms and opposite leg. | Breathe in slowly, then as you exhale, allow your muscles to soften into the pressure rather than tensing against it. | Begin rolling the ball slowly up toward the groin in small increments, pausing for 2–3 seconds on any area that feels noticeably tender or restricted. | When you find a tender spot, hold the ball still there and maintain steady pressure for 20–30 seconds until the discomfort begins to ease. | Continue working the ball along the full length of the inner thigh from just above the knee up to the groin, then reverse direction back down. | Complete 1–2 minutes on one leg, then switch to the other side and repeat the process. | Finish by performing a gentle static stretch of the inner thigh to reinforce the mobility gained from the release.

t: Place a lacrosse ball or massage ball on the floor in front of you. | Lie face down and position the ball under the front of one upper arm, roughly at the midpoint of the bicep brachii — between the elbow crease and the front of the shoulder. | Extend that arm forward at roughly a 45° angle from your torso with your palm facing down or slightly to the side. | Use your free arm and legs to brace against the floor, controlling how much of your bodyweight presses onto the ball. | Slowly roll your arm so the ball travels along the front of the upper arm, from just above the elbow crease toward the front of the shoulder. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold light, steady pressure on it for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly. | Continue rolling for 30–60 seconds total on that arm, then switch to the other side.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you. Place the rollball under your right calf, roughly at the mid-point between the ankle and the back of the knee. | Lift your hips off the floor slightly and prop yourself up on your hands behind you, so your body weight presses the calf down onto the ball. | Slowly roll your calf forward over the ball, moving from just above the ankle toward the base of the knee. Keep the movement controlled — about one inch per second. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold light pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily, until the tension decreases. | Continue rolling back down toward the ankle, covering the full length of the gastrocnemius (upper calf belly). | Rotate your leg slightly inward and repeat the rolling motion to reach the soleus, which runs deeper and along the inner edge of the lower calf. | Adjust the load by crossing your left ankle over your right leg to add more pressure, or keep both legs down to reduce it. | Spend 60–90 seconds total on each calf, then switch legs and repeat. | Finish with 2–3 slow ankle circles to encourage blood flow through the tissue.

t: Place a rollball against a wall at approximately shoulder height, then position your rear shoulder directly against the ball. | Lean your body weight gently into the ball so it presses into the posterior deltoid — the fleshy area at the back of your shoulder. | Stand with a slight bend in your knees and feet shoulder-width apart to maintain a stable, balanced stance. | Slowly roll the ball upward toward the top of the rear shoulder, pausing on any tender or tight spot you find. | Hold pressure on each tender point for 20–30 seconds, breathing deeply and allowing the muscle to relax into the ball. | Continue rolling the ball downward and outward, exploring the full area of the posterior deltoid. | Rotate your arm slowly inward and outward while maintaining ball pressure to increase the release effect on the muscle fibers. | Work each tight area for 1–2 minutes, then lower your arm and step away from the wall to assess your shoulder mobility.

t: Lie face down on the floor. t: Place a rollball on the floor and sit beside it, then carefully lower yourself so the ball sits just to one side of your spine in the lower back, not directly on the vertebrae. | Lean your body weight into the ball by supporting yourself on your hands or forearms and bending your knees with feet flat on the floor. | Breathe out and allow your muscles to relax into the pressure of the ball. | Slowly shift your body up and down a few centimeters to roll the ball along the erector spinae from the top of the hip toward the mid-back. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds until the tension softens. | Continue rolling and pausing on any additional tight areas along the same side of the spine. | When finished with one side, carefully roll off the ball, reposition it to the opposite side of the spine, and repeat. | Finish by moving gently off the ball, resting flat on your back for a moment before standing.

t: Place a rollball on the floor and stand or sit in a stable position near a wall or chair for balance. | Position the ball under the heel of one foot, keeping the opposite foot flat on the floor. | Shift enough weight onto the working foot to create comfortable but firm pressure on the ball. | Slowly roll the ball forward along the arch toward the ball of the foot, moving in a controlled, deliberate pace. | Pause on any tender or tight spots for 5–10 seconds to allow the tissue to release. | Continue rolling back toward the heel, sweeping the full length of the plantar fascia. | Angle the foot slightly inward, then outward, to cover the medial and lateral edges of the arch. | Perform 60–90 seconds of rolling on each foot, then switch sides.

t: Sit at a table or desk with your forearm resting palm-down on the surface. Place the rollball on top of the dorsal (back) side of your forearm, roughly halfway between the wrist and elbow. | Rest your opposite hand on top of the ball to control pressure. Your forearm stays flat and relaxed on the surface throughout. | Apply moderate downward pressure through your top hand so the ball presses into the forearm extensor muscles. t: Sit at a table or bench and place the rollball on the surface in front of you. | Rest your forearm on the table with the palm facing up, so the underside of your forearm (the flexor side) is exposed. | Position the rollball under your forearm, starting just above the wrist crease where the flexor tendons gather. | Apply gentle downward pressure through your forearm onto the ball, using your opposite hand on top of your forearm to add load as needed. | Slowly roll your forearm forward over the ball, moving from the wrist toward the elbow at a rate of roughly one inch per second. | When you encounter a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, until the tension begins to ease. | Continue rolling up toward the mid-forearm, covering the full length of the flexor muscle belly. | Rotate your forearm slightly inward or outward to shift the ball onto adjacent flexor muscles and ensure full coverage. | Spend 60–90 seconds on each forearm, then switch arms and repeat.

Bend both knees and keep your feet flat on the floor. | Shift enough body weight onto the ball so you feel moderate pressure in the outer hip tissue, but not sharp or shooting pain. | Slowly move your hips in small, controlled circles or inch forward and backward to scan for areas of increased tension in the gluteus medius. | When you find a tender or tight spot, stop moving and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and letting the muscle relax into the ball. | Когда напряжение в этой точке снизится, продолжите сканирование в поиске следующего участка ограничения, двигаясь от заднего края мышцы к передней части бедра. | To reach the anterior portion of the gluteus medius, rotate your hip slightly inward so the ball shifts toward the front of the outer hip. | Spend 60–90 seconds total on the right side, then reposition and repeat on the left hip.

t: Place a rollball on the floor and lie face-down, positioning the ball just inside the front of one hip bone (iliac crest), roughly an inch medial to the ASIS and low on the lower abdomen. | Lower yourself gently onto the ball so it contacts the soft tissue of the lower abdomen where the iliacus lies beneath, keeping most body weight through your forearms and opposite hip. | Breathe slowly and allow your abdomen to relax so the ball can sink progressively deeper toward the iliacus rather than pressing against braced abdominal muscles. | Scan for a tender or tight spot by making small, deliberate shifts of body weight — forward, back, or slightly side-to-side — until you locate a point of significant tension. | Hold sustained pressure on that tender point for 20–30 seconds, breathing deeply and letting the tissue soften under the ball. | Once the initial tenderness eases, slowly flex and extend the same-side hip by sliding the knee out and back, using the movement to further release the iliacus against the ball. | Continue for a total of 60–90 seconds per side, repositioning the ball slightly to address different portions of the muscle. | When finished, press up slowly, rest a moment, then switch to the opposite side.

t: Lie face down on a firm surface with the rollball placed on the floor in front of you. | Position the ball just medial to your hip flexor crease — roughly two to three finger-widths inside and below the front of your hip bone (ASIS), where the iliopsoas runs toward the lesser trochanter. | Lower your body so the ball contacts the soft tissue of the hip flexor. Support your upper body on your forearms, keeping your spine neutral and your neck long. | Shift your weight slowly onto the ball until you feel moderate pressure on the target tissue. You are looking for a sensation of deep tension or mild discomfort — not sharp or nerve-like pain. | When you locate a tender or dense area, hold still on that spot and breathe steadily for 20–30 seconds. Let the tissue soften before moving. | Make small, slow movements — rocking slightly forward, backward, or side to side — to explore adjacent tissue along the iliopsoas line. | To increase pressure, bend the knee of the working side and bring the heel toward your glutes. This shortens the hip flexor and exposes deeper tissue to the ball. | Spend 60–90 seconds on one side, then carefully lift your body off the ball, reposition, and repeat on the other side. | After rolling each side, stand and perform a brief hip flexor stretch to reinforce the increased range of motion you have just created.

t: Choose a firm, small ball (lacrosse ball or massage ball) and stand with your back toward a smooth wall. | Reach across your chest with the opposite hand to locate the infraspinatus — the fleshy area below the spine of your shoulder blade and just lateral to the inner edge of the scapula. | Place the ball between the wall and that spot, then shift your body weight gently into the ball to apply comfortable pressure. | Step your feet slightly away from the wall so your body leans back, increasing the load through the ball as needed. | Hold steady pressure on any tender spot for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and letting the muscle relax into the ball. | Make small, controlled movements — shift slightly up, down, or side to side — to explore the tissue and locate additional trigger points. | When you find a sore spot, pause and sustain pressure until the intensity reduces by roughly half before moving on. | Continue for 60–90 seconds on each side, then step away from the wall and gently roll your shoulder in circles to assess any change in mobility. | Switch sides and repeat the process on the opposite infraspinatus.

t: Stand facing away from a wall with a rollball in your hand. Place the ball between your upper back and the wall, positioning it over the infraspinatus — the muscular area on the back of your shoulder blade, below the spine of the scapula. | Lean your body weight back into the ball to create initial contact pressure. Keep your feet roughly shoulder-width apart and about one foot away from the wall so you can control how much load you apply. | Cross the arm on the working side across your chest, bringing your hand toward the opposite shoulder. This moves the scapula away from the spine and exposes more of the infraspinatus to the ball. | Using your legs to drive movement, slowly shift your body up, down, and in small lateral arcs so the ball rolls across the infraspinatus. Move at roughly one inch per second. | When you locate a tender or restricted spot, pause and hold steady pressure there for 20–30 seconds. Breathe slowly and allow the tissue to soften under the sustained load. | Continue exploring the infraspinatus by adjusting the height and lateral position of the ball, covering from just below the scapular spine down toward the inferior angle of the shoulder blade. | To increase pressure, bend your knees slightly and lean more of your body weight into the wall. To reduce it, stand more upright and bear less load. | Spend 60–90 seconds total on each side, then switch arms and repeat on the opposite shoulder.

t: Lie face down on the floor and position the rollball under your right outer thigh, roughly at mid-thigh level along the lateral edge of the quadriceps. | Prop yourself up on your forearms so your upper body weight is supported and you can control how much pressure your thigh applies to the ball. | Extend your right leg and allow it to relax so your body weight presses the vastus lateralis into the ball. | Slowly roll your thigh forward and back over the ball, moving from just above the knee toward the hip in a controlled manner — about one inch per second. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, until you feel the tissue soften and release. | Continue rolling along the full length of the lateral thigh, working from just above the knee to the outer hip. | Adjust load by bending the opposite knee and placing that foot on the floor to reduce pressure, or crossing the opposite ankle over the working leg to increase it. | Spend 60–90 seconds total on the right leg, then reposition the ball under the left outer thigh and repeat. | Finish with a gentle standing quad stretch to encourage blood flow through the released tissue.

t: Place the rollball on the floor and lie on your side with the ball positioned just below your armpit, against the outer edge of your back. | Extend your bottom arm overhead along the floor to open up the lat and give the ball room to work. | Stack your legs or bend your top knee and place that foot on the floor for balance. | Let your bodyweight sink onto the ball so it applies firm pressure to the lat tissue. | Slowly roll your torso forward and back a few centimeters to search for a tender or tight spot. | When you find a tight area, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly and allowing the tissue to relax. | Continue rolling in small increments along the length of the lat, from just below the armpit toward the mid-back, pausing at each tense point. | After working one side, roll off the ball, rest briefly, then repeat on the opposite side.

t: Choose your position: stand with your back against a wall, or lie on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. | Place a small firm rollball between your lower back and the wall or floor, positioning it on the muscle tissue just to one side of the lumbar spine — never directly on the vertebrae. | Slowly shift your body weight into the ball until you feel moderate, tolerable pressure on the target muscle. | Hold steady pressure on any tender spot for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing the muscle to relax. | Once the tension releases, nudge your body slightly up, down, or in a small circle to find the next tender area. | Continue exploring the erector spinae tissue on that side for 60–90 seconds before switching to the opposite side of the spine. | Keep your core lightly engaged and your glutes relaxed throughout to allow the lower back muscles to release fully. | Finish by gently rolling off the ball, resting for a moment, and performing a slow knee-to-chest stretch to further lengthen the lower back.

t: Sit on the floor and place the rollball behind you, angled roughly 30–45 degrees off the midline of your lower back, between your spine and the top of your pelvis on one side. | Slowly lean back and lower yourself onto the ball so it makes contact with the lateral lumbar region — not directly on the spine itself. | Bend both knees and plant your feet flat on the floor. Use your feet and hands to control how much body weight loads onto the ball. | Shift your hips slightly toward the side being worked to increase pressure on the quadratus lumborum and the lateral edge of the erector spinae. | Begin making small, slow movements — rolling diagonally along the muscle fibers from just above the pelvis toward the lower rib — covering a range of about three to four inches. | When you find a tender or restricted spot, hold still on that point for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the tissue to soften under the pressure. | Continue working the full diagonal path, pausing on any secondary tight spots for the same duration. | After 60–90 seconds, carefully sit up, reposition the ball on the opposite side, and repeat the process. | Finish with two or three slow, controlled knee-to-chest pulls on each side to encourage circulation through the worked tissue.

nE: Roll Ball Lying Semisplinalis Capitis Muscle Activation
nR: Активация полуостистой мышцы головы лёжа мячом

t: Place a rollball on the floor and lie on your back, bending your knees so your feet are flat on the floor. | Lift your head, position the ball at the base of your skull — roughly at the junction between your neck and the back of your head — and slowly lower your head onto it. | Allow the natural weight of your head to sink into the ball; do not press down forcefully. | Breathe slowly and let the surrounding muscles relax for 20–30 seconds as the initial tension begins to ease. | Make micro-adjustments by gently nodding your chin toward your chest or rotating your head a few degrees left or right to find tender spots. | When you locate a point of increased sensitivity, hold steady and breathe into the discomfort until you feel it soften — typically 20–45 seconds. | Reposition the ball slightly and repeat on any additional tight spots within the same region. | To finish, use both hands to support your head, lift it off the ball, and set the ball aside before lowering your head gently to the floor. | Rest for a moment, then slowly roll to one side before rising to avoid sudden head movement.

t: Stand facing a wall or lie face down on the floor — both positions work. If standing, place the rollball between your upper chest (just below the collarbone) and the wall at chest height. | Position the ball on the clavicular portion of the pectoralis major: approximately one to two inches below the center of your collarbone, just medial to the shoulder. | Lean your body weight gently into the ball so it compresses the upper chest tissue. Start with light pressure to assess sensitivity before adding more load. | Slowly roll the ball in small circles or short strokes along the upper chest, moving from the sternum outward toward the front of the shoulder, staying below the collarbone the entire time. | When you locate a tender or tight spot, stop rolling and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds. Breathe slowly and allow the tissue to relax under the pressure. | After the hold, continue rolling laterally toward the front of the shoulder, covering the full width of the clavicular head. | To increase pressure, shift more body weight into the wall or floor. To reduce it, step slightly back or prop yourself up more with your free arm. | Spend 60–90 seconds working through the upper chest on one side, then switch to the other side and repeat. | Finish by gently retracting your shoulder blades and taking two or three slow, full breaths to help the chest open up.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and place the rollball on the ground just below your right knee on the outer side of the lower leg. | Position the lateral calf — the area over the peroneal muscles — directly on top of the rollball, using your hands behind you for support. | Lift your hips slightly off the floor so your body weight presses your lower leg into the rollball. | Slowly roll the ball down the outer lower leg toward the ankle, moving about 2–3 centimetres per breath. | When you reach a tender or tight spot, pause and hold light pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds until the tension begins to release. | Continue rolling down to just above the outer ankle bone, then reverse direction and roll back up toward the knee. | Keep your upper body relaxed and breathe steadily throughout; avoid holding your breath. | Complete 2–3 passes along the peroneal muscles, then switch to the other leg and repeat.

t: Place a rollball on the floor and sit on your side, preparing to lower the inner surface of your lower leg onto the ball. | Lie on your side with your bottom arm extended or bent for head support, keeping your body in a comfortable straight line. | Position the rollball under the inner aspect of the lower leg of your bottom leg — roughly between the back of the shin bone (tibia) and the calf, where the posterior tibialis runs. | Stack your top leg either directly on top of the bottom leg or rest it slightly in front on the floor for additional stability. | Allow the weight of your lower leg to sink into the ball; do not press down forcefully with your hands or the top leg. | Slowly roll the leg forward and backward along the inner lower leg, scanning from just above the ankle to below the knee to locate tender spots. | When you find an area of increased sensitivity, pause and hold steady for 20–45 seconds, breathing slowly until you feel the tension begin to soften. | Continue rolling to any additional tight areas, spending equal time on each. | To finish, use your hands to lift the leg off the ball, set the ball aside, and rest for a moment before switching sides or standing up.

t: Place the rollball on the floor and lie face down with the ball positioned just inside your hip bone, in the lower-abdominal region where the psoas runs. | Support your upper body on your forearms, keeping your spine in a neutral position. | Shift your body weight gradually onto the ball until you feel moderate pressure on the target area. t: Lie face down on a firm surface such as a mat or carpet. Place the rollball on the floor beneath your abdomen, positioning it just below your navel and to one side of the midline. | Lower your body slowly onto the ball, supporting your upper body on your forearms to control how much of your weight presses into the abdominal tissue. | Begin with light pressure — only a fraction of your bodyweight — and assess your sensitivity before adding more load. | Slowly roll the ball in small, deliberate strokes along the length of the rectus abdominis, moving from just below the navel upward toward the lower ribs. | When you find a tender or tight spot, stop rolling and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds. Breathe slowly through the hold and allow the tissue to relax under the compression. | After each hold, continue rolling — either continuing upward toward the ribs or shifting slightly toward the midline — to cover the full surface of the rectus abdominis on that side. | Adjust the amount of pressure by shifting more or less body weight through your forearms. t: Lie on your back on a firm surface with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. | Place the massage ball beneath your upper back, positioning it between your spine and one shoulder blade to target the rhomboid area — not directly on the spine. | Cross both arms over your chest, or reach one arm across your body, to retract the shoulder blade and expose the rhomboid muscle beneath it. | Press through your feet to lift your hips slightly, loading your body weight onto the ball. | Slowly shift your body up and down, or side to side, rolling the ball across the rhomboid area in small, controlled movements. | When you find a tender spot, pause and hold steady pressure there for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing the tissue to soften. | Continue rolling across the full rhomboid region — from the upper border near the base of your neck down to the lower border near the mid-back — for 60–90 seconds per side. | Lower your hips, reposition the ball to the opposite side of your spine, and repeat on the other shoulder.

t: Stand with your back facing a wall and place the rollball between the wall and the upper back, just beside the base of your neck at the top of the shoulder blade. | Lean your body weight into the wall to compress the ball against the target area — the levator scapulae attachment near the superior angle of the scapula. | Adjust your feet a few inches away from the wall so you can control the amount of pressure applied through your bodyweight. | Tilt and rotate your head gently away from the side being worked to lengthen the levator scapulae and increase the stretch on the tissue. | Hold still on any tender point for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing the muscle to relax into the pressure. | Make small, controlled movements — shifting slightly up, down, or sideways — to locate additional areas of tension along the muscle. | Reduce pressure by standing more upright if the sensation becomes too intense; increase pressure by leaning further into the wall. | Once the area feels released, move the ball to an adjacent tender spot and repeat the process. | Complete the work on one side before repositioning the ball to mirror the same area on the opposite side.

t: Sit or stand beside a wall and hold the rollball in the hand on the side you intend to work. | Place the rollball between the wall and the upper back, positioning it just above the top inner corner of the shoulder blade where the levator scapulae attaches. | Lean gently into the wall so the ball takes on a comfortable amount of your body weight — you should feel noticeable pressure without sharp pain. | Drop that shoulder slightly downward to lengthen the levator scapulae and allow the ball to sink into the muscle. | Slowly rotate your head away from the side being worked and tuck your chin slightly toward the opposite collar bone to deepen the stretch. | Hold this position and breathe deeply, allowing the muscle to relax and soften into the ball for 20–40 seconds. | To explore the tissue further, make small, slow head rotations or gently nod your chin up and down while maintaining contact with the ball. | Release the pressure gradually, reposition the ball slightly higher or lower if needed, and repeat on the same spot or move to an adjacent area. | Switch sides and repeat the full sequence on the opposite levator scapulae.
