t: Set up two markers (cones, lines, or tape) about 5–10 metres apart on a flat surface. | Stand in an athletic stance at one marker with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hips lowered into a quarter-squat position. | Keep your chest up, core braced, and weight on the balls of your feet throughout the drill. | Push off your inside foot and shuffle laterally toward the opposite marker, moving both feet quickly without crossing them. | As you reach the second marker, tap it with your hand or foot to confirm full travel, then immediately reverse direction. | Shuffle back to the starting marker at maximum controlled speed, staying low and keeping your hips level. | Continue shuttling side-to-side for the prescribed time or number of repetitions, maintaining your athletic stance on every change of direction. | To finish, decelerate smoothly at the final marker rather than stopping abruptly.

t: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against a bench or step, knees bent and feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart. | Extend one leg straight out in front of you, keeping it roughly parallel to the floor, so only the working foot remains planted. | Place your hands lightly on the bench beside your hips for balance, or cross your arms over your chest. | Brace your core, tuck your chin slightly, and press your working foot firmly into the floor to pre-tension the glute. | Drive your hips upward by pushing through the working foot until your torso and working thigh form a straight line from your shoulders to your knee. | Pause at the top for one count, squeezing the working glute fully while keeping your hips level. | Lower your hips under control until they hover just above the floor without fully resting. | Complete all reps on one side before switching legs.

t: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and your arms at your sides. | Engage your core and curl your head and upper shoulders off the floor, keeping your chin lightly tucked and your lower back pressed into the mat. | Lift both legs off the floor, then raise your right leg toward the ceiling while extending your left leg out at roughly a 45-degree angle. | Reach both hands toward your right calf or ankle, keeping your elbows wide and your shoulders lifted throughout. | Pulse your right leg gently toward you twice with light assistance from your hands. | Switch legs in a controlled scissor motion — lower your right leg to the 45-degree position as you raise your left leg toward the ceiling. | Reach your hands toward your left calf or ankle and repeat the two pulses. | Continue alternating legs with a steady, controlled rhythm while maintaining the spinal flexion position and the lower back contact with the mat. | After completing the prescribed repetitions on each side, lower both legs and your head back to the floor in a controlled manner.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you and your hands placed on the floor just behind your hips, fingers pointing forward. | Brace your core and sit tall, keeping your spine neutral and your chest lifted. | Press your palms lightly into the floor to stabilize your torso without leaning heavily on your arms. | Exhale and raise both legs together off the floor until they reach roughly a 45-degree angle, keeping the knees straight or very slightly soft. | Hold the top position for one to two seconds, maintaining tension through your core. | Inhale and lower your legs in a controlled manner back toward the floor, stopping just before your heels touch down. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions without letting your lower back round excessively or your torso collapse. | After completing the set, lower your legs fully to the floor and release the brace.

t: Place a sturdy chair or flat bench behind you and stand in front of it with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes turned out slightly. | Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and extend your arms forward to shoulder height for balance. | Push your hips back and bend your knees simultaneously, sending your weight through your heels as you begin to descend. | Lower yourself slowly, maintaining an upright torso and keeping your knees tracking over your toes. | Continue descending until your glutes lightly touch the seat — do not fully sit down or relax your weight onto the chair. | Pause for one second at the bottom, keeping your muscles engaged and your feet flat on the floor. | Drive through your heels and mid-foot to press back up to a full standing position. | Squeeze your glutes at the top and reset your brace before beginning the next rep.

nR: Попеременные отведения со скруткой сидя на стуле

nR: Попеременные колено к локтю со скруткой сидя
nH: ברך למרפק לסירוגין עם פיתול בישיבה

t: Sit in the 45-degree sled machine and press your lower back, hips, and head firmly against the pad. | Place your right foot flat in the center of the platform at roughly hip width, with your toes angled slightly outward; rest your left foot on the frame or floor. | Grip the handles at your sides to anchor your upper body and brace your core. | Disengage the safety stops and hold the sled with your working leg extended, stopping just short of full knee lockout. | Inhale and lower the sled under control by bending your working knee slowly — take three to four seconds to descend — keeping your heel flat on the platform and your knee tracking in line with your toes. | Continue the descent until your thigh reaches roughly parallel to the platform or your lower back just begins to lift off the pad, whichever comes first. | Exhale and drive evenly through your full foot to press the sled back up, extending your knee and hip simultaneously, and stop just short of full lockout. | Engage the safety stops, switch feet so your left foot is on the platform, release the stops, and repeat the slow eccentric descent followed by a controlled press. | Continue alternating legs for the target number of reps per side, then engage the safety stops securely before exiting the machine.

t: Sit in the 45-degree sled machine and press your lower back and glutes firmly into the seat pad, with your head resting against the backrest. | Place both feet high on the footplate — near the upper edge — with a hip-width to shoulder-width stance and toes pointed slightly outward. | Ensure your entire foot, including your heels, is in contact with the footplate before unracking. | Grip the handles on either side of the seat to stabilize your upper body, then release the safety stoppers to take control of the sled. | Slowly lower the sled by bending your knees and allowing your hips to flex, keeping your lower back pressed into the pad throughout the descent. | Lower until your knees approach your chest or your thighs reach roughly parallel, stopping before your lower back peels away from the seat pad. | Drive through your heels to press the sled back up along the track, focusing on extending the hips and squeezing the glutes at the top. | Stop just short of fully locking out your knees at the top of each rep to keep tension on the muscles. | After completing your reps, rotate the safety stoppers fully into the locked position and confirm they are engaged before exiting the machine.

t: Set the Smith machine bar to approximately mid-thigh height and load it with your working weight. | Stand facing the bar with your feet hip-width apart, unhook the bar, and hold it with a shoulder-width underhand (supinated) grip. | Let the bar hang at arm's length against the front of your thighs, keeping your torso upright and your shoulders pulled back. | Initiate the curl by driving your elbows back behind your torso rather than forward, allowing the bar to travel up along your body — brushing the abdomen, then the chest — as your elbows travel rearward. | Continue dragging the bar up until your elbows are fully bent and the bar is at upper-chest or shoulder level. | Squeeze your biceps hard at the top for a one-count, keeping the bar close to your body throughout. | Lower the bar under control by reversing the path — letting it slide down your torso as your elbows drift forward — until your arms are fully extended. | Complete your reps, then re-hook the bar safely.

t: Set the Smith machine bar to shoulder height and load it with your working weight. | Position a flat bench or sturdy box about two feet behind the bar. | Step under the bar, rest it across your upper traps, and unrack it by rotating the safeties. | Walk forward until there is enough space for a full lunge stride, then place the top of your rear foot on the bench behind you. | Position your front foot far enough forward so that when you squat down your shin stays roughly vertical and your knee does not travel far past your toes. | Lower your hips straight down by bending the front knee and hip, keeping your torso upright and your core braced. | Descend until your rear knee approaches but does not touch the floor, or until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the ground. | Drive through your front heel and mid-foot to extend the knee and hip and return to the starting position. | Complete all reps on that leg, then re-rack the bar, switch legs, and repeat.

t: Set the Smith machine bar to roughly shoulder height and step under it so the bar rests across the front of your shoulders on your anterior deltoids. | Extend both arms straight out in front of you, parallel to the floor, with palms facing down — the classic 'Frankenstein' position. | Step your feet roughly shoulder-width apart with toes turned out slightly, far enough forward that your torso can stay upright during the descent. | Unrack the bar by rotating the hooks and stand tall with your chest up, core braced, and your upper back tight to hold the bar in place. | Begin the descent by bending your hips and knees together and sitting straight down rather than pushing your hips back, keeping the bar stable on your shoulders without gripping it. | Squat down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor or slightly below, maintaining an upright torso and keeping your knees tracking over your toes. | Drive through your full foot to press the floor away, extending your hips and knees at the same rate to return to the starting position. | Lock out at the top without hyperextending your lower back, then immediately begin the next rep or re-rack safely by rotating the hooks.

t: Set the Smith machine bar to roughly shoulder height and load it with an appropriate weight. | Place a stable platform or weight plate — 2–4 inches high — on the floor directly in front of the bar. | Step under the bar, position it across your upper traps, and unrack it. | Step one foot forward and place it flat on the platform, keeping the heel fully in contact with the surface. | Step the rear foot straight back until you are in a long split stance — far enough that your rear knee can reach near the floor at the bottom. | Stand tall with your torso upright, core braced, and hips square to the front. | Inhale and lower your body by bending both knees, letting the front knee track over your toes as you descend. | Stop when your rear knee is just above or lightly grazing the floor and your front thigh is at or below parallel. | Drive through your front foot to press back up to the starting position, complete all reps on one leg, then switch sides.

t: Set the Smith machine safety pins at the height the bar reaches when it is resting on your upper traps and your torso is hinged to roughly parallel with the floor — around hip height for most lifters. Test the height with an empty bar first. | Load the bar and rest it on the pins, then step under it so it sits across your upper traps, not on your neck. Set your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart with toes turned out slightly. | Push your hips back to settle into the hinged start position with the bar loaded on your traps, a soft bend in the knees, and a neutral (not rounded) spine from tailbone to skull. | Brace your core hard, set your shoulder blades back and down, and take the bar's weight off the pins. | Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand tall, keeping your spine neutral the whole way up. t: Sit tall on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you, feet flexed and hip-width apart. | Place your hands lightly behind your head or extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, whichever feels more comfortable. | Inhale to lengthen your spine, sitting as tall as possible and engaging your core. | Exhale and slowly rotate your upper body to the right, leading with your chest and keeping your hips and legs completely still. | Pause at the end of your comfortable range of motion for 1–2 seconds, feeling the stretch through your waist and obliques. | Inhale and return your torso back to the center with control. | Exhale and rotate to the left in the same controlled manner, again keeping the hips anchored to the floor. | Return to center, then repeat the sequence for the desired number of repetitions on each side.

t: Stand in your fighting stance with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hands raised to guard position. | Shift your weight onto your rear foot and begin rotating your hips and shoulders away from your target, initiating the spin. | Pivot on the ball of your rear foot, allowing your body to rotate 180 degrees so your back momentarily faces the target. | As your body continues rotating toward the target, lift the knee of your kicking leg to chamber height — roughly hip to mid-chest level. | Drive your hips through by extending the kicking leg outward in a sweeping hook motion, making contact with the heel or sole of the foot at the target. | Keep your standing knee slightly bent throughout to absorb force and maintain stability. | Pull the kicking leg back sharply after contact, reversing the hook motion to chamber the knee again. | Land in a controlled stance with your weight centered and your guard back up, ready to follow with the next technique.

t: Stand tall with your feet together and your arms at your sides. | Jump and simultaneously split your legs so your right foot lands forward and your left foot lands behind you, landing in a staggered stance roughly shoulder-width apart. | At the same time, swing your arms in opposition — right arm forward and left arm back — to mirror your leg movement. | Keep your torso upright, core braced, and land with soft knees to absorb the impact. | Jump again and switch legs and arms in a single fluid motion, so your left foot moves forward and your right foot moves back. | Continue alternating the split position at a controlled, rhythmic pace. | To finish, bring your feet together on a jump and return your arms to your sides.

t: Stand facing a sturdy box (6–18 inches tall) and step one foot forward into a split stance, with your front foot roughly two feet from the base of the box. | Sink into a lunge position — front knee bent to approximately 90 degrees, rear knee hovering just above the floor — with your torso upright and core braced. | Load your hips by driving them slightly back and keeping your front heel planted. | Swing your arms back to generate momentum, then explosively drive both arms upward as you push off both feet simultaneously. | Leave the ground with maximum power, extending fully through your hips, knees, and ankles at the peak of the jump. | While airborne, bring both feet together and position them to land simultaneously on top of the box with feet roughly hip-width apart. | Land softly with knees slightly bent, hips back, and weight distributed evenly across both feet to absorb impact. | Step back down to the floor one foot at a time, reset into the split stance, and repeat for the target number of repetitions before switching your lead leg.

t: Stand with your feet roughly two to three shoulder-widths apart and your toes turned out slightly, hands clasped in front of your chest or extended forward for balance. | Shift your weight to the right, pushing your hips back and bending your right knee as you descend into a lateral squat on that side. | Lower until your right thigh is roughly parallel to the floor (or as deep as your mobility allows), keeping your left leg straight and your left foot fully planted. | At the bottom of the squat, roll onto the outer edge of your left foot, allowing the sole to tilt slightly as your hips sink deeper and your torso leans forward with a neutral spine. | Pause briefly, feeling the stretch across your left inner thigh and groin. | Roll your left foot back to flat, then drive through your right heel to push yourself back up to the starting position. | Repeat for the desired reps on the right side before switching to the left.

t: Stand with feet hip-width apart, then step one foot forward roughly two to three feet, placing the ball of your back foot on the floor with your heel raised. | Align your front foot so the knee tracks directly over the second toe, and keep your back leg nearly straight with a soft bend at the knee. | Lift your torso to a tall, upright position — chest up, shoulders back, core braced — avoiding any forward lean. | Rest your hands on your hips or extend them alongside your body for balance. | Inhale, then lower your hips straight down by bending the front knee until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor or as low as control allows. | Keep your back knee hovering just above the floor without touching it, and maintain an upright torso throughout the descent. | Exhale and drive through your front heel to press the floor away, extending the front hip and knee to return to the starting high position. | Complete all repetitions on one side before switching legs, or alternate sides each rep depending on your training goal.

t: Start standing with your feet together and your hands relaxed at your sides. | Step your right foot forward roughly two to three feet and plant it flat on the floor, toes pointing straight ahead. | Lower your left knee toward the floor, keeping the left toes tucked under so you are in a low lunge position with the back knee close to — or resting lightly on — the ground. | Sink your hips down and forward until your right thigh is roughly parallel to the floor and your right shin is vertical. This is the low lunge base position. | Drive your right knee forward slightly over the toes to deepen the stretch in the left hip flexor while simultaneously pressing your right foot into the floor to engage the glutes and quadriceps. | To add the sprinter element, lean your torso slightly forward over the front thigh and drive both arms into a sprint-arm position — right arm back, left arm bent forward at roughly 90° — mimicking the upper-body mechanics of a running stride. | Hold the position for the prescribed duration or pulse gently through a small range of motion to increase hip-flexor release and glute activation. | Press through the right heel to stand back up, step your feet together, and repeat on the left side.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, then step one foot roughly two to three feet back, resting on the ball of your rear foot. Your front foot stays flat on the floor. | Place your hands on your hips or let them hang at your sides, and set your torso upright with your core lightly braced. | Inhale, then lower your body straight down by bending both knees simultaneously. | Continue descending until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor and your rear knee hovers just above the ground — do not let it make contact. | Keep your front knee tracking in line with your second toe throughout the descent, not caving inward or drifting far outside your foot. | Press through your front heel to drive back up to the starting position, exhaling as you rise. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat for the same number of reps.

t: Stand in a split squat position: step one foot forward and the other back so your feet are roughly hip-width apart and staggered about two to three feet in length. | Raise the heel of your front foot off the floor so you are balancing on the ball of that foot. Keep the rear foot flat on the floor with the heel down. | Stand tall with your torso upright, core braced, and hands on your hips or extended in front for balance. | Inhale and slowly lower your body straight down by bending both knees simultaneously. Maintain the raised front heel throughout the descent. | Continue descending until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor or your rear knee hovers just above the ground — whichever limit you reach first. | Pause briefly at the bottom, keeping your front knee tracking in line with your toes and your torso upright. | Drive through the ball of your front foot to press back up to the starting position, exhaling as you rise. | Complete all reps on one side before switching legs.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, then step one foot forward roughly 60–80 cm (2–2.5 feet) and the other foot back, coming onto the ball of your rear foot. | Brace your core, keep your torso upright, and ensure both feet point roughly forward. | Inhale and lower your hips straight down by bending both knees simultaneously — do not let the movement push your torso forward. | Descend until your rear knee is 2–5 cm above the floor, or until your front thigh is approximately parallel to the floor, whichever comes first. | Keep your front knee tracking in line with your second and third toes throughout the descent — do not let it cave inward. | Press through the heel and mid-foot of your front foot to drive back up to the starting position. | Exhale as you rise. Complete all reps on one side before switching legs.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes turned out slightly. Take a breath and brace your core lightly before you begin. | Slowly lower into a deep squat, pushing your knees out over your toes and keeping your heels flat on the floor. Hold the bottom position for 2–3 seconds, letting your hips sink toward the ground. | While in the bottom of the squat, place both hands on the floor inside your feet. Drive one knee out with your elbow and hold for 2–3 seconds, then switch sides. This is the hip-opener component. | From the deep squat, shift your weight fully onto one side and straighten the opposite leg out to the side, reaching the heel into the floor to stretch the adductor and hamstring. Hold for 2–3 seconds, then shift to the other side. | Return to the deep squat position. Place both hands on the floor, then lift your hips into a flat-back position (similar to a Romanian deadlift stretch), feeling the hamstrings lengthen. Pause for 2–3 seconds. | Lower back into the deep squat and rise to standing by driving through your heels and extending your hips and knees together. | Repeat the full sequence for 5–8 controlled cycles, moving smoothly between each position without rushing.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes turned out 15–30°. Let your arms hang at your sides or hold them in front for balance. | Look down at your feet and identify the line of each toe. Throughout the drill, your knee should track in line with that toe — not collapse inward or flare excessively outward. | Brace your core lightly, keep your chest tall, and begin the descent by pushing your hips back and bending your knees simultaneously. | Pause when your thighs reach parallel to the floor, or at the deepest point you can hold with flat feet and an upright torso. Check your knees: each one should be directly over the middle of the corresponding foot, pointing in the same direction as the toes. | If your knees have drifted inward (valgus collapse), press them out to realign them before continuing. Push your knees outward against the direction of any collapse as you ascend — think about spreading the floor apart with your feet. | Lock out your hips fully at the top, check your stance, and repeat for the target number of reps.

t: Stand at the base of a staircase or in front of a single step, feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides. | Hinge slightly at the hips and bend your knees into a quarter-squat to load your legs. | Swing your arms back, then drive them forward and upward as you push explosively through your feet to jump up onto the step. | Land softly on both feet simultaneously, absorbing the impact by bending your knees and hips — land on the balls of your feet first, then lower your heels. | Stand tall on the step for a brief moment to confirm balance before descending. | Step back down one foot at a time (or jump back down with control if your fitness level allows), returning to the starting position. | Reset your stance and repeat for the target number of reps or duration.

t: Stand upright facing a stair, step, or sturdy box with your feet hip-width apart and your core lightly braced. | Place your right foot flat on the stair so your entire foot — especially the heel — is fully supported. | Shift your weight onto your right foot and drive through that heel to push your body upward, extending your hip and knee. | Bring your left foot up to meet the right foot on the stair, standing tall with both feet on the step. | Step your left foot back down to the ground in a controlled manner, keeping the movement deliberate — not a drop. | Lower your right foot back to the starting position to complete one full rep. | Complete all reps on the right side, then switch to lead with your left foot for the next set, or alternate sides each rep.

t: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands resting on your thighs or hips. | Inhale fully through your nose to expand your ribcage and belly. | Exhale completely through your mouth, expelling as much air as possible. | At the end of the exhale, pull your navel inward and upward as hard as you can, as though trying to touch your spine with your belly button. | Hold this deep contraction for 15–30 seconds while continuing to breathe shallowly through your chest if needed, keeping the abdominal draw engaged. | Slowly release the contraction and allow your abdomen to relax fully. | Rest for a few seconds, then repeat for the prescribed number of sets.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, knees soft (slightly bent), and your weight evenly distributed across both feet. | Place your hands on your hips or extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height to act as a counterbalance. | Engage your core lightly and stand tall — keep your hips square and facing forward throughout the movement. | Exhale and slowly rotate your upper body to the right as far as is comfortable, leading with your chest rather than your shoulders. | Pause for one to two seconds at the end of the range, feeling the stretch along the left side of your waist and abdomen. | Inhale and return smoothly to the center without rushing. | Rotate to the left with the same controlled tempo, pause, and feel the stretch on the right side. | Return to center — that is one full repetition. t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your weight evenly distributed across both feet. | Raise your arms out in front of you at chest height, either clasping your hands together or holding them parallel, keeping them straight throughout the movement. | Brace your core and keep your hips square and facing forward — they should not rotate with your torso. | Exhale and rotate your upper body to the right as far as your range of motion comfortably allows, leading with your shoulders. | Pause briefly at the end of the rotation, feeling the contraction in your right oblique. | Inhale and rotate back through center, then continue rotating to the left side with control. | Pause at the left end range, feeling the contraction in your left oblique. | Continue alternating sides in a smooth, controlled rhythm for the desired number of reps or time.

t: Stand facing a wall or sturdy surface and place both hands on it at roughly chest height for support. | Step one foot back about one stride length, keeping the foot flat and pointing straight ahead. | Bend both knees, sinking your hips down and forward while keeping your back heel pressed firmly into the floor. | Continue bending the back knee until you feel a deep stretch low in the calf and along the Achilles tendon just above the heel — do not allow the heel to lift. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and letting the tension release gradually. | Gently straighten and shake out the leg, then switch legs and repeat on the other side. | Perform 2–3 holds per side, deepening the position slightly with each hold as the tissue relaxes.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your knees slightly soft, not locked out. | Place your hands behind your head with your fingers laced loosely — do not pull on your neck. | Engage your core by drawing your navel gently toward your spine. | Lift your right knee up toward hip height while simultaneously rotating your left elbow toward that knee. | Lower your right foot back to the floor as you return your torso to center. | Immediately lift your left knee and rotate your right elbow toward it, replicating the pedaling motion. | Continue alternating sides in a controlled, rhythmic pace — one knee drive and rotation equals one rep. | Keep your chest tall and your gaze forward throughout; avoid collapsing forward from the hips. | Complete the prescribed number of reps or time interval, then stand upright and lower your arms to finish.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and arms hanging relaxed at your sides. | Engage your core lightly to stabilize your torso and keep your spine neutral throughout the movement. | Raise one arm forward and up, initiating the circle from the shoulder joint while keeping the elbow gently extended. | Continue the arm overhead and then sweep it back and down in a full circular arc, passing close to your ear at the top. | As the first arm completes its downward arc, begin raising the opposite arm forward to start its own circle. | Alternate arms in a continuous, flowing rhythm so that one arm is always moving while the other finishes or starts a circle. | Keep each circle large and deliberate, fully extending through the top and following through behind the hip at the bottom. | Maintain smooth, controlled motion throughout — avoid shrugging the shoulder or rotating the trunk to compensate. | Complete the desired number of reps per arm, then lower both arms and relax.
tRu: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and arms hanging relaxed at your sides. | Напрягите корпус легким напряжением, чтобы стабилизировать туловище и сохранять нейтральное положение позвоночника на протяжении всего движения. | Raise one arm forward and up, initiating the circle from the shoulder joint while keeping the elbow gently extended. | Продолжайте движение руки над головой, затем плавно опустите ее назад и вниз по полной круговой дуге, проходя близко к уху в верхней точке. | Когда первая рука завершает дугу вниз, начните поднимать противоположную руку вперёд для её собственного круга. | Чередуйте руки в непрерывном плавном ритме, чтобы одна рука всегда двигалась, пока другая завершает или начинает круг. | Keep each circle large and deliberate, fully extending through the top and following through behind the hip at the bottom. | Maintain smooth, controlled motion throughout — avoid shrugging the shoulder or rotating the trunk to compensate. | Выполните желаемое количество повторений на каждую руку, затем опустите обе руки и расслабьтесь.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides, and your core lightly braced. | Raise both arms out to your sides until they are parallel to the floor, palms facing down. | Begin sweeping both arms forward and upward in unison, tracing the largest circle you can manage while keeping the movement smooth. | Continue the arc overhead until your arms are fully extended above your head, reaching as high as possible without shrugging your shoulders toward your ears. | Carry the circle behind you and downward, allowing the arms to sweep back and out to the sides in a wide, controlled arc. | Complete the full circle back to the starting position — this finishes one forward repetition. | Perform all reps in the forward direction, then reverse the motion: start by sweeping your arms back and up, over the top, and then forward and down. | Keep each circle slow and deliberate — aim for roughly two seconds per half-circle — so you feel the stretch through the chest and shoulders at every point in the arc. | Maintain an upright posture throughout; avoid leaning forward or backward as the arms pass behind or in front of you.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place your hands on your hips for proprioceptive feedback. | Soften your knees slightly so they are not locked out. | Begin the movement by pushing your hips forward, then sweep them to the right in a wide arc. | Continue the arc by shifting your hips behind you, then sweep them to the left to complete the circle. | Keep your torso as upright as possible throughout — let the hips do the moving, not the shoulders. | Complete 8–10 full circles in the clockwise direction, moving at a slow, controlled pace. | Pause briefly in a neutral stance, then reverse direction and complete 8–10 circles counter-clockwise. | Breathe steadily throughout; avoid holding your breath as you move through the end ranges.

t: Stand upright behind a wall, chair back, or sturdy surface and place both hands on it at hip to waist height for balance. | Shift your weight onto one foot, keeping a soft bend in the standing knee so the joint is not locked out. | Bend the working knee to approximately 90° and keep it at that angle throughout the movement. | Brace your core and keep your torso tall — avoid leaning forward at the hips. | Drive the working leg straight back and upward by squeezing the glute of that leg, leading with the heel rather than the knee. | Lift until your thigh is roughly parallel to the floor or until you feel full glute contraction, whichever comes first — do not arch the lower back to gain extra range. | Pause briefly at the top and hold the contraction for one count. | Lower the leg in a controlled manner back to the start position without letting the foot touch the floor if you are performing consecutive reps. | Complete all reps on one side before switching to the opposite leg.

t: Stand upright next to a wall or sturdy support and place one hand on it at roughly hip height for balance. | Shift your weight onto one foot and let the other foot float just off the floor, keeping both hips level and your torso vertical. | Brace your core lightly to prevent your lower back from arching before the movement begins. | Keeping the working knee fully straight and the foot flexed, squeeze your glute and drive the leg back and slightly upward in a slow, controlled arc. | Continue extending until the working leg is roughly 20–30 degrees behind the body, or until you feel your lower back beginning to arch — whichever comes first. | Pause for one second at the top, maintaining glute contraction and keeping the hips square to the wall. | Lower the leg back to the starting position under control, taking about two seconds on the way down. | Complete all reps on one side before switching legs.

t: Stand tall with your feet together and find a stable surface nearby if you need balance support. | Step your right foot forward roughly two to three feet, forming a staggered stance. | Lower your left knee toward the floor in a controlled manner, allowing the left foot to remain on its toes behind you. | Keep your torso upright and your front knee stacked directly over your front ankle — do not let it drift forward past your toes. | Shift your hips gently forward and downward until you feel a stretch along the front of the left hip and thigh. | Squeeze the glute of the rear leg lightly to increase the stretch and encourage a posterior pelvic tilt. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the hip flexors to relax with each exhale. | Press through the front foot to return to standing, then repeat on the opposite side. | Complete 2–3 rounds per side.

t: Stand upright with your feet together and your arms relaxed at your sides. | Cross your right foot behind your left foot, placing the right foot flat on the floor slightly to the left of the left foot. | Straighten both legs and keep your torso tall throughout the movement. | Shift your hips to the right by pushing them out to the side — you should feel a stretch along the outer right hip and thigh. | For additional depth, extend your right arm overhead and reach it gently to the left, creating a lateral lean that lengthens the entire right side. | Hold the stretched position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the outer hip and IT band to release with each exhale. | Return to the upright starting position by stepping your right foot back to center. | Repeat on the opposite side — cross the left foot behind the right, shift hips to the left — completing 2–3 rounds per side.

t: Fold a small towel into a flat pad and place it against a smooth wall at approximately head height. | Stand facing the wall with your feet shoulder-width apart, roughly a forearm's length away from the surface. | Place the palm of your working hand flat on the towel, elbow bent to about 90°, and upper arm roughly parallel to the floor. | Press lightly into the wall so the towel stays in contact with the surface throughout the movement. | Brace your core and stand tall — keep your torso upright and avoid leaning into the wall with your shoulder or chest. | Slowly slide the towel downward by rotating your upper arm inward at the shoulder, letting your hand travel from above elbow height to below it while the elbow stays in place. | Continue the slide until you reach the end of your comfortable internal rotation range — do not force past a point of strain. | Reverse the motion in a controlled manner, sliding the towel back to the starting position without losing contact with the wall. | Complete all reps on one side before switching arms, maintaining a steady, deliberate tempo throughout.

nR: Скольжения на зубчатые у стены с полотенцем стоя
nH: החלקה לשריר המסור בקיר בעמידה עם מגבת
t: Stand facing a smooth wall, roughly one arm's length away, with feet hip-width apart and a slight bend in your knees. | Fold a towel so it lies flat and place it against the wall at chest-to-shoulder height, holding one end in each hand with a comfortable overhand grip. | Lean gently into the wall so your palms press the towel firmly against the surface; transfer just enough weight forward to keep the towel in place. | Brace your core and align your body so your ears, shoulders, and hips form a straight line — avoid arching the lower back. | Before moving, actively push the wall away by protracting your shoulder blades: think of rounding the upper back slightly and spreading the shoulder blades wide apart. | Maintaining that protracted position, exhale and slide both hands upward along the wall in a controlled arc until your arms approach full overhead extension. | At the top, pause for a moment and reinforce the protraction by pushing harder into the towel, feeling the muscles along the sides of your ribcage engage. | Inhale and slide your hands back down to the starting position in a controlled manner, keeping light pressure on the towel throughout. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining active scapular protraction on every rep.

t: Place the wheel roller on the floor in front of you. t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms extended straight out in front of you at shoulder height, palms facing down. | Interlace your fingers so both hands are clasped together. | Begin rotating your clasped hands to the right as if wringing water out of a towel, allowing your forearms to twist and your right arm to roll over the left. | Continue the rotation until you feel a stretch through your forearms, upper arms, and into your shoulders and neck. | Hold the end position for 2–3 seconds, keeping your elbows as straight as you comfortably can. | Slowly reverse the motion, returning your hands to the starting position with palms facing down. | Repeat the twist in the opposite direction, rolling your left arm over the right, and hold for 2–3 seconds. | Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining an upright posture throughout.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, spine tall, and core lightly braced. | Let both arms hang at your sides with your palms facing inward or slightly forward. | Retract your shoulder blades gently to create a stable base before you lift. | Raise both arms simultaneously at roughly 30–45° out from the midline — forming a Y shape — until they are fully extended overhead. | Hold the top position for 1–2 seconds with your ears between your upper arms and your neck long. | Lower both arms slowly back to the starting position under control. | Repeat for the prescribed number of reps, maintaining upright posture throughout.

t: Stand with your feet roughly two to three times hip-width apart, toes pointing forward or turned out slightly. | Place your hands on your hips and stand tall, lengthening through your spine before you begin the fold. | Inhale to create length, then exhale and hinge at the hips — not the waist — folding your torso forward while keeping your back as flat as possible. | Lower your hands toward the floor, resting them on your shins, the floor between your feet, or blocks if you cannot comfortably reach the ground. | Allow your head and neck to relax downward without straining to look forward. | Press evenly through the entire foot — especially the outer edges — to keep your knees from collapsing inward. | Hold the position for five to ten slow, steady breaths, deepening the fold slightly on each exhale if your range allows. | To exit, bend your knees slightly, place your hands on your hips, and use your core to slowly hinge back upright on an inhale.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your arms extended overhead and your legs extended outward, forming a wide X-shape — like a starfish. | Press your lower back gently into the mat to engage your core before the first rep. | Inhale to prepare, then exhale forcefully as you crunch upward: simultaneously lift your shoulders off the mat and raise your legs, drawing your arms and legs toward each other at the centre. | At the top of the crunch, your body should form a shallow V-shape, with arms and legs hovering above the mat. | Hold the contracted position for one count, feeling your abdominals fully engaged. | Inhale as you slowly lower your arms and legs back to the full starfish position, keeping the movement controlled rather than dropping. | Allow your core to remain lightly braced even in the extended position — do not fully relax between reps. | Complete all reps, then lower fully to the mat to rest.

t: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your arms extended overhead and your legs spread wide, forming a star shape with your body. | Engage your core by gently drawing your navel toward your spine before the first rep. | Exhale and crunch upward, simultaneously reaching your right hand toward your left foot — raise both your upper back and the opposite leg off the floor to meet in the middle. | Hold the top position for a brief moment, feeling the contraction in your abs and obliques. | Inhale and slowly lower your arm and leg back to the starting spread-eagle position. | Repeat on the opposite side, reaching your left hand toward your right foot. | Continue alternating sides for the desired number of reps, keeping the movement controlled throughout.

t: Stand with your feet together and your arms resting at your sides. | Bend your knees slightly to load your legs for the jump. | Explosively push through the balls of your feet and jump straight up. | As you leave the ground, simultaneously spread your legs out to roughly shoulder-width or wider and raise both arms out and upward until your body forms a star shape. | Keep your core braced and your gaze forward throughout the airborne phase. | Land softly with both feet landing at the same time, absorbing impact by bending your knees as you touch down. | Immediately bring your feet back together and lower your arms to your sides to return to the starting position. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or time interval, maintaining a steady rhythm.

t: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, then step one foot forward roughly 2–3 feet so you are in a split stance with your front foot flat and your back heel raised. | Engage your core and keep your torso upright, shoulders stacked over your hips throughout the entire set. | Inhale and slowly lower your back knee toward the floor by bending both knees simultaneously, aiming for a 90-degree angle at each joint. | Stop when your back knee hovers 1–2 inches above the floor without letting it touch down. | Ensure your front knee tracks over your second toe and does not cave inward or shoot past your toes. | Exhale and press through the heel of your front foot to drive both legs back to the starting split-stance position. | Complete all reps on one side before switching legs, or alternate legs each rep as preferred. | Maintain the same foot position for the entire set — do not shuffle or reposition between repetitions.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your core lightly braced. | Step one foot forward into a lunge, lowering your back knee toward the floor until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the ground. | Hold the lunge position for a moment, keeping your torso upright and your front knee tracking over your toes. | Push through your front foot to rise up, simultaneously driving your rear leg forward and upward in a controlled kick. | Extend the kicking leg as fully as you can without rounding your lower back or leaning excessively forward. | Lower the kicking leg back down and step it behind you to return to the starting lunge position, or bring it forward to the floor to complete the rep. | Complete all reps on one side before switching legs, or alternate sides with each rep.

nE: Static Position Lying Back with Pad
nR: Статическая позиция лёжа на спине с подушкой
nH: עמדה סטטית בשכיבה על הגב עם כרית
t: Place a foam roller, folded towel, or firm pad on the floor perpendicular to your body. | Sit on the floor in front of the pad with your knees bent and feet flat. | Carefully lean back so the pad sits beneath your mid-back, roughly level with your shoulder blades. | Lower your upper back and head toward the floor, letting your spine gently drape over the pad. | Extend your arms out to the sides or rest them on your abdomen, whichever feels more relaxed. | Breathe slowly and steadily, allowing gravity to gradually increase the extension of your thoracic spine with each exhale. | Hold the position for 30 to 60 seconds, or as long as comfortable without pain. | To exit, engage your core, roll to one side, and use your arms to press yourself back up to seated.

tHe: Place a foam roller, folded towel, or firm pad on the floor perpendicular to your body. | Sit on the floor in front of the pad with your knees bent and feet flat. | הטה את גבך בזהירות כך שהמזרן נמצא מתחת לאזור האמצעי של הגב, בקו ישר עם לחיי הכתף. | Lower your upper back and head toward the floor, letting your spine gently drape over the pad. | Extend your arms out to the sides or rest them on your abdomen, whichever feels more relaxed. | נשם לאט ובצורה יציבה, מאפשר לכובד להגביר בהדרגה את ההרחבה של חוליות החזה עם כל נשימת פליטה. | Hold the position for 30 to 60 seconds, or as long as comfortable without pain. | To exit, engage your core, roll to one side, and use your arms to press yourself back up to seated.

t: Lie face-down on a flat, comfortable surface with your legs extended straight behind you and the tops of your feet resting on the floor. | Place your palms flat on the floor beside your chest, fingers pointing forward, elbows bent and close to your sides. | Gently press through your palms and forearms to lift your chest slightly off the floor, keeping your hips and pelvis grounded. | Find a comfortable degree of extension — a low sphinx position or a slightly higher prop — where you feel a mild stretch across your abdomen and hip flexors without pain. | Relax your glutes and lower back rather than actively squeezing them, allowing gravity and your body weight to deepen the stretch naturally. | Breathe slowly and evenly, letting your torso sink a little further into the stretch with each exhale. | Hold the position for 20–60 seconds, then gently lower your chest back to the floor to release.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you, or cross them comfortably — whichever position feels stable and allows your pelvis to sit level. | Place your hands on your thighs or let them rest gently on the floor beside your hips for light support. | Inhale and lengthen your spine upward, imagining the crown of your head pressing toward the ceiling to create space between each vertebra. | Exhale and decide which variation to hold: for a decompression stretch, stay tall and maintain this elongated posture; for a release stretch, gently round your lower and mid back, letting your chin drop slightly toward your chest. | Hold the chosen position without forcing or bouncing — the stretch should feel like a sustained, comfortable tension in the back, not a sharp or pinching sensation. | Breathe slowly and steadily throughout the hold, using each exhale to relax deeper into the stretch without collapsing your posture entirely. | After the target hold time — typically 20–60 seconds — slowly return to a neutral seated position by re-stacking your spine vertebra by vertebra from the base upward. | Pause for a breath, then repeat for the desired number of sets.

nE: Static Position Seated Back with Pad
nR: Статическая позиция сидя со спинкой с подушкой
nH: עמדה סטטית בישיבה עם משענת וכרית
t: Place a firm pad vertically against the back of a sturdy chair or bench so it will sit between your shoulder blades and your lower back when you sit down. | Sit upright on the chair with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and lean gently back until the pad makes full contact with your mid-to-lower back. | Allow your pelvis to settle in a neutral position — neither tucked nor excessively arched — so your natural spinal curves are supported. | Rest your hands loosely on your thighs or fold them in your lap to keep the upper body relaxed. | Take a slow, deep breath in through your nose, letting your ribcage expand against the pad. | Exhale fully through your mouth, allowing your torso to soften and gently sink further into the pad with each breath. | Hold the position for 20–60 seconds, breathing steadily and releasing any residual tension with each exhale. | To finish, engage your core lightly and sit forward away from the pad before standing.

t: Stand on a firm, flat surface with your feet hip-width apart and your toes pointing forward or very slightly outward. | Distribute your weight evenly across both feet — press firmly through the heel, the ball of the foot beneath the big toe, and the ball beneath the little toe. | Straighten your legs without locking your knees; keep a very slight, soft bend so the joints are not hyperextended. | Engage your core by gently drawing your lower abdomen inward, and squeeze your glutes lightly to support a neutral pelvis. | Lengthen your spine upward — imagine the crown of your head being pulled toward the ceiling — and allow your lower back to hold its natural curve without exaggerating it. | Roll your shoulders back and down away from your ears, letting your arms hang relaxed at your sides with palms facing your thighs. | Level your gaze so your chin is parallel to the floor and your neck is in line with the rest of your spine. | Breathe slowly and steadily through your nose, allowing your ribcage to expand in all directions without letting your chest flare or your lower back arch. | Hold the position for the target duration — typically 30 seconds to 2 minutes — then relax and repeat as needed.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your core braced in an athletic position. | Raise both arms overhead and slightly behind your head, keeping your elbows soft and your shoulder blades drawn together and down. | Shift your weight slightly onto the balls of your feet to load your hips and torso for the movement. | Explosively drive both arms forward and downward in a wide arc, as if throwing a large object toward the floor in front of you. | Fully extend your elbows at the bottom of the drive and squeeze your lats hard at the point of maximum arm extension. | Allow your torso to hinge slightly forward with the motion, keeping your spine neutral and your core engaged throughout. | Control the return by reversing the arc — lifting your arms overhead in a smooth, deliberate path back to the starting position. | Reset your posture, recheck your shoulder-blade position, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

t: Adjust the seat height so your knee has a slight bend (about 5–10°) when the pedal is at its lowest point, then adjust the handlebar height to a comfortable reach. | Sit upright on the seat and place both feet securely in the pedal straps or on the pedal platforms. | Grip the handlebars lightly with both hands to maintain balance without hunching forward. | Begin pedaling at a moderate, controlled cadence to warm up the legs for the first 1–2 minutes. | Increase your pedaling speed or resistance to your target intensity and maintain a steady, rhythmic stroke throughout the session. | Keep your knees tracking in line with your feet throughout each pedal revolution — avoid letting them bow inward or outward. | Breathe steadily and continuously; avoid holding your breath during high-intensity intervals. | When the session or interval is complete, reduce your cadence gradually over 1–2 minutes to cool down before stopping.

tHe: כוון את גובה המושב כך שהברך תהיה בכיפוף קל (בערך 5–10°) כשהדוושה בנקודה הנמוכה ביותר, ואז כוון את גובה הכידון להושטה נוחה. | Sit upright on the seat and place both feet securely in the pedal straps or on the pedal platforms. | Grip the handlebars lightly with both hands to maintain balance without hunching forward. | התחל לדווש בקצב מתון ומבוקר כדי לחמם את הרגליים בדקה עד שתי דקות הראשונות. | Increase your pedaling speed or resistance to your target intensity and maintain a steady, rhythmic stroke throughout the session. | Keep your knees tracking in line with your feet throughout each pedal revolution — avoid letting them bow inward or outward. | נשם בצורה יציבה והעמק את המתיחה מעט עם כל נשימת פליטה מבלי לכפות את התנועה. | When the session or interval is complete, reduce your cadence gradually over 1–2 minutes to cool down before stopping.

t: Adjust the seat height so your knee has a slight bend (about 5–10 degrees) at the bottom of each pedal stroke — a fully locked-out knee risks joint strain. | Set the handlebar height to a comfortable position that lets you sit upright or with a slight forward lean without rounding your lower back. | Strap or clip your feet securely into the pedals so they stay flat throughout the stroke. | Select your target resistance level on the leverage machine — start light to warm up, then increase to a level where you can sustain a cadence of 70–100 RPM. | Begin pedaling at a controlled pace, pushing down through the heel-to-midfoot and pulling through the upstroke if the pedals allow clip-in. | Keep your core lightly braced, shoulders relaxed away from your ears, and hands resting lightly on the handlebars — avoid gripping hard or pulling with your arms. | Maintain your target cadence for the planned duration, adjusting resistance as needed to keep effort in your intended heart-rate zone. | When the session ends, reduce resistance gradually and pedal at an easy pace for 2–3 minutes to cool down before stopping.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms raised overhead with elbows slightly bent. | Engage your core and set your shoulders back and down away from your ears. | Simultaneously step one foot back into a staggered stance while pulling both arms down and in toward your sides, driving your elbows toward your hips. | At the bottom of the arm pull, your elbows should be tucked close to your torso and your back foot should be firmly planted on the ball of the foot. | Return the stepping foot back to the starting position while raising your arms overhead to the starting position. | Immediately repeat the motion stepping back with the opposite foot, alternating sides each repetition. | Maintain a steady, rhythmic pace that keeps your heart rate elevated throughout the set. | Continue for the prescribed number of repetitions or duration, keeping your breathing controlled and consistent.

t: Stand on a step, box, or raised surface with one foot near the edge and the other foot hanging free off the side, hip-width apart. Stand tall with your hands on your hips or extended forward for balance. | Shift your weight onto the standing leg and brace your core. Keep a soft bend in the standing knee rather than locking it out. | Begin to hinge slightly at the hip and bend the standing knee, lowering your body slowly and under control. | As you descend, allow the heel of the free foot to reach toward the floor without letting it bear weight. Keep your chest up and your torso only minimally forward-inclined. | Continue lowering until the free heel lightly touches or nearly touches the floor — typically when the standing knee is bent 60–90 degrees. Do not let the standing knee cave inward. | Pause briefly at the bottom, then drive through the heel of the standing foot to press back up to the starting position. | Complete all reps on one leg, then switch sides.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, toes pointing forward or slightly out. | Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up and weight in your heels. | Hold the squat position throughout the exercise — do not rise out of it between steps. | Keeping your right foot planted, lift your left foot and step it out laterally about 12–18 inches, then place it down under control. | Shift your weight slightly to re-center yourself in the squat, then bring your right foot in to return to the starting stance width. | Repeat the step-out on the opposite side: step your right foot out, then bring your left foot in. | Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions or distance, maintaining a consistent squat depth throughout. | To finish, stand up from the squat by driving through your heels and extending your hips and knees fully.

t: Stand beside a sturdy platform or step box at a height that allows you to step up comfortably with a controlled motion. | Step your near foot onto the platform, driving through the heel to push your body up until you are standing fully on the platform. | As you reach the top, swing the trailing leg forward and across your body so it crosses to the opposite side of the platform. | Lower the crossover foot down to the far side of the platform or to the floor, stepping off with control. | Follow through by stepping the original foot off the platform so you are now standing on the opposite side. | Immediately step back up with what is now the near foot, repeating the crossover motion to continue alternating sides. | Maintain a steady, rhythmic pace — land softly with a slight bend in the knee to absorb impact on each step-down. | Continue for the desired duration or number of repetitions, keeping your torso upright and your core lightly braced throughout.

t: Place a sturdy, non-sliding chair on a flat surface. Stand facing the chair about a half-step away with your feet hip-width apart. | Place your entire right foot flat on the seat of the chair, keeping your torso upright. | Drive through your right heel to press your body upward, straightening your right knee and hip as you rise. | Bring your left foot up to the chair so you are standing with both feet on the seat, maintaining a tall posture. | Step your left foot back down to the floor in a controlled manner, bending your right knee and hip as you lower. | Bring your right foot back down to the starting position so both feet are on the floor. | Complete all reps on one side before switching legs, or alternate legs with each rep.

nH: מתיחה במכרע עם פיתול עם מקל
t: Stand upright holding a stick or dowel vertically in front of you with both hands, its base resting on the floor for support. | Step your right foot forward into a lunge, lowering your left knee toward the floor so your right thigh is roughly parallel to the ground. | Keep your torso tall and your right knee tracking directly over your right foot, not caving inward. | Plant the stick to the outside of your right foot and use it to stabilize your position. | On an exhale, rotate your torso to the right, leading with your chest and reaching your right arm back while the stick provides a counterbalance. | Hold the rotated position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and deepening the stretch with each exhale. | Return your torso to center, step your right foot back to standing, and repeat on the opposite side.

t: Stand tall with feet together, then step your feet wide apart — roughly two to three times shoulder width — with toes pointing forward. | Place your hands on your hips and engage your core to keep your spine long and upright throughout the stretch. | Slowly slide your feet further apart along the floor, distributing your weight evenly between both legs as you descend. | Keep your kneecaps and toes pointing straight up toward the ceiling — do not allow the legs to rotate inward or outward. | Lower your hips toward the floor by hinging at the hip joints while maintaining a neutral, upright spine — avoid rounding the lower back. | Place your fingertips or palms on the floor in front of you for balance as you sink deeper into the straddle position. | Hold the deepest comfortable position for 30–60 seconds, breathing deeply and evenly; inhale to lengthen the spine and exhale to relax further into the stretch. | To release, press firmly through both feet and use your hands for support as you slowly walk your feet back together and return to standing.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, your spine neutral, and your chin level. | Let both arms hang at your sides, then extend them straight back behind your body, keeping your elbows fully locked. | Interlace your fingers or clasp your hands together behind your back at hip height, if your range of motion allows — otherwise hold a folded towel between your hands at shoulder width. | Rotate your palms downward so they face the floor and confirm your elbows are still straight. | Squeeze your shoulder blades toward each other and gently lift your arms away from your lower back, feeling the stretch spread across your chest. | Keep your chest lifted and your upper back from rounding — the movement should come from your shoulders, not your spine. | Breathe steadily and hold the stretched position for 20–30 seconds. | Release by lowering your arms slowly and relaxing your shoulder blades before repeating.

nE: Straight Hip Single Leg Curl on Stability Ball
nR: Сгибания бедра одной ногой на фитболе
nH: כפיפות ירך ברגל אחת על כדור פיזיו
t: Lie on your back on the floor with your arms extended to your sides, palms flat for support. | Place your right heel on top of the stability ball, with your right leg nearly straight. | Raise your left leg off the ground, keeping it in line with or slightly above your right leg. | Press your right heel into the ball and engage your core to lift your hips just enough to keep them level — do not bridge high, maintain a neutral hip position close to the floor. | Curl the ball toward your glutes by bending your right knee, pulling the ball with your heel in a controlled arc. | Stop when your right knee reaches roughly a 90-degree angle and you feel a strong contraction in the back of your thigh. | Slowly extend your right leg to roll the ball back to the starting position, maintaining hip level throughout. | Complete all reps on the right leg, then switch legs and repeat.
tRu: Lie on your back on the floor with your arms extended to your sides, palms flat for support. | Place your right heel on top of the stability ball, with your right leg nearly straight. | Raise your left leg off the ground, keeping it in line with or slightly above your right leg. | Press your right heel into the ball and engage your core to lift your hips just enough to keep them level — do not bridge high, maintain a neutral hip position close to the floor. | Подтяните мяч к ягодицам, сгибая правое колено, подтягивая мяч пяткой по контролируемой дуге. | Stop when your right knee reaches roughly a 90-degree angle and you feel a strong contraction in the back of your thigh. | Slowly extend your right leg to roll the ball back to the starting position, maintaining hip level throughout. | Выполните все повторения на правой ноге, затем поменяйте ноги и повторите.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your arms extended straight toward the ceiling, directly above your shoulders. | Raise both legs to 90°, keeping them fully straight so your feet point toward the ceiling and your body forms an L-shape. | Inhale to brace your core and press your entire lower back firmly into the mat — eliminate any arch between your spine and the floor. | Maintaining the lower-back contact, slowly lower your right arm overhead toward the floor while simultaneously lowering your left leg toward the floor. | Move both limbs at the same controlled pace, stopping just before your lower back lifts off the mat. | Exhale and reverse the movement, returning your arm and leg back to the starting position. | Repeat on the opposite side — lower your left arm and your right leg simultaneously — to complete one full rep. | Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions, never allowing the lower back to arch away from the mat.

t: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your legs extended straight and your arms resting at your sides, palms facing down. | Flex your feet so your toes point toward the ceiling, pressing your heels firmly into the floor. | Brace your core by drawing your navel gently toward your spine, and squeeze your glutes before you begin the movement. | Drive through both heels to lift your hips off the floor, raising them until your body forms a straight diagonal line from your shoulders to your feet. | At the top, hold for one to two seconds while maintaining strong glute contraction and keeping your core engaged. | Lower your hips slowly and under control back toward the floor, stopping just before they make contact. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining consistent heel pressure and glute activation throughout every rep.
tRu: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your legs extended straight and your arms resting at your sides, palms facing down. | Flex your feet so your toes point toward the ceiling, pressing your heels firmly into the floor. | Напрягите пресс, подтянув пупок к позвоночнику, и сожмите ягодицы перед началом движения. | Оттолкнитесь обеими пятками, чтобы оторвать бёдра от пола, поднимая их до тех пор, пока тело не образует прямую диагональную линию от плеч до стоп. | Вверху задержитесь на одну-две секунды, сохраняя сильное напряжение ягодиц и включённый корпус. | Lower your hips slowly and under control back toward the floor, stopping just before they make contact. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining consistent heel pressure and glute activation throughout every rep.
tHe: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your legs extended straight and your arms resting at your sides, palms facing down. | Flex your feet so your toes point toward the ceiling, pressing your heels firmly into the floor. | הדק את הליבה במשיכת הטבור בעדינות לכיוון עמוד השדרה, וכווץ את הישבן לפני תחילת התנועה. | Drive through both heels to lift your hips off the floor, raising them until your body forms a straight diagonal line from your shoulders to your feet. | בשיא החזק לשנייה-שתיים תוך שמירה על כיווץ ישבן חזק וליבה מופעלת. | Lower your hips slowly and under control back toward the floor, stopping just before they make contact. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining consistent heel pressure and glute activation throughout every rep.

t: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your legs straight and together, arms resting at your sides with palms facing down. | Flex your feet so your toes point toward the ceiling, creating tension through your legs and engaging your posterior chain. | Press your arms and upper back firmly into the floor to create a stable base. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes, then drive your hips upward off the floor by pressing through your heels. | Continue raising your hips until your body forms a straight diagonal line from your shoulders to your heels. | Hold the top position for one to two seconds, maintaining the squeeze in your glutes and keeping your legs fully extended. | Lower your hips in a controlled manner back toward the floor without fully relaxing, stopping just before they touch. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, maintaining control throughout each repetition.

t: Start on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips, forming a tabletop position with a neutral spine. | Brace your core gently to stabilize your lower back and keep your hips level — avoid letting them rotate or tilt. | Keep the working leg fully straight, then press it back and upward in a controlled arc, leading with the heel. | Continue lifting until your leg is roughly parallel to the floor or slightly above, squeezing your gluteus maximus firmly at the top of the movement. | Hold the contraction for one count at the top, ensuring your hips remain square to the floor and your lower back does not hyperextend. | Slowly lower the leg back toward the starting position under control, stopping just before the knee touches the floor. | Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other leg.
tRu: Start on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips, forming a tabletop position with a neutral spine. | Слегка напрягите пресс, стабилизируя поясницу и удерживая бёдра ровно — не давайте им разворачиваться или наклоняться. | Keep the working leg fully straight, then press it back and upward in a controlled arc, leading with the heel. | Продолжайте поднимать, пока ваша нога не станет примерно параллельна полу или чуть выше, сильно сжимая ягодицы в верхней точке движения. | Hold the contraction for one count at the top, ensuring your hips remain square to the floor and your lower back does not hyperextend. | Slowly lower the leg back toward the starting position under control, stopping just before the knee touches the floor. | Выполните все повторения на одну сторону, затем перейдите на другую ногу.
tHe: Start on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips, forming a tabletop position with a neutral spine. | הדק בעדינות את הליבה כדי לייצב את הגב התחתון ולשמור על אגן מאוזן — הימנע מסיבוב או הטיה שלו. | Keep the working leg fully straight, then press it back and upward in a controlled arc, leading with the heel. | Continue lifting until your leg is roughly parallel to the floor or slightly above, squeezing your gluteus maximus firmly at the top of the movement. | Hold the contraction for one count at the top, ensuring your hips remain square to the floor and your lower back does not hyperextend. | Slowly lower the leg back toward the starting position under control, stopping just before the knee touches the floor. | בצע את כל החזרות בצד אחד לפני המעבר לרגל השנייה.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs fully extended and feet together, toes pointing toward the ceiling. | Extend your arms overhead or cross them over your chest, depending on your preferred starting position. | Brace your core and press your lower back toward the mat before initiating the movement. | Exhale and curl your torso upward, leading with your chest rather than your chin, until your torso is roughly perpendicular to the floor. | Keep your legs flat on the mat throughout — do not let your heels rise. | Pause briefly at the top, feeling the contraction in your abs and hip flexors. | Inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the mat under control, resisting the urge to drop quickly. | Reset your brace and repeat for the desired number of reps.
tRu: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs fully extended and feet together, toes pointing toward the ceiling. | Extend your arms overhead or cross them over your chest, depending on your preferred starting position. | Напрягите корпус и направьте поясницу к коврику перед началом движения. | На выдохе скрутите корпус вверх, начиная движение грудью, а не подбородком, пока корпус не окажется примерно перпендикулярно полу. | Keep your legs flat on the mat throughout — do not let your heels rise. | Pause briefly at the top, feeling the contraction in your abs and hip flexors. | Inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the mat under control, resisting the urge to drop quickly. | Восстановите напряжение корпуса и повторите желаемое количество повторений.

t: Load the axle bar and set it on the floor; approach and position your mid-foot directly under the bar, feet hip-width apart. | Apply chalk generously to both hands, covering the fingers and palm — chalk is essential with a thick-axle handle. | Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to reach the bar; grip it with a double-overhand (pronated) grip, hands just outside your legs, fingers wrapped fully around the bar with no hook grip. | Flatten your back, lift your chest, and pull your shoulder blades down and back to create a rigid torso. | Take a deep breath into your belly, brace your core as hard as possible, and build tension through your lats by trying to 'bend the bar' around your shins. | Drive your feet through the floor to initiate the pull; keep the bar in contact with your shins as your hips and shoulders rise together. | As the bar passes your knees, drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to finish the lockout — stand fully upright with hips through and knees straight. | Hold the lockout position for a moment if required by the event, then hinge at the hips and lower the bar under control back to the floor. | Release your grip, reset your stance and bracing, and repeat for the required number of repetitions.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and the rope running straight ahead, with the sled or load positioned at the far end. | Lean your torso slightly back into a braced, upright position; grip the rope firmly with both hands as far up the rope as you can comfortably reach. | Pull the rope toward you with your first hand, driving your elbow back and down to your hip to complete the stroke. | As your first hand reaches your hip, immediately reach forward with your other hand and take a new grip as high up the rope as possible. | Continue in a smooth, alternating hand-over-hand rhythm — each reach as long as you can manage without losing grip pressure. | Keep your torso braced and upright throughout; avoid rounding your lower back or falling backward between strokes. | Continue pulling until the sled reaches you or the set distance is covered, then release the rope and rest.

t: Stand with your feet roughly hip-width apart, toes pointed out slightly, with the atlas stone resting on the ground between your legs. | Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to lower yourself until you can wrap both arms around the stone, getting your forearms underneath it as low as possible. | Pull the stone tight into your lap by driving your elbows under it — your torso should be nearly vertical at this point, with the stone resting against your thighs. | Take a deep breath, brace your core hard, and keep your chest tall and back as straight as possible throughout the lift. | Drive through your legs by extending your hips and knees to raise the stone up your body, using your thighs as a shelf to re-grip as needed. | Continue extending your hips and leaning slightly back to load the stone onto the top of your thighs at roughly hip height. | From the hip position, explosively extend your hips forward and shrug upward, driving the stone up your torso toward chest height. | As the stone reaches chest height, use your arms and chest to guide it up and over the lip of the platform or barrel, extending fully to deposit it on top. | Step back under control once the stone is secured on the platform, reset your stance, and repeat for the required number of lifts.

t: Place two barbells parallel to each other on the floor, spaced roughly hip-width apart, and load each with equal weight. | Stand between the barbells with your feet hip-width apart, hinge at the hips, and grip each bar with a firm overhand grip just outside your legs. | Brace your core, retract your shoulder blades, and take a deep breath into your abdomen before initiating the lift. | Drive through your heels to stand tall, extending your hips and knees simultaneously as if performing a deadlift, until you are fully upright with the barbells hanging at your sides. | Hold the barbells with straight arms and tightly packed shoulders — avoid shrugging or letting the shoulders roll forward. | Begin walking with controlled, deliberate steps, maintaining an upright torso and keeping your gaze forward throughout. | Keep your core braced and your breathing rhythmic for the entire distance; avoid leaning to either side or letting the bars sway. | At the end of the distance, hinge at the hips and lower both barbells to the floor under control, following the same mechanics used to pick them up.

t: Position yourself at one end of the vehicle with your feet roughly hip-width apart and your toes pointing slightly outward. | Squat down and slide your hands under the bumper or chassis edge, gripping as wide and securely as possible with both palms facing up. | Brace your core tightly, keep your chest up, and set a neutral spine before you begin to lift. | Drive through your legs explosively, extending your hips and knees together to break the vehicle off the ground. | As the vehicle rises past knee height, shift your hips forward and begin pushing with your upper body, transitioning from a pulling to a pressing motion. | Continue driving with your chest and upper arms, pushing the vehicle upright until it tips past its balance point. | Step back quickly and under control as the vehicle falls forward and lands on its far end. | Reset your stance, walk around to the new end, and repeat for the desired number of flips.
