t: Load the implement to the target weight and confirm the pivot post is secure before starting. | Stand beside the horizontal arm and grip it firmly with both hands, keeping it roughly at hip height. | Brace your core, set your chest tall, and take a short breath before lifting the arm off any support. | Begin walking forward in a controlled circle around the central post, keeping your steps short and deliberate. | Maintain an upright torso throughout — avoid leaning backward or letting your hips drop excessively. | Keep your grip tight and elbows slightly bent to reduce stress on the wrists and forearms. | Drive through your thighs and glutes with each step, especially as fatigue accumulates. | Continue for the prescribed number of laps or distance, then lower the implement safely to its rest position.

nE: StrongMan Dumbbell One Arm Clean and Jerk
nR: Стронгмен: взятие с толчком одной рукой с гантелью

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the dumbbell on the floor just outside your right foot. Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to reach down and grip the dumbbell with a neutral grip, keeping your back flat and chest up. | Brace your core and set your lats. Your hips should be below your shoulders and your shoulder should be directly over or slightly in front of the dumbbell. | Initiate the clean by driving through your heels to extend your hips and knees explosively, pulling the dumbbell up close to your body. As the dumbbell reaches hip height, shrug your shoulder hard. | Continue pulling by driving your elbow high and fast. As the dumbbell reaches chest level, rotate your elbow under the dumbbell and drop into a quarter-squat to catch it at shoulder height in the rack position — dumbbell resting on your shoulder with your elbow pointing forward. | Stand tall from the quarter-squat to reach the fully upright rack position. Pause briefly to establish balance and a firm base. | Dip straight down by bending your knees 4–6 inches, keeping your torso vertical. Drive forcefully back up through your legs to load the dumbbell upward. | As the dumbbell leaves your shoulder, punch your arm overhead while splitting your feet front-to-back or pushing straight up into a slight squat. Lock your elbow out fully at the top. | Recover your feet to parallel and stand tall with the dumbbell pressed firmly overhead, arm fully extended and shoulder packed. | Lower the dumbbell under control back to the shoulder, then to the floor to complete one rep. Complete all reps on one side before switching arms.

t: Sit on the board facing your opponent with your feet firmly planted against the footboards, knees bent and positioned outside your arms. | Grip the wooden stick with both hands using a full overhand grip, hands approximately shoulder-width apart, placed between your opponent's grip points. | Brace your core, set your back into a rigid, slightly forward-leaning position, and press your feet hard into the footboards before the pull begins. | At the start signal, drive through your legs into the footboards and pull the stick toward your hips, engaging your back, arms, and entire posterior chain simultaneously. | Keep your elbows close to your torso and use your bodyweight as leverage by leaning back into the pull while maintaining a flat, braced spine. | If your opponent surges, resist by reinforcing your grip, pushing harder through your feet, and maintaining your position on the board without lifting your hips. | Continue pulling and countering your opponent's force until you extract the stick from their hands or pull them off the board, then release in a controlled manner. | When training solo, sit on the floor with your feet braced against a wall or anchor point, grip a resistance band or rope at the same height, and practice both explosive burst pulls and sustained isometric holds. | Rest fully between sets to allow grip and full-body recovery before repeating.

t: Lie face-down on the floor with your arms extended fully overhead, legs straight, and toes pointing away from you. | Engage your core and glutes, then simultaneously lift your chest, arms, and legs off the floor into the Superman position. | Hold the Superman position briefly to stabilize your spine and confirm your glutes and lower back are fully contracted. | Bend both elbows and pull them back toward your hips in a rowing motion, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top. | Pause for one count at the peak of the row, feeling the contraction across your upper and mid back. | Reverse the motion by extending your arms back overhead while keeping your chest and legs lifted off the floor. | Lower your chest, arms, and legs back to the floor in a controlled manner to complete one repetition.

t: Lie face down on the floor with your body fully extended and a folded towel looped under a door or around a sturdy fixed object at floor level directly in front of you. | Grip one end of the towel in each hand with your arms extended overhead, palms facing each other, and take up the slack so there is light tension on the towel. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to prepare for the lift. | Exhale and simultaneously raise your chest, arms, and legs off the floor — entering the superman position — keeping your neck neutral and your gaze toward the floor rather than straight ahead. | From that suspended position, pull the towel toward your chest by driving your elbows back and down, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of the row. | Hold the top position for one count, feeling the contraction through your upper back, rear shoulders, and posterior chain. | Slowly extend your arms back out in front of you, then lower your chest and legs to the floor in a controlled manner. | Reset your body position fully before beginning the next rep, and repeat for the target number of reps.

t: Lie face-down on a mat with your legs straight and your forehead resting lightly on the floor. | Bring your arms into a W position: bend your elbows to roughly 90 degrees, pull them back toward your torso, and point your hands toward the ceiling with palms facing down. | Engage your core and squeeze your glutes before initiating the movement. | Exhale and simultaneously lift your chest, arms, and legs off the floor, keeping your neck neutral and gaze directed toward the floor. | At the top, hold the W arm shape — elbows wide and pulled toward your hips, hands near ear level — and avoid letting your arms drift forward into a Y position. | Hold the raised position for 1–2 seconds, focusing on squeezing the rear deltoids and mid-back muscles. | Inhale and slowly lower your chest, arms, and legs back to the starting position with control. | Repeat for the prescribed number of reps, maintaining consistent form throughout each repetition.

t: Lie face down on the floor with your legs straight, toes pointed, and arms extended overhead in a Y shape as your starting position. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and simultaneously lift your chest, arms, and legs off the floor into the Superman hold — your body should form a gentle arc. | While holding the lift, bend your elbows and pull your arms back and down until they form a W shape — upper arms roughly in line with your shoulders, elbows bent about 90°, and hands near ear height. | Pause briefly in the W position, actively squeezing your shoulder blades together and keeping your chest and legs elevated. | Slowly extend your arms back overhead into the full Y position, keeping them off the floor throughout the movement. | Pause again in the Y position, maintaining the Superman lift with your chest and legs still raised. | Lower your chest, arms, and legs back to the floor with control to complete one repetition. | Reset your breath and repeat for the desired number of reps.

t: Position a bar in a rack or on a Smith machine at roughly hip height — lower means harder; higher means easier. | Sit on the floor under the bar, grip it with both hands shoulder-width apart, palms facing toward you (supinated grip), and arms fully extended. | Extend your legs out in front of you so only your heels touch the floor, and lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from heels to shoulders. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips level and your body rigid throughout the movement. | Initiate the pull by driving your elbows toward your hips and squeezing your shoulder blades together. | Pull your chest up to the bar in a controlled manner, keeping your body in a straight plank — avoid letting your hips drop or your lower back arch. | Hold the top position briefly when your chest reaches the bar and your elbows are fully bent. | Lower yourself back to the starting position with control until your arms are fully extended, then repeat for the desired number of reps.

t: Grip the pull-up bar with your palms facing toward you (supinated) and your hands shoulder-width apart or slightly closer. | Hang at full arm extension with your feet off the floor, allowing your shoulders to decompress fully into a dead hang. | Brace your core, engage your glutes, and cross your feet or bend your knees to stabilise your lower body. | Depress and retract your shoulder blades — pull them down and together — before initiating the pull. | Drive your elbows down and back toward your hips to pull your chin above the bar, leading with your chest. | Hold briefly at the top with your chin clear of the bar and your shoulder blades fully contracted. | Lower yourself under control back to a full dead hang before beginning the next repetition.

nR: Растяжка в висе на перекладине супинацией
t: Stand beneath a pull-up bar or similar overhead bar so it is within easy reach overhead. | Reach up and grip the bar with both hands using an underhand (supinated) grip — palms facing toward you, hands roughly shoulder-width apart. | Bend your knees or lift your feet so your bodyweight hangs from the bar with your arms fully extended. | Let your bodyweight settle while keeping your shoulders packed down away from your ears and your elbows straight. | Relax into the hang and allow gravity to deepen the stretch through your biceps and forearms — keep the elbows extended and do not force the position. | Breathe slowly and steadily, easing a little deeper into the stretch with each exhale. | Hold the stretched position for 20–40 seconds, or as long as you can maintain a controlled, relaxed hang. | To finish, place your feet back on the floor to unload your arms before releasing the bar.

t: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and your arms resting at your sides. | Draw your right knee into your chest, wrapping both hands around your shin briefly to create a light compression through the hip. | Extend your right arm out to the side at shoulder height, palm facing up, to anchor that shoulder to the floor. | Use your left hand to gently guide your right knee across your body toward the floor on the left side, stacking the right knee roughly at hip height. | Turn your head to the right, away from the direction your knees are pointing, to extend the rotational stretch through the cervical spine. | Press your right knee gently downward with your left hand if it does not reach the floor, without allowing your right shoulder to lift. | Hold the position for 20–60 seconds, breathing slowly and letting your torso release further into the twist with each exhale. | Return your knee to center and lower your leg back to the floor, then repeat on the opposite side.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your arms extended out to your sides at shoulder height, palms facing down. | Bend your knees to roughly 90 degrees and lift your feet off the floor so your thighs are vertical and your shins are parallel to the ground. | Brace your core lightly and keep your shoulders pressed flat against the mat throughout the movement. | Slowly lower both knees together to the right, letting them travel toward the floor while keeping your left shoulder from lifting. | Lower only as far as your range of motion allows without discomfort, pausing briefly at the end of the range. | Reverse the movement and sweep both knees back through center and over to the left side in a controlled arc. | Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions, moving at a slow, steady tempo.

t: Kneel on the floor and interlace your fingers, placing your forearms flat on the mat shoulder-width apart to form a stable triangular base. | Set the crown of your head — not your forehead or the back of your skull — on the mat inside your cupped hands, so your hands cradle the back of your head. | Tuck your toes, lift your knees, and walk your feet in toward your elbows until your hips stack above your shoulders as much as possible. | Engage your shoulder blades by pressing your forearms firmly into the mat and lifting your shoulders away from your ears; this protects the neck throughout the pose. | If you are a beginner, position yourself facing a wall about one foot away so the wall can catch your feet if you go too far. | Draw your core in and up, then slowly lift one foot off the floor, bending the knee and bringing it toward your chest. | When you feel balanced, lift the second foot and bring both knees to your chest before gradually straightening the legs toward the ceiling. | Hold the inverted position for 5–30 seconds while breathing steadily, keeping your core firm and your shoulder blades active. | To come down, bend your knees back to your chest, lower your feet to the floor one at a time, and rest in Child's Pose for several breaths.

t: Set the suspension straps to a height where your body will be at roughly a 30–45 degree angle to the floor when you hang beneath them — lower positions increase difficulty. | Stand beneath the anchor point, take a wide overhand grip on the handles with your hands noticeably wider than shoulder width, and walk your feet forward until your arms are fully extended and your body forms a straight line from heels to head. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your body rigid so your hips do not sag or pike throughout the movement. | Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blades and driving your elbows out to the sides and back, not toward your hips. | Pull your chest toward the handles until your hands are at or near your ribcage and your elbows clear the line of your torso. | Pause briefly at the top, squeezing your upper back and rear shoulders at full contraction. | Lower yourself with control back to the fully extended starting position, allowing your shoulder blades to protract without losing body tension. | Repeat for the target number of repetitions, maintaining a rigid plank position on every rep.

t: Set the suspension straps so the foot cradles hang roughly 6–12 inches off the floor, which puts your body close to parallel when you are in a plank. | Kneel facing away from the anchor point and place the tops of both feet into the foot cradles. | Lower onto your forearms with your elbows directly under your shoulders, hands flat or clasped, and press up into a forearm plank so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core firmly, squeeze your glutes, and make sure your hips are level — neither sagging toward the floor nor piking toward the ceiling. | Keeping your elbows planted and your body rigid, push through your forearms to drive your whole body backward toward your feet, so your shoulders travel behind your elbows and your arms end reaching out ahead of your head. | Pause for a brief moment at the end of the saw, where the lever is longest and the tension on your core and anterior deltoids peaks. | Pull your body forward over your elbows until your shoulders are stacked above them again and you are back in the starting plank position. | Continue sawing back and forward in a slow, controlled rhythm for the desired number of reps or time, maintaining a rigid body throughout. | Finish by returning to the plank, lowering your knees to the floor, and stepping your feet out of the cradles one at a time.

t: Set the suspension straps to approximately waist height and stand facing the anchor point. | Hold both handles with a light, relaxed grip — arms nearly extended — to provide balance only, not to pull yourself upward. | Stand with your feet hip-width apart, toes pointing straight ahead. If a raised surface or step edge is available, position the balls of your feet on it so your heels can lower below foot level for a greater stretch. | Brace your core, stand tall, and keep your knees straight but not locked throughout the movement. | Press through the balls of your feet to rise onto your toes, lifting your heels as high as possible. | Pause at the top for a full second, squeezing the calves, before beginning the descent. | Lower your heels slowly — 2 to 3 seconds — until you feel a complete stretch in the calf, dropping below the step level if your setup allows. | Complete your reps with a controlled tempo, letting the straps stabilize you rather than carry any of the load.

t: Set the suspension trainer handles at approximately hip height, with both handles even and parallel to the floor. | Grip one handle in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing inward), then jump or step up so your arms are fully extended and your body is supported above the handles. | Lean your torso slightly forward — roughly 20–30 degrees from vertical — to shift emphasis onto the chest rather than the triceps. | Keep your core braced, your legs together or slightly crossed behind you, and your shoulders pulled down away from your ears. | Inhale and bend your elbows to lower your body in a controlled manner, allowing your elbows to flare naturally outward at roughly a 45–60 degree angle from your torso. | Descend until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, or until you feel a deep stretch across your chest without shoulder discomfort. | Exhale and press through the handles to drive your body back up to the starting position, squeezing your chest at the top. | Complete your reps, then step or hop off the handles to dismount safely.

t: Anchor the suspension straps at a height that places the handles roughly at chest level when you hold them at arm's length while standing. | Face away from the anchor point and grasp one handle in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other or slightly inward. | Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight diagonal line from head to heels, with your weight leaning forward into the straps — the more horizontal your body, the harder the exercise. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your body rigid as a plank throughout the set. | Inhale, then bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the handles in a controlled arc, allowing your elbows to flare out to roughly 45 degrees from your torso. | Lower yourself until your hands are at approximately chest height and your chest is between the handles, pausing briefly at the bottom. | Exhale and press through the palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position, actively squeezing your chest as you reach full extension. | Maintain strap tension and body alignment throughout — do not let your hips sag or your lower back arch. | Complete the desired repetitions, then step forward to release tension from the straps before letting go of the handles.

t: Set the suspension trainer handles to chest height and face away from the anchor point. | Grip one handle in each hand with your palms facing down and step forward so the straps are taut and your body is angled forward from your feet. | Extend your arms in front of your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down throughout the movement. | Lower your chest toward the handles by bending your elbows and allowing them to flare out to roughly 45–75° from your torso. | Continue lowering until your chest reaches the level of your hands, without letting your hips sag or your lower back arch. | Press back out through your palms, extending your arms until you return to the starting position. | Complete your reps, then step back to release tension from the straps.

tHe: כוון את ידיות רצועות האימון לגובה החזה ועמוד עם הגב לנקודת העיגון. | Grip one handle in each hand with your palms facing down and step forward so the straps are taut and your body is angled forward from your feet. | Extend your arms in front of your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. | תכווץ את שרירי הליבה, כווץ את השרירים הגלוטיאליים, ושמור על להבות כתף מושכות לאחור ולמטה לאורך כל התנועה. | Lower your chest toward the handles by bending your elbows and allowing them to flare out to roughly 45–75° from your torso. | Continue lowering until your chest reaches the level of your hands, without letting your hips sag or your lower back arch. | לחץ חזרה דרך כפות הידיים, תוך יישור הידיים עד שתחזור לעמדת המוצא. | Complete your reps, then step back to release tension from the straps.

t: Set the suspension straps to a height where you can hang at full arm extension with your feet off the ground, or slightly bent at the knees if the anchor is low. | Grip the handles with a supinated (palms facing you) grip, hands roughly shoulder-width apart. | Hang with arms fully extended and shoulders slightly retracted — avoid letting your shoulders shrug up toward your ears. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your body in a straight or slightly hollow position throughout the movement. | Initiate the pull by driving your elbows down and back toward your hips, not by curling your wrists or swinging your torso. | Continue pulling until your chin clears the level of your hands and your elbows are fully bent. | Pause briefly at the top, maintaining tension in your lats and biceps. | Lower yourself under control back to full arm extension over 2–3 seconds. | Reset your shoulder position at the bottom before beginning the next repetition.

t: Set the suspension trainer straps to mid-length. The more horizontal your body — feet farther from the anchor — the greater the resistance. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and lock in a neutral spine. Let your elbows travel slightly back and close to your sides at roughly a 45° angle to your torso — not flared wide. | Continue lowering until your chest is level with your hands and you feel a full stretch across the chest, while keeping the straps taut and your body in a straight line. | Drive through your palms and press yourself back up until your arms are fully extended, squeezing your chest at the top of the rep. | Walk your feet back toward the anchor to bring yourself upright and release tension, then step out of the straps to finish the set.

t: Set the suspension trainer so the foot cradles hang about 12–18 inches off the floor. | Kneel in front of the anchor point, place one foot at a time into the cradles, and extend into a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and establish a straight line from your heels to the top of your head before starting any movement. | Exhale and draw your knees toward your chest by rounding your lower back and contracting your abs, allowing your hips to rise as your knees come in. | Pause briefly at the top when your knees are near your elbows and your abs are fully contracted. | Inhale and slowly extend your legs back to the starting plank position, resisting the pull of gravity throughout the return. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, keeping your hips level and your core engaged on every rep.

t: Adjust the suspension straps to roughly chest height and stand facing the anchor point, holding one handle in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other. | Walk your feet toward the anchor until your body is at an angle — the more you lean back, the harder the movement; aim for about 45° to start. | Extend your arms fully in front of you, keep your body in a straight line from heels to head, and brace your core so your hips don't sag. | Initiate the pull by squeezing your rear deltoids and retracting your shoulder blades slightly. | Drive your elbows up and out to the sides, keeping them above shoulder height, and pull the handles toward your face until your hands are level with your ears. | At the top, externally rotate your shoulders so your knuckles point toward the ceiling and your upper arms are parallel to the floor. | Pause for one count at the top with your rear delts fully contracted. | Lower under control by reversing the path — elbows leading outward and down — until your arms are fully extended again. | Complete all reps, then walk your feet back away from the anchor until you are standing upright and unloaded before releasing the handles.

t: Anchor the suspension straps at a high, overhead point and face away from the anchor point. | Grip one handle in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and step forward so you are leaning into the straps at roughly a 30–45° angle to the floor. | Extend your arms out in front of you at chest height, elbows very slightly bent — this is your starting position. | Inhale and slowly open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc, keeping the slight elbow bend consistent throughout. | Lower until your arms are in line with your shoulders and you feel a strong stretch across your chest — do not allow your hips to drop or your lower back to arch. | Exhale and squeeze your chest to bring your hands back together in front of you, reversing the arc. | Return to the starting position with hands touching or nearly touching and your body in a straight plank-like line. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining tension on the straps throughout each rep.

t: Set the suspension straps to a mid-length so the handles hang at roughly chest height when you stand in front of the anchor point. | Grip one handle in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other, and step forward so your body is at an angle to the floor with arms extended out to the sides. | Brace your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels — do not allow your hips to sag or pike. | With a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms out to the sides in a controlled arc until you feel a stretch across your chest. t: Set the pulley to a low-to-mid height — roughly hip to chest level — and attach a single handle or loop grip. | Stand facing the cable machine and grip the handle with one or both hands in full supination: palm or palms turned up toward the ceiling. | Step back from the machine and shift your weight away from it so the cable pulls taut and begins to support a portion of your bodyweight. | Allow your arm or arms to extend forward and slightly downward, keeping your elbow soft but close to straight so the cable tension is directed through the biceps and forearm. | Lean your torso back gradually, loading more of your bodyweight into the cable until you feel a clear stretch running through the front of the upper arm and outer forearm. | Hold the supinated grip firmly and let gravity and the cable tension deepen the stretch — do not force additional rotation at the elbow. | Breathe slowly and steadily, relaxing the target muscles further with each exhale. | Hold the stretched position for 20–40 seconds, or as long as you can maintain controlled supination and stable footing. | Shift your weight back toward the machine to unload the cable, then return to an upright position before releasing the handle.

t: Set the suspension straps to mid-length and hold one handle in each hand, standing facing away from the anchor point. | Step your feet back so your body is at a slight forward lean, arms extended in front of you at chest height with a firm grip. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and align your body in a straight line from head to heels. | Inhale, then slowly reach both arms forward and diagonally to one side — rolling out at roughly a 30-to-45-degree angle from your centerline — until your arms are nearly overhead. | Keep your hips level and resist any rotation in your torso; the obliques on the opposite side should feel the stretch and load. | Pause briefly at the end range without letting your lower back arch or your hips drop. | Exhale and pull your arms back down toward your hips along the same diagonal path, using your obliques and lats to drive the return. | Complete all reps to one side, then reset and repeat to the opposite diagonal.

t: Set the suspension straps to mid-calf height and face away from the anchor point. | Kneel and slip both feet into the foot cradles, then lower your hands to the floor directly under your shoulders. | Extend your legs behind you so your body forms a straight line from head to heels — this is your suspended plank starting position. | Brace your core, press your legs firmly together, and keep your arms fully extended with your shoulder blades drawn down. | Exhale and drive your hips straight up toward the ceiling, pulling your feet toward your hands to form an inverted V shape. | Pause briefly at the top with your hips as high as comfortable, keeping your legs as straight as possible and your arms locked out. | Inhale and slowly lower your hips back down under control until your body returns to the straight plank position. | Repeat for the target number of reps, maintaining a neutral spine between reps and not allowing your hips to sag.

t: Stand facing the suspension strap anchor and grasp one handle with one hand, keeping your arm extended and your feet hip-width apart. | Lean back until your body is at an angle that challenges you — the more parallel to the floor, the harder the movement. Keep your free arm extended toward the anchor to start. | Brace your core and maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout the entire movement. | Keep the working arm long and rotate your torso open, away from the anchor, reaching your free hand down and back toward the floor. | Let your hips and upper back turn with the reach so your chest faces out to the side, keeping the working shoulder blade set and the strap under tension. | Reverse the rotation by driving your working elbow back and turning your torso square to the anchor, sweeping your free hand back up toward the anchor point. | Pull until your working hand reaches the side of your chest and your body is back in a straight line, with your shoulder blade retracted and depressed. | Pause briefly with your core tight, then rotate open again under control to start the next rep. | Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other hand.

t: Set the suspension straps to mid-length and anchor them at a sturdy fixed point behind you at roughly hip height. | Stand facing away from the anchor, reach back between your legs, and grasp one handle in each hand with a neutral grip. | Step forward until the straps are taut and you feel tension pulling your arms back. Your feet should be about shoulder-width apart. | Brace your core, keep a neutral spine, and begin the movement by pushing your hips back and hinging forward at the waist — not by rounding your lower back. | Continue hinging until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor and the handles have traveled between your legs toward the anchor. Keep your knees soft and your back flat throughout. | From the bottom position, drive your hips forward explosively, squeezing your glutes hard as you reach full hip extension. | Let the drive of your hips bring your torso back to an upright standing position, allowing the handles to travel forward between your legs until they finish in front of your hips with your arms straight. | Control the return: resist the strap tension as you hinge back down for the next rep rather than letting it yank you forward. | Complete your set, then step back toward the anchor to release tension before letting go of the handles.

t: Set the suspension straps to a height that allows you to hang at full arm extension with your feet clear of the floor. | Grip the handles with your palms facing each other or slightly supinated, and let your body hang freely with your arms fully extended. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and hold your body in a straight line from head to heels. | Begin each rep by depressing and retracting your shoulder blades — pull your shoulders away from your ears and draw them back toward your spine before bending your elbows. | Drive your elbows down and back, pulling your chest toward the handles until your chin clears the level of your hands. | Pause briefly at the top and feel the contraction across your lats and upper back. | Lower yourself under control to full arm extension, maintaining body tension throughout, then repeat.

t: Set the suspension straps so the handles hang at a height you can reach while standing — roughly arms-length overhead when you stand beneath them. | Grip the handles with a neutral or semi-supinated grip, palms facing each other or partially toward you. | Hang at full arm extension, shoulders relaxed up toward your ears, feet off the floor or lightly touching for assistance if needed. | Depress and retract your shoulder blades — pull them down and back — before initiating the pull. | Drive your elbows down and back, pulling your chest toward the handles while keeping your core braced and your body in a straight line. | Continue pulling until your chin clears the handles and your chest approaches them, pausing briefly at the top. | Lower yourself under control back to a full hang, allowing your shoulder blades to protract at the bottom. | Complete the desired number of reps, then carefully step down or lower your feet to the floor.

t: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to a height of roughly 12–18 inches off the floor — lower handles increase difficulty. | Kneel in front of the handles and grip one in each hand with a neutral or slightly pronated grip, keeping your thumbs wrapped around the handles. | Walk your feet back and extend into a high plank position, with your body forming a straight line from your head to your heels and your arms fully extended beneath your shoulders. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and pull your shoulder blades down and together to stabilize the handles before beginning the movement. | Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the space between the handles, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45–75° angle to your torso. | Continue lowering until your chest reaches handle height, or until you feel a controlled stretch in your chest — maintain a rigid body position throughout. | Press through your palms and drive your chest away from the handles until your arms are fully extended again. | Complete your reps, then walk your feet forward and return to the kneeling position before releasing the handles.

t: Anchor the suspension trainer overhead, at or above head height, and hold one handle in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing down. | Walk your feet forward until the straps are taut and your body is angled back — begin with a moderate lean of around 45 degrees and make the exercise harder by walking your feet closer to directly below the anchor. | Extend your arms fully in front of you so the straps take your weight; your body should form a straight line from head to heels with your core engaged. | Retract your shoulder blades and begin the pull by driving your elbows out to the sides and slightly back, leading with the elbows rather than the hands. | Pull yourself up until your hands are level with your ears and your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your elbows flared wide rather than tucking them toward your torso. | Pause briefly at the top with your shoulder blades fully retracted and depressed, feeling the posterior deltoids and upper-back muscles contract. | Slowly lower yourself back to the start under control, allowing your arms to extend fully before beginning the next repetition. | Complete all reps, then step your feet back to release tension from the straps.

t: Stand facing the anchor point and hold one suspension handle in each hand with your palms facing each other, arms extended in front of you at roughly chest height. | Shift your weight onto your left foot and step your right foot back, placing the ball of your right foot on the floor about two to three feet behind you. | Keep your chest tall and your core braced as you bend both knees, lowering your right knee toward the floor in a controlled descent. | Lower until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor and your rear knee hovers just above the ground, or as deep as your mobility allows. | Drive through your left heel to stand back up, fully extending the hip and knee of your front leg. | Return your right foot to the starting position beside your left foot to complete one rep. | Complete all reps on one side before switching, or alternate legs each rep depending on your training goal.

t: Set the suspension handles to approximately chest height and stand facing the anchor point. | Grip one handle in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and walk your feet forward until your body leans back at roughly a 45° angle — the more horizontal your body, the harder the exercise. | Extend your arms straight in front of you toward the anchor, keeping a slight bend in the elbows and your core braced. | Squeeze your shoulder blades together and open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc, driving your elbows back and out until your hands are roughly level with your shoulders. | Hold the end position for a beat, feeling the contraction in your rear deltoids and upper back. | Lower your arms back to the start position slowly and under control, resisting the pull of the straps. | Complete all reps, then walk your feet back until you are standing upright and the straps are slack before letting go of the handles.

t: Set the suspension trainer handles to roughly waist height and face the anchor point, holding one handle in each hand with palms facing each other. | Walk your feet forward toward the anchor point until your torso is angled back at roughly 45° from vertical, with your arms fully extended in front of you. | Plant your heels firmly into the floor and sit your hips back and down, letting the straps support you so your hips are clearly flexed and your chest stays lifted with a neutral spine. tHe: Set the suspension trainer handles to approximately hip height and stand facing the anchor point, a handle in each hand. | Shift your weight onto your right foot and lift your left foot off the floor. | Cross your left ankle over your right knee to form a figure-4 shape, keeping your left shin roughly parallel to the floor and your hips level. | הדק את הליבה, שמור על חזה גבוה ואחוז בידיות באחיזה קלה — מספיק רק לשמירת שיווי משקל. | Hinge slightly at the hip, then bend your right knee and lower your hips toward the floor in a controlled descent, aiming for 90° of knee flexion or deeper if your mobility allows. | Keep your right knee tracking over your right toes throughout the squat and avoid letting it collapse inward. | Drive through your right heel to stand back up, squeezing your glute at the top to fully extend the hip. | בצע את כל החזרות ברגל ימין, ואז החלף צדדים וחזור על התרגיל.

t: Set the suspension trainer so the foot cradles hang low enough that you can lie on the floor with your legs nearly straight and your feet secured inside the cradles. | Lie on your back with your feet looped into the cradles, ankles comfortably braced, and your legs roughly hip-width apart with a slight bend at the knees. | Extend your arms along your sides or cross them over your chest to keep the movement honest and avoid pulling on your neck. | Brace your core and press your lower back toward the floor to engage your abdominals before you begin. | Curl your chin toward your chest, then continue lifting your torso in one smooth arc until you are sitting fully upright over your hips. | Pause briefly at the top, keeping your core tight and your spine tall. | Lower yourself under control back to the starting position, resisting the descent rather than dropping, until your upper back contacts the floor. | Complete all reps, then carefully remove your feet from the cradles.
tRu: Set the suspension trainer so the foot cradles hang low enough that you can lie on the floor with your legs nearly straight and your feet secured inside the cradles. | Lie on your back with your feet looped into the cradles, ankles comfortably braced, and your legs roughly hip-width apart with a slight bend at the knees. | Extend your arms along your sides or cross them over your chest to keep the movement honest and avoid pulling on your neck. | Напрягите корпус и направьте поясницу к полу, включив пресс перед началом движения. | Поднимите подбородок к груди, затем продолжайте поднимать туловище по одной плавной дуге, пока не сядете прямо над тазом. | Pause briefly at the top, keeping your core tight and your spine tall. | Lower yourself under control back to the starting position, resisting the descent rather than dropping, until your upper back contacts the floor. | Выполните все повторения, затем осторожно снимите ноги из держателей.
tHe: Set the suspension trainer so the foot cradles hang low enough that you can lie on the floor with your legs nearly straight and your feet secured inside the cradles. | Lie on your back with your feet looped into the cradles, ankles comfortably braced, and your legs roughly hip-width apart with a slight bend at the knees. | Extend your arms along your sides or cross them over your chest to keep the movement honest and avoid pulling on your neck. | הדק את הליבה ולחץ את הגב התחתון לכיוון הרצפה כדי להפעיל את הבטן לפני שמתחילים. | Curl your chin toward your chest, then continue lifting your torso in one smooth arc until you are sitting fully upright over your hips. | Pause briefly at the top, keeping your core tight and your spine tall. | Lower yourself under control back to the starting position, resisting the descent rather than dropping, until your upper back contacts the floor. | בצע את כל החזרות, ואז הסר בזהירות את רגליך מהמגרעות.

t: Grip both suspension strap handles with your palms facing down and step back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels at roughly a 45° angle or lower to the floor — the more horizontal you are, the harder the movement. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and align your head, hips, and heels in a rigid plank position before beginning. | Inhale and begin lowering your chest toward the handles by bending your elbows, keeping them at roughly a 45° angle from your torso rather than flaring them straight out. | As you descend, simultaneously drive one knee out to the side and up toward the same-side elbow in a wide arc — this is the Spiderman knee drive. | Lower until your chest is level with the handles and your knee is as close to the elbow as your hip mobility allows. | Exhale and press back up explosively through the handles while returning the leg to its starting position. | Maintain a locked plank through the hips — do not let them sag or pike during the press. | Alternate the knee drive each rep, or complete all reps on one side before switching. | Rerack by walking your feet toward the anchor point and releasing the straps under control.
tRu: Grip both suspension strap handles with your palms facing down and step back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels at roughly a 45° angle or lower to the floor — the more horizontal you are, the harder the movement. | Напрягите корпус, сожмите ягодицы и выровняйте голову, бёдра и пятки в жёсткое положение планки перед началом. | Inhale and begin lowering your chest toward the handles by bending your elbows, keeping them at roughly a 45° angle from your torso rather than flaring them straight out. | Опускаясь, одновременно отведите одно колено в сторону и вверх к одноимённому локтю по широкой дуге — это колено «человека-паука». | Lower until your chest is level with the handles and your knee is as close to the elbow as your hip mobility allows. | Exhale and press back up explosively through the handles while returning the leg to its starting position. | Maintain a locked plank through the hips — do not let them sag or pike during the press. | Чередуйте вынос колена каждое повторение или выполните все повторения на одну сторону перед сменой. | Rerack by walking your feet toward the anchor point and releasing the straps under control.
tHe: Grip both suspension strap handles with your palms facing down and step back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels at roughly a 45° angle or lower to the floor — the more horizontal you are, the harder the movement. | תכווץ את שרירי הליבה, כווץ את הישבנים, ויישר את הראש, המותניים והעקבים בתנוחת פלאנק נוקשה לפני שתתחיל. | Inhale and begin lowering your chest toward the handles by bending your elbows, keeping them at roughly a 45° angle from your torso rather than flaring them straight out. | בירידה, דחוף בו־זמנית ברך אחת הצידה ומעלה לעבר המרפק באותו צד בקשת רחבה — זוהי דחיפת ברך ספיידרמן. | Lower until your chest is level with the handles and your knee is as close to the elbow as your hip mobility allows. | Exhale and press back up explosively through the handles while returning the leg to its starting position. | Maintain a locked plank through the hips — do not let them sag or pike during the press. | החלף את דחיפת הברך בכל חזרה, או בצע את כל החזרות בצד אחד לפני ההחלפה. | Rerack by walking your feet toward the anchor point and releasing the straps under control.

t: Stand facing the suspension anchor point and hold one handle in each hand with a neutral grip, arms extended at roughly shoulder height. | Set your feet together or slightly staggered, then walk them toward the anchor to the distance you want — the closer your feet, the steeper the lean and the greater the resistance. | Lean back so your bodyweight is supported by the straps, and brace your core so your body forms a straight line from heels to head. | Simultaneously sweep one arm forward and upward (anterior arc) while the other arm sweeps backward and to the side (posterior arc), keeping both elbows softly extended throughout. | Continue until your front hand is at or just above shoulder height in front of you and your rear hand is at shoulder height behind your hip — this is the split position. | Pause briefly at the end range, feeling the stretch and contraction across both deltoid heads. | Slowly reverse the motion, bringing both arms back to the starting position under control. | Complete all reps on this arm configuration, then switch the forward and rear arms to train symmetrically on both sides.

t: Adjust the suspension strap to mid-calf height and stand facing away from the anchor point. | Place the top of your right foot into the strap's foot cradle, letting it hang behind you. | Step your left foot forward so you are in a lunge position with your left knee above your left ankle, rear right leg extended behind you. | Lower your right knee toward the floor until your left thigh is roughly parallel to the ground, keeping your torso upright. | Drive forcefully through your left heel and midfoot to push your body upward. | As you rise, drive your right knee forward and upward until your thigh reaches hip height, mimicking the drive phase of a sprint. | Pause briefly at the top, balancing on your left leg with your right knee raised. | Reverse the movement under control, lowering your right foot back into the lunge position. | Complete all reps on one side before switching the foot in the strap.
tRu: Отрегулируйте петлю подвесного тренажёра на высоту середины голени и встаньте спиной к точке крепления. | Place the top of your right foot into the strap's foot cradle, letting it hang behind you. | Step your left foot forward so you are in a lunge position with your left knee above your left ankle, rear right leg extended behind you. | Lower your right knee toward the floor until your left thigh is roughly parallel to the ground, keeping your torso upright. | Сильно оттолкнитесь левой пяткой и серединой стопы, чтобы поднять тело вверх. | Поднимаясь, подайте правое колено вперёд и вверх до высоты бедра, имитируя фазу отталкивания в спринте. | Pause briefly at the top, balancing on your left leg with your right knee raised. | Reverse the movement under control, lowering your right foot back into the lunge position. | Выполните все повторения на одной стороне перед тем, как сменить ногу в стропе.
tHe: כוון את רצועת המתח לגובה אמצע השוק ועמוד עם הגב לנקודת העיגון. | Place the top of your right foot into the strap's foot cradle, letting it hang behind you. | Step your left foot forward so you are in a lunge position with your left knee above your left ankle, rear right leg extended behind you. | Lower your right knee toward the floor until your left thigh is roughly parallel to the ground, keeping your torso upright. | Drive forcefully through your left heel and midfoot to push your body upward. | בעלייה, דחוף את ברך ימין קדימה ומעלה עד שהירך מגיעה לגובה האגן, כמו בשלב הדרייב של ספרינט. | Pause briefly at the top, balancing on your left leg with your right knee raised. | Reverse the movement under control, lowering your right foot back into the lunge position. | בצע את כל החזרות בצד אחד לפני החלפת הרגל ברצועה.

t: Set the suspension straps to a length where the handles hang at approximately waist height when you stand facing the anchor point. | Stand facing the anchor, feet shoulder-width apart or slightly wider, toes angled out 15–30 degrees. | Grasp both handles with a firm overhand grip and extend your arms so there is light tension in the straps. | Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and shift your weight back slightly into your heels. | Begin the descent by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, allowing them to track over your toes. | Lower yourself until your thighs reach parallel to the floor or as deep as your mobility allows, using the strap tension to counterbalance and maintain an upright torso. | Pause briefly at the bottom with your weight distributed across the full foot. | Drive through your heels and midfoot to extend your hips and knees simultaneously, rising back to the starting position. | Stand tall, fully extend your hips, and reset your brace before starting the next rep.

t: Adjust the suspension straps to a length where you can reach the handles comfortably with your arms fully extended overhead when standing tall. | Stand facing the anchor point and hold one handle in each hand with your arms raised directly overhead, palms facing each other. | Set your feet shoulder-width apart with toes turned out slightly, and brace your core. | Push your hips back and bend your knees to descend into a squat, keeping your chest up, your arms straight overhead, and your weight evenly distributed across your feet. | Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, or as deep as your mobility comfortably allows. | Drive through your heels to press the floor away and return to the starting position, squeezing your glutes at the top. | Reset your posture and brace before each subsequent rep.

t: Set the suspension straps to a length where the handles reach roughly hip height when you stand facing the anchor point. | Stand facing the anchor point and grasp one handle in each hand with a neutral grip, arms extended in front of you. | Walk your feet forward and lean back slightly until there is moderate tension in the straps with your arms straight and your weight settled through your heels. | Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to lower into a squat, keeping your chest up, knees tracking over your toes, and arms extended as you descend. | At the bottom of the squat, pause briefly with your thighs at or near parallel to the floor. | Drive explosively through both feet to stand, simultaneously pulling the handles forcefully toward your chest by retracting your shoulder blades and driving your elbows back. | At the top of the movement, your legs should be fully extended and the handles should be drawn close to your torso with elbows pointed back. | Lower the handles under control as you descend back into the next squat, maintaining strap tension throughout. | Complete all reps with a smooth, coordinated squat-and-pull rhythm before returning to the start position.

t: Set the suspension straps to approximately chest height and stand facing away from the anchor point. | Grip one handle in each hand with an overhand grip, arms extended in front of you at chest height, and walk your feet forward until the straps are taut. | Lean your body forward slightly so the straps bear some of your weight — this is your starting position. | Brace your core firmly, squeeze your glutes, and establish a straight line from head to heels before you move. | Inhale and slowly extend your arms overhead in a wide arc, allowing your body to lean further toward the anchor while maintaining the rigid plank position throughout. | Continue reaching until your arms are fully extended overhead and your torso approaches parallel to the floor, or as far as core tension allows without your lower back arching. | Pause briefly at full extension to confirm your body line is still straight. | Exhale and drive your arms back down and toward your hips in a controlled arc to return to the starting position. | Reset your brace at the top of each rep and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

t: Adjust the suspension trainer so the foot cradles hang approximately 6–12 inches above the floor. | Kneel facing away from the anchor point and place one foot, then the other, into the suspension foot cradles with the tops of your feet resting in the cradles. | Walk your hands out and lower yourself into a high plank position — hands directly under your shoulders, body in a straight line from heels to head. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and ensure your hips are level and not sagging or piking upward. | Keeping your body rigid, slide your feet apart and your hands out to the sides to form a wide star shape, spreading as far as you can control with good form. | Hold the star position for the target duration — typically 10–30 seconds — breathing steadily while maintaining a neutral spine. | Slowly draw your hands and feet back in toward the center to return to the high plank position. | Rest briefly, then repeat for the prescribed number of sets.

nR: Сгибания ног с прямым бедром на петлях
t: Attach the suspension trainer to a sturdy overhead anchor and adjust the straps so the foot cradles hang roughly ankle height above the floor. | Lie on your back with your head pointing away from the anchor, slide both heels into the foot cradles, and extend your legs fully. | Press your arms flat against the floor alongside your torso to create a stable base. | Drive through your heels to lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to feet — this elevated bridge is your starting position. | Keeping your hips raised and your body in that straight line, exhale and curl both heels toward your glutes by bending at the knees. | Continue curling until your knees reach approximately 90 degrees and you feel a strong contraction in your hamstrings. | Inhale and slowly extend your legs back to the straight starting position, resisting the straps throughout the return. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions without letting your hips drop between reps.

t: Set the suspension straps to a height where the handles hang roughly at hip level when you are standing in front of the anchor point. | Face away from the anchor, reach back, and grip one handle in each hand with palms facing inward or slightly down. | Walk your feet forward until your body is angled forward and your arms are extended behind you, supporting most of your bodyweight. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels. | Bend your elbows to lower your body toward the floor, keeping your upper arms close to your sides and your elbows pointing straight back rather than flaring out. | Lower until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor or your elbows reach approximately 90 degrees of flexion — whichever comes first without losing a neutral spine. | Press through your palms and extend your elbows forcefully to return to the starting position, keeping tension on the triceps throughout. | Complete the desired number of reps, then step back toward the anchor to release the load safely before letting go of the handles.

t: Set the suspension straps to a mid-length position and face away from the anchor point. | Grip both handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down, and walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line at roughly a 45° angle to the floor — the more horizontal you are, the harder the movement. | Brace your core and lock your body into a rigid plank from head to heels before beginning. | Inhale and lower your forehead toward the handles by bending your elbows, allowing them to travel forward alongside your head — keep them close together, not flaring outward. | Continue until your upper arms are alongside your head and the handles are at or behind ear level, with your elbows deeply bent. | Exhale and extend your elbows to press the handles forward and away, driving through the triceps brachii until your arms are straight again. | Maintain a locked core and straight body line throughout — do not let your hips sag or pike during the movement. | Complete all reps and walk your feet toward the anchor point to exit under control.

t: Anchor the suspension straps overhead and adjust them so the handles hang at roughly hip height when you stand facing the anchor. | Hold one handle in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and walk your feet forward toward the anchor until your body leans back at roughly a 45° angle to the floor. | Brace your core and set your body in a straight line from head to heels, letting the straps take your weight. | Pin your upper arms against your sides and hold them fixed there, elbows bent to roughly 90° so your forearms point up toward the anchor — this is your starting position. | Exhale and extend your elbows fully, driving the handles down and back past your hips until both arms are straight and your triceps are fully contracted. | Pause briefly at full extension to squeeze the triceps. | Slowly bend your elbows to lower your body back to the starting position, controlling the descent to avoid swinging. | Complete your reps, then walk your feet back until you are standing upright before releasing the handles.
tRu: Закрепите подвесные петли над головой и отрегулируйте их так, чтобы рукояти висели примерно на высоте бёдер, когда стоите лицом к креплению. | Hold one handle in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and walk your feet forward toward the anchor until your body leans back at roughly a 45° angle to the floor. | Напрягите корпус и выстройте тело в прямую линию от головы до пяток, перенеся вес на петли. | Pin your upper arms against your sides and hold them fixed there, elbows bent to roughly 90° so your forearms point up toward the anchor — this is your starting position. | Exhale and extend your elbows fully, driving the handles down and back past your hips until both arms are straight and your triceps are fully contracted. | Pause briefly at full extension to squeeze the triceps. | Slowly bend your elbows to lower your body back to the starting position, controlling the descent to avoid swinging. | Выполните свои повторения, затем отойдите ногами назад, пока не встанете прямо, прежде чем отпустить рукояти.
tHe: עגן את רצועות האימון מעל הראש וכוון אותן כך שהידיות יתלו בערך בגובה האגן כשאתה עומד מול העוגן. | Hold one handle in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and walk your feet forward toward the anchor until your body leans back at roughly a 45° angle to the floor. | הדק את הליבה וקבע את הגוף בקו ישר מהראש עד העקבים, תוך נתינת לרצועות לשאת את משקלך. | Pin your upper arms against your sides and hold them fixed there, elbows bent to roughly 90° so your forearms point up toward the anchor — this is your starting position. | Exhale and extend your elbows fully, driving the handles down and back past your hips until both arms are straight and your triceps are fully contracted. | Pause briefly at full extension to squeeze the triceps. | Slowly bend your elbows to lower your body back to the starting position, controlling the descent to avoid swinging. | Complete your reps, then walk your feet back until you are standing upright before releasing the handles.

t: Adjust the suspension straps to waist height and stand facing the anchor point. | Grip both handles together with both hands, interlacing your fingers or stacking your palms, and step back until the straps are taut with your arms extended straight in front of you. | Set your feet hip-width apart, brace your core, and keep your hips in a neutral position. | Lean back slightly so your body forms a straight line from heels to shoulders, creating tension through the straps. | Keeping your arms straight and hips square, rotate your torso to the right by driving your clasped hands to the right side of your body. | Pause briefly at the end of the range of motion, keeping your hips square and your obliques under tension. | Reverse the movement under control, returning your hands to center. | Rotate to the left in the same controlled manner, pausing at the end range. | Continue alternating sides for the prescribed number of repetitions.

t: Anchor the suspension straps overhead and shorten them so the foot cradles hang around ankle to mid-shin height, then kneel and place both feet in the cradles, laces down. | Walk your hands out into a push-up plank position with arms fully extended, wrists under shoulders, and body in a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to stabilize the plank before initiating any movement. | Exhale and drive both knees toward your left armpit by flexing the hips and rotating the pelvis to the left. | Pause briefly when the knees are as close to the armpit as your range of motion allows. | Inhale and extend the hips slowly, returning your feet to the starting plank position under control. | On the next repetition, drive both knees toward the right armpit, alternating sides each rep. | Complete the prescribed number of repetitions per side while maintaining a neutral spine throughout.
tRu: Закрепите подвесные петли над головой и укоротите их так, чтобы петли для стоп висели примерно на высоте лодыжек и середины голени, затем встаньте на колени и поместите обе стопы в петли шнуровкой вниз. | Walk your hands out into a push-up plank position with arms fully extended, wrists under shoulders, and body in a straight line from head to heels. | Напрягите корпус и сожмите ягодицы, чтобы стабилизировать планку перед началом движения. | Exhale and drive both knees toward your left armpit by flexing the hips and rotating the pelvis to the left. | Pause briefly when the knees are as close to the armpit as your range of motion allows. | Inhale and extend the hips slowly, returning your feet to the starting plank position under control. | On the next repetition, drive both knees toward the right armpit, alternating sides each rep. | Выполните указанное количество повторений на каждую сторону, сохраняя нейтральное положение позвоночника.
tHe: עגן את רצועות האימון מעל הראש וקצר אותן כך שעריסות הרגליים יתלו בגובה הקרסול עד אמצע השוק, ואז כרע והנח את שתי כפות הרגליים בעריסות כשהשרוכים פונים למטה. | Walk your hands out into a push-up plank position with arms fully extended, wrists under shoulders, and body in a straight line from head to heels. | הדק את הליבה וכווץ את הישבנים כדי לייצב את הפלאנק לפני כל תנועה. | Exhale and drive both knees toward your left armpit by flexing the hips and rotating the pelvis to the left. | Pause briefly when the knees are as close to the armpit as your range of motion allows. | Inhale and extend the hips slowly, returning your feet to the starting plank position under control. | On the next repetition, drive both knees toward the right armpit, alternating sides each rep. | בצע את מספר החזרות לכל צד, שומר על עמוד שדרה נייטרלי לכל אורך התרגיל.

t: Stand facing the suspension anchor point and grip both handles with both hands, arms extended forward at chest height. | Walk your feet forward and lean back so your body is at a diagonal angle, with arms fully extended and weight supported by the straps. | Brace your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels throughout the movement. | Rotate your torso to one side, sweeping both hands across your body in a controlled arc while keeping your arms relatively straight. | Continue rotating until your arms are extended to the side and your torso has turned as far as your range of motion allows. | Pause briefly at the end range, feeling the tension in your obliques and anterior deltoid. | Slowly reverse the rotation, pulling back through center with control. | Complete all reps to one side, then switch to the other side.

tHe: Stand facing the suspension anchor point and grip both handles with both hands, arms extended forward at chest height. | Walk your feet forward and lean back so your body is at a diagonal angle, with arms fully extended and weight supported by the straps. | הדק את הליבה ושמור על הגוף בקו ישר מהראש ועד העקבים לאורך כל התנועה. | Rotate your torso to one side, sweeping both hands across your body in a controlled arc while keeping your arms relatively straight. | Continue rotating until your arms are extended to the side and your torso has turned as far as your range of motion allows. | Pause briefly at the end range, feeling the tension in your obliques and anterior deltoid. | Slowly reverse the rotation, pulling back through center with control. | בצע את כל החזרות לצד אחד, ואפנה לצד השני.

t: Set the suspension trainer handles low to the ground, roughly 6–12 inches above the floor. | Face away from the anchor point and place both feet through the handles so the tops of your feet rest inside the loops. | Walk your hands out to a strong push-up position, arms fully extended, body in a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core and keep your hips level to establish a stable starting plank. | Exhale and drive both knees up and diagonally across your body toward one elbow, rotating through your waist. | Pause briefly at the top of the rotation, squeezing your obliques. | Return both feet under control back to the starting plank position. | Repeat the movement toward the opposite elbow, alternating sides each rep.

t: Set the suspension straps to roughly hip height — the lower the handles, the more challenging the exercise. | Stand facing the anchor point, grip both handles with an underhand grip (palms facing up), and walk your feet forward until your body leans back at a diagonal angle. | Extend your arms fully, plant your heels on the floor, and let your body hang at your chosen angle — start with a moderate incline before progressing to a more horizontal position. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a rigid straight line from your head to your heels. | Initiate the pull by driving your elbows back and close to your sides, not by shrugging your shoulders. | Row your chest up toward the handles until your hands reach the sides of your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top. | Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then lower yourself under full control until your arms are fully extended. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, then walk your feet back toward the anchor point to return to standing.

t: Stand facing the suspension anchor point and grip both handles with an overhand grip at about chest height. | Step your feet in toward the anchor until the straps are taut and your arms are fully extended in front of you. | Shift your weight back so that the straps support your full bodyweight and your hips are behind your heels. | Allow your head to drop between your arms and round your upper back deliberately, letting the straps pull your arms forward. | Tuck your chin to your chest and press your shoulder blades apart to deepen the stretch through the upper back. | Breathe slowly and hold the stretched position for the prescribed time, relaxing further into the stretch with each exhale. | To exit, keep your grip and walk your feet back away from the anchor until you are standing upright again.

t: Adjust the suspension straps to a length where the handles hang at about hip height when you stand facing the anchor point. | Grasp one handle in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other, and step back until the straps are taut. | Walk your feet forward to hip-width apart under or slightly in front of the anchor point and lean back until your arms are straight and your body sits at roughly a 45-degree angle with the floor, heels on the ground. | Brace your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels throughout the set. | With a slight bend in the elbows, raise both arms out and upward at roughly 45 degrees from your midline, forming a wide Y shape overhead. | Lift until your hands are above head height in the Y position, thumbs pointing back toward the ceiling to externally rotate your shoulders. | Pause briefly at the top with your shoulder blades retracted and depressed. | Lower your arms under control back to the starting position, maintaining tension through the straps throughout the descent. | Repeat for the target number of reps without letting your hips sag or your lower back arch.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms at your sides, and your weight evenly distributed through both feet. | Inhale and sweep both arms out to the sides and then overhead, reaching long through your fingertips and lifting through the crown of your head. | Exhale and hinge forward from the hips — not the waist — keeping a long, neutral spine as you lower your torso toward the floor. | Allow your arms to follow the arc of a dive, sweeping forward and then down toward the ground as your torso descends. | Once your hands reach the floor or your maximum comfortable range, let your knees soften slightly if your hamstrings are tight. | Pause briefly at the bottom, releasing tension in your lower back and letting your head hang heavy. | On an inhale, sweep your arms out to the sides again and use your core and hip flexors to rise back to standing with a long spine. | Return to the starting position with your arms overhead, then lower them to your sides to complete one repetition.

t: Stand tall with your feet together or hip-width apart, arms resting at your sides and weight evenly distributed through both feet. | Inhale and raise both arms overhead, interlacing your fingers and turning the palms to face the ceiling. | Root down through both feet and engage your core lightly to protect the lower back. | On your next exhale, slowly lean your entire torso to the right, keeping both arms straight and both feet planted firmly on the floor. | Hold the position for 2–3 breaths, feeling the stretch along the left side of your body from hip to fingertip. | Inhale to return to center with both arms still extended overhead. | Exhale and lean to the left, holding for 2–3 breaths to stretch the right side equally. | Return to center on an inhale, then lower your arms back to your sides to complete one full repetition.

t: Lie on your back on a flat surface with both legs extended and your arms at your sides, palms pressing firmly into the floor. | Brace your core and press your lower back into the floor to stabilize your pelvis before the movement begins. | Lift one leg a few inches off the floor, keeping it straight and your foot softly flexed. | Trace a large, smooth circle with that leg — sweep it outward to the side, arc it down toward the floor, cross it past the midline, and return it to the starting position. | Keep your core engaged and your hips squared to the ceiling throughout the circle so the pelvis does not rock or tilt. | Complete the prescribed number of circles in one direction, then reverse and repeat in the opposite direction. | Switch legs and perform the same number of circles on the other side. | Breathe steadily and rhythmically throughout the set to support the aerobic demand of the drill.

t: Push off the wall or step into the water and extend your body into a horizontal, face-down position with your head in line with your spine. | Begin the arm cycle: reach one arm fully forward, enter the hand thumb-first into the water, and extend through the shoulder. | Pull that arm through the water in a high-elbow catch, sweeping it back along your centerline and finishing the stroke at your hip. | As one arm finishes the pull, recover it above the water with a high elbow and swing it forward to re-enter while the opposite arm begins its catch. | Keep a continuous flutter kick throughout — alternating small, quick up-and-down kicks driven from the hips, with relaxed ankles and feet just breaking the surface. | Rotate your body 30–45° toward the recovering arm on each stroke cycle; use that rotation to drive power into the pull rather than swimming flat. | To breathe, rotate your head with your body roll to the side — not upward — inhale quickly as your mouth clears the water, then return your face to the water and exhale steadily. | Maintain a streamlined body position throughout: hips near the surface, core engaged, and head neutral so water meets your forehead at the hairline.

t: Set up four cones in a T shape: place cone A at the starting line, cone B 10 yards directly ahead, and cones C and D each 5 yards to the left and right of cone B. | Stand behind cone A in an athletic stance — feet shoulder-width apart, knees bent, weight forward over the balls of your feet. | On your signal, sprint forward from cone A to cone B and touch the base of the cone with your right hand. | From cone B, shuffle laterally to your left toward cone C, keeping your hips square to the front and your feet from crossing. | Touch cone C with your left hand, then immediately shuffle to your right all the way past cone B to cone D. | Touch cone D with your right hand, then shuffle back to your left until you reach cone B. | Touch cone B, then backpedal in a straight line — staying low and facing forward — back to cone A. | Drive your arms actively throughout every phase to maintain stride rate and generate power through the cuts. | Stop the clock when you cross cone A and record your time; rest fully for 60–90 seconds before the next repetition.

t: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and your arms reaching overhead along the floor. | Press your lower back gently into the mat and engage your abdominals to prepare your core. | Inhale, then as you exhale begin to curl your chin toward your chest and peel your spine off the mat one vertebra at a time. | Simultaneously lift both legs to approximately 45 degrees, keeping them straight and together. | Continue rolling up until you are balancing on your sit bones with your torso and legs forming a V shape, arms reaching forward parallel to your legs. | Hold the top position for a breath, keeping your spine long, waist lifted, and legs steady. | Inhale, then slowly lower your arms, torso, and legs back to the mat in a controlled reverse roll. | Return fully to the starting position with your back and legs flat on the floor before beginning the next repetition.

t: Stand tall with your feet together and arms at your sides, fixing your gaze on a single point in front of you to establish balance. | Bend both knees slightly, shifting your weight onto your left foot. | Lift your right leg and cross it over the left thigh, squeezing the thighs together. If possible, hook the right foot behind the left calf. | Extend both arms straight forward at shoulder height, then cross the left arm over the right at the elbows. | Bend the elbows and bring the forearms upright, wrapping the right hand around to meet the left palm if your flexibility allows. | Lift the elbows to shoulder height and gently press the forearms away from your face to deepen the stretch across the upper back and shoulders. | Sink the hips slightly lower, as if sitting back into a chair, to increase the stretch through the outer hip of the crossed leg. | Hold the pose for 5–10 slow breaths, keeping your gaze steady and your standing foot firmly rooted. | Slowly unwind the arms and legs, return to standing, and repeat the pose on the opposite side.

t: Sit on the very edge of a firm table or plinth so your hips are at the table's border. | Lie back slowly while holding both knees to your chest to flatten your lower back against the table. | Keep one knee hugged firmly to your chest throughout the test to stabilize the pelvis and eliminate lumbar lordosis. | Lower the opposite (test) leg off the edge of the table, allowing gravity to pull it toward the floor. | Observe whether the test-side thigh rests flat and parallel to the table; a thigh that stays elevated indicates iliopsoas tightness. | Check whether the knee of the test leg bends to approximately 90 degrees; reduced knee flexion suggests rectus femoris tightness. | Note whether the test leg abducts (drifts outward) away from the midline; lateral drift indicates IT band or TFL tightness. | Return the test leg to the chest, sit up carefully, and repeat the assessment on the opposite side. | Record the angle and any compensations observed for each hip to guide stretching or rehabilitation priorities.

t: Sit at the very edge of a flat bench or table so that your hips are at the edge and you can safely lie back. | Bring both knees toward your chest as you lower your back down onto the surface, using your hands behind your thighs for support. | Once lying flat, pull one knee firmly into your chest and hold it there with both hands — keep this position throughout the test. | Let the other leg lower toward the floor in a relaxed, passive manner, releasing any muscular effort in that leg. | Observe or have a partner observe the position of the lowered leg: the thigh should be roughly parallel to the table and the knee should flex to approximately 90 degrees if hip flexor length is adequate. | Note any deviation: if the thigh rises above horizontal, the iliopsoas is likely shortened; if the knee fails to reach 90 degrees of flexion, the rectus femoris may be restricted. | Return the lowered leg to your chest, sit up carefully, and repeat the assessment on the opposite side.
