t: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, arms resting at your sides. | Cross your right ankle over your left knee so that your right knee points out to the side in a figure-4 position. | Press through your left foot and drive your hips up into a single-leg glute bridge, squeezing the gluteus maximus and engaging the hamstrings to hold the position. | Once your hips are lifted and stable, reach your right arm up toward the ceiling, keeping the elbow straight. | Slowly rotate through your thoracic spine, lowering the right arm across your body and toward the floor on the left side while your hips remain elevated. | Follow the movement with your head and eyes, allowing the upper back to rotate as far as comfortable without letting the hips drop. | Pause for 2–3 seconds at the end range, feeling the stretch across the latissimus dorsi, obliques, and posterior shoulder. | Reverse the rotation to return the arm to the ceiling, then lower your hips to the floor to complete one repetition. | Complete all reps on this side, then switch — cross the left ankle over the right knee and repeat with the left arm sweeping.

t: Start on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, spine in a neutral position. | Inhale to prepare, then on the exhale slide your right arm along the floor underneath your left arm, palm facing up. | Continue threading the arm through until your right shoulder and right side of your head rest on the floor. | Allow your right shoulder to sink toward the ground while your left arm remains extended in front of you for support. | Keep your hips level and stacked over your knees — do not let them shift to one side or rotate along with your upper body. | Hold the stretch for 20–45 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the thoracic spine to rotate further with each exhale. | To release, press through your left hand and slowly return your right arm back to the starting position. | Reset to the all-fours position, then repeat on the opposite side by threading your left arm under your right arm.

t: Stand or sit tall with your spine neutral and one arm extended in front of you at shoulder height, palm facing down. | Curl your thumb across your palm toward the base of your little finger. | Wrap your remaining four fingers over your thumb to hold it gently in place. | Slowly bend your wrist downward, toward the floor, until you feel a moderate stretch along the top of your thumb and the outer forearm. | Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and keeping your shoulder relaxed. | Slowly release your wrist and uncurl your thumb. | Repeat on the same hand for the prescribed number of holds, then switch to the opposite hand.

nE: Tibial Flexion Stretch On Wall Bar
nR: Растяжка сгибания голени на шведской стенке
nH: מתיחת כפיפת שוק על סולם שוודי
t: Stand facing the wall bar and grip it at roughly hip to waist height with both hands, feet hip-width apart. | Step one foot forward and place it flat on the floor, approximately 15–20 cm from the base of the wall. | Keep your back foot on the floor with toes pointing straight ahead, maintaining a slight bend in the back knee for balance. | Keeping the front heel firmly pressed into the floor, slowly shift your weight forward and drive the front knee toward the wall, allowing the ankle to dorsiflex. | Use the bar for support — do not pull yourself forward with your arms; let your body weight create the stretch organically. | Continue pushing the knee forward until you feel a distinct stretch along the back of the lower leg, Achilles tendon, and calf. | For a deeper stretch targeting the soleus and Achilles, allow a slight bend in the front knee; for more gastrocnemius emphasis, keep the front leg straighter. | Hold the stretched position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and relaxing further into the stretch with each exhale. | Slowly return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite leg. Perform 2–3 holds per side.

t: Stand tall near a wall or sturdy surface for balance. Shift your weight onto your left foot. | Step your right foot back and place the top of the right foot flat on the floor, toes pointing directly behind you. | Soften your right knee so it is slightly bent — this is the semi-flexed position that defines the stretch. | Keeping your torso upright, slowly press your right shin and ankle toward the floor by gently sinking your hips downward. | Stop when you feel a firm, comfortable stretch along the front of the right shin and into the top of the foot. You should not feel sharp pain. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and steadily throughout. | Ease out of the stretch by lifting your foot, returning to a standing position. | Repeat on the opposite side, then perform 2–3 rounds per leg as needed.

t: Begin on all fours in a tabletop position with your wrists directly under your shoulders, your knees under your hips, and your spine neutral. | Brace your core lightly and keep your neck in line with your spine — avoid looking up or letting your chin drop to your chest. | On an inhale, simultaneously extend your right leg straight back and reach your left arm forward, raising both limbs until they are parallel to the floor. | Pause for one breath in the extended position, creating length from your fingertips to your heel while keeping your hips level. | On an exhale, round your spine toward the ceiling and draw your right knee and left elbow together underneath your torso. | Hold the curled position briefly, bringing your knee and elbow as close together as your range of motion allows, with your spine fully rounded. | Return slowly to the extended position on your next inhale, then repeat the curl for your target number of reps before switching sides. | After completing the same number of repetitions with your left leg and right arm, lower both limbs and return to a neutral tabletop to rest.
tRu: Встаньте на четвереньки в положение столешницы: запястья точно под плечами, колени под бёдрами, позвоночник в нейтральном положении. | Легко напрягите пресс и удерживайте шею на одной линии с позвоночником — не смотрите вверх и не опускайте подбородок к груди. | On an inhale, simultaneously extend your right leg straight back and reach your left arm forward, raising both limbs until they are parallel to the floor. | Pause for one breath in the extended position, creating length from your fingertips to your heel while keeping your hips level. | On an exhale, round your spine toward the ceiling and draw your right knee and left elbow together underneath your torso. | Hold the curled position briefly, bringing your knee and elbow as close together as your range of motion allows, with your spine fully rounded. | Return slowly to the extended position on your next inhale, then repeat the curl for your target number of reps before switching sides. | Выполнив то же количество повторений левой ногой и правой рукой, опустите обе конечности и вернитесь в нейтральное положение на четвереньках для отдыха.

t: Sit or stand in a comfortable position with the arm you plan to treat resting on your thigh or a flat surface, palm facing up. | Form a loose fist or extend the fingers of your opposite hand, and position your thumb or knuckles at the wrist end of the forearm. | Apply moderate downward pressure with your thumb or knuckles into the soft tissue of the forearm. | Slowly glide your pressing hand up the forearm toward the elbow, maintaining consistent pressure throughout the stroke. | When you encounter a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for five to ten seconds before continuing the stroke. | Return your pressing hand to the starting position at the wrist and repeat the stroke, adjusting the angle slightly to cover different areas of the forearm. | After three to five passes along the inner forearm, rotate the arm so the palm faces down and repeat the process on the outer forearm. | Complete three to five minutes of work on each forearm, then gently shake out the hand and wrist to encourage circulation.

t: Stand upright with your feet together and your arms relaxed at your sides. | Step one foot forward about 12–18 inches and flex that foot so the heel stays on the ground and the toes point up toward the ceiling. | With a tall spine, hinge forward from your hips — not your waist — until you feel a stretch along the back of the extended leg. | Reach both hands down toward the toes of the extended foot, keeping your back flat and your chest open. | Hold this position for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and evenly. t: Sit tall on a chair or stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, spine neutral, and shoulders relaxed away from your ears. | Let your chin drop gently toward your chest, feeling a mild stretch along the back of your neck. | Slowly roll your right ear toward your right shoulder, pausing for one to two seconds when you feel a gentle pull on the left side of the neck. | Continue the arc by tilting your head back slightly, looking up at the ceiling without compressing the back of the neck. | Roll your left ear toward your left shoulder, pausing again for one to two seconds. | Return your chin back toward your chest to complete one full circle. | Reverse direction and perform the same slow circular sweep the opposite way. | Complete three to five slow circles in each direction, then return your head to a neutral upright position.

t: Sit on the floor or on a bench with your legs extended in front of you and your torso upright. | Place the Tiger Tail roller horizontally across the outer lower leg, positioning it just below the head of the fibula — the bony prominence on the outside of the knee. | Rest your opposite hand on top of the roller to apply additional downward pressure and control the amount of force you use. | Slowly roll the tool down the outer lower leg toward the lateral ankle, taking 2–3 seconds per pass to cover the full length of the peroneals. | When you find a tender spot, pause over it and hold steady pressure for 20–30 seconds until you feel the tension begin to release before continuing. | Work back up toward the fibula head and repeat, completing 2–3 passes over the entire length of the muscle group. | Between passes, rotate your foot slightly inward and then outward to expose different fibers of the peroneal group to the roller. | Complete 2–3 minutes of rolling on each leg, then switch sides.

t: Stand or sit tall with your spine neutral and your feet roughly hip-width apart. | Raise your right arm straight overhead, then bend your elbow so your right hand drops behind your head toward the center of your upper back. | Bring your left hand up and place it on your right elbow, just above the joint. | Gently pull your right elbow toward the midline and slightly backward to deepen the stretch along the back of your upper arm. | Hold the position while breathing steadily, keeping your neck relaxed and your chin level — do not let your head jut forward. | Maintain an upright torso; avoid leaning to the side or letting your lower back arch excessively. | Hold for 20–40 seconds, or as long as instructed, feeling a comfortable stretch along the triceps and into the shoulder. | Release the pull, lower both arms, and shake them out gently. | Repeat on the opposite side, raising your left arm overhead and assisting with your right hand.

t: Start on all fours with your wrists directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips, spine neutral. | Exhale and round your spine upward, drawing your right knee toward your nose and tucking your chin to your chest. | Inhale and slowly extend your right leg back and up, raising it as high as comfortable while lifting your head and gazing forward. | Bend your right knee, bringing the foot toward your head, then reach your right hand back to take hold of the right ankle or foot. | Press the foot gently into your hand to deepen the backbend, arching the spine and opening the chest. Let each exhale release tension in the hip flexor and chest. | Release the foot, extend the arm forward, and return to the all-fours starting position. | Repeat on the opposite side, performing equal time or reps on each leg.

t: Stand tall at one end of a clear, flat surface with your feet together and arms extended out to your sides at shoulder height. | Fix your gaze on a point directly ahead at eye level to anchor your balance throughout the movement. | Step forward with one foot, placing the heel directly in front of the toes of the standing foot so the feet form a continuous line. | Shift your weight smoothly onto the front foot as you bring it fully down, keeping your hips level and avoiding sideways sway. | Bring the back foot forward and again place the heel directly against the toes of the foot now in front, continuing the heel-to-toe chain. | Maintain a slight bend in the knee of the standing leg to engage the stabilising muscles and absorb any balance corrections. | Keep your core braced and your arms gently active — make small, controlled adjustments with your hands rather than large swinging motions. | Continue walking in a straight line for the target distance or rep count, then pause, turn carefully, and walk back. | Perform the prescribed number of lengths and finish by returning to a neutral standing position.

t: Stand facing the tire with your feet hip-width apart and your toes close to its base. | Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to squat down, sliding your fingers under the tire's lower edge with your palms facing up and your spine in a neutral position. | Brace your core, take a breath into your belly, and grip the tire firmly with both hands. | Drive explosively through your heels, extending your hips and knees to lift the tire off the ground — keep it close to your body throughout the pull. | As the tire rises past hip height, step forward to close the gap and shift your hands from underneath to a pushing position on the side of the tire. | Drive through your palms, pressing the tire forward and over until it falls flat on the ground. | Walk to the opposite side of the tire, reset your stance and grip, and begin the next rep.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides or held lightly in front of you for balance. | Shift your weight forward onto the balls of your feet, lifting your heels slightly off the ground. | Spring upward by quickly extending through your ankles and pushing off with your toes, leaving the ground with a small, controlled jump. | Keep the jump compact — focus on height generated by ankle extension rather than by bending your knees deeply. | As you rise, keep your core braced and your torso upright with a neutral spine. | Land softly on the balls of your feet, absorbing impact through your ankles and allowing your heels to lightly kiss the ground. | Rebound immediately into the next jump, maintaining a continuous, rhythmic cadence with minimal ground contact time. | Complete the target number of reps or duration, then lower both heels fully to the floor to rest.

t: Kneel on the floor on a mat or soft surface with your knees together and feet pointing straight back. | Tuck all ten toes under so the balls of your feet press into the floor and your toes are dorsiflexed. | Slowly sit back toward your heels, shifting your bodyweight onto your tucked toes. | Place your hands on your thighs or the floor for balance as needed. | Keep your spine upright and your torso relaxed — avoid hunching forward. | Hold the position for 30–60 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the stretch to deepen gradually. | To release, lean forward slightly, lift your hips, and untuck your toes before returning to a neutral kneeling position.

t: Sit on the floor with your back flat against a wall and your legs extended straight out in front of you, feet together and toes pointing up. | Press your lower back gently into the wall and sit tall, engaging your core before you begin. | Extend both arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, parallel to the floor. | Inhale to prepare, then exhale as you rotate your torso to one side, reaching both hands toward the toes on that side. | Keep your legs pressed firmly into the floor and your quadriceps contracted so your knees remain straight throughout the movement. | Hold the rotated position for one second, feeling the obliques engage on the working side. | Inhale as you return to the centered starting position with your back against the wall. | Repeat the reach on the opposite side to complete one full repetition. | Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides or held out slightly for balance. | Rise onto the balls of your feet, lifting your heels as high as you comfortably can while keeping your ankles straight and stable. | Begin walking forward, maintaining the raised-heel position with every step. | Keep your core lightly braced and your torso upright — avoid leaning forward at the hips. | Take small, controlled steps, landing each foot on the ball rather than letting the heel drop between strides. | Keep your knees soft but do not bend them excessively; aim for a natural, fluid gait. | Continue for the target distance or time, then lower your heels gently to the floor to finish. | To return, walk back the same way or simply lower your heels and walk normally.

t: Grip an overhead bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with an overhand grip, thumbs wrapped fully around the bar. | Jump or step up so that your chin clears the bar and your chest is close to it — this is your starting position. | Pull your shoulder blades down and together, keeping your chest open and your torso from swinging. | Hold your elbows at full flexion with your chin above the bar, maintaining a slight forward lean of the torso. | Breathe steadily throughout the hold without letting your shoulders shrug up toward your ears. | Aim to hold the position for the target duration — typically 5 to 30 seconds depending on your strength level. | Lower yourself under control until your arms are fully extended, then release the bar.

t: Stand tall with your feet together, arms relaxed at your sides, and your core lightly braced. | Take a step forward with your right foot to create a short walking stride. | As you shift your weight onto the right foot, swing your left leg straight forward and upward, keeping the knee fully extended. | Simultaneously reach your right arm forward and down toward the toes of your rising left foot. | Aim to bring your hand and foot as close together as possible without rounding your lower back or bending the raised knee. | Lower the left foot to the ground in front of you to take a step, then repeat the movement on the opposite side. | Swing the right leg up while reaching the left arm toward the right foot. | Continue walking forward in this alternating pattern, maintaining an upright torso and a controlled, deliberate kick on each rep. | Complete 10–20 total reps (5–10 per leg) or cover the prescribed distance before moving on to the next warm-up drill.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging at your sides. | Brace your core and keep your chest up to establish a neutral spine before you move. | Step one foot out at roughly a 45° diagonal angle (forward-lateral) or a rear-lateral angle, depending on the variation you are using. | Sink into the lunge by bending both knees, lowering your hips toward the floor until your front thigh approaches parallel to the ground. | Keep your front knee tracking over your second toe and avoid letting it cave inward. | Drive through the heel of your stepping foot to push the floor away and return to the starting position. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch legs, or alternate legs each rep.

t: Stand with a sturdy box or step at roughly a 45° diagonal to your front-right, feet hip-width apart. | Shift your weight onto your left foot, then pivot on your right hip and place your right foot fully on the step, toes pointing along the diagonal. | Let your torso and hips rotate to face the step as the foot lands, keeping your chest up and core braced. | Drive through your right heel to press yourself up onto the step, straightening your right leg at the top. | Bring your left foot up beside your right foot so you are standing tall on the step. | Step your left foot back down to the floor with control, rotating back to your start position, then follow with your right foot. | Complete all reps on one side, then set the step at a 45° diagonal to your front-left and repeat with the left leg leading.

t: Sit upright in a chair or stand with your feet hip-width apart, shoulders relaxed and arms resting at your sides. | Slowly tilt your head to the right, bringing your right ear toward your right shoulder until you feel a gentle pull along the left side of your neck and upper trapezius. | Reach your right hand over the top of your head and rest it lightly on the left side of your head, just above the ear — do not pull; allow the weight of your relaxed hand alone to deepen the stretch gradually. | Actively press your left shoulder downward, away from your ear, to increase the stretch through the upper trapezius and the side of the neck. | Hold this position for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing the muscles to lengthen with each exhale. | Gently lift your head back to center, remove your hand, and pause for a few seconds before switching sides. | Tilt your head to the left, place your left hand lightly on the right side of your head, and hold for another 20–30 seconds. | Return to the starting position and repeat for 2–3 sets per side.

t: Load the trap bar and step inside it, positioning your feet hip-width apart with the bar centered over your mid-foot. | Hinge at the hips and push them back until your torso is roughly 45° to the floor — or closer to parallel for a stricter row — then grip the neutral handles firmly with both hands. | Slightly bend your knees, brace your core, and pull your shoulder blades back and down to set a flat, neutral spine before the first rep. | Take a breath in, brace hard, and drive your elbows straight back and slightly flared — keeping them close to your body — until the handles reach your lower ribcage. | Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement for a brief pause to maximize mid-trap and rhomboid recruitment. | Lower the handles under control along the same path, fully extending your arms and allowing your shoulder blades to protract slightly at the bottom. | Reset your brace at the bottom of each rep without losing the hip-hinge position, then initiate the next pull. | After completing your set, lower the bar to the floor in a controlled manner by pushing your hips back and bending your knees — do not let it drop from a bent-over position.

t: Place a pair of weight plates or a sturdy platform inside the trap bar frame and step onto them, positioning yourself in the center of the bar. | Set your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart with your toes pointed slightly outward, so the handles sit alongside your hips. | Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to lower yourself down and grip the neutral handles firmly, keeping your thumbs wrapped around them. | Before lifting, take a deep breath into your belly, brace your core hard as if you are about to absorb an impact, and lock your lats down toward your back pockets. | Straighten your back, lift your chest slightly, and push the floor away through your feet to initiate the lift — do not jerk the bar off the platform. | Drive your hips forward as the bar clears the height of the platform, extending your knees and hips simultaneously until you are standing tall with the bar at hip level. | Pause briefly at the top with your hips fully extended — do not hyperextend your lower back. | Lower the bar under control by hinging at the hips first, then bending your knees as the bar descends past them, until the plates return to the platform. | Reset your brace and posture fully between reps before initiating the next pull.

t: Stand between the high parallel bars and grip each bar firmly with a neutral grip (palms facing inward), arms fully extended and shoulders directly above your hands. | Lift your feet off the floor and cross your ankles behind you to keep your lower body still throughout the set. | Keep your torso as upright as possible and your elbows tracking straight back — avoid letting them flare out to the sides. | Inhale and lower yourself by bending your elbows, descending until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the bars or until you feel a mild stretch in your triceps. | Pause briefly at the bottom without sinking your shoulders past your wrists. | Press back up through your palms, straightening your elbows fully at the top without locking them out aggressively. | Complete your reps, then step or hop down to dismount safely.

t: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart. | Place your hands on the floor directly behind your hips, fingers pointing forward toward your feet. | Press through your palms and lift your hips slightly off the floor to establish the starting position. | Slowly slide your hips forward and away from your hands, bending your elbows to lower your body toward the floor. | Stop when you feel a firm stretch across your triceps, chest, front shoulders, and lats — your elbows should be bent and pointing behind you. | Keep your chest open and avoid rounding your upper back. | Hold the stretched position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the muscles to relax on each exhale. | Press back through your palms to return your hips to the starting position and release the stretch.

t: Sit on the edge of a sturdy bench and place your palms on the edge beside your hips, fingers pointing forward, hands shoulder-width apart. | Slide your hips forward off the bench so your arms take your bodyweight, keeping your hands fixed on the bench edge. | Walk your feet out and lower your hips so your body angles downward — your head and shoulders should descend below the level of the bench surface. | Keep your arms straight and your elbows unlocked at the starting position, core braced and glutes lightly engaged. | Inhale, then bend your elbows and lower your body in a controlled manner, keeping your elbows tracking close to your sides rather than flaring outward. | Descend until your upper arms are approximately parallel to the floor or until you feel a deep stretch in the triceps, whichever comes first. | Pause briefly at the bottom, then exhale and press through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the starting position. | Squeeze your triceps at the top of each rep without fully locking out the elbows, then immediately begin the next controlled descent.

t: Set a fixed bar (pull-up bar, Smith machine bar, or rack bar) at approximately chest to shoulder height. | Stand facing the bar and grip it with both hands just inside shoulder-width, using an overhand (pronated) grip with your thumbs wrapped fully around the bar. | Step back slightly and lean your body forward so your arms are extended in front of you and your body forms a diagonal line from head to heels — the greater the lean, the harder the exercise. | Brace your core and keep your body in a straight plank-like alignment: head neutral, hips level, and feet flat on the floor. | Slowly bend your elbows, lowering your forehead toward the bar while keeping your upper arms close to your head and your elbows pointing forward. | Continue descending under control until your elbows are at roughly 90° or your forehead nears the bar. | Press through your triceps to fully extend your elbows and return to the starting position. | Maintain full-body tension throughout and avoid letting your hips sag or pike. | Complete all reps, then step forward to release tension before letting go of the bar.

t: Set a barbell in a rack, or find a fixed bar, at roughly hip height — the lower the bar, the more of your bodyweight you will press. | Stand facing the bar and grip it with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended. | Walk your feet back until your body forms a diagonal line from head to heels, with your weight shifted onto your hands; keep your body completely straight and your core braced. | Tuck your elbows in close to your sides — they should travel straight back toward your hips, not flare out to the sides. | Bend your elbows to lower your chest and upper arms toward the bar in a controlled descent, keeping the rest of your body rigid. | Stop when your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, or when your chest is just above the bar — whichever comes first. | Press through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the starting position, squeezing the triceps at full extension. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, then step forward to release the bar.

t: Stand or sit tall with your feet hip-width apart and your spine in a neutral, upright position. | Raise your right arm directly overhead, then bend the elbow so your right hand drops toward the center of your upper back. | Reach your left hand up and grasp your right arm just above the elbow. | Gently pull your right elbow toward your left ear until you feel a mild stretch along the back of your upper arm through the triceps brachii. | Keep your head upright and avoid letting your lower back arch excessively as you apply the pull. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the muscle to relax into the stretch. | Release the arm slowly and lower it back to your side. | Repeat on the opposite side, performing the same number of holds per arm.

t: Stand facing a wall at arm's length. Keep your feet about hip-width apart and your posture tall. | Raise one arm overhead and bend the elbow so your palm and forearm press flat against the wall, with your upper arm close to your ear. | Adjust your position so the bent elbow sits as high on the wall as is comfortable, roughly at or above head height. | Without moving your forearm off the wall, slowly rotate your body away from the wall — turning your chest and torso to the opposite side. | Continue rotating until you feel a firm stretch along the back of your upper arm. Do not force the position past the point of mild tension. | Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily. Avoid holding your breath or shrugging your shoulder. | Rotate back to the starting position, lower your arm, and repeat on the opposite side.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent at roughly 90 degrees and your feet lifted so your shins are parallel to the floor. | Place your hands lightly behind your head with your elbows wide, or cross your arms over your chest — whichever feels more comfortable. | Press your lower back gently toward the mat to establish a neutral spine and engage your core before you begin. | Exhale and simultaneously lift your shoulder blades off the mat and draw your knees toward your chest in a controlled motion. | Hold the contracted position for a brief moment when your torso and knees are closest together. | Inhale and slowly lower your shoulder blades back toward the mat while returning your knees to the starting position, shins parallel to the floor and feet off the ground. | Complete the desired number of reps, then lower your feet to the floor with control.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides. | Dip into a quarter squat — bend your knees to roughly 45° — to pre-load your legs and establish the starting position for each rep. | Drive explosively through your feet to jump as high as you can, fully extending your hips and ankles at takeoff. | At the peak of the jump, pull both knees up toward your chest as high as possible. | Keep your hands at chest or hip height as a target — aim to bring your knees up to meet your hands at the top of each jump. | Release your knees quickly and extend your legs downward to prepare for landing. | Land softly on the balls of your feet with your knees slightly bent to absorb the impact. | Immediately dip back into the quarter-squat position and repeat for the desired number of reps.

t: Place two parallettes on the floor roughly shoulder-width apart, handles parallel, and kneel behind them. | Grip each parallette firmly with a full wrap of the fingers, wrists neutral, and arms straight. Position your hands so your wrists sit directly below your shoulders in the start position. | Lean your torso forward over your hands until your shoulders are ahead of your wrists, distributing your weight through your palms and fingers. | Push actively through the parallettes, protracting your shoulder blades (rounding the upper back) and depressing your shoulders away from your ears. | Keep leaning forward until your feet unweight, then lift your knees off the floor and draw them in toward your chest, shins parallel to the ground or slightly angled upward. | Brace your core and keep pressing down through the parallettes to hold the tuck. Your hips should stay at roughly the same height as your shoulders or slightly lower. | Hold the position with straight arms, active shoulder depression, and a tight tuck — avoid letting the hips sag below the hands. | Lower your feet back to the floor with control to dismount. Do not drop suddenly or release grip tension until your feet are grounded.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and your arms stretched overhead along the floor. | Engage your core by drawing your navel gently toward your spine to protect your lower back. | On an exhale, simultaneously lift your upper body and bend your knees, pulling them toward your chest while reaching your hands forward toward your feet. | Aim to bring your hands close to your shins and lift your shoulder blades fully off the mat at the top of the movement. | Hold the tucked position for a brief pause, keeping tension in your abs throughout. | On an inhale, slowly lower your upper body back to the mat while extending your legs, returning to the starting position with control. | Reset your arms overhead and repeat for the target number of reps.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your arms crossed over your chest or hands lightly behind your head — do not interlace your fingers. | Raise both legs until your thighs are perpendicular to the floor and your knees are bent at roughly 90 degrees, shins parallel to the ground. | Brace your core by drawing your navel gently toward your spine, and press your lower back into the mat. | Exhale and curl your right shoulder blade off the mat, rotating your right elbow toward your left knee while keeping your left shoulder blade in contact with the floor. | Hold the top position for a brief pause, feeling the contraction through your right oblique and across your rectus abdominis. | Inhale as you lower your right shoulder back to the mat under control — do not drop or bounce. | Exhale and repeat on the opposite side, curling your left shoulder toward your right knee. | Continue alternating sides for the target number of reps, keeping your legs stable and your lower back pressed into the mat throughout.

t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward, and arms extended in front of you at chest height or crossed over your chest. | Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and push your hips back as you bend your knees to lower into a squat. | Descend until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your heels flat and your knees tracking over your toes. | At the bottom of the squat, rotate your torso to one side — right shoulder toward your right knee — while keeping your hips level and stable. | Hold the twist for one count, feeling the stretch through your obliques and outer hip. | Rotate your torso back to center, then drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand back up to the starting position. | On the next repetition, twist to the opposite side, alternating sides with each squat.

tHe: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward, and arms extended in front of you at chest height or crossed over your chest. | הדק את הליבה, שמור על חזה גבוה ודחוף את האגן לאחור תוך כיפוף הברכיים לירידה לסקוואט. | Descend until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your heels flat and your knees tracking over your toes. | בתחתית הסקוואט, סובב את הגו לצד אחד — כתף ימין לעבר ברך ימין — תוך שמירה על אגן מאוזן ויציב. | Hold the twist for one count, feeling the stretch through your obliques and outer hip. | Rotate your torso back to center, then drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand back up to the starting position. | On the next repetition, twist to the opposite side, alternating sides with each squat.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides. | Take a controlled step forward with your right foot, landing in a split stance with both feet pointing straight ahead. | Sink your hips toward the floor until your right thigh is roughly parallel to the ground, keeping your left knee hovering just above the floor. | Place your left hand on the floor beside your right foot for balance support. | Rotate your right arm and torso upward and to the right, reaching toward the ceiling and opening your chest. | Hold the end position for 2–3 seconds, breathing steadily and letting your hips sink a little deeper with each exhale. | Return your right arm down and press through your right foot to step back to the starting position. | Repeat on the opposite side by stepping forward with your left foot and rotating to the left. | Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

t: Lie face down on a mat with your arms extended overhead, legs straight, and forehead lightly resting on the mat. | Engage your core and glutes before initiating any movement. | Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the mat by squeezing the erector spinae and glutes. | At the top of the lift, rotate your torso to one side by twisting through the obliques, reaching one arm slightly higher while the opposite leg lifts a little higher. | Hold the rotated position for one to two seconds, feeling tension in the back and obliques. | Return to the neutral superman position — arms and legs lifted but spine centered. | Rotate to the opposite side in a controlled manner, matching the hold duration. | Lower your arms, chest, and legs back to the mat with control to complete one full repetition. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating the twist direction each rep.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your arms extended in front of you at chest height, hands clasped or palms facing each other. | Brace your core, lengthen your spine, and soften your knees slightly to allow free hip rotation. | Initiate the twist by rotating your torso to one side — lead with your shoulders while your core does the work, not your arms. | Continue the turn by pivoting your rear foot and allowing your hips to rotate fully in the same direction as your torso until you are facing roughly 90 degrees from the start. | From the fully turned position, execute the lift phase by driving your clasped hands or extended arms upward overhead in a smooth, controlled arc. | Hold the top position for a brief moment, feeling the obliques and lateral core working to stabilize your rotated, extended posture. | Lower your arms back to chest height with control, then reverse the turn by unwinding your hips and torso back to the starting position. | Perform all reps on one side, then repeat the sequence rotating to the opposite side.

t: Stand tall with your feet together or hip-width apart, arms extended overhead, and your core lightly braced. | Inhale to prepare, then exhale as you hinge forward at the hips, keeping a slight bend in your knees to protect the lower back. | Reach your right hand down toward your left foot while extending your left arm behind you for counterbalance, keeping both arms long. | Touch or come as close as possible to your left toes with your right hand, feeling a stretch through your left hamstring and right erector spinae. | Hold the end position for one to two seconds without bouncing. | Exhale and slowly return to the upright starting position, using your glutes and lower back to drive the ascent. | Immediately hinge forward again and reach your left hand toward your right foot, mirroring the same movement on the opposite side. | Continue alternating sides in a smooth, controlled rhythm for the target number of repetitions or time.

nE: Two handed hang back stretch (with Training Wall Bars)
nR: Вис на двух руках с растяжкой назад (на шведской стенке)
nH: תלייה בשתי ידיים עם מתיחה לאחור (על סולם שוודי)
t: Stand facing the wall bars and grasp a bar at approximately chest to shoulder height with both hands, palms facing away from you (overhand grip). | Step your feet back from the wall bars until your arms are fully extended and your body is angled away from the bars. | Allow your hips to drop back and down, shifting your weight onto your heels so you create a gentle backward lean. | Let your head drop between your arms and relax your neck and shoulders completely. | Round your upper back slightly, allowing the stretch to travel through the thoracic spine and into the lower back. | Breathe slowly and deeply, using each exhale to relax further into the stretch without forcing additional range. | Hold the position for 20 to 60 seconds, maintaining a passive hang rather than actively pulling. | To release, walk your feet forward toward the wall bars, return to an upright position, and release the bar.

Позвольте каждому выдоху помочь вам расслабиться глубже в позиции, а не форсировать глубину. | Hold the position for 20 to 60 seconds, maintaining a passive hang rather than actively pulling. | To release, walk your feet forward toward the wall bars, return to an upright position, and release the bar.
tHe: Stand facing the wall bars and grasp a bar at approximately chest to shoulder height with both hands, palms facing away from you (overhand grip). | Step your feet back from the wall bars until your arms are fully extended and your body is angled away from the bars. | תן לאגן לרדת לאחור ולמטה, תוך העברת המשקל לעקבים ליצירת הטיה עדינה לאחור. | Let your head drop between your arms and relax your neck and shoulders completely. | Round your upper back slightly, allowing the stretch to travel through the thoracic spine and into the lower back. | נשיר לאט ועמוק, משתמש בכל נשימה כדי להרפות עוד יותר אל תוך המתיחה בלי לכפות על טווח נוסף. | Hold the position for 20 to 60 seconds, maintaining a passive hang rather than actively pulling. | To release, walk your feet forward toward the wall bars, return to an upright position, and release the bar.

nE: Two Legged Inverted Staff Pose Dwi Pada Viparita Dandasana
nR: Перевёрнутый посох на двух ногах (Дви Пада Випарита Дандасана)
nH: תנוחת המטה ההפוך על שתי רגליים דווי פאדה ויפריטה דנדאסאנה
t: Begin lying on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Place your palms on the floor beside your ears, fingers pointing toward your shoulders, and lift into a full wheel (Urdhva Dhanurasana). | Lower the crown of your head to the floor and walk your forearms down one at a time so the elbows are bent and the hands interlace behind the head, forming a triangular base of support. | Press through your forearms and the crown of your head to lift your chest and lengthen your spine upward. | Straighten both legs one at a time, extending them fully along the floor with the feet flat or the toes pressed into the mat. | Draw your shoulder blades together and down your back to broaden the chest and deepen the spinal extension. | Breathe steadily, holding the pose for 5–10 slow breaths while maintaining length through the spine rather than compressing the lower back. | To exit, bend your knees and walk your feet back in, then carefully lower your torso to the floor, returning your head last.
tRu: Лягте на спину, согните колени и поставьте стопы ровно на пол на ширине бёдер. | Place your palms on the floor beside your ears, fingers pointing toward your shoulders, and lift into a full wheel (Urdhva Dhanurasana). | Lower the crown of your head to the floor and walk your forearms down one at a time so the elbows are bent and the hands interlace behind the head, forming a triangular base of support. | Press through your forearms and the crown of your head to lift your chest and lengthen your spine upward. | Straighten both legs one at a time, extending them fully along the floor with the feet flat or the toes pressed into the mat. | Сожмите лопатки вместе и вниз по спине, чтобы расширить грудь и усилить разгибание в позвоночнике. | Дышите ровно, удерживая позу 5–10 медленных дыханий, сохраняя длину позвоночника, а не прогибая поясницу. | To exit, bend your knees and walk your feet back in, then carefully lower your torso to the floor, returning your head last.
tHe: התחל בשכיבה על הגב עם ברכיים כפופות וכפות רגליים שטוחות על הרצפה ברוחב האגן. | Place your palms on the floor beside your ears, fingers pointing toward your shoulders, and lift into a full wheel (Urdhva Dhanurasana). | Lower the crown of your head to the floor and walk your forearms down one at a time so the elbows are bent and the hands interlace behind the head, forming a triangular base of support. | Press through your forearms and the crown of your head to lift your chest and lengthen your spine upward. | Straighten both legs one at a time, extending them fully along the floor with the feet flat or the toes pressed into the mat. | Draw your shoulder blades together and down your back to broaden the chest and deepen the spinal extension. | נשום באופן יציב, החזק את התנוחה ל-5–10 נשימות איטיות תוך שמירה על אורך בעמוד השדרה במקום לדחוס את הגב התחתון. | To exit, bend your knees and walk your feet back in, then carefully lower your torso to the floor, returning your head last.

nE: Two Legs Hammer Curl with Towel (VERSION 2)
t: Sit on the floor or on the edge of a firm, flat surface and fold a bath towel lengthwise into a long strip. | Loop the center of the towel around the arches of both feet, then hold one end of the towel in each hand with a neutral grip — palms facing each other as in a hammer curl. | Extend your arms straight and raise both legs off the floor so the towel is taut between your hands and feet before the movement begins. | Sit tall with your spine upright, shoulders pulled back and down, and core braced to prevent your torso from rocking. | Begin the curl by bending both elbows simultaneously, driving your knuckles upward toward your shoulders while keeping your palms facing each other throughout. | Hold your legs steady — your feet and legs are the anchor providing resistance, so any unintended movement of the feet reduces the load. | Continue curling until your hands are at or near shoulder level and you feel a strong contraction in your brachioradialis and upper arms. | Slowly extend your elbows back to the starting position over two to three seconds, maintaining towel tension and keeping your legs elevated. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions without allowing the towel to go slack between reps.

nE: Two Legs Reverse Biceps Curl with Towel (VERSION 2)
nR: Обратные сгибания двумя ногами с полотенцем (вариант 2)
nH: כפיפות הפוכות בשתי רגליים עם מגבת (גרסה 2)
t: Loop a towel around a sturdy overhead anchor point — a door frame, pull-up bar, or structural beam — and let both ends hang down within reach. | Lie on your back on the floor directly beneath the anchor, with your arms extended overhead and your hands gripping one end of the towel each, palms facing down (pronated grip). | Raise both legs off the floor and hold them at a comfortable angle, keeping your core braced so your body forms a rigid plank from shoulders to feet. | Exhale and pull your torso upward by driving your elbows toward your hips, keeping the pronated grip throughout the movement. | Continue curling until your hands reach the sides of your chest or your elbows are fully flexed — whichever your range of motion allows. | Hold the top position for a brief pause, squeezing the elbow flexors. | Inhale and lower yourself back to the starting position under full control until your arms are fully extended. | Repeat for the target number of reps without letting your hips sag or your legs drop.

t: Stand between two vertical ropes hanging parallel and close together. Reach up and grasp one rope in each hand at roughly the same height, slightly above your head. | Pull your shoulder blades down and back to engage your lats before you begin climbing. | Simultaneously pull both ropes downward by driving your elbows toward your hips, lifting your body off the ground. | As your hands reach chest or chin level, re-grip higher up each rope — right hand then left hand (or both together if the ropes are close enough) — before your arms extend fully. | Keep your core braced and your body as vertical and controlled as possible throughout the climb; avoid excessive swinging or kipping. | Continue alternating pulls and re-grips, maintaining tension in your lats and a firm grip, until you reach your target height. | To descend, lower yourself hand-over-hand in a controlled manner, resisting the urge to slide or drop quickly.

t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart on a firm, flat surface with enough clear space in front of and around you. | Bend your knees and hips into a quarter-squat, swinging your arms back to load the jump. | Drive your arms forward and upward as you extend through your hips, knees, and ankles to jump as high as you comfortably can. | While in the air, identify your landing foot and draw the opposite knee up slightly to prepare for a single-leg landing. | Land softly on the ball of your chosen foot first, then let your heel settle as you absorb the impact by bending your knee and hip — aim for a 45–60° knee bend at the bottom. | Keep your landing knee tracking over your second toe and your torso upright; avoid letting the knee cave inward. | Hold the single-leg landing position for one to two seconds to confirm balance and control before resetting. | Return both feet to the ground, reset your stance, and repeat for the desired number of reps, alternating the landing leg each set or each rep.

t: Set a bar in a rack or Smith machine at roughly hip height — lower means more horizontal body angle and greater difficulty. | Lie underneath the bar and grip it with a supinated (underhand, palms-up) grip, hands shoulder-width apart. | Extend your legs and drive your heels into the floor so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your hips level — your body should remain rigid throughout the movement. | Pull your shoulder blades together and down before initiating the pull. | Drive your elbows toward your hips and pull your chest up to the bar, keeping your elbows close to your torso. | Pause briefly at the top when your chest nearly touches the bar and your shoulder blades are fully retracted. | Lower yourself under control back to the starting position with arms fully extended. | Repeat for the desired number of reps without letting your hips sag or your core disengage.

t: Begin in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart, wrists directly under your shoulders, body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your sides as you lower your body toward the floor in a slow, controlled descent — this is chaturanga dandasana. | Lower until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, elbows at a 90-degree angle, and pause briefly without letting your hips sag or rise. | Press through your palms and roll over your toes to shift into upward-facing dog: straighten your arms, lift your chest, draw your shoulders back and down, and let only your hands and the tops of your feet contact the floor. | Hold the upward-facing dog position for one breath, keeping your thighs lifted off the floor and your neck long. | Exhale, tuck your toes, and press your hips up and back to transition into downward-facing dog, forming an inverted V-shape. | In downward-facing dog, straighten your arms, press your heels toward the floor, and lengthen your spine away from your hands. | Hold for one to three breaths before stepping or jumping your feet toward your hands to return to the top of the sequence or to a standing position.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and arms stretched overhead, holding the stability ball in both hands. | Press your lower back gently into the mat and engage your core before beginning the movement. | Exhale and simultaneously lift your arms (with the ball) and both legs off the floor, curling your torso and hips upward to form a V shape. | At the top of the movement, transfer the stability ball from your hands to your feet by squeezing it between your ankles. | Slowly lower both your arms and legs back toward the floor in a controlled descent, keeping the ball gripped between your feet. | Without allowing your legs or upper back to touch the floor completely, reverse the motion: raise both arms and legs again to form the V shape. | At the top, transfer the ball back from your feet to your hands. | Lower back down with control to complete one full repetition. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, maintaining a tight core and steady breathing throughout.

t: Step onto the treadmill and stand with feet on the side rails before starting the belt. | Set the speed to a comfortable walking pace — typically 2.5–4.0 mph — and step onto the moving belt. | Stand tall with your head up, eyes forward, and shoulders relaxed and slightly back. | Swing your arms naturally at your sides, bending them at roughly 90 degrees and alternating in sync with your opposite leg. | Strike the ground with your heel first, rolling through the midfoot and pushing off with your toes on each step. | Keep your core gently braced and your hips level throughout the stride — avoid excessive side-to-side swaying. | Breathe steadily and rhythmically; you should be able to hold a conversation without gasping. | If using an incline, increase the grade gradually (1–3%) to simulate outdoor terrain and increase intensity without raising speed. | When your session is complete, reduce the speed gradually, step to the side rails, and let the belt stop before stepping off.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, shoulders relaxed, and arms hanging at your sides. | Shift your weight onto your left foot and drive your right knee upward until your thigh is at least parallel to the floor. | At the same time, swing your left arm forward and your right arm back in a natural walking rhythm. | Lower your right foot back to the floor with control, landing softly through the ball of your foot. | Immediately shift your weight and drive your left knee up to the same height while swinging your right arm forward. | Continue alternating knees in a deliberate walking pace, maintaining an upright torso throughout. | Keep your gaze forward and your core lightly braced on every step to prevent your trunk from leaning backward. | Continue for the prescribed duration or distance, maintaining consistent knee height on each repetition.

t: Set the treadmill to its lowest speed (0.5–1.0 mph) before stepping on the belt. | Stand facing the rear of the treadmill and lightly grip both side rails for balance. | Step onto the moving belt and let it guide your feet into a smooth backward walking rhythm. | Once you feel stable, gradually increase the speed to a comfortable pace — typically 1.5–2.5 mph for most users. | Keep your torso upright and your core lightly braced; avoid leaning forward or hunching over the console. | Look straight ahead or slightly downward toward the belt — do not crane your neck to look behind you. | Take short, controlled steps, landing on the ball of your foot and rolling back through the toes to push off. | Maintain your grip on the rails whenever you feel unsteady, and release them gradually as your balance improves. | To finish, slow the belt back to its lowest speed, grip the rails firmly, and step off the sides of the treadmill — never jump off a moving belt.

t: Step onto the elliptical machine and grip the moving handlebars lightly with both hands, ensuring your feet are fully centered on the foot pedals. | Set the machine to your target resistance and incline level for VERSION 7 — a moderate resistance that challenges the legs without forcing you to lean heavily on the handles. | Begin pedaling forward in a smooth, fluid oval motion, allowing the machine to guide your stride rather than forcing a shortened or exaggerated range of motion. | Drive the handlebars with your arms in opposition to your legs — push forward with the right arm as the left leg drives forward — to engage the upper body and distribute the workload. | Maintain an upright posture with your chest lifted, shoulders relaxed away from your ears, and a slight engagement of your core throughout the session. | Keep your heels pressed into the foot pedals throughout the stride to maximize glute and hamstring activation and reduce excess pressure on the knees. | Monitor your pace and breathing, aiming for a conversational intensity — you should be able to speak in short sentences but feel your heart rate elevated. | Cool down during the final 3–5 minutes by gradually reducing speed and resistance before stepping off the machine. | Carefully step off the pedals only after the machine has come to a complete stop, holding the stationary handlebars for balance.

t: Step onto the side rails of the treadmill and set your desired speed — 2.5 to 4.0 mph is a typical walking range for most people. | Start the belt and step onto it, placing your feet hip-width apart and letting the belt carry your foot back naturally. | Stand tall with your head up, shoulders relaxed and slightly back, and your gaze forward rather than down at your feet. | Swing your arms in opposition to your legs — left arm forward as right foot strikes, right arm forward as left foot strikes — bending your elbows to roughly 90°. | Strike the belt with your heel first, then roll through the midfoot and push off with your toes as the foot leaves the belt. | Keep your core lightly braced and your hips level throughout each stride — avoid excessive side-to-side sway. | Breathe steadily through your nose and mouth; you should be able to speak in short sentences at a comfortable walking pace. | When you finish, straddle the belt on the side rails, reduce speed to zero, then step off — do not jump off a moving belt.

nE: Wall Assisted Handstand to Tuck Planche Negative
nR: Стойка у стены в планш в группировке (негатив)
nH: עמידת ידיים בסיוע קיר לירידה לפלאנש בקיפול
t: Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor about 30–45 cm from a wall, fingers spread wide and pointing forward. | Kick up into a handstand with your heels lightly resting against the wall, arms fully locked out and body vertical. | Squeeze your glutes, brace your core hard, and protract (push away) your shoulder blades to establish full body tension. | Tuck both knees toward your chest simultaneously, shifting your center of mass forward and away from the wall. | Begin leaning forward through your shoulders, letting your hips drop slowly by increasing the forward tilt of your torso. | Maintain straight, locked arms throughout — resist the descent using shoulder flexion strength and core tension, not by bending your elbows. | Lower your body as slowly as possible, aiming to hold the tucked horizontal position (tuck planche) for a beat before continuing. | Either hold the lowest position you can control for 1–3 seconds, or continue descending until your knees or feet touch the floor in a controlled manner. | Rest fully before the next repetition — this is a high-neurological-demand movement; 2–3 minutes between sets is appropriate.

t: Stand facing a wall with your feet shoulder-width apart and a target mark on the wall roughly 10 feet (3 m) high; hold a medicine ball at chest height with both hands. | Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and push your hips back to begin the squat descent. | Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping your knees tracking over your toes and the ball at chest level. | Drive explosively through your heels to stand, extending your hips and knees simultaneously. | As you reach full hip extension, use the momentum to press and throw the medicine ball upward toward the target on the wall. | Watch the ball as it hits the target and rebounds off the wall. | Catch the ball with both hands at chest height, absorbing the impact by softening your elbows. | Immediately use the catch momentum to flow into the next squat descent without pausing. | Repeat for the prescribed number of reps or time, maintaining a smooth, rhythmic squat-throw-catch cycle throughout.

nE: Wall Facing Single Leg Split Handstand Hold
nR: Стойка лицом к стене на одной ноге в шпагате
nH: החזקת עמידת ידיים מפושקת ברגל אחת מול קיר

t: Stand facing a wall at arm's length and place both palms flat against it at roughly shoulder height and shoulder width apart. | Shift your weight onto your right foot, keeping a soft bend in the right knee. | Brace your core and keep your hips level — avoid tilting or rotating the pelvis. | Slowly extend your left leg straight back behind you, leading with the heel, until you feel a strong contraction in the left glute. | Pause briefly at the top of the range, then lower the foot under control until the heel lightly taps the floor. | Complete all reps on the left side, then switch to the right leg. | Throughout the set, keep your chest up and avoid arching the lower back to force extra range.

t: Stand facing a smooth wall, about one foot away, feet hip-width apart and core braced. | Place both palms flat on the wall at chest height, slightly narrower than shoulder-width, fingers pointing upward. | Lean your body weight gently into your hands so there is moderate pressure against the wall. | Bend your elbows slightly — about 20 to 30 degrees — so the triceps are already under light tension. | Without moving your shoulders or body, press your palms firmly into the wall to straighten your elbows, contracting the triceps brachii at the end of the movement. | Immediately release just enough to return to the slightly bent starting position — this short, controlled return is the 'pulse.' | Repeat the press-and-release in a steady, rhythmic tempo, keeping the range of motion small and intentional throughout each rep. | Keep your back flat, hips neutral, and avoid shrugging your shoulders toward your ears. | Complete the target reps, then step back from the wall and relax your arms.

t: Place a weight plate or low step against the wall and stand with your back flat against the wall, heels on the elevated surface and toes pointing slightly outward. | Walk your feet forward until your shins are roughly vertical or your knees are just slightly in front of your ankles. | Slide your back down the wall until your thighs are parallel to the floor (or as close as your mobility allows), forming a 90° angle at the hips and knees. | Press your entire back — lower back included — firmly into the wall and keep your head neutral. | Distribute your weight evenly through the full foot, letting the heel elevation naturally shift load toward the quads and glutes. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes lightly, and hold the position for the target duration while breathing steadily. | To finish, press through your heels and walk your feet back toward the wall to stand upright.

t: Stand with your back flat against a smooth wall, feet together or no more than a few inches apart and roughly 12–18 inches out from the wall. | Slide your back down the wall until your hips and knees are at approximately a 90-degree angle and your thighs are parallel to the floor. | Check that your knees are directly over your ankles, not caving inward or drifting past your toes. | Press your entire back, from your lower back to your upper back, firmly into the wall throughout the hold. | Keep your arms either extended in front of you or resting lightly on your thighs — do not use them to push off your knees. | Hold the position for the target duration, breathing steadily and keeping your core braced. | To finish, push through your heels and slide back up the wall to a standing position.

t: Start in a push-up position with your heels against the base of a wall, arms fully extended, hands shoulder-width apart, and core braced. | Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs so your body forms a rigid plank — this position is your base for the entire movement. | Begin walking your feet up the wall one step at a time, simultaneously walking your hands backward toward the wall to keep your body aligned. | Continue the coordinated hand-and-foot walk until your chest is as close to the wall as your current strength and mobility allow, ideally within a fist's distance. | Hold the near-vertical position for a breath, pressing firmly through your hands and maintaining full-body tension. | Reverse the movement by stepping your feet down the wall and walking your hands away from the wall at the same pace. | Continue until you return to the starting push-up position with your heels back at the wall's base. | Rest briefly, then repeat for the target number of reps.

t: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides, and core lightly braced. | Step your right foot forward into a forward lunge, lowering your back knee toward the floor until both legs reach roughly 90 degrees; hold for one breath, then return to standing. | Step forward again into a lunge and add a torso rotation toward the lead knee, extending both arms to the side to open the thoracic spine; return to standing. | Lunge forward a third time and reach both arms overhead and slightly back to open the hip flexors and extend the lumbar spine; hold for one breath, then return to standing. | Step your right foot out wide to the side into a lateral lunge, pushing the hips back and keeping the opposite leg straight to stretch the inner thigh and groin; return to standing. | Step your right foot behind you into a reverse lunge, lowering the back knee toward the floor to stretch the front of the hip; hold for one breath, then push through the front heel to stand. | Repeat the entire five-move sequence on the left leg, matching the same order of movements. | Complete 2–3 full rounds per side, moving at a controlled, rhythmic pace throughout.

t: Step your right foot forward into a deep lunge, lowering your left knee toward the floor and keeping your right shin vertical. | Place both hands flat on the floor on either side of your right foot to establish your base position. | Rotate your right arm up toward the ceiling, opening your chest and turning through your upper back — hold briefly, then return your hand to the floor. | Bring your right elbow down toward the inside of your right foot, deepening the hip flexor and inner-thigh stretch — hold briefly. | Press your right hand into the floor and reach your left arm straight overhead, creating a lateral lean through your waist — hold briefly. | Place both hands back on the floor, then shift your hips back to straighten your right leg and stretch the right hamstring — hold briefly. | Return to the deep lunge position and raise both arms overhead, reaching up to open the shoulders and extend the thoracic spine — hold briefly. | Lower your arms and rotate your torso to the right, extending your right arm behind you at shoulder height to stretch the back and waist — hold briefly. | Return to the starting position, then switch legs and repeat the full seven-position sequence on the left side. | Complete the desired number of rounds on each side before moving into your main training session.

t: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands relaxed at your sides. | Step your right foot forward into a lunge, lowering your left knee toward the floor until both knees are bent at roughly 90°. Keep your torso upright. This is your base position for all six moves. | Position 1 — Hip sink: Press your hips gently downward to open the front of the left hip. Hold 2–3 seconds. | Position 2 — Thoracic rotation: Place both hands on your right thigh and rotate your torso to the right, reaching your right arm overhead toward the ceiling. Hold 2–3 seconds. | Position 3 — Side reach: Return to center and extend your left arm up and over to the right, stretching the left side of your waist. Hold 2–3 seconds. | Position 4 — Elbow drop: Lower your right elbow to the floor inside your right foot, opening the hip further. Hold 2–3 seconds. | Position 5 — Hamstring shift: Straighten your right leg and hinge your hips back with a flat back to stretch the back of the right thigh. Hold 2–3 seconds. | Position 6 — Rotation return: Rebend the right knee, rotate your torso back to center, and push through your right foot to return to standing. | Repeat the full six-position flow on the left side, stepping the left foot forward.

nE: Weighted Standing Neck Extension (with head harness)
nR: Разгибания шеи стоя с весом (с упряжью)
nH: פשיטות צוואר בעמידה עם משקל (עם רתמת ראש)

Brace your core lightly to stabilize your spine. | Let your head drop forward slowly into full cervical flexion, chin moving toward your chest, until the weight hangs freely in front of you. | Keep your shoulders relaxed and down — do not shrug or assist the movement with your upper body. | Exhale and extend your neck deliberately, raising your head from flexion through neutral and then very slightly past neutral so the cervical extensors reach full contraction. | Pause for a count at the top with the muscles fully contracted. | Inhale and return your head forward under full control, resisting the pull of the weight all the way back to the fully flexed starting position. | Complete your reps, then unload the weight from the harness before removing the harness from your head.

t: Stand with your feet roughly shoulder-width apart and your core braced. t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and core braced. Hold a weight plate, dumbbell, or medicine ball at chest height with both hands and arms slightly extended. | Engage your core and set your shoulders back and down. nH: הילה עם מייס פלדה עם משקל
t: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, core braced and glutes lightly engaged. | Hold the steel mace (or weight) at chest height with both hands gripping the handle close together, mace head pointing upward. | Tilt the mace to one side and begin guiding it backward and upward, initiating the circular path around your head. | Keep your head still and chin slightly tucked as the mace passes behind your head — do not duck or crane the neck. | Continue the arc smoothly so the mace travels around the back of the skull, staying as close to the head as control allows. | Guide the mace forward and back to the starting position in front of your chest to complete one full circle. | Perform the prescribed number of reps in one direction, then reverse the direction for the same count. | Maintain an upright torso throughout — avoid leaning or rotating the trunk to compensate for the weight.

nH: סקוואט עם מייס פלדה עם משקל
t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly, and the steel mace held vertically in front of your body at chest height with both hands gripping the handle. | Brace your core, pull your shoulder blades back and down, and keep your chest tall throughout the movement. | Inhale and initiate the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees simultaneously, keeping the mace close to your body. | Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, or as low as your mobility comfortably allows, while maintaining an upright torso. | Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and prevent them from caving inward as you lower. | Pause briefly at the bottom of the squat with your weight distributed evenly through both feet. | Exhale and drive through your heels to press the floor away, extending your hips and knees simultaneously to return to the starting position. | Fully extend at the top without hyperextending your lower back, then reset your brace before the next repetition. | Complete the desired number of repetitions, then carefully lower the mace before setting it down.

nE: Weighted Straight Leg Toe Touch Crunch
nR: Скручивания с касанием носков прямых ног с весом
nH: כפיפות עם נגיעות אצבעות ברגליים ישרות עם משקל
t: Lie flat on your back on the floor or a mat with your legs extended straight up toward the ceiling, perpendicular to your torso. | Hold a weight plate or dumbbell with both hands, arms extended overhead or resting on your chest — for maximum load, keep the weight extended directly above your chest as you prepare to crunch. | Press your lower back firmly into the floor and brace your core before initiating any movement. | Exhale and contract your abdominals, curling your upper back off the floor and reaching the weight upward toward your toes. | Drive the crunch from your abs — avoid pulling with your neck or jerking the weight to create momentum. | At the top, aim to bring the weight as close to your feet as your flexibility allows while keeping your legs fully straight and your lower back on the floor. | Pause briefly at the peak contraction, then slowly lower your upper back back to the floor under control. | Inhale as you descend and return to the starting position with your arms extended and upper back just touching the mat. | Repeat for the desired number of reps without losing tension in the abdominals between repetitions.

t: Lie flat on a bench and select a light weight plate (5–10 lb to start). Hold it between both palms with your fingers pointing away, arms extended toward the ceiling directly over your chest. | Squeeze your palms forcefully into the plate before the set begins and commit to maintaining that inward pressure for every rep — the constant squeeze is the defining technique of this exercise. | Retract and depress your shoulder blades against the bench, plant your feet firmly on the floor, and take a full breath to brace your core. | Lower the plate in a controlled arc toward the middle of your chest, keeping your elbows slightly soft and the squeeze unbroken the entire way down. | Stop when the plate is just above your chest — do not let the squeeze relax or rest the plate on your sternum. | Press upward and very slightly inward, driving through your chest while continuing to squeeze the plate together, until your arms return to full extension above your chest. | Pause briefly at the top to feel peak contraction in the sternal pec, then begin the next controlled descent. | After completing all reps, lower the plate to your chest and sit up carefully before releasing the squeeze.

nR: Скручивания со скруткой с весом (на скамье)
t: Sit on the end of a flat bench and secure your feet — hook them under a foot pad if the bench has one, or have a partner hold them down — with your knees bent at roughly 90°. | Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest or behind your head, keeping your arms in that position throughout the set. | Lean back until your torso is at approximately 45° to the bench — this is your starting position. | Brace your core and begin curling your ribcage toward your hips, initiating the movement with your abs rather than pulling with your neck or shoulders. | As you reach the midpoint of the crunch, rotate your right shoulder toward your left knee, adding the twist on top of the flexion. | Hold the top position for one count, feeling the contraction in your obliques and rectus abdominis. | Slowly lower back to the starting 45° position in a controlled manner — do not let the weight pull you all the way down to the bench. | On the next rep, rotate your left shoulder toward your right knee, and continue alternating sides for the desired number of reps.

t: Place the bosu ball dome-side up on the floor and sit on the dome, centering your hips on its highest point. | Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest with both hands. | Lean your torso back to roughly 45 degrees while extending your legs straight out in front of you, keeping your feet just off the floor — this is your starting position. | Brace your core firmly to stabilize your balance on the dome before beginning each rep. | Simultaneously draw your knees toward your chest while lifting your torso forward to meet them, compressing your midsection into a tight V shape at the top. | Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your rectus abdominis and hip flexors. | Slowly lower your torso and legs back to the starting position under control, resisting the descent rather than letting gravity drop them. | Keep your feet from touching the floor between reps to maintain continuous tension through the rectus abdominis and iliopsoas. | Repeat for the target number of reps, maintaining a stable, centered position on the dome throughout.

t: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, positioned close to your glutes. | Place your hands on the floor beside your ears, fingers pointing toward your shoulders, elbows bent and pointing toward the ceiling. | Press your feet firmly into the floor and engage your legs to stabilize your lower body. | On an exhale, press through your hands and feet simultaneously to lift your hips and chest off the floor. | Straighten your arms as much as possible and let the crown of your head lift away from the floor as your chest opens upward. | Draw your shoulder blades toward each other to open the chest further and keep your knees tracking over your feet, not splaying outward. | Hold the position for 3–5 breaths, maintaining steady inhalations and exhalations. | To exit, tuck your chin toward your chest and slowly lower your spine back down to the floor one vertebra at a time.

t: Kneel on a mat and grip the ab wheel handles with both hands, positioning the wheel directly beneath your shoulders. | Brace your core firmly, draw your ribs down, and tuck your pelvis slightly to create a neutral spine before you begin. | Squeeze your glutes to lock your hips in place and prevent your lower back from arching during the roll. | Inhale and slowly roll the wheel forward, extending your hips and arms simultaneously in a controlled arc toward the floor. | Keep your elbows locked straight as you descend — do not bend them or shift the work to your arms. | Roll out as far as you can while maintaining a neutral spine; stop the moment you feel your lower back begin to arch. | Hold the extended position for one count, maintaining full-body tension from your hands through your knees. | Exhale and drive your lats and abs to pull the wheel back toward your knees, leading with your hips rather than pushing with your arms. | Return to the starting position with your hips stacked over your knees and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
