t: Stand with your feet set wider than shoulder-width apart and toes turned out 30–45 degrees. | Stand tall with your chest up, shoulders back, and arms extended in front of you at chest height for balance. | Brace your core and begin to lower yourself by pushing your knees out in line with your toes while sending your hips back and down. | Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping your chest upright and your heels flat on the ground. | Pause briefly at the bottom without collapsing your knees inward or rounding your lower back. | Drive through your entire foot to press the floor away, extending your hips and knees simultaneously as you rise. | Stand fully upright at the top, squeezing your glutes, before beginning the next rep.

t: Stand beside or over a bench and position your feet significantly wider than shoulder-width, with toes angled out 30–45°. | Stand tall with your chest up and arms extended forward or relaxed at your sides for balance. | Brace your core, take a breath in, and keep your spine in a neutral position. | Begin the descent by pushing your knees outward in line with your toes and sending your hips back and down. | Lower yourself in a controlled manner until your hips lightly touch the edge of the bench, keeping your chest up and torso as upright as possible. | Pause briefly at the bottom without collapsing your knees inward or relaxing your core. | Press through your full foot to drive back up to standing, extending the hips fully at the top. | Exhale as you return to the starting position, reset your brace, and begin the next rep.

t: Grip a pull-up bar with an underhand (supinated) grip, hands set wider than shoulder-width — typically 1.5 to 2 times shoulder width. | Hang at full arm extension with your shoulders relaxed and your body straight, crossing your ankles behind you if needed to keep your legs clear of the floor. | Depress and retract your shoulder blades slightly before you begin the pull — this pre-activates the lats and protects the shoulder joint. | Exhale and pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down and back, keeping them flared slightly outward rather than tucking them in. | Continue pulling until your chin clears the bar and your chest approaches it, squeezing the lats and upper back at the top. | Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower yourself back to a full hang over 2–3 seconds, resisting the descent rather than dropping. | Allow your arms to reach full extension at the bottom and your shoulders to rise slightly before initiating the next rep. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, maintaining control throughout without swinging or kipping.

nE: Wide Grip Pull-Up on Dip Cage
nH: מתח באחיזה רחבה על מתקן מקבילים
t: Stand beneath the dip cage's pull-up bar and reach up to grip it with both hands, palms facing away from you, placed 4–6 inches wider than shoulder-width on each side. | Hang at full arm extension with your feet off the floor, allowing your shoulder blades to rise slightly into a dead hang. | Depress and retract your shoulder blades — pull them down and together — before initiating the pull. | Drive your elbows down and out to the sides, keeping them flared rather than tucking them in. | Pull your chest toward the bar, aiming to bring your chin above bar level at the top of the movement. | Squeeze your lats and upper back briefly at the top, holding the contracted position for one count. | Lower yourself in a controlled manner — taking 2–3 seconds on the descent — back to a full dead hang. | Reset your shoulder blades at the bottom before beginning the next repetition.

t: Grip a pull-up bar with both hands roughly 1.5 to 2 times shoulder-width apart, palms facing away from you (pronated grip). | Hang at full arm extension with your shoulders relaxed and your core lightly braced — this is the dead hang starting position. | Before you pull, tilt your head forward slightly and tuck your chin toward your chest so the bar has a clear path behind your head. | Initiate the pull by depressing and retracting your shoulder blades, then drive your elbows down and back toward your hips. | Continue pulling until the bar contacts the upper trapezius, just above the base of the neck — do not force the bar down to mid-neck level. | Pause briefly at the top with your elbows pointing down and slightly back, feeling the lats fully contracted. | Lower yourself under control over 2–3 seconds back to the full dead hang, letting your shoulder blades rise and upwardly rotate at the bottom. | Reset your head position on each rep and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

nE: Wide legged Forward Bend Prasarita Padottanasana

t: Stand at the center of your mat and step your feet 3–5 feet apart, with the outer edges of your feet parallel to the short edges of the mat and toes pointing forward or very slightly inward. | Place your hands on your hips, inhale to lengthen through the crown of your head, and feel the spine grow long. | On an exhale, hinge forward from the hips — not the waist — keeping your back flat and your torso long as you lower toward the floor. | Place your fingertips or palms on the floor directly beneath your shoulders, arms straight, and continue to lengthen the spine rather than rounding it. | On each subsequent exhale, allow the torso to descend further. If your flexibility allows, walk your hands back between your feet and let the crown of your head reach toward the floor. | Press the outer edges of both feet firmly into the floor, gently draw the inner thighs upward, and soften your knees slightly rather than locking them out. | Breathe slowly and hold the pose for 5–10 full breaths, using each exhale to release a little more tension through the hips and hamstrings. | To exit, place your hands back on your hips, engage your core, and rise slowly with a flat back on an inhale. Step your feet together and return to standing.

t: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your feet set wider than hip-width apart. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and create a straight line from head to heels — no sagging hips or raised backside. | Keeping your hips level and your torso from rotating, lift your right foot and tap it out to the right, roughly 12–18 inches wider. | Return your right foot to the starting position with control. | Repeat on the left side — tap left foot out to the left, then return. | Continue alternating sides for the target number of reps or time, maintaining a rigid, non-rotating plank throughout. | To finish, lower your knees to the floor in a controlled manner.

t: Stand facing a wall at arm's length and place both hands flat on the wall at chest height, wider than shoulder-width apart — roughly 1.5 times shoulder width. | Step your feet back slightly so your body forms a straight diagonal line from head to heels, with your weight resting on the balls of your feet. | Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips stay level and your body does not sag or pike. | Inhale and slowly bend your elbows, lowering your chest toward the wall at a controlled pace — aim for a 2-second descent. | Keep your elbows at roughly a 45–60° angle to your torso rather than flaring them straight out to the sides. | Lower until your nose or chest nearly touches the wall, maintaining that straight body line throughout. | Exhale and press both hands firmly into the wall, extending your elbows to push yourself back to the starting position. | Pause briefly at the top with arms fully extended but elbows not locked out, then begin the next rep.

t: Sit at the assisted pull-up or seated pull-up machine and adjust the knee pad or seat so your legs are secured and your arms can fully extend overhead when gripping the bar. | Reach up and grip the wide bar with an overhand (pronated) grip, placing your hands well outside shoulder-width — roughly 1.5 times shoulder-width is a useful starting point. | Sit tall, brace your core lightly, and let your arms fully extend so you feel a gentle stretch across your lats before you begin. | Inhale, then initiate the pull by depressing and retracting your shoulder blades — think 'pull your shoulder blades down and into your back pockets.' | Drive your elbows down and out to your sides, pulling the bar (or yourself) down until the bar reaches chin or upper-chest level. | Squeeze your lats and upper back at the bottom of the movement for a brief moment. | Exhale and slowly extend your arms, returning to the full overhead position with control — do not let the weight stack drop or your shoulders shrug up. | Complete all reps, then release the weight stack gently.

nE: Wide Stance Jump Squat to Narrow Stance Jump Squat
nH: סקוואט בקפיצה מעמידה רחבה לעמידה צרה
t: Stand with your feet set wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out slightly, and your arms hanging at your sides. | Push your hips back and lower into a squat until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up and your knees tracking over your toes. | Drive through your feet explosively to jump straight up off the floor, extending your hips and knees fully at the top. | While in the air, bring your feet together so that you land with them hip-width apart or narrower — this is the narrow stance. | Absorb the landing by bending your knees and sitting your hips back immediately into a narrow-stance squat, keeping your heels flat and your chest upright. | Without pausing at the bottom, drive through your feet again and jump straight up, spreading your feet apart in the air so you land back in the wide stance. | Absorb this landing the same way — soft knees, hips back — and use the stretch-shortening response to flow directly into the next jump. | Continue alternating between wide and narrow landings in a controlled, rhythmic pattern for the desired duration or number of reps.

t: Place your hands wider than shoulder-width on the floor, fingers pointing forward, with your body in a straight line from head to heels — this is your starting position. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and ensure your hips are level before beginning the movement. | Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows outward at roughly a 45° angle to your torso, keeping your body rigid throughout the descent. | Press back up to the top of the wide push-up position, fully extending your arms without locking the elbows. | Walk or hop both hands inward so they are roughly shoulder-width apart or closer, directly under your shoulders. | Lower your chest again toward the floor with your elbows tracking closer to your sides in the narrow position. | Press back up to the top of the narrow push-up position to complete one full rep cycle. | Walk or hop your hands back out to the wide position and repeat the sequence for the desired number of reps.

t: Find a flat, open surface — a track, field, or clear stretch of pavement — at least 20–40 meters long. | Stand at your starting line with a staggered stance, one foot slightly in front of the other, leaning forward from the ankles. | Drive powerfully off your rear foot and accelerate to maximum speed as quickly as possible, pumping your arms in sync with your legs. | Run at full effort for the designated distance (typically 20–100 meters), maintaining an upright but slightly forward-leaning torso. | Decelerate gradually after crossing the finish line — never come to an abrupt stop. | Walk or lightly jog back to the start line as your recovery interval, then repeat for the target number of sprints.

t: Lie flat on your back with your arms extended out to the sides, palms pressed down for support. | Brace your core and lift both legs off the floor, raising them until they are perpendicular to the ground (straight up toward the ceiling). | Keep both legs fully straight and pressed together throughout the movement. | Slowly lower your legs to one side in a controlled arc, stopping a few inches above the floor or at the limit of your controlled range. | Pause briefly, then use your obliques to sweep the legs back up through vertical. | Continue the arc to the opposite side, lowering with the same controlled tempo. | Pause again, then sweep back to vertical to complete one full repetition. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, maintaining a slow, deliberate pace throughout.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides. | Step your right foot forward into a long lunge, lowering your left knee toward the floor and keeping your torso upright. | Place both hands flat on the floor just inside your right foot for support. | Reach your left arm up toward the ceiling, rotating your upper body and opening your chest to the left — follow your hand with your eyes. | Hold the rotated position for 1–2 seconds, then return your left hand to the floor. | Drive your right hip back and straighten your right leg, shifting your weight backward into a hamstring stretch with your right foot flat on the floor. | Pause for 1–2 seconds in the hamstring stretch, then return your hips forward to the lunge position. | Step your right foot back to the starting position and repeat the entire sequence leading with your left foot. | Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions, moving slowly and with control through each position.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides. | Step your right foot forward into a deep lunge, lowering your left knee toward the floor or hovering it just above the ground. | Place both hands on the floor inside your right foot, shoulder-width apart, and settle your hips toward the ground to feel the stretch through your hip flexor and groin. | Lift your right hand off the floor and rotate your torso to the right, reaching your arm toward the ceiling while keeping your hips square and your gaze following your hand. | Hold the rotated position for one to two seconds, then return your hand to the floor. | Press through your right heel and straighten your right leg as much as your hamstring allows, shifting your hips back slightly to deepen the hamstring stretch. | Return to the lunge position and lower both hands back to the floor. | Push back to standing and repeat the full sequence on the opposite side.

t: Stand or sit tall with your spine neutral and shoulders relaxed. | Extend one arm straight in front of you at shoulder height, palm facing down. | Use your free hand to gently grasp the fingers of the extended hand from above. | Curl the fingers and wrist of the extended arm downward, pointing your fingertips toward the floor. | Apply light steady pressure with your free hand to deepen the bend until you feel a mild stretch along the top of the forearm. | Keep the elbow of the extended arm straight but not locked throughout the stretch. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly and steadily. | Gradually release the pressure, straighten the wrist, and return to the starting position. | Repeat on the opposite arm, performing 2–3 rounds per side.

t: Sit or stand with a tall spine, arms extended in front of you at approximately shoulder height, palms facing down. | Relax your fingers and allow your wrists to drop into full flexion so the backs of your hands face upward — this is your starting position. | Slowly extend your wrists back to a neutral position, keeping your forearms still and moving only at the wrist joint. | Continue past neutral into gentle wrist extension, feeling a mild stretch across the forearm flexors. | Reverse the direction and lower your wrists back through neutral and into full flexion again, moving with deliberate control. | Repeat this flexion-to-extension arc in a smooth, continuous rhythm for the target number of repetitions or time. | Keep the movement isolated to the wrist joint — your elbows and shoulders should remain relaxed and stationary throughout. | At the end of the set, hold the bottom of the flexion range for 2–3 seconds to deepen the stretch before releasing.

t: Stand or sit upright and extend one arm straight in front of you at roughly shoulder height, elbow fully locked out. | Rotate your forearm so your palm faces upward (supinated position). | Relax your wrist and let gravity begin to extend it so your fingers drop toward the floor. | With your free hand, gently grasp the back of the fingers on the stretching arm. | Apply light downward pressure with your free hand to deepen the wrist extension. | While maintaining that extension, guide the hand slightly toward the little-finger side — this is the ulnar deviation that stretches the radial deviators. | Hold the end position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the forearm muscles to relax into the stretch. | Release the overpressure gradually, return your wrist to neutral, and repeat on the opposite arm.

nE: Wrist Ulnar Deviator And Extensor Stretch
nH: מתיחת פושטים ומקרבים גומדיים של שורש כף היד
t: Stand or sit upright with your working arm extended in front of you at roughly chest height, elbow straight but not locked. | Turn your palm to face downward so the back of your hand faces the ceiling. | With your free hand, gently grasp the back of the fingers of your extended hand. | Slowly bend your wrist downward — curling the fingers toward the floor — until you feel a mild stretch along the top and outer side of your forearm. | At the same time, guide the hand slightly toward the thumb side (radial deviation) to increase the tension on the ulnar deviators along the outer forearm. | Hold the stretched position for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the forearm muscles to relax into the stretch. | Release the hand slowly and return the wrist to a neutral position. | Switch arms and repeat the same sequence on the other side.

nE: Wrist Ulnar Deviator And Flexor Stretch
nH: מתיחת מכופפים ומקרבים גומדיים של שורש כף היד
t: Stand or sit upright and extend one arm straight in front of you at roughly shoulder height, elbow fully extended. | For the extensor stretch: rotate your palm to face down and use your opposite hand to press the back of your fingers gently toward the floor, flexing your wrist until you feel a stretch across the top of your forearm. | While holding that flexed position, draw your hand slightly toward your thumb side (radial deviation) to increase the stretch along the ulnar side of your forearm where the ulnar deviator muscles run. | Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily, then release the pressure and return your wrist to neutral. | For the flexor stretch: rotate your palm to face up and use your opposite hand to press your fingers gently back toward your body, extending your wrist until you feel a stretch along the underside of your forearm. | Hold for 20–30 seconds, then release and return your wrist to neutral. | Lower your arm, shake it out gently, and repeat the full sequence on the opposite arm. | Complete 2–3 rounds per arm, working within a comfortable range of motion throughout.

t: Stand on the center of a resistance band with both feet hip-width apart. | Cross the band in front of you to form an X, then hold one end in each hand at hip height with your palms facing inward. | Hinge slightly at the hips, soften your knees, and brace your core to enter an athletic stance. | Step your right foot out to the right, maintaining tension on the band and keeping your toes pointed forward. | Follow with your left foot, bringing your feet back to hip-width apart — do not let the feet touch. | Continue stepping laterally in one direction for the prescribed number of steps or distance. | Reverse direction and walk back to the starting point to complete one full repetition. | Keep your torso upright and your hips level throughout the entire movement. | Maintain steady tension on the band handles so the X cross stays in place under your feet.

t: Set up four markers (cones, spots, or tape) in an X pattern: place two markers roughly 3–5 meters apart horizontally and two more 3–5 meters apart vertically, so the four points form a cross or diamond shape. | Start at the center of the X, standing in an athletic ready position — knees slightly bent, weight on the balls of your feet, eyes forward. | Sprint to the front-left marker, touch it or step on it, then immediately change direction. | Sprint diagonally across the X to the back-right marker, touch it, and change direction again. | Sprint to the front-right marker, touch it, then immediately sprint diagonally to the back-left marker to complete the full X pattern. | Return to the center to finish one repetition, or continue moving through the pattern for a timed set. | Keep your hips low and your first step explosive on every direction change to maintain speed and control throughout the drill.

t: Kneel on the floor with your knees together and the tops of your feet flat on the mat, toes pointing straight back. | Lower your hips back and sit on your heels so your buttocks rest evenly on both heels. | Place your hands palms-down on your thighs, just above the knees. | Lengthen your spine upward, lift the crown of your head toward the ceiling, and gently draw your shoulders back and down. | Tuck your chin very slightly to keep the back of your neck long and neutral. | Close your eyes or soften your gaze, breathe slowly and deeply through your nose, and hold the pose for 1–5 minutes. | To release, lean forward onto your hands, lift your hips, and uncurl your feet one at a time before standing.

t: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and weight balanced evenly across both feet. | Mark or visualize a zigzag path on the floor with target points alternating to your left and right, spaced roughly 1–2 feet apart. | Drive off both feet simultaneously and hop diagonally forward and to the right, landing softly on the balls of your feet. | Absorb the landing by allowing your knees and hips to bend slightly, keeping your chest tall and core braced. | Without pausing, immediately explode off both feet again and redirect diagonally forward and to the left, hitting the next target point. | Continue alternating right and left hops in a fluid zigzag pattern, maintaining a consistent rhythm throughout. | Keep your arms loose and pumping to assist with balance and momentum during each redirect. | Complete the designated number of repetitions or distance, then land with control and hold the final position for one second to confirm balance. | Rest as needed, then repeat for the programmed number of sets.
